- **Paradigm prints no "Your character has been saved." on exit: the wait ends straight in the entry menu** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08, user: "this is the entire exit sequence on paradigm"; first seen in report `paradigm-20261008-125639`)*. In order:
  - `exit`
  - `You will exit after a period of silent meditation.`
  - about seven seconds with no prompt printed, a row of dots building up as it counts out;
  - the party lines when in one: `<Name> is no longer following you.` for each follower, then `Your party has been disbanded.`
  - the board's banner and the entry menu (`[E] . Enter the Realm` … `[X] . Exit Game`), under a `[PARADIGM]:` prompt.
- **The wait builds a row of dots on both realms** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08, user)*. A command typed during it lands after the dots so far (`...par` in the Paradigm capture).
- **A command sent during the wait is refused: `You may not perform any commands while waiting to exit!`** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08, user capture: an `sn` and a `par` each got it)*.
- **An attack calls the exit / quit wait off on both realms; whether the player can stop it differs by realm.**
  - **Paradigm: once the wait has started the player can't stop it, `break` included, but an attack can** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09, user: "typing break during the exit wait does not cancel it on paradigm")*: if a monster or NPC attacks you during the wait, the logout is called off.
  - **Paradigm: an attack prints `Your meditation has been interrupted - you may not exit now!`, the same wording as Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, user's Paradigm capture (screenshot))*. The capture, in order:
    ```
    [HP=234/MA=116]:exit
    You will exit after a period of silent meditation.
    ...
    You may not perform any commands while waiting to exit!
    par
    You may not perform any commands while waiting to exit!
    Your meditation has been interrupted - you may not exit now!
    The razor boar lunges at you, but you dodge out of the way!
    The razor boar impales you with its tusks for 19 damage!
    [HP=215/MA=116]:
    ```
    - The start line is followed by a line of dots (`...`).
    - A command typed during the wait (here `par`) is refused with the same line as on Stock, and no statline prompt shows between those lines during the wait: the typed `par` sits on a line of its own.
    - In this capture the interrupt line printed before the attack's own lines, and the statline prompt came back after the round's lines. The capture doesn't show whether a prompt directly follows the interrupt line when no other output is pending.
    - (What Paradigm prints here was `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` on 2026-10-08; settled 2026-10-09 by this capture.)
  - **Stock: the exact word `break` cancels the wait** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_execute_input` @0x450100–0x45015c → `_stop_users_exit` @0x420548)*. Only the whole word counts, not an abbreviation. Any other command gets `You may not perform any commands while waiting to exit!`, with no prompt after it.
  - **Stock: cancelled by `break` or by an attack, the game prints `Your meditation has been interrupted - you may not exit now!` and then the prompt** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_stop_users_exit` @0x42057a, @0x420586)*. The wait flag is cleared and the action delay zeroed, so commands are accepted again at once. (The printed line was `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`; settled for Stock 2026-10-09 from the DLL.)
  - **Stock: any attack attempt on you calls it off, hit or miss**: a monster's swing (`_attack_monster_user` @0x42e5fd, before the hit roll), a monster's cast at you (`_monster_cast` @0x427e05), another player's attack (`_attack_user_user` @0x42c13f, @0x42c171) and another player's spell on you (`_cast_user_target` @0x444c03).
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` On Stock, does `Your meditation has been interrupted - you may not exit now!` print on the end of the wait's row of dots when nothing was typed during the wait? The engine prints each `...` with no line end (@0x4232a6) and the interrupt string has no leading `\r` (@0x42057a), so by the code the row would read `................Your meditation has been interrupted - you may not exit now!`. The Paradigm capture in this topic doesn't settle it: a refused command had ended the dots' row before the line printed. A capture of an attack during a wait with nothing typed, on either realm, settles it. The client reads both shapes.
- **What Stock's exit routine does, in order** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_quit` @0x46196c, `_fast_update_character` @0x423161–0x42326d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **Two routes reach it:** the bare word `x`, which `_execute_input` tests as a whole word before the confusion roll and the command table (@0x45025e), and the `quit` command of the command table (*Command words and abbreviations*). `exit` is a different command there, the exits display, which fits the capture in the *Stock: `quit` starts the logout* bullet of this topic.
  - **At 0 HP or below both are refused, with different lines:** `x` gets `You may not exit MajorMud while you are mortally wounded!` from the exit routine (@0x46198e), and `quit` is stopped earlier by the dropped-character gate with `You may not do that while you are mortally wounded!` (*Health, resting & recovery → 0 HP — dropped / bleeding out*).
  - **At the command:** a running fight is ended with `*Combat Off*` (@0x4619c6); `You will exit after a period of silent meditation.` prints, then a line break and one dot; 6 is added to the action delay; the waiting flag is set; sneaking ends; the room sees `<Name> sits down and meditates.` (@0x461a59). No prompt is printed.
  - **During the wait:** each fast tick that leaves the delay above 0 prints `...` (@0x4232a6). From 6 that is five ticks, so by the code the row is 1 + 15 = 16 dots and the wait is 5 to 6 ticks. (The captured row in this topic shows 15 dots; which count is off by one wasn't settled.)
  - **On the sixth tick:** the waiting flag clears; the character leaves the game (`_cleanup_when_user_leaves`) and is saved; the board's text block #78 prints; then the hard-coded prompt `[MAJORMUD]: ` (@0x423203); and everyone in the game sees `<Name> just left the Realm.` (@0x42323c).
  - **A clean exit is not a hang-up and costs nothing** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, same routines)*: that branch (@0x423154–0x4231df) runs none of the hang-up routine's penalty code, doesn't set the hang-up flag (player word `+0x6f4`, mask 0x20) and doesn't call the death check; it sets the user's substate to 0x38 (@0x4231d8), and the hang-up routine does nothing for a user whose substate is under 0x82 (@0x408e37–0x408e3e), so the link dropping at the menu afterwards costs nothing either. The penalty and what the client makes of it are in *Hang-up / lost carrier*.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` `Your character has been saved. …` is not among the DLL's strings, and text block #78 is the only output between the dots and the prompt. Is the whole saved sentence that board-editable text block, so that a sysop could reword all of it and only the `[MAJORMUD]: ` prompt is fixed by the engine?
  - **The same `[MAJORMUD]: ` prompt follows the other ways out:** running out of BBS credits (`You have run out of credits for Major Mud.`, `_slow_update_character` @0x4225b6, with the `just left the Realm.` line to the game) and a death with no lives left (*Death & corpse recovery → Death lines & the miracle-save*).
- **A Stock login starts with the character's state flags cleared** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_load_player` @0x41543a, @0x4153de; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The whole flag word that holds sneaking, dragging, resting and the exit wait is zeroed and following is cleared, so none of them survives a login.
- **The entry menu takes whatever is sent next as a selection and redraws itself**, under a `[PARADIGM]:` prompt on that board *([OBSERVED] same report)*. `e` enters the realm, in either case: `e` and `E` work the same *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08, user)*.
- **Paradigm runs its cleanup live, with the game up; Stock cannot** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "it does a live cleanup which stock cannot do")*. A Stock board goes down for its cleanup, so players are put out of the game for it; a Paradigm realm stays up through it. So logging off ahead of a cleanup is a Stock matter only.

**Client use:**
- The cleanup-logoff orchestrator (`CleanupLogoutOrchestrator`) drops the carrier on any of three signs that the character is out: the saved line (`KnownPatterns.RealmExitSaved`), the entry-menu row, and on Stock the engine's own `[MAJORMUD]:` prompt. The prompt is no line, so it comes from the wire scanner: `WirePromptScanner.RealmLeftPromptObserved` fires for a `[MAJORMUD]:` standing where a prompt goes (never inside text the active statline pattern matched), and `CleanupLogoutOrchestrator.NoteRealmLeftPrompt` acts on it only while its own exit is out. It was added because the saved sentence is probably the board-editable text block #78 (the `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` in this topic), while the prompt is fixed in the engine (user, 2026-10-09: "yes"). A wait-timeout remains the last fallback. (An earlier line named only the saved line, with the entry-menu row and a wait-timeout as fallbacks; superseded 2026-10-09.)
- **An exit the game calls off sends the orchestrator back to waiting for a safe room** (`CleanupLogoutOrchestrator.OnRealmExitInterrupted`, `KnownPatterns.RealmExitInterrupted`, read at the start of a row or after the wait's dots). The room must then read safe without a break for one combat round (`InterruptSettle`, `TickEngine.CombatTickInterval`) before the exit is sent again. After three called-off exits (`MaxInterruptions`) it stops waiting and the timeouts decide: one re-send, then the carrier drop. **Client policy:** the safe-room check can't see every attacker (another player, a monster set not to be attacked, one unseen in the dark), and each exit sent ends a fight in progress. Before 2026-10-09 the line was not read: the exit was re-sent blind after 15 s and the carrier dropped at 30 s, mid-fight.
- `InGameCapture.AtBoardMenu` is set when the saved line or the entry-menu row is seen after the character has been in the game, and cleared by the next statline prompt or the link ending. While it is set `EngineSendGate` holds every automatic command, `OutboundMovementObserver` doesn't read a typed selection as a move, `MessageCandidateWatcher` stages nothing, and `StatlineReconciler` is re-armed so it waits for a room display. Before this the party poll, a buff, `sn` and `set statline full` were each sent into the menu, and the `e` typed to re-enter was tracked as a step east (report `paradigm-20261008-125639`).
- The client does not hold its engines during the wait itself, only once the menu or the saved line arrives: an attack can call the logout off, and combat and healing have to be free to answer it. So an automatic command sent in that window is refused with the line above, which costs nothing.
- The wait's start line, its refusal line and its row of dots are router patterns (`KnownPatterns.RealmExitMeditation`, `RealmExitWaiting`, and `RealmExitDots` for the row of dots) so they aren't staged as unrecognized lines; nothing acts on those three. The interrupt line is a pattern too (`KnownPatterns.RealmExitInterrupted`) and is acted on, as the bullet before this one records. (An earlier line said the wait's lines are patterns only so they aren't staged; superseded 2026-10-09 for the interrupt line.)

### Command words and abbreviations
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`) · Realm: Stock*

The command words are built into the DLL as a letter-by-letter table (`_parse_command` @0x40dd44 and `_parse_p/r/s/t/u/w_command`). Unless a bullet says otherwise, what follows is tagged *[OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `_parse_command` run in an emulator for every prefix; not hand-read*. Four entries were also read by hand: `a` (@0x40de88), `aa` (@0x40e507), `kil` (@0x410999) and `bre` (@0x40ea7e).

- **Only the first word of a line is looked up, case-blind, and it must follow the table letter by letter.** A word that runs past a command's spelling is not that command (`getx`, `whox`, `attacks`, `breaks` are nothing). Each prefix has its own entry, and many short prefixes are entries for nothing, so an abbreviation works only from the length listed here.
- **Attacks:**
  - attack: `a`, `at`, `att`, `atta`, `attac`, `attack`, and also `au`;
  - bash: `bas`, `bash`, **`aa`**, `al`…`allout`, `forc`, `force` (all one command; see *Combat → Attack command words*);
  - backstab: `bs`, `backs`…`backstab` (`b`, `ba`, `bac`, `back` are nothing);
  - smash: `sma`, `smas`, `smash` (`sm` is nothing);
  - punch: `pu`, `pun`, `punc`, `punch`, and also `pur` and `purg` (`purge` in full is another command);
  - kick: `kic`, `kick` (**`k` and `ki` are nothing**);
  - jumpkick: `ju`…`jumpkick`;
  - `kil` and `kill` are the dead killblow command (*Combat → Attack command words*).
- **`break`:** `bre`, `brea`, `break`. `br` is not break: it is the channel broadcast (*Talk & chat channels → Channel broadcast (`'`, `-`, `br`) and `join`*).
- **`quit` against `quiet`:** `q` and `quit` in full are quit; `qu`, `qui`, `quie` and `quiet` are quiet (`bri`…`brief` does the same). `exi`, `exit`, `exits` are the exits display. The bare word `x` is tested before the table (*Realm exit / logoff sequence*).
- **`sneak`:** `sn`…`sneak`. **`hide`:** `hid`, `hide` (`hi` is nothing). **`search`:** `sea`…`search` (`se` is southeast).
- **`status`:** `st`, `sta`, `stat`, `statu`, `status`. `stas`, `stash` is stash and `statl`…`statline` is statline.
- **`spells`:** `sp`…`spells`. **`powers`:** `po`…`powers`.
- **`who`:** `who` only, or `sc`, `sca`, `scan` (`wh` is nothing; `whi`…`whisper` is the telepath).
- **Resting:** `rest` only in full (`re`, `res` are nothing; `rese`…`research` is a dead command). Meditate is `med`…`meditate`; `me` and `mes`…`mesmerize` are the dead mesmerize command.
- **Items and inventory:** `g`, `ge`, `get`; `dro`, `drop` (`dra`, `drag` is drag; `dr` is nothing); `i` or `inve`…`inventory` (**`in` and `inv` are nothing**; `invi`…`invite`, `invo`…`invoke` = cast); `eq`…`equip`; `wea`, `wear` (`weal`…`wealth` is wealth); `rem`…`remove`; `us`, `use`; `bu`, `buy`.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Paradigm's accepted abbreviations of `inventory` are not recorded. `OutboundOpenObserver` matches Stock's table (`i`, or `inve` and longer) when it counts the inventory reads out for `ChestOpenTracker`. Question: which forms does Paradigm take for `inventory`?
- **Doors:** `op`…`open`; `pi`…`picklock`; `loc`, `lock` (`lo`, `loo`, `look` are look).
- **Others a client sends:** `l` look; `c`, `ca`…`cast`; `par`, `part`, `party` (`p`, `pa` are nothing); `hea`…`health` and also `he` (`hel`, `help` is help); `exp`…`experience`; `trai`, `train` (`tr`, `tra` are nothing; `trac`, `track` is track); `fo`, `fol`…`follow`; `le`, `lea`, `leav`, `leave` *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, the same emulator run: all four return command 56, `_cmd_leave`)*; `bg`, `gb`, `broadg`…`broadgang`; `gos`…`gossip`.
- **Moves:** `n`, `s`, `e`, `w`, `ne`, `nw`, `se`, `sw`, `u`, `d` and the full words. Partial spellings mostly fail: `no`, `nor`, `nort`, `so`, `sou`, `sout`, `ea`, `we`, `wes` are nothing; `eas`, `dow`, `up`, `northe`…, `northw`…, `southe`…, `southw`… work.
- **Single letters that are nothing:** `b f h j k m o p r t v y z`.
- **Punctuation leads:** a word starting `'` or `-` is the channel broadcast; `/` the telepath; `>` the directed say; `?` help.
- **Words the table knows that do nothing** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_handle_commands` jump table @0x4137a6; the handlers return "not a command", e.g. `_cmd_killblow` @0x451673, `_cmd_tame` @0x4528e3, `_cmd_mesmerize` @0x4528ea, `_cmd_identity` @0x4541ea)*: `take`, `throw`, `fire`, `shoot`, `donate`, `play`, `text`, `sound`, `autocombat`, `defend`, `hunt`, `dismiss`, `research`, `identity`, `tame`, `mesmerize`, `kill`. The line is then handled like any unrecognised one.
- **A line whose first word is nothing is tried as one of the room's exit words and as a spell's cast code; what is left is a social or speech** (spoken, or refused with `Your command had no effect.` in talk slow): see *Talk & chat channels → Directed say vs undirected say*. So with talk fast, `take sword`, `kill rat` or `ki rat` is said to the room.
- **Some commands only run when the word stands alone** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_handle_commands` @0x41416c, @0x413bd6, @0x413bae, @0x41400b, @0x41404c, @0x41408d; `_cmd_experience` @0x45a821)*: `who` / `scan`, `spells`, `powers`, `quiet` / `brief`, `verbose`, `version` and `exp`. With anything after the word the line is not a command.
- **Replies of the small housekeeping commands** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` strings @0x47d2f5, @0x47d305, @0x47d32c, @0x413adb, @0x48b8b0)*: `quiet` / `brief` → `Quiet mode set`; `verbose` → `Verbose mode set`; `version` → `MajorMUD v %s`; `save` → `You may not save your character. You must exit normally so that …`; `exp` → `Exp: %s Level: %d Exp needed for next level: %s (%s) [%s%%]` (current exp, level, exp still to earn, the next level's total, a percentage).

### Character settings — `set` and the `pro` sheet
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_set` @0x458b60, `_display_profile` @0x43ae7c) · Realm: Stock*

- **`set <option>` toggles and `set <option> <value>` sets.** The settings are per character and saved with it. Replies:
  - `set talk` (or `set speech`) `fast|slow`: see *Talk & chat channels → Talk modes are per-realm configuration*; bad value `Valid talk options: FAST, SLOW`.
  - `set responses brief|verbose` → `Responses to talking will be brief now.` / `Responses to talking will be verbose now.`; bad value `Valid interrupt options: BRIEF, VERBOSE` (the engine's own wording). Brief replaces the `You say "…"` echo: see *Talk & chat channels → Directed say vs undirected say*.
  - `set telepath on|off` → `Telepaths will no longer be blocked.` / `Future telepaths will be blocked.`; `Valid telepath options: ON, OFF`.
  - `set maxpages <n>`, `set maxgossip <n>`, `set maxauction <n>`: see *Talk & chat channels → Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement* and *Talk & chat channels → Gossip and auction*.
  - `set gossip on|off`, `set auction on|off` → the lines in *Talk & chat channels → Gossip and auction*; `Valid gossip options: ON, OFF`, `Valid auction options: ON, OFF`.
  - `set page on|ok|off` → `Paging is now set to Ok.` / `Paging is now set to Off.`; `Valid page options: ON/OK, OFF`.
  - `set entrances on|off` → `You will now see game broadcasts such as user entrances and exits.` / `You will no longer see game broadcasts such as user entrances and exits.`; `Valid entrance options: ON, OFF`.
  - `set messages high|medium|low` → `All messages will now be displayed.` / `Only some messages will be displayed now.` / `Only important messages will be displayed now.`; `Valid messaging options: High, Medium, Low`. Bare `set messages` cycles high → low → medium → high.
  - `set receive on|off` → `You will now accept items/currency from other players.` / `You will refuse any gifts from other players.`; bad value `Valid interrupt options: ON, OFF` (the engine's own wording).
  - `set interrupt on|off` → `PVP Combat will now interrupt your typing and output.` / `PVP Combat will be displayed as normal messages.`; `Valid interrupt options: ON, OFF`.
  - `set warning on|off`: see *Character stats & progression → How your alignment moves during play*.
  - `set style technical|fantasy` → `You will now receive technical style messages.` (the two-word form prints it misspelt, `You will now receive techincal style messages.`) / `You will now receive fantasy style messages.`; `Valid style options: TECHNICAL, FANTASY`. Technical style changes the `who` table (*The `who` listing*).
  - `set palette 0|1|2|3` → `You will now use colour palette number 0.` (… `1.`, `2.`, `3.`); `Valid palettes are: 0, 1, 2, 3`.
  - `set keep on|off` → `If you die/reroll you will keep some of your experience.` / `If you die/reroll you will start with 0 experience.`, followed by `(Currently disabled on this system)` when the board has it off; `Valid KEEP options: ON, OFF`.
  - `set gang online|all` → `You will now only see online gang members.` / `You will now see all gang members.`; `Valid gang options: Online, All`.
  - `set gender male|female` → `You are now male!` / `You are now female!`, or `You hand over <coins> and you are now male!` when the board charges for it; `Valid gender options: MALE, FEMALE`, `You cannot afford to do that!`, `You may not do that here!`.
  - `set suicide` → `Enter the current password:` or `Enter New Password:`, and the next line typed is taken as the password.
    - **Any prefix of `suicide` opens it** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_set` @0x458b60: the option word is tested with `sameto(margv[1], "suicide")` @0x458ba1; Realm: Stock)*: `set sui`, `set s` and `SET  SUICIDE` all reach the prompt.
    - **`suicide` and `reroll` are one command** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, `_cmd_suicide` @0x4692be serves both; Realm: Stock)*. With a password set it prints `Enter your suicide password:` (@0x4693c8) and takes the next line as the password. *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10 (user): the prompt appears on the cursor's line on both Stock and Paradigm.)*
    - **None of these prompts ends its line until it is answered**, so a client sees the prompt as a completed line only after the password has been sent *([OBSERVED], capture noted in `SuicidePasswordTracker`)*.
    - **Two refusals take the place of the prompt** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock DLL)*: `You may not suicide or reroll during a tournament.` (@0x4692d2) and `You may not suicide or reroll in this room!` (@0x469346).
    - **The password is echoed as `*`; Realm: differs.** (An earlier note had this as a review's read of the Stock DLL with no address, tagged `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`; superseded 2026-10-10.)
      - **Paradigm prints one `*` for each character sent, whatever the length** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "on paradigm it asterisks whatever you send as input for the password"; Realm: Paradigm)*.
      - **Stock calls `echsec('*', 8)` where each password is read** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`: in `_cmd_set`'s suicide branch @0x458bcc (a password is already set) and @0x458c06 (none is yet), and in `_cmd_suicide` @0x4693e4; Realm: Stock)*. The first argument is the echo character, the second is 8. `echsec` is the board's routine, imported by the DLL (@0x478a1e), so the DLL does not show how many `*` it prints. The DLL itself sets no length: the new password is stored with a plain `strcpy` (@0x408793) and compared with `sameas` (@0x408509, @0x408650).
      - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` On Stock, does the board stop taking (and echoing) the password at 8 characters, or echo one `*` for every character sent as Paradigm does? Asked 2026-10-10: the user doesn't know which.
      - **Client policy** (2026-10-10, user: "id fall to it functions the same as paradigm"): until Stock's echo is seen, the client assumes Stock echoes as Paradigm does, and masks a run of any length.
      - **Client policy:** nothing in the client counts on a length. A run of `*` of any length after `Enter your suicide password:`, `Enter the current password:` or `Enter New Password:` is the echo on both realms, and a bug report writes the run as `[redacted]` so it doesn't show how long the password is (`BugReportScrub`); the stored password is sent whole (`SuicideHandler`) and stored whole (`SuicidePasswordTracker`).
    - **Client use:** `SuicideHandler` (`@suicide` sends the stored password only on the prompt, alone on the cursor row or straight after the statline as the configured pattern reads it, `WirePromptScanner.TrySplitPromptRow`; either refusal ends the wait; the send gate and the telepath pacer, `TelepathPacer.Hold`, are held in between, since whatever line reaches the game first after `suicide` is taken as the password); `SuicidePasswordTracker.IsSetSuicide` / `PasswordEntryLikely` and `SentCommandTrail.RowIsGamePrompt` (a line typed at any of these prompts is never kept in a bug report; a typed `suicide` covers the user's own next line, which an engine's line in between doesn't use up).
  - `set statline …`: see *Statline & prompt shape*.
  - `set follow blind|normal`: see *Party → Following the leader: follow / drag movement*; bad value `Valid follow options: BLIND, NORMAL`.
  - Anything else: `Valid SET options: SUICIDE, MAXPAGES, MAXAUCTION, MAXGOSSIP, FOLLOW, INTERRUPT, RECEIVE, WARNING, TELEPATH, ENTRANCES, TALK, PALETTE, PAGE, KEEP`.
- **`set messages` filters room lines by a priority each line is sent with**: 0 always shows; 1–10 shows unless the viewer is on Low; 11–20 shows only on High (`_tell_room` @0x46b090–0x46b0b2). Say, yell, directed say and socials are sent at 0, so they are never filtered. Which lines carry a higher priority was not surveyed.
- **`[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` The option word may be abbreviated, and the first option it fits wins.** Each test is the host's prefix compare, tried in a fixed order: maxpages, maxgossip, maxauction, gender, style, interrupt, gossip, auction, keep, responses, messages, receive, warning, gang, telepath, palette, entrances, page, statline, follow, speech / talk. By that order `set st full` would be taken as **style** (`Valid style options: TECHNICAL, FANTASY`), and `statline` needs at least `sta`. This rests on the host's compare doing what its name says; does `set st full` answer with the style line on a Stock board?
- **`pro` prints the settings back, one `Label: value` row each, in this order:** `Life for this CHAR  %s minutes`, `Display Mode:       Verbose|Brief`, `Statusline:         On|Full|Off` (or the custom template itself), `Broadcast Channel:  %d`, `Talking speed:      Fast|Slow`, `Follow Mode:        Blind|Normal`, `Attack Interrupts:  On|Off`, `Receive Items:      Enabled|Disabled`, `Warn on Evil:       Yes|No`, `Allow Telepaths:    Yes|No`, `Block Entrance Msg: Yes|No`, `Allow Gossip:       Yes|No (%d every 3 seconds)`, `Allow Auction:      Yes|No (%d every 3 seconds)`, `View gang members:  Online|All` (only in a gang), `Keep some exp:      Yes|No`, `Messages:           High|Medium|Low`, `Paging:             Ok|Off (%d every 3 seconds)`, `Talking Responses:  Brief|Verbose`, `Style:              Technical|Fantasy`, `Colour Palette:     %d`, then `You do not have a suicide password set.` when none is set. It carries no evil-point number (*Character stats & progression → How your alignment moves during play*).

### The `who` listing
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_scan_of_users` @0x43a2d9) · Realm: Stock*

- **`who` and `scan` are the same command**, and it runs only when typed alone (*Command words and abbreviations*).
- **Frame:** `         Current Adventurers`, `         ===================`, a blank line, then one row per player. Nobody listed: `There are no users in the game at the moment.`
- **Row:** the alignment title right-aligned in 8 columns, the name, one marker character, the level title, then ` of <gang>` when in a gang (format `%s%8.8s %s%s  %c  %s%s%s ` @0x484d76). The left column can read `Lawful` in place of the title, on one value of a character field and with a board option on (@0x43a7a4–0x43a7b6).
- **The marker between the name and the title is that player's gossip switch:** `x` when they have gossip off, `-` otherwise (@0x43a740–0x43a74e, @0x43a787–0x43a795). It says nothing about whether the player is alive or dropped.
- **The row's last field is the word `EDITED` or a space** (@0x484d0f; set from a character field that wasn't identified). This routine prints no single-letter role markers.
- **With `set style technical` the same command prints a different table**: header `Title` / `Name` / `Reputation` / `Gang/Guild`, rows `%s%-15.15s %s%-20.20s%c%c %s%-10.10s %s%-19.19s %s%-6.6s` (@0x484d16), where the two flag characters are `g` (gossip off) and `a` (auction off).
  - **Both styles as seen on a Stock board** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, the user's capture; player names left out)*. `set style` alone toggles it: `You will now receive technical style messages.` / `You will now receive fantasy style messages.`
    - Technical: a header row `Title           Name                    Reputation Gang/Guild`, a rule of `=-=-=-…`, then one row per player: level title, full name, reputation (`Lawful`, `Good`, `Neutral`, …), and the gang or `None`.
    - Fantasy: `Current Adventurers`, a rule of `=`, a blank line, then `<reputation> <First Last>   -  <title>` with `  of <gang>` after the title for a gang member. A player whose reputation reads `Neutral` in the technical table has **no word** in the fantasy row's left column.
  - **The style setting does not exist on Paradigm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user)*.
- **Accounts carrying one host flag (not identified) are left out of the list** (@0x43a5e4–0x43a5ee).

**Client use:**
- `WhoListParser` reads both layouts into the same record (name, alignment, title, gang), so every consumer of the player list sees one shape.
  - Fantasy rows: the marker between the name and the title (`-` or `x`) is read past and not recorded. A trailing `EDITED` is dropped; before 2026-10-09 it was read as part of the title, or of the gang when there was one. A gang whose own name ends in a separate word `EDITED` loses that word, since the two can't be told apart.
  - Technical table: the header `Title` / `Name` / `Reputation` / `Gang/Guild` and the `=-=-` rule open the block; a row is cut by column (title 15, name, the two flag characters, reputation, gang 19). `None` is no gang, and what follows the gang column (the row's last field) is dropped. The reputation must be an alignment word or `Neutral`, which keeps other lines in the block from reading as rows. The name column is taken as 20 or 21 wide: in the capture in this topic `Reputation` stands one column further right than the engine's format puts it, in the header too.
- **A blank left column in the fantasy style is stored as `Neutral`**, the word the technical table prints for the same player. `AlignmentTracker.SelfAlignment` reads that record, so Stock's alignment check through `who` (`AlignmentGearCheck`) takes a blank as Neutral, not as unknown.

### Hang-up / lost carrier
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_ljngame_huprou` @0x408d9a) · Realm: Stock (Paradigm where a bullet says so)*

- **A hang-up takes the character out of the game in the same call; it is not left standing in the room.** The routine saves the character, applies the penalty of this topic if one is due, tells the game, and clears the player slot (@0x408dc7 … @0x4091da).
- **Everyone in the game sees `<Name> just disconnected!!!`** (three exclamation marks, @0x409152), not the `just left the Realm.` line of a normal exit.
- **A hang-up while in the realm can carry a penalty, set by the board.** `.MSG` option #38 has four levels (`_reload__wccmmud` @0x40141d; the DLL's own initial value is `HIGH`, which is not a board's value):
  - `HIGH`: every hang-up while in the realm;
  - `MEDIUM`: only when in autocombat or being attacked (@0x408edf–0x408f01);
  - `LOW`: only when in PvP combat (@0x408f0b–0x408f20);
  - `NONE`: never.
- **What boards really set** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user)*: the penalty depends on the BBS's configuration, and most boards that have one take HP only. It applies to a hang-up in PvP as well as one in a fight with a monster.
- **Paradigm penalises only a hang-up in active PvP, and takes HP only: it drops no items** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; Realm: Paradigm)*. The user's words: "paradigm only has a hp penalty for hanging in active PVP, it doesnt drop items. if it did drop items, it'd be the same as stock, right into the room except with no room item maximums so it'd never spill over".
  - The second sentence is what the user expects Paradigm would do if it dropped items, not something seen: straight onto the floor of the room. Paradigm rooms have no item cap (*Death & corpse recovery → Deathpile — where the items go*), so nothing would fail to fit.
  - Stock does not spill a hang-up drop: an item that doesn't fit the room is lost (**Items**, under *What the penalty takes* in this topic) *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "if dll reads as vanish, they vanish")*. (An earlier note asked whether a Stock hang-up drop spills into connected rooms as a deathpile does; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **What the penalty takes:**
  - **With HP above 0: a random share of max HP**, between options #58 and #59 percent of it (each 0–100; initial values 25 and 50) (@0x408f38–0x408f88).
    - **The share is taken off HP with no floor** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_ljngame_huprou`; Realm: Stock)* (`sub` @0x408f88), so it can leave HP at or below 0, and at or under the death threshold. The death check that ends the routine (@0x409180) then kills: **a penalised hang-up at low HP can be a death too**, when HP minus the share is at or under the threshold (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*). When it lands at or below 0 and above the threshold the check does nothing (@0x419ad9–0x419af3) and the character is saved at that HP.
  - **With HP at or below 0: the death threshold is added to HP** (@0x408f9b), which puts it at or under the threshold, and the routine ends in the death check (@0x409180). So a penalised hang-up while dropped kills the character, with the normal death handling.
  - **Items: up to option #60 of them (0–100, initial value 100) are taken and put on the visible floor of the room the character is in; one that doesn't fit is gone** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_ljngame_huprou` @0x408fa9–0x409114, `_remove_item_from_inventory` @0x41b2c8, `_add_item_to_room` @0x41d0a1; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "if dll reads as vanish, they vanish"; Realm: Stock)*.
    - **Which slots:** every other inventory slot (0, 2, … 98 of 100; @0x40905d, @0x40906d), then every other key-ring slot (0, 2, … 48 of 50; @0x409102, @0x409111). One count runs through both loops and each stops when it reaches option #60 (@0x409060–0x40906b, @0x409105–0x40910f). With the option at 0 neither loop runs.
    - **Per inventory slot:** an empty slot or an item with no record is passed over (@0x408fb5, @0x408fd6). A LoyalItem (ability 100; 21 ability words read from +0x2f6, @0x408fed–0x409005) is left on the character and not counted. Anything else is removed from the character first (@0x40901b) and only then placed.
    - **The removal takes the first copy of that item number counted from slot 0**, not necessarily the slot being looked at (@0x41b317–0x41b321). A worn copy is taken off the body when no other copy is left (@0x41b39b–0x41b408), so worn gear is dropped like carried gear.
    - **A `Destroy On Death` item is removed, counted and never placed** (item byte +0x42c, @0x409023 → @0x409050). It is the byte `_check_kill_user` tests to send an item `to its rightful place` in place of the floor (@0x419dd4 → @0x419ebc). That it is the data's `Destroy On Death` column is read from that behaviour and from its neighbours +0x42a and +0x42b behaving as `Retain After Uses` (@0x41b554) and `Not Droppable` (@0x41fad5), not from a field table.
    - **Any other item goes to `_add_item_to_room` for that one room, visible side** (@0x40903f). When that returns -1 the item is not counted and nothing puts it back (@0x409047–0x409048): it is in no inventory and no room. The loop goes on to the next slot with its count unchanged.
    - **So a full room costs more, not less:** a failed placement doesn't use up the option's count, so in a room that can take nothing the loop goes on through every other inventory slot and each non-loyal item it reaches is lost. Option #60 limits how many items land or are destroyed by flag, not how many are taken.
    - **`_add_item_to_room` places in the room it is given and nowhere else** (`_get_room_data` @0x41d0b1; no exit is walked). The deathpile's outward walk is `_dispose_of_item_in_room` / `_dispose_of_item_in_trail` (*Death & corpse recovery → Deathpile — where the items go*), which the hang-up routine does not call. It returns -1 when the room or item record is missing (@0x41d0c8–0x41d0d2), when `_add_logical_to_room` refuses (a limited item already at its limit, @0x44b70d–0x44b718), or when no slot takes it (@0x41d1e1–0x41d1f7). An item with no uses count (-1) joins a pile of the same item already lying there (@0x41d173–0x41d189); otherwise it needs one of the 17 visible slots (@0x41d1a4–0x41d1d2; *Items, inventory & equipment → Room item capacity: drop refusal*).
    - **Keys differ in two ways** (@0x409082–0x4090ff): a LoyalItem key stays on the ring but is counted (@0x4090b9 → @0x4090ff), and a key whose placement fails is counted as well as lost (the result of @0x4090f6 is discarded, @0x4090fe).
- **Where it is free:** in a `Protected` room when not in autocombat and not being attacked, and in a `Colliseum` room while arenas are in normal mode (@0x408e70–0x408ea9).
- **The next login says so:** `Last time you were on, you disconnected while playing.` then `The gods have punished you appropriately.` (`_load_player` @0x41541d, @0x415428). The flag behind it is set on every in-realm hang-up outside the two free cases, even when the option is `NONE` and nothing was taken (@0x40913b).
  - **They print once, on the first entry after such a hang-up** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_load_player`; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: the flag (player word `+0x6f4`, mask 0x20) is tested at @0x415409 and the whole word is cleared straight after the lines (@0x41543a), so the next load prints nothing. An entry that doesn't show them doesn't follow a non-free hang-up, or another session loaded the character in between.
- **The order of an in-realm hang-up, from start to end** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_ljngame_huprou` @0x408d9a, `_check_kill_user` @0x419a33, `_save_player` @0x46df70; Realm: Stock)*:
  - **The character is saved first, as it stands** (@0x408dc7), before anything is taken.
  - **The two free cases are tested next** (@0x408e70–0x408eb2). A free hang-up skips the level test, the penalty and the flag (jump to @0x409143).
  - **Then the level** (@0x408ed6–0x408f28; the byte at `ds:0x482d68`: 1 `HIGH`, 2 `MEDIUM`, 3 `LOW`). A hang-up the level doesn't penalise skips the penalty (jump to @0x40911a) and still gets the flag.
  - **Then the HP part** (@0x408f2e–0x408fa2), **then the item loops** (@0x408fa9–0x409114). The item loops run in both HP cases, so **the items are dropped before the death**.
  - **Then the flag** (@0x40913b), `<Name> just disconnected!!!` to the game (@0x409152–0x409170), and **the death check, `_check_kill_user`** (@0x409180). The check is called on every one of these paths, the free and the unpenalised ones too. It returns at once with HP above 0 (@0x419a58–0x419a60) and with HP above the death threshold (@0x419ad9–0x419af3), so a dropped character whose hang-up was free or not penalised is left dropped, at the HP it had. **A `Colliseum` room with arenas in normal mode is the exception**: there the check skips the threshold test and takes any HP of 0 or less as the colliseum's free death (@0x419ac6–0x419ad7; *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*), so a character that hangs up dropped in one comes back with its HP put back, in the death room, with its lives unchanged. (An earlier form of this bullet had every free hang-up leave a dropped character dropped; corrected 2026-10-10.)
  - **Last, the character is saved again and its slot cleared** (`_cleanup_when_user_leaves` @0x4091ac, `_save_player` @0x4091ba, `_clear_player` @0x4091c7 and @0x4091da). The two tests ahead of that second save (@0x409191–0x4091a2) are the ones `_save_player` makes itself (@0x46df92–0x46dfaa), so a character that can be saved at all is saved after the penalty.
- **So a penalised hang-up while dropped, or at an HP the share takes under the threshold, is a full death that nobody at the keyboard sees** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_check_kill_user` @0x419a33; Realm: Stock)*:
  - `You have been killed!` (@0x419b03), the miracle line and `You have %d lives left.` (@0x41a160, @0x41a173) are printed to a user whose link is gone. The room sees `<Name> is dead.` (@0x419b83).
  - A life is taken (@0x41a0f0), HP and mana are set to their maximum (@0x41a11a–0x41a12f), the character is put in the death room (@0x41a136–0x41a142) and saved there (@0x41a1d3). What a death does besides is in *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*.
  - **Its items lie in two lots**: up to option #60 of them on the visible floor of the room, from the penalty's own loops (**Items**, under *What the penalty takes* in this topic), and the rest as a deathpile from the same room, placed and spilled as any death's (*Death & corpse recovery → Deathpile — where the items go*). Coins go to that room's coin counts (*Death & corpse recovery → Coins in the deathpile*).
  - **The next entry shows no death line.** The character stands in the death room at full HP with one life fewer; the two login lines of the *The next login says so* bullet of this topic are all that is printed.
  - On the last life the character record is deleted (*Death & corpse recovery → Death lines & the miracle-save*), so there is no next entry.
- **A room can name another room, on its own map, that a character who leaves the game in it is put in** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, corrected 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`; Realm: Stock)*: room field `+0x570`. When it is not 0 the player's room number is set to it on a hang-up, both the free one (@0x408eb2–0x408ecb) and the rest (@0x40911a–0x409135), and on a normal quit: `_cmd_quit` sets player flag `+0x6f4` mask 0x08 (@0x461a25), and `_fast_update_character` on that flag applies the field, runs `_cleanup_when_user_leaves` and saves the character (@0x423154–0x4231aa). (An earlier form of this bullet said the flag was not traced to what sets it; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **That it is the room's leave-the-game room is inferred from position and behaviour, not read from a field table**: it sits directly after the graveyard field `+0x56c` (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*), and the room-update code compares and copies the two together (@0x45c151–0x45c169, @0x45c775–0x45c787). The imported `Rooms` table has no such column.
  - On a hang-up the move comes after the item loops and before the death check, which takes the death room from the player's room at that moment (@0x419a9b–0x419aa7, @0x419df1–0x419dfd). So in such a room the penalty's items fall where the character stood and the deathpile in the room the field names.
- **A death by a hang-up shows on the way back in: the character stands where the dead arrive** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: both)*. The user's words: "we'll know immediately upon logging in that if our hangup resulted in our death, because we'll be in one of the rooms where you go when you die in a map. so if we were in darkwood forest, got low, hungup and got hit with a hangup penalty then we logged back in and were in the halls of the dead, that hangup killed us." Recorded for both realms: the user gave it as the rule and named no realm, and nothing in this topic or the DLL makes it differ (on Paradigm a penalised hang-up "works the same as stock", the Paradigm bullet of this topic). Which room that is, room by room, is on record for Stock only.
  - **Stock: it is the graveyard of the room the hang-up left the character in** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` and map file `wccmp002.dat`; Realm: Stock)*. The routine first puts the character in the room's leave-the-game room when it has one (the *A room can name another room* bullet of this topic), and the death check then reads the graveyard field of the room the character is in (@0x419a9b–0x419aa7, @0x419c0f–0x419c23; the rooms are in *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*, the table under *Graveyard rooms are per-map*). 366 rooms have a leave-the-game room, and for 101 of them the dead of a hang-up arrive somewhere else than the dead of an ordinary death:
    - 95 rooms of map 17 name `17/3247` (`Grand Chamber`) for both; `17/3247` names no graveyard, so the dead of a hang-up there go to the defaults (`1/2189`, or `1/142`);
    - `17/3231`, `17/2019`, `17/3028`, `12/2381` and `12/2378` leave through `17/2982`, `17/1`, `17/1`, `12/1` and `12/1`, which name none: the defaults again;
    - `17/2020` names `17/2514` and leaves through `17/1791`, whose graveyard is `17/2415`.

    So the dead of a hang-up arrive in one of 16 named rooms or the two defaults.
  - **Two rooms leave the game through the room their dead arrive in** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, same file; Realm: Stock)*: `17/785` and `17/1773`, both through `17/2415` (`An Open Grave`). A character that hangs up in one comes back in `17/2415` dead or alive.
  - **A character the hang-up did not kill comes back in the room it left, or in that room's leave-the-game room** (the same reading; Realm: Stock).
  - **Paradigm:** the zones it shares with Stock send their dead where Stock does, and `14/1077` is where the dead of Albion arrive (the rooms that can be reached from it without a boat); for the rest of Paradigm's own rooms the per-room data is not on record (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*, the Paradigm bullets under *Graveyard rooms are per-map*).
- **Paradigm: a penalised hang-up kills the same way as on Stock** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; Realm: Paradigm)*. The user's words: "yes it works the same as stock, paradigms pvp HP hang penalty is 10% and i believe death is at -30 HP". So a hang-up in active PvP while dropped, or with HP low enough for the share to take it under the death threshold, is a death there too.
  - **Paradigm's PvP hang-up penalty is 10% of max HP** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; Realm: Paradigm)*.
  - **The death threshold there is whatever that board sets** (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*); the user's "i believe death is at -30 HP" is one board's figure as remembered, and nothing relies on it. (An earlier note here asked whether −30 is Paradigm's threshold; withdrawn 2026-10-10 on the user's ruling that the client should not care what the figure is.)
  - (An earlier note asked whether a Paradigm character that hangs up in active PvP while dropped, or low on HP, dies; settled 2026-10-09.)
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` **Does Paradigm print anything at the login after a penalised hang-up, the way Stock prints `Last time you were on, you disconnected while playing.`?** The user (2026-10-10): "i dont know, i assume it prints the same as stock". An assumption, so the client does not require the line on Paradigm; if it sees the Stock line on a realm that isn't Stock it logs that it did (`HangupItemRecheck.NoteHangupLoginLine`). Realm: Paradigm.
- **Nothing raises a character's HP while it is out of the game** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; Realm: both)*. What can still change it between leaving and the next entry is the hang-up routine itself, as this topic has it: the penalty's share, a death (HP to its maximum) and, on Stock, the colliseum's free death.
- `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` A normal logoff runs a different routine with no penalty (`_ljngame_lofrou` @0x408d3c), and the hang-up routine skips a slot that is already cleared (@0x408e21). Which of the two the BBS-level exit (`=x`) reaches is host behaviour and not in this DLL. On a Stock board with the penalty on, does `=x` in a fight or while dropped cost HP or items, and does the next login print the two lines?
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **the client records a board's penalty per realm and hangs up exactly as configured regardless.** The user enters it in Settings → BBS on the realm (`RealmProfile.HangupPenaltyEnabled`; `HangupPvpHpFromPercent` / `HangupPvpHpToPercent` / `HangupPvpItemsDropped` for a hang-up in PvP combat; `HangupPvePenaltyEnabled` with `HangupPveHpFromPercent` / `HangupPveHpToPercent` / `HangupPveItemsDropped` for one in a fight with a monster; `HangupOutsideFightPenaltyEnabled` for every hang-up, at the PvE figures). The HP pair starts at 25 and 50; the item count starts at 0, not the DLL's 100, because most boards take HP only. No hang-up is sent, held, delayed or skipped because of it: that stays with Disable Hangups, the health settings, the PvP actions and `@panic`.
- **On Paradigm `;o` is answered `Goodbye!` and the board drops the link at once** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, report `paradigm-20261009-081205`; Realm: Paradigm)*. It was sent from the game prompt, both while meditating and while walking.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **a `;o` the player sends is a relog, and an `=x` is a log-off that stays off.** The user: "`;o` should disconnect then reconnect if used, that is the behavior players are used to, for ;o, whereas =x is disconnect and dont reconnect". So when the link drops within 15 seconds of either going out through the player's own send path (typed, a macro or alias, or a remote `@do`), the client dials back in and logs in after `;o` whatever the BBS reconnect triggers say, and stays disconnected after `=x`. An engine hang-up or an `@relog` that sends the realm's exit command keeps its own meaning even when that command is one of the two.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **`@hangup` and `@relog` are obeyed with Disable Hangups on.** The user: "@hangup and @relog need to be adjusted to ignore the "disable hangups" toggle... they should always work if we were sent them". They still need the sender's Hangup/disconnect grant.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **on a realm recorded as dropping items, the client checks the room for them on the way back in.** The user's words: "if the BBS has drop items as a hang penalty when we enter, we should check the room we're in for any items we were holding but now arent". It applies when `RealmProfile.HangupPenaltyEnabled` is on and `HangupPvpItemsDropped` is above 0, or `HangupPvePenaltyEnabled` is on with `HangupPveItemsDropped` above 0. It still changes nothing about when or whether the client hangs up.
  - The check is once per connection, after the login's `i`: what was held before the link dropped and is short now, by name and count, is taken from the room's floor list with `get`, as many copies as are both short and lying there. Coins are left out. A lost carrier is treated the same as a deliberate hang-up, so what is held is saved on every exit from the game.
  - **It takes back no more copies than the realm's settings say a hang-up drops**: the larger of `HangupPvpItemsDropped` and, when `HangupPvePenaltyEnabled` is on, `HangupPveItemsDropped`, since the client can't know afterwards which side applied. A check that carries items over from one cut short by the link dropping again may take that count for each of the drops. The realm's figure is a safe cap because what lands on the floor never exceeds option #60's count (**Items**, under *What the penalty takes* in this topic).
  - **What the penalty destroyed can't be found**: an item that didn't fit the room, or a `Destroy On Death` item. The check reports it as missing and not on the floor.
  - **There is no realm-specific code.** It runs only where the realm's settings say items drop, so it is idle on Paradigm as the user describes that realm.
  - The item check does not read the two login lines of this topic: they are recorded for Stock only, and the flag behind them is set even when nothing was taken. (The death check of this topic's later Client policy does read them, on Stock.)
  - **A death voids the stored list** until an inventory is read again (`PostDeathInventoryRefresh` asks for one at the graveyard): until then the client's inventory record still names what went into the deathpile, and the 0-HP case of this topic ends in a death.
  - Nothing is picked up when the map is sure of both rooms and the character came in at another than it left, or while a hostile monster the client isn't fighting is in the room; with a fight on, the pickup waits for it to end. When the map can't say, the floor of the room it is in is checked (`HangupItemRecheck.CheckRoom`), unless a move has gone out since the game was entered or the check had already given up its hold on movement: then nothing is picked up without the map vouching for the room.
  - A room that shows no display (dark, or the character blinded) ends the check as "couldn't see the floor", not as the items being gone.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **gear the check picks back up is put on by the equipment manager, not by death recovery.** The user's words: "if the gear was dropped due to the hangup penalty, after it picks it back up, it should send the command to equip whatever set was last equipped (default, rest, walking, etc) and then let the equipment manager handle re-equipping it rather than having a dedicated recovery toggle from another system that is unrelated (hangup is not death recovery)".
  - The set last equipped is `EquipmentManager.CurrentSetId`, which is kept in memory: known after a reconnect, not after the client restarts. Then the set automation would have on at that moment stands in (`AutoEquipCoordinator`'s own choice for the posture, an enabled set only).
  - The set is applied only when at least one picked-up item is in it, through the automatic apply (`EquipmentManager.ApplyBySetId`) and under Auto-All. There is no toggle for it.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: **a death by the hang-up penalty is recognised on the way back in and recorded as any other death.** The user's words: "yes, it should recognize hanging up while dropped with hp penalties on hang, cause the character to die and properly record the death." It changes nothing about when or whether the client hangs up.
  - **When it is looked for:** the stored list says the character was dropped, or had no more HP than the largest share the realm's settings give for that hang-up, with `HangupPenaltyEnabled` on. The share is `HangupPvpHpToPercent` in a fight with a player; `HangupPveHpToPercent`, with `HangupPvePenaltyEnabled`, in a fight with a monster, or in no fight when `HangupOutsideFightPenaltyEnabled` is on as well.
  - **The low-HP case stays** *(user, 2026-10-09: "keep the low hp case")*. It is the same death by the engine reading of this topic (*The share is taken off HP with no floor*).
  - **One setting for each of the board's levels** *(user, 2026-10-09: "have a setting for each type if it means we act differently from the clients auto-response")*: the master switch is the `LOW` level (PvP only), the PvE box `MEDIUM` (while attacked), and `HangupOutsideFightPenaltyEnabled` (Settings → BBS, **Also penalised outside a fight (every hang-up)**, per realm, at the PvE figures) `HIGH`. The client does act differently by it: after a hang-up outside any fight it holds movement for the check, and sends a `stat` when none was read, only on a realm set as penalising every hang-up. (An earlier form had the PvE box stand for both `MEDIUM` and `HIGH`; superseded 2026-10-09.) The item pickup of this topic does not read it.
  - **The settings can't name the free rooms or the death threshold.** So they only decide whether to look; what the character comes back with decides whether it died. Whether the character was in a fight is the client's own reading at the drop (`PvpFight.IsActive` or a recent player attack; `PlayerState.InCombat` or a hostile monster in the room).
  - **No manual "add a death" is offered** *(user, 2026-10-09: "no, death recovery should know all the messages at time of death, to capture the log and thats good enough if it fails to capture the room somehow")*.
  - **What counts as a death: a life lost, with the room it came back in agreeing; or that room, where no count was kept.** Exactly one life fewer than the character left the game with is a death; the same count or more is not; two or more fewer is not recorded. Both counts must come from the game: "before" is on the stored list only when a `stat`, or a seen death's readout, gave it on that connection, and "now" is a `stat` read on this connection. HP and the pack never say "died", and neither does the room the character stands in later: all change by playing on, and the list can be older than the hang-up. (An earlier form of this rule also took HP risen, another room and something held gone as a death when the lives weren't known; dropped 2026-10-10 after review: it recorded deaths that hadn't happened. The form after it let a life lost say it and nothing else; widened 2026-10-10, on the user's statement, to the one room below.)
    - **The room it came back in** *(user, 2026-10-10: the *A death by a hang-up shows on the way back in* bullet of this topic)* is the first room the map confirms on that connection, before any move has gone out. A room confirmed only after a move, or one the map merely still holds from before the link dropped, is not it. It reads three ways:
      - **where the dead of the room it hung up in arrive, and not that room itself:** a death by this hang-up puts it there;
      - **the room it left the game in:** no death moved it, on any game data;
      - **any other room:** no death by this hang-up, where the list of arrival rooms is the world's own (next bullet). Elsewhere it says nothing.
    - **How far the Stock list is trusted depends on the game data** (`HangupArrivalListTrust`; **Client policy**, review 2026-10-10, and the user's rulings of that day in *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*):
      - **an unmodified Stock set** (the set's `Info` row has `Legit` 1 and `Custom` `Default`, as the 1.11p export does): trusted in full;
      - **Paradigm** (`Legit` 2): trusted in full for the zones it shares with Stock. For Paradigm's own rooms (map 18, every room past the last Stock room number of its map, and the 57 Stock numbers that are another place there (73 in an earlier form, which counted the sixteen `Blank` rooms of map 1 with them), *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*) the list has nothing. The sixteen `Blank` rooms of map 1 are read as shared, with Paradigm's own arrival room: `1/2190`, and not the defaults the Stock file gives their numbers (user, 2026-10-11, same topic; `HangupDeathArrivalRooms.ListedOn`). One of them that is in Albion (it can be walked to from `14/1077` without a boat) says yes when the character comes back in `14/1077`, and nothing else says anything for it, "it never moved" included: a hang-up goes through the room's leave-the-game room first, and Paradigm's are not in the data. One outside Albion says nothing at all. (An earlier form took the list by Stock's room-number ranges, and `14/1077` as a yes for any Paradigm-only room; superseded 2026-10-10.);
      - **anything else** (a Stock board whose sysop may have edited its rooms: `Legit` 0, or another `Custom` name; or no set): the list says "that is where they arrive" and "it never moved", never "that is the wrong room". (An earlier form trusted the list in full on every set `GameDataCache.ActiveRealm` calls Stock, and only as far as this on Paradigm; superseded 2026-10-10.)
    - **What the client learns from the deaths it sees** *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-10-10: "yes, learn how they're associated to rooms from the DLL, the same rule applies on paradigm, we just dont know what the rooms are exactly because they dont come across in the MDB"; kept "per game data set"; the user's three rulings of 2026-10-11 are quoted in the sub-bullets they decide)*:
      - **What is learned:** one reading, "room died in → room arrived in", from a death whose lines were read. The room died in is the one the map was sure of when the death came (not with a move in flight). The room arrived in is the one the first room display after the death showed that is not of the room died in, with nothing sent in between that could move the character, and only when the map confirms it. An arena death teaches nothing (it is the arena's own rule), and neither does a graveyard too dark to show, a display the map can't place, or a room drawn after the game was left and entered again.
      - **Only a display the map was still waiting on the death for teaches** *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11)*. The display has to come while the map has placed nothing since the death (`RoomConfidence.PendingRespawn`), or while it is sure of the room died in (that room drawn once more). A display that settles a move the map knew of comes from `RoomConfidence.Pending` and shows where that move led: a drag by the party leader, the character's own step. It teaches nothing and ends the wait. **Known limit:** a summon in that moment can't be told from the death's own relocation, the map hearing of neither, and the room it shows is learned; the room's reading is then corrected like any misreading, by the right one being seen as often (the *Two readings of one room* sub-bullet).
      - **A room is never learned as its own arrival room** *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11)*. The death lines print no room, so a display asked for while the death is being carried out can be of the room died in. That display teaches nothing and does not end the wait: the next one is waited for. The wait ends after 60 seconds (`ArrivalRoomLearner.Window`; the graveyard's own display has been seen to take about 37 seconds to come, and the bound is a backstop), or at once when anything goes out that can move the character: a move (`OutboundMovementObserver.MoveSent`), or any line that is an exit command of some room in the graph, a text exit or a room command (`RoomGraphManager.IsExitCommandSomewhere`; the character's room is not known between the death and the display, so every room's commands count). A room that really is its own graveyard is never learned this way: on Stock the list has such rooms, and elsewhere they stay unlearned.
      - **A death seen in one room stands for its land** *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-10-11: "we should assume that if we die in one map/room landmass (connected rooms) that all rooms that map/room number is connected to, and share map numbers... goto the same place, but if we die in a room that we think should be that place and dont end up there.... that should definitely be recorded"; superseding the first build's "one room teaches that room only", 2026-10-10)*. A room's land is what an outward walk from the room DIED IN reaches without leaving that room's map (`WalkReach.OnItsMap`): every exit in a direction, whatever stands in it, and the room commands that land on the same map; never onto another map and back, and never a boat. A room with no reading of its own takes the reading of every room on its map whose land it lies in (`LearnedArrivalLookup.For`). Nothing is worked out until a hang-up is judged, a death is learned or a bug report is written. Then the room's whole map is cut once into its knots of rooms that reach each other (`MapLands`, kept with the graph), and what a land says is kept per knot until the store or the map changes.
        - **Shadowmere's land is 4,904 rooms, nearly all of map 5, and one death there speaks for all of it until a room shows otherwise** *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11: decided from the user's ruling above, not asked)*. That is what "connected rooms" that "share map numbers" means on a map that size.
        - **A boat landing room on map 14 whose land lies on map 13 is a land of one room** *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11: decided from the same ruling, not asked)*: a death on the pier teaches the pier only, and a death inland does not speak for the pier.
        - **A death that ends as its land already has it makes no entry for its room** *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11)*. In a room with no reading of its own, it is counted on the reading it bears out (`LearnedArrivalRoomStore.LearnNearby`; the file's `Nearby` count on that reading), and the land goes on speaking for the room. So only a land's first word and its exceptions get entries, and the file doesn't come to hold every room anyone died in. Not so in Albion, where a land's reading is not set against the vault: a death there that doesn't end in `14/1077` is always the room's own entry.
        - **What that gives on Paradigm** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, the room graph built from the Paradigm 1.9.1 set)*: from `14/9` (`Port Blackwater, Gatehouse`) or `14/759` (`Blackwater Harbor, Wharf`) 490 rooms; from `13/11000` (`Tal'kiran Shore, Stone Pier`) 556; from `5/1` (`Shadowmere Town Gates, Inner Bailey`) or `5/3` 4,904 of map 5's 4,943; from `14/1077` 9,859 (Albion without `2/11960`). None of these shares a room with another. The landing rooms on map 14 are lands of one room each, their only exit leading onto map 13: `14/1813` (`Cliffside Beach, Small Pier`), `14/1812` (`Shoreline, Sandy Beach`) and `14/15000` (`Tal'kiran Shore, Stone Pier`). Behind them on map 13, `13/999` is in a land of 1,919 rooms (`Frozen Wasteland`, `Icy Mountain Path`) and `13/235` in one of 773 (`Shoreline`, `Jungle Trail`), again with no room in common, with each other or with Tal'kiran's. The names Terra Ista and Terra Fuego are not in the Rooms table.
      - **A room's own reading always wins, and one that differs from its land's is recorded** (the same ruling: "that should definitely be recorded"). A death that ends somewhere else than the room's land says, or than Albion says (`14/1077`), is stored as that room's own reading and used for that room from then on. The log has one warning naming the room, the arrival expected and the one seen. The land keeps its reading for its other rooms. Which reading is the land's when it has two: the one borne out by at least two deaths in different rooms and by more than any other, a room with the reading counting one and each death counted on it from another room one more (`LearnedArrivalLookup.LandSays`); until there is one, a room with no reading of its own takes every reading its land has, and coming back in any of them says yes. In Albion only a death seen in the room itself stands against the vault; what another room of the land showed does not (`HangupDeathArrivalRooms.LearnedFor`).
      - **Where it is kept:** with the game-data set, in `learned-arrival-rooms.json` beside the imported tables (never in one of them), shared by every board and character on the set. A second client on the set takes the file in on its heartbeat, and a write merges with what is on file. The file carries a `Version` (1) and, for each room, each arrival room seen with the number of times it was seen (`Times`) and of deaths elsewhere in its land counted on it (`Nearby`), the reading in use first. Nothing in the store throws into the line pump: a write that fails is logged once as a warning, kept in memory and tried again on the next learn or heartbeat; a file that does not parse is logged once, and moved aside to `learned-arrival-rooms.json.bad` before the first write so that nothing in it is written over; a file that can be neither read nor moved aside is said once for each, not on every heartbeat; a file of a later version is neither read nor written.
      - **Never over the list.** Where the list is the world's own (an unmodified Stock set, a zone Paradigm shares with Stock) nothing is learned and nothing learned is read. A death seen is set against where a DEATH in that room ends by the list, which is the room's own graveyard (`HangupDeathArrivalRooms.DeathArrivalsOn`); the list itself is of where a hang-up's dead arrive, and for the 101 rooms with a leave-the-game room that changes it (the *A death by a hang-up shows on the way back in* bullet of this topic) the two differ. So a death seen in `17/3250` that ends in `17/3247` is the list agreeing, and nothing is logged. (An earlier form compared with the hang-up list and logged a warning for those rooms; superseded 2026-10-11.) On Paradigm a death seen to end where the list doesn't allow is logged as a warning naming the rooms, not learned, and the list stands. On a board whose rooms may have been edited it is learned, as one more room.
      - **A Stock board with edited rooms, played on the standard data set** *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-10-11: "yes, on a stock edited board, if the map/room numbers dont line up to the 1.11p data set... they can send us to different places... also if the bbs is running edited, it -should- have its own MDB and not be using the 1.11p dataset, but if they are playing an edited bbs and using the standard 1.11p dataset... idk what we should do"; the answer to the "idk" is the review's, 2026-10-11)*. A death seen on an unmodified Stock set that ends in a room the list doesn't allow for the room died in (not the list's room or a look-alike of it, the default pair or the room's own graveyard) is taken as evidence that the BOARD's rooms were edited. It is counted on the board's realm (`RealmProfile.DeathsContradictingStandardArrivalRooms`, by `StandardListContradictions`), and each one is logged as a warning naming the rooms.
        - **Two such deaths mark the board, not one** *(review 2026-10-11)*. The map can be sure of a room and wrong, in a grid of same-named rooms, and one death then looks like it ended in the wrong place on a board that is standard. The first is said and changes nothing, and nothing is learned from it; its warning says one more will mark the board. (An earlier form marked the board at the first; superseded 2026-10-11.)
        - **Marked, the board is read as any board with edited rooms** (`HangupArrivalListTrust.Unverified`): the list says yes and never no, and learned readings are read and written, the death that marked it included. The reading goes in the set's file, where only a board read that way uses it; on another board with the same set the list is still the world's own.
        - **The count belongs to the board and the data set it was seen on** *(review 2026-10-11)*: the set's name is kept beside it (`RealmProfile.DeathsContradictingStandardArrivalRoomsOn`), and it counts for nothing while the realm plays another set. So pointing the realm at another set starts afresh, and there is nothing to clear by hand.
        - **Counting it throws nothing**: it happens inside the room display's handling. A board file that can't be written is logged once as a warning, and the count, held on the realm in memory, goes out with the board's next save.
        - The evidence has to be as solid as any learned reading (a death seen, both rooms confirmed).
      - **A learned room says yes, and never no; and its yes is weaker than the list's.** Coming back in it after a hang-up in that room, or in a room of its land, is "where its dead arrive", on the same terms as Albion's vault: no other room is the wrong one on its strength, the room left included. The reason for both halves is the leave-the-game room: the data doesn't carry one for these rooms, and what was seen is where a death ends, not where a hang-up's dead do.
        - It never says no, because a hang-up's dead may arrive somewhere else than a death's.
        - Its yes can be a survivor's. `17/3250` and 94 more rooms of Stock's map 17 name `17/3247` both as graveyard and as leave-the-game room, so a character that hangs up there and lives comes back in the very room a death there ends in. So with no lives count from before the hang-up, a learned yes, whether the room's own or its land's, records a death only when HP was read at the first prompt (`HangupDeath.Judge`, `entryRoomLearned`):
          - **where the room's yes alone would decide** (nothing owned for a death to take), that HP has to be above the HP the character left with;
          - **with a pack found stripped of what a death takes**, HP read and not saying no is enough *(**Client policy**, review 2026-10-11: decided, not asked)*. Unread, it is not: a penalty that drops items strips a survivor too, and where the learned room is also the room's leave-the-game room the survivor stands in it. (An earlier form let a stripped pack do with HP unread; superseded 2026-10-11.)

          Without that the check is told and not recorded. In an arena room, where the room's yes is the whole case, a learned yes needs HP read at the first prompt and above 0 (`HangupDeath.JudgeArena`). With a life seen lost, a learned room counts as a listed one does.
      - **Two readings of one room are a dispute, and the one seen a second time wins** *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-10-11: "no room will send someone to two different places.. each room has their assigned death revival rooms... the DLL might explain how its set/works for stock/1.11p data set. but its not anything we can see in game data sets that are exported in other versions of the game"; superseding the first build's "both are kept and neither is used" with no way out, 2026-10-10)*. The file counts how many times each reading of a room was seen. While a room has two readings seen once each, neither is used, with one warning in the log. The first reading to be seen again wins: the other is dropped, logged at Info.
        - **A reading seen twice or more stays in use against a different sighting, which is kept beside it as a challenger and takes over when it has been seen as often** *(review 2026-10-11)*. One stray sighting changes nothing in use (one warning). At two against two the later one is in use, and the one it replaced is kept beside it in turn; each further sighting of either moves its count, and whichever draws level takes over. The change is logged at Info with both rooms and both counts. So no reading is fixed for good: the same misreading made twice, or a graveyard a board has since moved, is corrected by seeing the right room as often. (An earlier form dropped every differing sighting once a reading had been seen twice, so two sightings stood against any number after them; superseded 2026-10-11.)
        - Nothing is edited by hand. The engine's two default rooms (`1/2189` and `1/142`, *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*) are one reading: a room seen to send its dead to either stands for both, since which of the two a character gets goes by its evil points.
      - **Client use:** `ArrivalRoomLearner` (fed by `RoomTracker.PlayerDeathObserved`, `RoomTracker.StateChanged`, `OutboundMovementObserver.MoveSent` and `InGameCapture.InGameChanged`; `RoomTracker.LastDeathRoomConfirmed`) learns, and `ArrivalRoomLearner.ObserveOutbound`, fed every outbound line by `MainWindowViewModel.SendUserInput`, ends its wait on a room command. `LearnedArrivalRoomStore` keeps (`AppPaths.LearnedArrivalRoomsFile`; `LearnedArrivalOutcome` is what a sighting came to), `LearnedArrivalLookup` reads a room's own reading or its land's (`LearnedArrival` is an arrival room with the room the death was seen in; `WalkReach.KnotOnItsMap` names the land it keeps an answer for), and `HangupDeathArrivalRooms.ArrivalsOn` / `LearnedFor` / `Read` use it (`HangupEntryRoomReading.LearnedFrom` and `Learned`). `AppServices.HangupArrivalListTrust` reads the board's mark (`StandardListContradictions.Marked`), and `StandardListContradictions.Note` counts toward it. (An earlier form of this line had `AppServices.NoteDeathContradictedStandardArrivalRooms` write the count; moved 2026-10-11.) The record and the notice say `(learned from a death seen there)`, or `(learned from a death seen in <room>, a room of the same land)`. The bug report's Session section carries **Learned arrival rooms**: how many rooms the set has, the disputed ones with their readings, the readings in use that have another seen beside them (with both counts), the rooms whose own reading differs from their land's, the lands with two readings, the pair the last hang-up death check went by (`HangupItemRecheck.LastLearnedArrivalUsed`), and how many of this board's deaths have contradicted the standard list. Its **Game data files** count leaves `learned-arrival-rooms.json` out (`BugReportContext`).
    - **The map knows a room by its name and the exits it prints, so the room it confirms can be a look-alike of the room the character is in** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, the Stock 1.11p and Paradigm 1.9.1 Rooms tables, and `RoomTracker` run on both)*. Two arrival rooms are caught by it, and `RoomGraphManager.CouldBeTakenFor` finds such pairs from the data (same name, and every exit the one prints is an exit of the other; a text exit and a hidden exit of any kind, `Hidden/Passable` included, print on no exits line):
      - `11/35` `Portal Room`, where the dead of 39 rooms of map 11 arrive, prints only `south` (its three portals are text exits), and `11/37` `Portal Room` has exactly a south exit: the map confirms `11/37`. Coming back in the look-alike, having hung up in a room that doesn't look like it, is read as coming back where the dead arrive, and the wording names both rooms;
      - `15/2057` and its arrival room `15/2056` are both `Dark Cave` with a south exit: the map stays on `15/2057`. That is not "the room it left", and the room says nothing.
    - **It says nothing** when the room hung up in or the room come back in isn't known, when the character hung up in a room that is its own dead's arrival room or leaves the game through it (`17/785`, `17/1773`), and when a connection since the hang-up sent a move before the map had confirmed any room (`HeldAtDisconnect.MovedBeforeEntryRoomKnownSince`): the room a later connection starts in is then one it walked to.
    - **With both counts read the lives decide, and the room must agree.** One life fewer with the room saying "not here" is not recorded, and is told (the *What can take a death away again* list below).
    - **With no count from before the hang-up, the room can say it**: back where its dead arrive, with nothing left at the first inventory read of what a death takes, nothing worn, and on Stock the board's lines printed, is a death. It is recorded with the lives a `stat` gives on that connection, which is waited for (and asked for) as below; with the master switch off the terminal is told that typing `stat` and `i` will answer it, as it is when a count was kept.
    - **A character that owned nothing a death takes needs only the room** *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-10-10: asked whether the arrival room alone is enough when the character owned nothing a death takes, "yes")*: no item but those that stay with it, and no coin, so there is nothing for it to come back stripped of. Every "no" that still applies is kept: the room, HP at the first prompt, a piece worn, the board's lines on Stock, and the lives when both counts were read.
    - **Otherwise the room alone never records a death** (**Client policy**): a character that hung up low, was walked to the temple on another client and left the game there stands in the same room, still holding its gear. So the stripped pack is required, and where what it held isn't known it stays "can't tell". (An earlier form also left a character that held nothing a death takes at "can't tell"; superseded 2026-10-10 by the bullet above.)
