  - **A clean exit raises no question.** Leaving by the game's own exit command, the link still up (the character saved, the board's menu showing), is not a hang-up and costs nothing (*Realm exit / logoff sequence*); the stored list is marked so and never looked into. Only the link going down while in the game is a hang-up. The mark is not set for a dropped character, which the game won't let leave that way (`You may not exit MajorMud while you are mortally wounded!`, *Realm exit / logoff sequence*), and a game prompt read after it takes it off again: a chat line can look like the exit's own.
  - **What can take a death away again.** A life can be lost on another client between two sessions of this one. A life lost is not recorded, and the terminal is told, when what the entry showed says it wasn't lost to this hang-up:
    - **HP at the first prompt after the hang-up is 0 or less, under what the character left with, or exactly what it left with short of its maximum** (a death sets HP to its maximum on both realms, *Death & corpse recovery → Death wipes all effects*; nothing else raises it while out of the game, the *Nothing raises a character's HP* bullet of this topic). With no life known lost, the same reading closes the question without a `stat` and without a word.
    - **The room it came back in is the room it left, or (on Stock) any room its dead don't arrive in** (the *What counts as a death* bullet above). With no life known lost, that closes the question the same quiet way.
    - **Any item of the list that a death takes, or any of its coins, is still held at the first inventory read** (both realms: a death takes every item but those that stay with the character, and every coin, to the floor on Stock and into the corpse on Paradigm, *Death & corpse recovery → Deathpile — where the items go*). "Any", not "all": one torch burnt on another client must not hide a pile got back there. Items that stay with the character through a death (`DeathPileRules`: loyal, major-cursed) don't count, so a real death that leaves only those held is still a death; a list of nothing but those, and no coins, can't be read this way. An item the game data doesn't know is taken for one a death takes. (An earlier form asked that everything be still held; superseded 2026-10-10.)
    - **A piece is worn at the first inventory read**: any piece, on both realms. On Stock the engine takes everything off at a death (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*); on Paradigm that is confirmed for a loyal piece only, and a worn cursed piece is treated as Stock's engine does by **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-10; the `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` in that topic).
    - **The board did not print its two login lines since the hang-up** (Stock only: the *They print once* bullet of this topic; whether Paradigm prints them is the `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` beside the Paradigm bullet of this topic).
    - **The list is another character's**: it carries the name off the `stat` screen of the connection it was written on, and a different name on this connection's `stat` (a profile copied or shared between characters) answers nothing, about a death or about dropped items. That one is not told: there is nothing to tell this character.
  - **One case nothing on the connection separates** *(**Client policy**)*: the character was played from another client in between, and that session itself ended in a death by a hang-up. It comes back stripped with a life less, on Stock with the board's lines printed, and every check above passes. So the record never claims more than it knows: its message line, and the terminal notice, say the room and time are where this client last had the character, and that the pile is where it died if it was played from another client since.
  - **It is judged on what the first entry after the hang-up showed, whenever the answer comes.** HP is taken at the first prompt and the pack at the first inventory read. The login's own `stat` normally gives the lives; when none has, the check sends one `stat`, under Auto-All and only while it still holds movement. Otherwise it sends nothing and the question stays open, without a hold, until any `stat` is read on that connection (the user's own included); the terminal is told once that typing `stat` and `i` will answer it. With no `stat` read before the link drops, nothing is recorded.
  - **The stored list always describes the hang-up it is judged for.** It is written on every save in the game once an inventory has been read on that connection. With none read, the older list stands, except when the link drops with the character low enough for the penalty to kill: then a list is written for that hang-up anyway (room, time, HP, the lives and name if a `stat` gave them on that connection) with what was held marked unknown, and a death recorded from it lists no pile and says so.
    - **The older list is settled before it is replaced.** When its hang-up is known not to have killed (it couldn't, or the character came back at 0 HP or less, under what it left with, or as it left short of its maximum), its lives and name are still current and go onto the new list; so does what it held, when no move was sent on the connection and the realm's penalty takes no items. That is the commonest way the penalty kills: a hang-up that leaves the character dropped, a re-entry with the monster still there, and a second hang-up at the first prompt, before any `stat` or `i`. The death is then recorded at the second hang-up's room and time, with the pile from the older list. When the older hang-up could have killed and was never judged, it is judged then: a `stat` on that connection showing one life fewer is a death by it, recorded at once from the older list (its pile everything on the list that a death takes, since no inventory was read since); where it can't be told, the terminal says so as the list is let go. Off Stock that judgement is told, not recorded, since no inventory read separates a death by the hang-up from a life lost on another client; unless the room it came back in is where its dead arrive, which does. A count is not carried when the character came back with more HP than it left with (HP cannot rise out of the game except by a death, so a hang-up the client took to be harmless may have killed).
    - **With no room display read on the connection, the fight is the one the older list has**: the client can't say what is in the room, and a character hung up again at its first prompt is in the fight it left.
    - A connection that came and went with no inventory read and nothing that could kill leaves the older list to be judged later, and hands on what it saw of the entry (the board's lines, HP at the first prompt, the room it came back in): on Stock the lines print on that first entry and not again, and by the next connection the character may stand somewhere else.
  - **The lives on the list are never a stale count.** They go on it only when the game gave them on that connection. A life asked back after a death (`sys god <name> add life`) and a level trained (on Stock a level gives lives, *Death & corpse recovery → Death lines & the miracle-save*) change the game's count with no screen saying so: the count is then unknown at once, and a `stat` is sent for it five seconds later, under Auto-All.
  - **The record** is the one a death line makes (`DeathRecord`): the room and time of the stored list, the lives read now, and as the pile what was held then and was not held at the first inventory read (worn pieces with their slots; everything else as the inventory words it; the coins). Keys and the lit light are on it: they drop at a death like the rest *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, to "Do a lit light and keys drop at death?": "yes"; the fact's home is *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*)*. (An earlier form left them off to match the witnessed record of that time; reversed 2026-10-10.) On Stock that pile is the two lots of this topic, both in the room the character was in. When the room it came back in said so, the record's message line and the terminal notice name it: `It came back in <room>, where the dead of <room> arrive.`
  - **A death found at the login gets what a death is owed; one found later gets its record only.** At the login, while movement is still held and nothing has run: no death sound, no backscroll death log, no HP-floor reading and no respawn-room wait, but the movement engines are stopped, the loop set aside at the disconnect is dropped, a default task still waiting to start is called off for the connection, Death Recovery's held re-equip list is dropped, navigation's intent is cleared and the character's own buff timers are cleared (*Death & corpse recovery → Death wipes all effects*). Found later (the hold had been given up, or a `stat` was read long after the pass), the character has played on since: the record is made and the terminal told, and the engines and buff timers are left as they are. Either way a Sysop god life is asked for unless the master switch is off (**Client policy**, user: with the master switch off nothing automatic is sent), and never for an arena death, which spent none (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*).
  - **The item pickup of this topic stands down** when a death is recorded: what is missing is the pile, which is neither picked up nor reported as dropped by a hang-up.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: **a hang-up while dropped in an arena room is recorded as an arena death.** Asked whether a hang-up in an arena room that turns out to have killed should appear in the history as an arena death, the user answered "yes".
  - **When it is looked for:** the stored list says HP was 0 or less in one of the `Colliseum` rooms (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*, the 118 rooms of type 5), and the game was not left by its own exit. It is looked for on any realm, whatever its penalty settings: on Stock the death check takes any HP of 0 or less in such a room as the colliseum's free death on every hang-up path, the free and the unpenalised ones too (the *order of an in-realm hang-up* bullet of this topic). Movement is held from the connect as for the other question.
  - **The lives can't say it, so the room does.** An arena death takes no life on either realm (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*), so the rule of the Client policy above finds nothing. It is an arena death when the first room the map confirms on the way back in, before a move has gone out, is where that arena room's dead arrive and is not the room hung up in (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*, the graveyard table), and HP at the first prompt, when read, is above 0 (the arena's death puts HP back). A `stat` read on that connection gives the record its lives; one is asked for as for the other question.
  - **It is recorded without a lives count from before** *(user, 2026-10-10: asked whether an arena hang-up death may be recorded without a lives count from before, an arena death costing no life, "yes")*. One corner is told and not recorded: the realm's settings penalise that hang-up, so an ordinary death is possible too (the next bullet), the lives weren't read before, and what the character held can't say (nothing a death takes was on the list, or the list doesn't know). Then nothing tells an arena death from an ordinary one, a life gone.
  - **What hands it back to the ordinary rule:** a life lost (one fewer than the list has), or nothing left at the first inventory read of what a death takes. Those are the marks of an ordinary death, which a hang-up while dropped in one of these rooms is on Stock with the arena switch off (`0x4790e8`; the settings can't see it, and no colliseum line is ever read across a hang-up, so the room it comes back in and what it comes back with are all there is to go by on Stock too). Back in the room it left, or still dropped, is no death of either kind.
  - **Where it can't be told:** the room it came back in wasn't confirmed before it moved; or it hung up in a room that is its own dead's arrival room (`16/542` and `17/2426` among the arena rooms). Nothing is recorded then.
  - **One case nothing separates:** a character healed and walked to that arrival room on another client, and left the game there. It holds its gear either way. The record made then costs nothing but a row in the history.
  - **The record** is the one a witnessed arena death gets (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*, the arena **Client use**): `DeathRecord.NothingLost`, no worn, carried or coin lists, status Recovered with the note `Arena death: nothing was lost.`, the room and time of the stored list, the lives read now. Its message line begins `Died in an arena room after the link went down (not seen: worked out on entering the game).` and names the room it came back in. Found at the login, the engines are stopped and the buff timers cleared as for any death (the Stock engine ends the character's spells before the colliseum test, @0x419bb4–0x419c04); Death Recovery's held re-equip list is kept, the gear being still in the pack, `AutoOpenManager` is not told of a pile, and no Sysop god life is asked for.
  - **Paradigm: a hang-up while dropped in an arena room can be the arena's death, nothing lost, as on Stock** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: Paradigm)*. Asked whether hanging up while dropped in an arena on Paradigm is an arena death (nothing lost), as on Stock: "yes, it can be". The client treats the two realms alike here, and records one only when it sees the character back where that arena's dead arrive. (Was `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`; settled 2026-10-10.)
- **Client use:**
  - `HangupDeath.JudgeArena` holds the arena rule; `HangupItemRecheck.ArenaDeathPossible` raises the question, `HangupItemRecheck.Verdict` asks it ahead of `HangupDeath.Judge`, and `HangupItemRecheck.RecordArenaDeath` makes the record through `UnwitnessedDeath.NothingLost`, which `RoomTracker.NoteUnwitnessedDeath` writes as `NoteDeath` writes a witnessed arena death (it sets `RoomTracker.LastDeathTookNothing` too). `DeathRecoveryManager.OnDeathInferred` keeps its held re-equip list for one. The bug report's **Held list on file** marks an arena room, and **Hang-up death check** reads `died in the arena`.
  - `HangupDeath.Suspected`, `HangupDeath.RuledOut` and `HangupDeath.Judge` hold the rule, `HangupDeath.CarriedOf` and `HangupDeath.Pile` build the pile. Which items stay through a death comes from `AppServices.EveryItemOfThisNameStaysOnDeath` (`DeathPileRules`), read by `HangupItemRecheck.TakenStillHeld` and the worn check; `HangupItemRecheck.SettleOlderList` settles an older list as a new one replaces it. `HangupItemRecheck` asks the question in the same pass as the item check, ahead of it (`DeathSuspected`, `OtherCharacter`, `AskDeath`, `RecordDeath`), holding movement from the connect as it does for items; a question it can't answer stays open after the pass and `NoteLivesRead` answers it (`AnswerOpenQuestion`). `HangupPenaltyNotice.HpShareTop` reads the realm's settings for it.
  - `HangupDeathArrivalRooms` holds the Stock list of where the dead of a hang-up arrive (`For`), Paradigm's `ParadigmAlbionVault`, and reads the room come back in against them (`Read`, giving a `HangupEntryRoomReading`; an earlier form was `EntrySays`, told by `AppServices` whether the realm is Stock). `AppServices.HangupArrivalListTrust` says how far the list goes, from `GameDataCache.ActiveRealm` and `GameDataCache.ActiveSetIsVanillaStock`, and `RoomGraphManager.CouldBeTakenFor` which rooms the map can't tell an arrival room from. `HangupDeathArrivalRooms.ListCovers` says whether the list speaks for a room on that game data and `ArrivalsOn` which rooms its dead arrive in and what that rests on; `WalkReach` (through `AppServices.InParadigmAlbion`) is Paradigm's Albion. The bug report's **Held list on file** words the same (`BugReportBuilder.HangupArrivalText`), naming Albion when that is what decides. `HangupItemRecheck.OwnedNothing` reads the list for a character that held nothing a death takes, and `HangupItemRecheck.SayWaiting` tells the terminal when a `stat` is what is missing. `HangupItemRecheck.NoteRoomDisplayed` takes the first room `RoomTracker` confirms on the connection with no move sent, `HangupItemRecheck.EntryRoom` words it, and `HangupDeath.Judge` takes it as `entryRoom`. The bug report's **Held list on file** says where the list's dead arrive and the room an earlier connection came back in, and **Hang-up death check** what the room said.
  - `HeldAtDisconnect` carries `Character`, `Hp`, `MaxHp`, `Lives`, `PvpFight` (`PvpFight.IsActive`, or an attack in `PvpAttackWatcher.Recent` within 30 seconds), `InCombat`, `Worn`, `Carried`, `Coins`, `ItemsUnknown`, `CleanExit`, `LoginLinesSeenSince`, `HpAtFirstEntrySince` and `EntryRoomSince` beside the item rows. `MainWindowViewModel`'s Disconnected handler calls `HangupItemRecheck.NoteLinkDropping` first, so the list is written before the fight state is torn down; `HangupItemRecheck.LeaveGame` decides what is written (`Leaving`).
  - `KnownPatterns.HangupLoginNotice` matches the first login line, and `HangupItemRecheck.NoteHangupLoginLine` takes it; `StatParser.LastCaptureReadLives` says a `stat` capture gave the lives. `SysopGodLifeRecovery.LifeRequested` and the two train lines (`KnownPatterns.TrainAttainLevel`, `TrainAttainNextLevel`) reach `HangupItemRecheck.NoteLivesChangedUnread`.
  - `RoomTracker.NoteUnwitnessedDeath` appends the record through the same `AppendDeathRecord` as `NoteDeath`. It raises `UnwitnessedDeathRecorded` for every record (`DeathRecoveryManager.OnUnwitnessedDeathRecorded`, and `SysopGodLifeRecovery.OnDeath` behind `AutoModeController.KillSwitchEngaged`) and, for a death found at the login only (`UnwitnessedDeath.AtEntry`), `PlayerDeathInferred`, never `PlayerDeathObserved`. Subscribed to that one: `PlayerDeathMovementHalt.StopEngines`, `LoopRunner.ClearPendingReconnectResume`, `DefaultTaskRunner.OnDeathInferred`, `DeathRecoveryManager.OnDeathInferred`, `NavigationViewModel.ClearNavIntentOnDeath` and `CastingDirector.ClearSelfBuffTracking`. The walker and Auto-Lair keep nothing over a reconnect to drop.
  - The bug report's Session section carries **Hang-up death check** (`HangupItemRecheck.LastDeathCheck`), **Held list on file** shows the list's HP, lives and fight, and **Default task stood down for a hang-up death** says whether the task was called off.
  - `HangupPenaltyNotice.MaxItemsDropped` is the gate and the cap. `HangupItemRecheck` runs the check: it writes `CharacterProfile.HeldAtDisconnect` (the realm it was taken on, the room, `PenaltiesSpanned`, and `HeldItem` rows of name and count) on every profile save made in the game once an inventory has been read on that connection, holds movement on `MovementCoordinator.HangupItemCheckGate` from the connect until the check ends (or until the game isn't entered, or no inventory read, in time), and compares through `HangupItemPlan` (`Held`, `Missing`, `Pickup`, `Capped`). The gets go out through `AutoGetItemsManager.CollectNamed` (counted per realm by `CountedCommand.Emit`, *Items, inventory & equipment → Item batching: Paradigm counted commands vs Stock one-per-command*), and the gear set is applied again through `AutoEquipCoordinator.ReapplySetAfterItemsReturned`.
  - The bug report's Session section carries **Hang-up item check**, **Missing after hang-up** and **Held list on file** (`BugReportBuilder`).
  - `HangupPenaltyNotice.ForHangup` words one Info log line (`[Hangup]`) when the client sends a hang-up on a realm with a penalty recorded. `AppServices.LogHangupPenalty` calls it from `HealthManager.ExecuteEscape` (the health settings' hang-up, a received `@panic`, the PvP response's `HangUpForPvp`, and a `Hangup`-relationship monster's `HangUpForMonster`; *Combat → Neutral monsters and kill-on-sight*), `HangupHandler` (`@hangup`) and `RelogHandler` (`@relog`). The PvP side is named for the PvP response's hang-up or while `PvpFight.IsActive`, else the monster side while `PlayerState.InCombat`; with neither it gives the rule without naming a side.
  - `HangupPenaltyNotice.Describe` fills the bug report's **Realm hang-up penalty** line (Session section, `BugReportBuilder`).
  - `SentExitCommand` remembers a `;o` or `=x` from `MainWindowViewModel.SendUserInput`; the Disconnected handler there reads it after `HangupSignal` and `RelogSignal` and classifies the drop as a relog or a stay-off (report `paradigm-20261009-081205`).
  - `HangupHandler` and `RelogHandler` no longer read Disable Hangups.

### MegaMUD `messages.md` format
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 (user + decode of both stock/paramud files)*

- **MegaMUD's "Messages/Responses" catalogue ships as a plain-text `messages.md`,** one per game-type folder: `…(Stock)/Default/messages.md`, `…(Paramud)/Default/MESSAGES.md`. It is the ORIGINAL source that our Messages seed (and Triggers seed) were derived from.
- **Every record is rigidly 3 lines, `\r\n`-terminated.** This was validated on 612 stock / 840 paramud records, with zero misalignment.
- **Line 1 is `name : FLAGS(4-hex) : ACTION(decimal) : RESPONSE`.**
  - `name` is the message name. **A spell's message is named exactly after the spell, and an item's after the item.** Paramud names item procs after the item (e.g. `acid slasher`), while stock used a generic effect name (e.g. `acid hits`). This name is how a message is linked to its spell/item.
  - `FLAGS` holds the Effects checkboxes as an **additive hex bitfield**, with the same bit layout as our `MessageFlags`: `0001` Blinded, `0002` Confused, `0004` Poisoned, `0008` Losing-HP, `0010` Movement-prevented, `0020` Attack-prevented, `0040` Diseased, `0080` HP-regen, `0100` Find-in-conversations*, `0200` Mana-regen, `0400` Find-in-text*, `0800` reserved*, `1000` Ends-combat, `2000` Last-action-failed, `4000` Use-when-chasing*, `8000` Disabled. (`*` = the find-mode/chasing bits the importer strips.) Validated end-to-end against message text.
  - `ACTION` is the Action radio, a top-down index 0–6: 0 Ignore, 1 Check-who's-in-room, 2 Wait-until-wears-off, 3 Rest-full-HP, 4 Rest-full-Mana, 5 Don't-rest-run, 6 Hangup. **Read but NOT emitted**: the client's own engines/settings handle every one of these, so a MudPlay message is recognition only and carries no action.
  - `RESPONSE` is the literal text that MegaMUD would send when it sees the line echoed from the server. **Read but NOT emitted**: in MudPlay, a player response to a seen line is a *Trigger*, not a message.
- **Line 2 is the Message line** (the pattern matched on the wire).
- **Line 3 is the Ends-with line (wear-off).** It is **blank when the effect has no wear-off**.
- **Tokens are `{dmg}` (numeric), `{target}`, `{source}`,** which `CasterMessageMatcher` already understands, plus `{1}` = a user-defined **wildcard** handled by the Triggers matcher.
- **The .md is the source for THREE of our tables, not just Messages:**
  - A record whose name matches a Spell goes to the Messages seed with `Spells#N`.
  - One that matches an Item goes to the Messages seed with `Items#N`.
  - One that carries an ailment flag / applied+wear-off goes to the Messages seed (ConditionTracker detector).
  - **Everything else (pattern + response/action) goes to the Triggers seed.** Examples: `1 life left` → say warning + hangup; the separate `X end` records → response `stat` to refresh status.
- **Decoding to our record:** if Ends-with is present OR there is an ailment flag, it becomes `AppliedMessage` (+`AppliedEndsWith`); otherwise it becomes `CasterMessage`.

## Talk & chat channels

How the game's talk modes and chat channels behave: say forms, the gang channel's speak verb, how the server echoes our own messages, and how telepaths are throttled and acknowledged.

### Talk modes are per-realm configuration
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **Talk fast / slow is each character's own setting on both realms, and every character starts on fast** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; the Stock engine reads the same, `_cmd_set` @0x458e04 / @0x45a30d, `_create_player` @0x4164e5)*. (An earlier note said talk modes differ per realm as game configuration; superseded 2026-10-09: the mode is per character, and what differs per realm is the empty-room rule in the next bullet.)
- **What differs per realm is a say in talk slow with nobody else in the room** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user)*. With `set talk slow`, a say begun with the period still goes out on Paradigm when the room is empty. On Stock someone else has to be in the room for it to go out; alone, it doesn't (the engine answers `Your command had no effect.`: *Directed say vs undirected say*).
- **The keyboard period is a say-precursor and stays unbindable.**
- **The `set talk` replies on Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_set` @0x458e04 / @0x45a30d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - `set talk fast` (or `set speech fast`) answers `Anything you type which is not recognized will be sent to the room.`; `set talk slow` answers `To talk to the room, you must begin your line with a %c` (the say character). Bare `set talk` toggles: `Talking mode is slow now.` / `Talking mode is fast now.`
  - The command `talk fast` / `talk slow` sets it with no reply; anything else after `talk` prints `Talk syntax is TALK {Fast/Slow}`.
  - `pro` shows it as `Talking speed:      Fast|Slow` (*Wire, prompt & command output → Character settings — `set` and the `pro` sheet*).
- **On Stock the say character and the yell character are board options, `.` and `"` unless the board changed them** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` start-up @0x40123e–0x401253; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*.

### Directed say vs undirected say
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 (user)*

- **A directed say is `><name> <message>`** (`>` verb + name, no precursor). It says the message TO one person in the room, so in a crowded room they know it's aimed at them.
- **The undirected say is the say-precursor `.<message>`**, which is room-wide. It is distinct from the directed say.
- **What Stock does with a line that is no command, exit word, cast code or social** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_execute_input` @0x450a4d–0x450b40; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - first character is the say character: said, in either talk mode;
  - first character is the yell character: yelled, in either talk mode;
  - talk fast, and the first character is not `/`: the whole line is said;
  - otherwise (talk slow): `Your command had no effect.`
- **Say on the wire, Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, same routine, strings @0x488792, @0x488859, @0x488849)*: the room sees `<name> says "<text>"` in green (`ESC[0;32m`); the speaker sees `You say "<text>"`, or **`Well Spoken...`** in its place with `set responses brief`.
- **Yell on the wire, both realms** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p, same routine, strings @0x4887a0–0x4887f7; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user: "its the same on both realms", so Paradigm sends the same text)*: the same room sees `From <name> (Yelling): "<text>"`; each room one exit away on the same map hears `Someone yells from above "<text>"`, `Someone yells from below "<text>"` or `Someone yells from the <direction> "<text>"`, with the yeller not named; the speaker sees `You yell "<text>"` or `Well Spoken...`.
- **In talk slow, speech nobody could hear is answered `Your command had no effect.` instead of `You say …`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_execute_input` @0x450c82, `_tell_room` @0x46b10c)*. The echo prints when talk is fast or when at least one player who isn't hidden received the line. So a slow-talk `.hello` in an empty room, or with only hidden players in it, draws the no-effect line. (*Combat → Attacking a monster that isn't in the room* has the same pair of answers for a mistyped attack.)
- **A silenced character can't speak** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_execute_input` @0x450915, `_cmd_direct_message` @0x45756c; which ability sets the flag wasn't traced)*: any speech prints `You cannot speak!` and a directed say `You may not direct any messages right now.`
- **The directed say's three views, Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_direct_message` @0x45748d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: the target sees `<name> says (to you) "<text>"`; everyone else in the room sees `<name> says (to <target>) "<text>"`; the sender sees `--- Message Directed to <target> ---`, with the target's own first name.
  - **Refusals, in the order tested:** a bare `>` → `You have to direct something!`; a space after the `>` → `You have to specify a person to direct to.`; your own name → `Why are you directing messages to yourself?`; no such player online → `Cannot find user!`; sender silenced → `You may not direct any messages right now.`; target not in the same room, or hidden → `--- Message Not Sent ---`.
  - **A directed say uses up one of the target's telepath slots** (@0x4575e4; no cap is tested here, but it is the counter a telepath tests): see *Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement*.

**Client use:**
- The client answers a say-channel `@`-command with a directed say at the sender (`RemoteCommandManager.SendReply`).
- Yell lines from other players are chat: `ChatLineDetector` keeps all three forms (`From <name> (Yelling): "`, `Someone yells from … "`, `<name> yells "`) out of the game-output lane, and `DefaultPatterns` pattern `conversation.yell` (`KnownPatterns.ConversationYell`) classifies them for `ChatRouter` as `ChatChannel.Yell`. The unnamed next-room yell gets the speaker `Someone`, the word the game prints; where it came from (`above`, `below`, `the <direction>`) is carried from the line's own words in `ChatLogEntry.HeardFrom`, shown by the Conversation row as `Someone (from the north)` and kept in the talk log. A yell carries no remote command (`RemoteCommandManager.MapChannel` leaves `Yell` unmapped).

### Self-echo on public / broadcast channels
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 (user)*

- **On a public / broadcast channel (gangpath, gossip, auction, broadcast) the server echoes our own message back tagged with our character name**, e.g. `Raijin gangpaths: <msg>`. It does **NOT** use `You`.
- **Only the directed/room channels use the `You` form:** say → `You say "…"`, telepath echo → `--- Telepath sent to X ---` / `--- Telepath Sent to <Name> ---`. The client reads either casing (`ConversationTelepathOut`, registered in `DefaultPatterns`, is case-insensitive, as is `TelepathPacer`'s acknowledgement match). See *Talk & chat channels → Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement*.
- **Stock echoes gangpath, gossip and auction to the sender by name, but not the channel broadcast** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_tell_gang` @0x46ae71, `_tell_game` @0x46aef1, `_tell_group` @0x46ae25; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_tell_gang` and `_tell_game` send to everyone including the sender (`<name> gangpaths: `, `<name> gossips: `, `<name> auctions: `). The channel broadcast goes out through `_tell_group`, which skips the sender, and `_cmd_broadcast` prints nothing to the sender afterwards. **On Paradigm the channel broadcast is echoed to its sender** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, the user's Paradigm capture: `br h` answered `Broadcast from <Name> "h"`, in yellow)*: the sender sees the same `Broadcast from <Name> "<msg>"` line the other members do. So the broadcast echo in the first bullet of this topic is Paradigm's, and it keeps the `Broadcast from` form, not a `<Name> broadcasts:` one. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **A sender's own gossip or auction echo can be dropped by their own cap** (*Gossip and auction*).

**Client use:**
- In `RemoteCommandManager`, the null-/`You`-speaker self-echo guard can't catch a public-channel self-echo, so it must compare the speaker against our own name (`SelfNameProvider` → `PartyManager.LocalCharacterName`, given-name form). Otherwise our own gangpath'd `@`-command (e.g. `@timer sync`) is read back as an inbound command and bounces a denial at the whole gang.

### Gang channel speak verb (`bg`)
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-04 (user)*

- **The gang-channel speak verb is `bg`** (broadcast-gang), with `gb` and the `broadg…`/`broadgang` long forms as equivalents.
- **`gang` is NOT a speak command** — sending `gang <msg>` does not reach the gang.
- **Stock wire text and the bare form** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_broadgang` @0x4585cc, `_tell_gang` @0x46ae71; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - `bg <msg>` reaches every online member of the gang, the sender included, as `<name> gangpaths: <msg>` (@0x48a9bb), with no cap on how many.
  - Not in a gang, with or without a message: `You are not in a gang at the present!`
  - **Bare `bg` lists the gang instead of speaking**: online members only, or all members, per `set gang online|all`.
  - The table of command words agrees with the forms in this topic: `bg`, `gb` and `broadg`…`broadgang` are the gang verb and no spelling of `gang` is a command (*Wire, prompt & command output → Command words and abbreviations*).

**Client use:**
- Anything we emit on the gangpath channel (remote `@`-command replies, level-up announces, party `bg @heal`) must use `bg`.
- The alias-collision table in `AliasEngine` already reserves `bg`/`gb`/`broadg…` as the gangpath forms.

### Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-24 (user; report `stock-20260924-011014`)*

- **Telepaths are throttled, and each one is acknowledged in send order.** Every telepath gets exactly one reply line, in the order they went out:
  - `--- Telepath Sent to <Name> ---` — delivered.
  - `--- Telepath Not Sent ---` — it didn't reach its target because of throttling.
- **Read the acks positionally.** Three telepaths fired in a burst answered by one "Sent to" and then two "Not Sent" means the first arrived and the 2nd and 3rd were dropped and must be resent.
- **Pacing telepaths (and party/game-entry chatter) about 100 ms apart avoids the throttle.**
- **The ack may be glued after the prompt:** `[HP=32/MA=27]:--- Telepath Sent to Raijin ---`.
- **The ack names the full player name even when the telepath used an abbreviation** (`/raij`).
- **A shortened name reaches a player only when it fits exactly one** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user; Realm: both, by the user's statement of the same day that "chat channels are the same on paradigm as they are on stock")*. A telepath addressed with the first letters of a name reaches the player when that player is the only one in the game the letters fit. When the letters fit two players (`/bo` fitting both `<Bob>` and `<Boris>`), the telepath reaches neither of them until enough letters are typed to fit exactly one. The Stock code reads the same way: the prefix match under *How Stock's telepath works* in this topic.
  - **An ambiguous target draws the ambiguous-name reply, and nothing is sent** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user screenshot)*. `/<abc> hi`, where `<abc>` fits two players in the game, was answered with the reply recorded in *Wire, prompt & command output → Fixed command replies (refusals and housekeeping notices)*, bullet "An ambiguous name": the `Please be more specific.` line, then one `-- <Name>` row per player the letters fit (two rows in the screenshot), then the prompt. No `--- Telepath Sent to <Name> ---` line appeared. As drawn in the screenshot the reply was red; rendered colours follow the palette. For the telepath this is what the Stock code note under *How Stock's telepath works* left unfollowed ("what the player then sees wasn't followed").
- **Seen in report `stock-20260924-011014`**, where a party-join probe burst lost `@level` + `@version`.
- **How Stock's telepath works** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_whisper` @0x4571f2; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **Forms:** `/name msg`, the name glued to the slash, or `whisper name msg` (`whi`…`whisper`). The target sees `<sender> telepaths: <msg>` (@0x48a3eb), with the sender's first name.
  - **The name is matched as a prefix of the online players' names, an exact name winning outright** (`_get_user_number` @0x41df6e). Two or more prefix matches make the command return without printing a line of its own; what the player then sees wasn't followed.
  - **Refusals, in the order tested:** no message → `You have to telepath something!`; a space after the slash → `You have to specify a person to telepath to.`; the sender has telepaths blocked → `You may not telepath while you are blocking telepaths.` (so `set telepath off` blocks sending too); your own name → `Why are you telepathing to yourself?`; nobody of that name → `Cannot find user!`; then the three causes of `--- Telepath Not Sent ---` in the *three causes* bullet of this topic; last, `whisper name` with no message → `What do you really mean?`
  - **A telepath is not limited by distance, and a dropped character can send one**: the routine compares no rooms, and the command is on the dropped allow-list (*Health, resting & recovery → 0 HP — dropped / bleeding out*).
- **On Stock `--- Telepath Not Sent ---` has three causes, and the sender can't tell them apart** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_cmd_whisper` @0x45730c–0x45733e)*: the target is over its page cap for this tick, the target has telepaths blocked (`set telepath off`), or the target has `forget`-ed the sender (*`forget`*).
- **On Stock the throttle is the target's own setting, counted per 3-second tick over all senders** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_cmd_whisper` @0x45730c, `_cmd_set` @0x459326–0x459381, `_medium_update_character` @0x4228c4, `_create_player` @0x41661e; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - Each character has a count of pages received and a cap. The telepath is refused when the target's count is already above its cap; otherwise the count goes up by one and the telepath is delivered. The count is zeroed on the engine's medium pass (*Timing & rounds → The engine clock — one fast tick drives every timer*).
  - So a target with cap `N` takes `N + 1` telepaths per tick, from all senders together. Directed says to that player and BBS pages count toward the same number.
  - **The cap is `set maxpages <n>`, typed by the receiving character**: it stores `min(n, 255)`, answers `Maxpages set to <n>`, and is saved with the character. Bare `set maxpages` answers `Please specify the maximum number of pages: SET MAXPAGES <n>`.
  - **Paradigm:** `set maxpages 255` does not work there, and the user doesn't think Paradigm has this limit at all *(user 2026-10-09)*.
  - **A new character's cap is 3**, so the fifth telepath to reach it inside one tick is refused. A loaded character whose stored cap is 0 is given 1 (`_load_player` @0x415523–0x415552), so the third is. `pro` shows the cap as `Paging:             Ok|Off (%d every 3 seconds)`.
  - **Receivers are at the default cap** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "almost all players keep this setting at default. every capture you've seen its been at default settings")*. At the default of 3 a receiver takes four telepaths per 3-second tick, from all senders together.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` By the DLL the count has no notion of spacing, so on Stock 100 ms pacing alone can't keep a fifth telepath to one receiver inside one tick from being refused. That sits beside the *Pacing telepaths … about 100 ms apart avoids the throttle* bullet of this topic, which came from the user and report `stock-20260924-011014`. What would settle it: whether the paced bursts in that report ever put more than four telepaths on one receiver inside three seconds. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; the user's 2026-10-09 answer covered the receivers' cap.)

**Client use:**
- `BossTimerSyncCollector` (`Begin`, `StandingOf`, `OnePlayerAsked`) takes a telepathed `@timer sync` as having asked the player the `--- Telepath Sent to <Name> ---` line names, never the name as typed: a typed name may be shortened, and one that fits two players reaches neither. With no such line nobody was asked, and a telepathed timer is then listed for a pick, never merged in or synced (the rule itself is the **Client policy** under *Channel broadcast (`'`, `-`, `br`) and `join`*).
- `ChatRouter.TakeTelepathConfirmed` pairs a `--- Telepath Sent to <Name> ---` line with a pending telepath whose addressed name begins `<Name>`, case-blind, since the acknowledgement gives the name in full: of those, the one addressed by the most letters, and the oldest of those addressed alike (2026-10-11). A shortened name is delivered only when it fits one player (the first bullet of this topic), so of two pending sends that begin `<Name>`, the one with fewer letters may be the one refused as fitting a second player, and the acknowledgement is the more specific one's. The acknowledgement of a telepath the client sent, by the full name or by a longer prefix for another player's `@do`, therefore takes that send and never an older shortened request of the user's that reached nobody. `TelepathPacer.OnAck` pairs differently and is left as it was: it looks only at its oldest telepath in flight and retires it when its addressed name begins `<Name>`, which is what its resend order rests on. A send whose reply was not an acknowledgement (no such player, letters that fit two players, `--- Telepath Not Sent ---`) is never handed to an acknowledgement for another name; it goes stale after 15 s (the notice of that quotes the send only when it was the client's own line, never the user's words). Two of those replies end the pending send at once (2026-10-16): `--- Telepath Not Sent ---` once `TelepathPacer` has given up on that telepath after its three tries (`TelepathPacer.GaveUp` → `ChatRouter.TelepathGivenUp`; a refusal it resends does not, since the acknowledgement of the resend has to find the pending send), and the ambiguous-name reply when that telepath was the last line written to the wire as the reply began, was the only telepath still awaiting an answer, and every `-- <Name>` row begins with the letters it was addressed to (`ChatRouter.TrackAmbiguousReply`, `TelepathPacer.LastWrittenTelepath`; the reply is shared with `look`, `ask` and other commands, so nothing else ties it to a telepath). A `look` or `ask` written just before a telepath, whose reply arrives after the telepath went out with rows that begin with the telepath's letters (`look bo` → `-- bone`, `-- bottle` against `/bo …`), drops that telepath's pending send; that fails safe, since its acknowledgement then takes nothing. Either drop is logged at Debug. Otherwise, until it goes stale, an acknowledgement naming a player its letters begin is paired with it when no pending send is addressed to that player by more letters: a refusal the pacer never saw go out (a telepath typed a key at a time), or an ambiguous-name reply that arrived after another line had gone out or while another telepath was unanswered. Whose send it was (the user's own, or one the client made by itself or for another player's remote command) is carried with the pending send to its acknowledgement (`ChatRouter.OutgoingTelepathWasUsers`). Whose send a line was comes only from the line as it went out: a whole line sent with the send gate saying it is the user's (a button, a macro, a trigger, an event, an alias), or a line typed at the terminal, told from the keys typed (`SentCommandTrail.TypedLineEntered`, told only a line the trail itself keeps in the clear: one typed while nothing is kept, or at a prompt that is not the game's own, may be a password and is told to nobody, and neither is one longer than the trail keeps). A row the board shows back is never a send of the user's: it is queued only to give the Conversation window a sent telepath's text when no send was seen for it, and not queued at all when it is the copy of a line sent in the last 15 s (`ChatRouter.TryCaptureShownTelepath`). (An earlier note said `--- Telepath Not Sent ---` never drops the pending send; superseded 2026-10-16 by the give-up drop above.)
- The app takes a `@roomba sync`, a `@loop send yes` or a `@timer sync` of ours as the user's request only when the user sent it (`TransferChannels.IsUsersOwn`, `MainWindowViewModel.OnChatForTransfers`): for a telepath, the acknowledgement is of a send of the user's; for a line on gangpath, say or the broadcast channel, the user sent a line carrying those words on that channel in the last 15 s (`ChatRouter.UserSentLately`, `TransferChannels.CarriesOn`, which reads the speak forms recorded in *Gang channel speak verb (`bg`)*, *Channel broadcast (`'`, `-`, `br`) and `join`* and *Talk modes are per-realm configuration*, and takes a form it does not know for the channel the line came back on). The echo of our own line on a shared channel is no word of whose send it was: the client says such lines for another player's `@do` or relay-back. One that was not the user's starts no Roomba merge and accepts no loop; for a timer sync the merge window still opens, says so, and every answer is listed for a pick: nothing that answers it is merged in or synced, on any channel.

### Gossip and auction
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_gossip` @0x469431, `_cmd_auction` @0x4695bf, `_tell_game` @0x46aef1) · Realm: Stock*

- **The bare word toggles the channel.** `gossip` alone answers `You will no longer receive gossip messages.` / `You will now receive gossip messages.`, and `auction` alone the same with `auction`. `set gossip on|off` and `set auction on|off` do the same. So a `gos` sent with an empty message switches gossip off.
- **Wire text:** every in-game player with the channel on, the sender included, gets `<name> gossips: ` and then the rest of the line as typed; `<name> auctions: ` likewise.
- **Refusals:** `You may not use gossip - please contact your sysop.`; with your own gossip off, `You may not use gossip while your gossip is turned off.` then `Type 'gossip' to turn gossip on again.` Auction has the same three with `auction` in place of `gossip`.
- **Each listener has its own cap per 3-second tick, `set maxgossip <n>` and `set maxauction <n>`** (answers `Max gossips set to <n>` / `Max auctions set to <n>`; at most 255; a new character has 3 of each). A listener over its cap is skipped without a word to the sender (@0x46af59–0x46af8b). The counts are zeroed on the same medium pass as the telepath count (*Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement*).
  - **Each gossip costs a listener two counts**, since the line is sent as two pieces (@0x469588, @0x4695b0). At the default 3 a listener gets two whole gossips per tick.
  - **The sender's own echo goes through the same cap**, so a sender who out-runs their own `maxgossip` sees no echo of the later gossips, and no refusal line either.
- **`who` shows who has gossip off** (*Wire, prompt & command output → The `who` listing*).
- **The profanity filter, when the board has it on, drops the message with `You are using too much profanity - your message is not sent.`** It covers say, yell, gossip, auction and the channel broadcast.

### Channel broadcast (`'`, `-`, `br`) and `join`
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_broadcast` @0x4543f9, `_cmd_join`, `_tell_group` @0x46ae00) · Realm: Stock*

- **A numbered channel, separate from gossip and the gang channel.** `join <n>` answers `You just joined channel %d.`; the channel's members see `<name> just joined your channel (<n>)` / `<name> just left your channel (<n>)`. The syntax line is `Syntax: JOIN {group number} or {user name} or GANG {gangname}`.
- **`'msg`, `-msg` or `broadcast msg` (`br`…) reaches the other members of your channel** as `Broadcast from <name> "<msg>"` (@0x489849). The sender gets no echo (*Self-echo on public / broadcast channels*).
- **Bare `'` or `br` lists the channel:** `The following users are on channel %d:` and the names.
- **Not on a channel, the command isn't a command** (@0x454627), so `'hello` falls through to speech: said aloud in talk fast, `Your command had no effect.` in talk slow.
- **A broadcast on a channel ends neither a sneak nor a hide** *(Realm: both. Stock: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`. Paradigm: [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user: speaking on a broadcast channel does not end a sneak there either, "chat channels are the same on paradigm as they are on stock")*. On Stock, `_cmd_broadcast` (@0x4543f9–0x45462f) writes neither the sneak bit (the word at `+0x6f4`) nor the hidden byte `+0x5f6`: everything it calls is the channel getter (@0x416ddd, reads `+0x5f2`), the name getter (@0x416c89), the profanity check, the print routines and `_tell_group` (@0x46ae00), which has no such write either. The dispatcher's case for it (@0x413de7–0x413df5) has none, and the routine isn't among those listed under *What ends a sneak* in *Movement & navigation → Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine*, a list the client treats as true on both realms by the policy recorded there.
  - **Not on a channel it is speech, and speech ends both.** The fall-through of the bullet above lands in the say path, which clears the sneak bit and the hidden byte (`_execute_input` @0x450a93–0x450a9b).
  - (Was `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` for Paradigm, asking whether `br <msg>` on a channel leaves a sneak and a hide in place there as on Stock, with no Paradigm capture of a broadcast sent while sneaking on record; settled 2026-10-11 by the user's statement above. There is still no Paradigm capture.)

**Client use:**
- `RemoteCommandManager` reads `Broadcast from <name> "<msg>"` as a channel a remote command can arrive by, only while `RemoteCommandManager.DisableBroadcastChannel` is off (the Talk tab's box, ticked by default), and answers on it with `br <msg>` (`SendLine`). With the box unticked every remote command is read there, under the gates of the other channels (**Client policy**, user 2026-10-11); of the client-to-client transfers only `@timer sync` goes by it (`TransferChannels`), `@dupe` is dropped there as on say, and a relay-back (`&@`) is echoed on the channel like any answer (user, 2026-10-11: "if a remote command was issued on a channel, it should respond on that channel except for the sneak/say case"). (Until 2026-10-11 the channel carried the transfers alone.) Paradigm's `br` and its echo to the sender are in *Self-echo on public / broadcast channels*; the echo is skipped by the own-name guard there, and by `BossTimerSyncCollector` for our own `@timerdata`.
- `RemoteCommandManager.SendLine` sends a broadcast answer on the channel whether or not the character is sneaking, on both realms: only an answer to a say goes by telepath then. So `BossTimerSyncCollector.AnswersAreTakenOn` takes telepath after a said request and after no other.
- **Client policy** (decided 2026-10-11): `BroadcastAnswerBudget` bounds what the client says on the channel to one answer a minute to each speaker and four speakers a minute. `RemoteCommandManager` counts the four speakers a minute twice over (`OpenBroadcastAnswer`): once for speakers who hold the permission for what they sent (a command's reply, a `@timerdata` set, a relayed command, a refusal with a reason), once for the Failure message to speakers who do not, so refusals never take a granted speaker's place. The one answer a minute to a speaker is across both: answered in either, they wait the minute (`WhyNotOnBroadcast`). (The split is a review decision of 2026-10-11, not yet put to the user.) An answer is everything said for one line of the speaker's: a multi-line `@timerdata` set counts once, and so does a handler's later result after its first reply (`MayAnswerOnBroadcast`). A line whose answer the bound would hold back is not acted on; a granted speaker's command that says nothing is not counted. Every `br` line counts against the user's own input (*Wire, prompt & command output → Command rate limit (typing/sending too fast)*), and a player with no permission is still answered once.
- **Client policy** (decided 2026-10-11): a relay-back (`&@`) of a command taken by telepath and gangpath only (`@dupe`) is dropped on every channel, and nothing is relayed on the broadcast channel while the client does not know its own name (`RemoteCommandManager.HandleRelayBack`). A relay-back whose payload has `suicide` among its words is refused on every channel by the rule that refuses `@do … suicide` (`SendsSuicide`).
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-11: "if we hold an active timer on a boss, and we ask for a sync, if the timer they give us is different than what we hold it syncs, if we dont hold a timer, it merges in. if we ask in a channel where multiple people can or did respond, we do the same thing, compare all responses to the timer we hold, if there are conflicts, they all get listed in the menu and the user has to pick which timer they want in their data."; and of a public channel, "anyone that responds with data should be compared as long as their response is a correct response and not malformed or a fake answer"): every well-formed answer to a `@timer sync` of the user's is compared, boss by boss, with the timer held at that moment, co-kills within a minute being the same timer (`BossTimerSyncViewModel.Classify`, `SameTimer`, `IngestOffer`).
  - **A timer held is one still running**, as a responder's own set counts it (`BossTimerStore.StatusFor`; a Cleanup boss with no cleanup time set counts as none here, though the Bosses tab shows it DEAD, `IsCleanupDead`): an expired timer counts as holding none (user, 2026-10-17: "Expired = none"; `BossTimerSyncViewModel.Held`). (Until 2026-10-17 any stored kill time counted as held, expired or not.)
  - **The one thing asked is a telepath of the user's to one player, and the answer is that player's** (the player the game showed the telepath reaching, *Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement*; `BossTimerSyncCollector.OnePlayerAsked`, `TimerSyncStanding.TheOneAsked`): decided as it arrives. None held, for a boss on our list: merged in. The same: nothing. Differs: it syncs (ours is replaced, with no pick).
    - **Not while another telepath request of the user's waits for the game to show it sent** (2026-10-17): players may be asked one after another without waiting, and the first one's answer can arrive before the game confirms the next request. That answer is gathered, not written, until the game has shown every such request sent, or reached nobody, or a confirmation could no longer be paired with it (`ChatRouter.UsersTelepathAwaiting`, 15 s; asked of the chat log's pending sends, so a window opened by the first request's confirmation still sees a second one already sent); it is then judged as the one player's if that player is still the only one asked, and with the other replies if not (`BossTimerSyncCollector.AwaitingTelepathSent`, `BossTimerSyncViewModel.JudgeHeldBack`).
  - **Several can or did answer** (gangpath, say, the broadcast channel; more than one player telepathed in the window; a shared channel listened on as well, asked before or after; `TimerSyncStanding.OneOfSeveral`): nothing is decided on the first arrival (user, 2026-10-11: "for the timer rules, if we ask on gang, say, broadcast we can expect multiple replies... so in the case of multiple replies, for us holding no timer, ALL replies have to match each other otherwise open the picker, and for us holding a timer ALL replies have to match our timer otherwise open the picker").
    - **The replies are gathered until none has come for 10 s** (`BossTimerSyncViewModel.QuietPeriod`; every request and every line of every reply starts the 10 s again, `BossTimerSyncCollector.Activity`), then judged together (`BossTimerSyncViewModel.Settle`). The figure is a client choice, set against the pacing: a set is sixty timers at most, a dozen or so lines, written one after another on a shared channel and `TelepathPacer.Gap` (100 ms) apart by telepath.
    - **None held:** merged in only if every reply that named the boss agrees (the co-kill minute); one reply alone agrees with itself. If they differ, every reply stays listed, default "take none", and nothing is written.
    - **A timer held:** every reply matches it, nothing; any differs, those that differ are listed beside ours, default "keep ours". This is decided as each reply comes, since neither outcome writes.
    - A boss only some responders named is judged on the replies that named it.
    - **A reply after the others were judged** is compared with what we hold then: the same, nothing; different from ours or from the timer just merged in, listed against it, our side naming whose was merged in; the first to name a boss, gathered in its turn for another 10 s.
    - **A pick can be applied before the 10 s are up** and is written like any pick. **Closing the window before then writes nothing that was not applied:** the gather is abandoned, the timer still pending judges nothing, and the program log names the bosses left.
  - **A timer of ours that changed after the user first asked in the window is never written over as an answer arrives** (2026-10-11): a kill of our own, a clear, an edit. An answer that differs from what we then hold is listed instead of merged in or synced, from the one player asked as at the judging of gathered replies, and our side of the row says it changed since asking (`BossTimerSyncViewModel.ChangedSinceAsked`). What the window itself merged in, synced or wrote for a pick applied is not such a change (`WriteOwn`), and neither is a timer running out. "Asked" is when the request went out, as the user pressed Enter or the button sent it (`ChatRouter.UsersLineSent`), not when the game showed it; a window the request's echo opens is handed our kill times as they stood then (`MainWindowViewModel.OnUsersLineSentForTimerSync`, `BossTimerSyncViewModel.KillTimesNow`). (An earlier note counted a pick applied as a change and took "asked" from the game's echo; superseded 2026-10-17.)
  - **What answers no request of the user's is only ever listed** (`TimerSyncStanding.NotAsked`), whether we hold a timer or not: a telepath from a player the user did not ask; a telepath after a request whose acknowledgement never came; anything answering a request the client sent for another player (a relay-back, a `@do`, a `@party` relay), on any channel. A request the client telepathed for another player asks nobody, and neither does the acknowledgement of any other telepath (`ChatRouter.OutgoingTelepathWasUsers`).
  - **A boss not on our list always asks**; a pick of it adds the boss to the list.
  - **A pick is not written over a timer of ours that changed after its row was built**, for a boss on our list or one added since (`BossTimerSyncViewModel.Apply`). Changed is the stored kill time: one that only ran out is no change, and the pick is written (`OurKillMoved`).
  - **What is compared is a set that arrived whole and decodes** (`BossTimerSyncCollector.Ingest`): a set never completed is never delivered; one that does not decode is discarded with a warning in the program log; a number that is no boss in the game data, sent with no name, is listed and skipped at Apply. A well-formed answer carrying a made-up time cannot be told from a true one, and is compared like any other.
  - A set with a piece heard on the channel is a set heard on it; its listed rows are marked `heard on broadcast`.
  - (The rule that replaced it merged the first answer on a shared channel in as it arrived and listed a second that differed against it; refined the same day, 2026-10-11, to gather the replies and judge them together.)
  - (An earlier rule, 2026-10-11, made every answer on a shared channel a pick; superseded the same day. It was drawn from the user's "if we ask on a channel with multiple people, a dialog is supposed to pop up and the user picks…", and for a telepath to one player "if the timer they asked for, was missing on their end, just adopt it".)
- `BossTimerSyncViewModel` sends `br @timer sync` for its Broadcast choice. On Stock the sender sees no echo, so `MainWindowViewModel.OnChatForTransfers` cannot see a hand-typed one go out.

### `forget`
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_forget` @0x4762d4, `_is_user_forgotten` @0x47638f) · Realm: Stock*

- **`forget <name>` toggles a player on your forget list**: `You have now forgotten <name>` / `You have no longer forgotten <name>`. Bare `forget` prints `Forgotten Users:` and one name per line, or `You have not forgotten any users.` A full list answers `Your forget list is too long.`
- **The list lasts one session.** It is kept with the connection and emptied at log-off (@0x408d4b, @0x408db9).
- **A forgotten player's telepaths get `--- Telepath Not Sent ---`** (*Telepath throttle and per-telepath acknowledgement*). The test compares the forgotten name with the sender's whole first name, case-blind (@0x4763c1). The routine has two more callers. One is `invite`, which refuses with `You cannot invite %s.` (*Party → Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`*); the other was not read.
