## Health, resting & recovery

How HP works from full health down through dropping and death, how monster health reads via `look`, what does and doesn't let you rest, and how mana regenerates (including rerolling mana-regen roll spells).

### Max-HP sources
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **Class sets the base health rolls; race adjusts them; level scales within those bounds.** The same class differs by race, and max HP climbs with level between the race/class-determined floor and ceiling.
- **The Health stat scales HP regen and also feeds max HP.** Higher Health means faster natural recovery (a regen rate on a scale), and it adds to max HP too — `CharacterCalculator.CalcMaxHp` uses `health/2 + (health-50)*level/16` (see *Character stats & progression → Health (HEA) — max HP and HP regen*).

### Positive HP — fully functional
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **At any positive HP (1 … max) the character keeps every normal action.** HP level alone imposes no restriction.
- **Ailments are a separate axis.** Status afflictions can still block actions (e.g. a *held* status stops movement server-side), but that is independent of HP.

### 0 HP — dropped / bleeding out
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **Hitting 0 HP drops the character.** They can **no longer move on their own**, and can **no longer fight or cast spells**. A dropped character is out of the action entirely, not merely immobile.
- **A drop means bleeding out.** Left unreversed, HP keeps trending toward the BBS death threshold (see *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*).
- **Stock bleeds 1 HP every 30 s** *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `_slow_update_character`; [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*. At HP ≤ 0 the 30 s tick takes 1 HP instead of paying regen, then checks the death threshold. So an un-aided character at `−n` dies after about `(|threshold| − n)·30 s` unless aided or healed. Paradigm is assumed the same *(**Client policy**, user 2026-09-30)*.
  - **The tick is the fixed 30 s slow tick** that also pays regen, every character in one pass *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-30, `_slow_update_character` @0x4221ad; see *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster HP regen*)*.
  - **Poison still runs first:** a poisoned character sees `You feel ill.` and loses the poison amount, then a dropped one also loses the 1 HP bleed in the same tick.
- **Dropping removes you from the party** — see *Party → Dropping (0 HP) or instant death removes you from the party* and *Party → Dropped ally rescue*.
- **The game rejects every action command while dropped / mortally wounded** — except `sys …` commands (see *Sysop commands → Sysop power gating*). Movement, casting, aiding and telepaths all bounce with `You may not do that while you are mortally wounded!`, `Your command had no effect.`, or (for remote / telepath commands) `{command invalid or not allowed}`.
- **On Stock a dropped character may still use a fixed list of commands, the telepath among them** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_handle_commands` @0x4136cf–0x413780, the compare chain @0x4136e9–0x41374c; command words re-read 2026-10-17 by emulating `_parse_command` @0x40dd44 over every input it branches on, handlers from the switch table @0x4137a6; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The gate runs when HP is 0 or below (`[user+0xb0]`, @0x4136cf) **or the character is paralysed** (Paralyze, ability 75: word `user+0x6f4` bit 0x800, set by `_update_dynamic_with_ability` @0x43ddaf and cleared by `_negate_dynamic_with_ability` @0x43dfd0; an earlier note called this flag unidentified, superseded 2026-10-17). No spell in either imported set carries ability 75 (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Ailment identification — which spells cause disease / poison / blind / hold*), so in practice only HP sets it off. Every other recognised command then prints `You may not do that while you are mortally wounded!` (@0x413759), the paralysed character included.
  - **Allowed, with the words the parser takes** (`st[atus]` means `st`, `sta` … `status`):
    - telepath: any first word starting `/` (`/name msg`), or `whi[sper] name msg`. `whisper` is the telepath, not an in-room whisper; both print `%s telepaths: …` (`_cmd_whisper` @0x4571f2).
    - broadcast: any first word starting `'` or `-`, or `br[oadcast]`. With no text it lists the channel's users (`_cmd_broadcast` @0x4543f9).
    - `l[ook]`; `st[atus]`; `he[alth]`; `i` or `inve[ntory]` (`in` and `inv` match nothing); `ke[ys]`; `who` (exact) or `sc[an]` (`wh` matches nothing); `exp[erience]` (`ex` matches nothing); `pr[ofile]`; `to[pten]`; `?` or `hel[p]` (`h` matches nothing).
    - `statl[ine] on|off|full`: needs the second word, else `Syntax: STATLINE {ON/OFF/FULL}`.
    - `qu[iet]` and `bri[ef]`: one handler (`q` alone is quit). `verb[ose]`: any word starting `verb` is verbose (`vers…` is version, refused).
    - `fe[edback] <text>` (`_send_feedback_mail` @0x40add5); `glo[bal] …` passes the rest to the BBS global-command handler (`_cmd_global` @0x4697a8); `sy[sop] …`: every `sys` line passes, its subcommands check the sysop key themselves (`_cmd_sysop` @0x4626f9).
    - `suicide` and `reroll`: full word only (`_cmd_suicide` @0x4692be).
    - `sa[ve]`: allowed, but it only prints `You may not save your character. You must exit normally…` (@0x413adb); it never saves.
    - dead: `soun[d]` (@0x413b28) and `id[entity]` (`_cmd_identity` @0x4541ea always returns 0) do nothing.
    - The command numbers let through are 12–15, 17–19, 23, 41, 43, 44, 49–53, 58, 71, 74, 75, 87, 106, 113, 130.
  - **One-word commands with extra words don't run.** `status`, `health`, `inventory`, `keys`, `who` / `scan`, `profile`, `quiet` / `brief`, `verbose` and `save` test for exactly one word (e.g. @0x413b47, @0x414010, @0x414171, @0x414315); with more, the line falls through as plain text (the next bullet) after passing the gate.
  - **Refused, among others:** every move, `bg`, `gossip`, `auction`, the directed say `>`, `set`, `par`, `join`, `aid`, `rest`, `break`, `q` / `quit`.
  - **`x` skips the gate but is still refused:** `_execute_input` catches an exact `x` (@0x45025e) and calls `_cmd_quit`, which answers `You may not exit MajorMud while you are mortally wounded!` (@0x46198e) instead of the gate's line.
  - **A line that is no command at all never reaches the gate** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-17, static reading; not checked in game)*: `_parse_command` returns 0 and `_handle_commands` exits (@0x413692) before the HP test. `_execute_input` @0x45003c then tries, in order:
    1. the room's exit words and special command: HP above 0 only (@0x4503f3);
    2. a spell typed by its cast code: HP above 0 and not paralysed (@0x450840 / @0x450855); otherwise there is no refusal line, and the text drops through;
    3. the Mute check, `You cannot speak!` (@0x450915);
    4. profanity;
    5. actions / socials (`_handle_ljn_actions` @0x4604c7): no HP test at the top, but its helpers were not read;
    6. say / yell (0x450a3f–0x450d0e): no HP test.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` **So a dropped (or paralysed) Stock character's `.text` and `"text` look like they reach the room.** In fast talk mode, which a new character has by default (`player+0x5f4`, set in `_create_player` @0x4164e5), any unrecognised text is spoken (@0x450a93). That includes a cast code, the dead `sound` / `identity`, and an allowed one-word command given extra words. In slow mode only `.` and `"` lines are spoken, and anything else prints `Your command had no effect.` (@0x450ca5). Does a dropped Stock character's `.text` reach the room? (An earlier note asked the same from the speech path alone; the gate and talk-mode findings above added 2026-10-17.)
  - **The telepath bounce in the *game rejects every action command* bullet of this topic is taken as Paradigm's only** *(user 2026-10-09: "assume the telepath rejection is paradigm only")*; on Stock a dropped character can telepath, per the allow-list above. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **Two reversals bring a dropped character back into the positive:**
  - **another player** issues `aid <name>` on them, or
  - a **healing spell** lifts their HP above 0.
- **`aid` stops the bleeding; it doesn't stand them up — on both realms** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user; Stock mechanics [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `aid` + `_slow_update_character`)*. They stay down until their HP is **positive** — 0 doesn't count.
  - `aid` on a character at HP ≤ 0 marks them stabilised, and from then on the 30 s tick gives **+1 HP** instead of taking one, and skips normal regen, until HP is positive. The mark clears once HP is above 0, by that tick or by resting *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-30: the aided flag is byte `+0x6a8`, set by `_cmd_aid` @0x458261, cleared @0x4223fe / @0x422d19)*.
  - So without heals, an aided character at `−n` stands up after about `(n + 1)·30 s`. A heal can end that at any point. The deepest living HP is the death floor + 1, so the longest the climb can take is `|floor|·30 s`. *(The 30 s rate is from the Stock engine; Paradigm is assumed the same — **Client policy**, user 2026-09-30.)*
  - Wire text: the aider sees `You have aided <name>, <his/her> wounds are now healing.`; the target sees `<name> has aided you.`; `aid` on someone above 0 HP answers `<name> is in no need of assistance.`.
  - *(Earlier notes read "aid lifts them back above 0" as immediate; it's the slow climb on both realms. Superseded 2026-09-27.)*
- **Any player can `drag <name>` a dropped character** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*. The dropped character then **follows wherever the dragging player moves** — their only way out of the room until aided or healed. In a party the client leaves it to the leader (see *Party → Dropped ally rescue*).
- **A dropped character can still hang up.** Dropping blocks in-realm *actions* (move / fight / cast), but the **carrier drop / main-menu exit** (the Game-Exit command, e.g. `=x` / `;o`; see *Wire, prompt & command output → Realm exit / logoff sequence*) **still goes through at 0 HP or below** — the BBS-level `=x` works at any time *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*. So the emergency-hangup escape stays available all the way through the bleeding-out window.
  - **Client use:** if the connection isn't closed after the exit command, the client closes the socket itself (`HealthManager.SetHangupDisconnect` → `MainWindowViewModel.RequestHangupDisconnect`, after a short flush delay).
  - **On Stock the in-game exit is refused while dropped, and a lost carrier can be penalised** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_quit` @0x461984, `_ljngame_huprou` @0x408f91–0x409180; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The in-game `x` and `quit` are both refused at 0 HP or below (*Wire, prompt & command output → Realm exit / logoff sequence*). On a board whose hang-up penalty applies, a carrier drop at 0 HP or below kills the character (*Wire, prompt & command output → Hang-up / lost carrier*, which also holds the open question of whether the BBS-level `=x` counts as a hang-up).
- **HP percentage goes negative while bleeding out.** HP% is a plain `hp / maxHp` ratio with no clamp at zero, so a dropped character reads a **negative percentage**. Where `par` still lists the member it shows it as such (e.g. a member driven to −12/200 HP reads a negative HP%) — but **by realm** (2026-09-26, user): on **Stock** a dropped member is removed from the party at once, so `par` never shows them; on **Paradigm** `par` is believed to show the negative HP% *([NEEDS CONFIRMATION])* — see *Party → Dropping (0 HP) or instant death removes you from the party*. A percentage-based threshold is therefore a continuous scale from 100 % down through 0 % into the negatives, exactly like an absolute-HP scale.
- **Client use:**
  - The client's low-HP auto-hangup fires down to (but not past) the BBS death floor, giving a dropped-but-not-yet-dead character a last chance to disconnect before dying. Its "hang up if below" trigger can be set anywhere on the HP% scale, including negative.
  - Client engines that keep firing commands while dropped accomplish nothing but noise — a dropped / mortally-wounded local player must suppress engine command output until healed / aided.

### Rest and meditate tick timing
*Status: per-bullet tags · Realm: differs*

- **Stock engine timers** *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p timer setup)*. The engine runs four background passes, all counted off one 1-second tick — see *Timing & rounds → The engine clock — one fast tick drives every timer*:
  - the 1 s tick itself (rest and meditate counters);
  - every 3 ticks (spell-round durations);
  - every 5 ticks (combat energy);
  - every 30 ticks (passive regen and bleeding out).
- **Stock's passive tick pays whatever the character is doing** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, `_slow_update_character`)*. The 30-tick pass tests no fighting, resting or meditating flag: HP below max gains the HP amount, mana below max gains the mana amount. Poison comes off first; a character at 0 HP or less bleeds (or, once aided, gains 1) instead of regenerating HP.
  - **The game sends a fresh prompt when that pass changed anything**, and stays silent when it didn't. That unprompted statline is the passive tick on the wire.
- **Stock's rest and meditate ticks count from the command, in fast ticks** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, `_handle_commands`, `_fast_update_character`)*:
  - `rest` sets the resting flag and zeroes a per-character counter (`+0x7b2`), then prints `You are now resting.`. Each fast tick adds 1 while the flag is up; when the counter passes 20 it is zeroed and the rest amount is paid. So the first rest tick is the 21st fast tick after the command, and they repeat every 21.
  - `meditate` does the same with its own counter (`+0x7eb`) and `You are now meditating.`; the counter pays when it passes 14, so every 15 ticks.
  - **Typing `rest` (or `meditate`) again while already resting zeroes the counter**, which pushes the next tick a full 21 (15) ticks out.
  - **Each rest or meditate tick sends a fresh prompt**, paid or not: a rest tick at full HP still redraws it.
  - Meditation ends itself when mana reaches max: `You awake from deep meditation feeling stronger!`, then the prompt.
- **Passive regen** — the amounts are in *Character stats & progression → Health (HEA) — max HP and HP regen* and *Mana regeneration & the ManaRgn breakpoints*:
  - **Stock: HP and mana together every 30 s** *([OBSERVED] DLL, the 30-tick pass)*.
  - **Paradigm: mana every 30 s, standing HP every 10 s** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, report `paradigm-20261004-024314` and the same character's live program log)*. Mana pays its whole amount once per 30 s, standing or resting, in a fight or out of one (`+7` for the captured character). Standing HP pays a third of its 30 s amount three times: on the mana pass and 10 and 20 s after it (`+1` each) — until a rest moves it, as the next bullet says.
  - **The standing HP gain comes two rounds after the character's last HP gain, a rest gain included, so a rest can leave it a round off the mana pass** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, the first character's live program log)*. Before its rest the standing gains fell on the mana pass (`02:46:56.6`, `02:47:25.9`). The rest's last gain came at `02:53:41.5`; standing gains followed at `02:53:51.6`, `:54:00.7`, `:10.8`, `:20.8`, `:30.9`, while the mana pass came at `02:54:25.9`, `:56.1` and `02:55:26.3`, 5 s off them. After the next rest the same: last rest gain `02:56:45.7`, first standing gain `02:56:55.8`. Mana kept its own 30 s pass throughout.
- **Resting on Stock: an extra HP tick every 21 s** *([OBSERVED] DLL; [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*. It pays `3 × max(1, (level+20)·HEA/750)`, then the HP-regen percent bonus, **in addition to** the 30 s tick.
- **The HP-regen percent bonus is the last step, on the whole amount of the tick** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p; Stock)*. The 30 s pass (`_slow_update_character` @ `0x42235d`–`0x4223bd`) works out `base = max(1, (level+20)·HEA/750)` and then `(percent + 100) × base / 100`. The rest tick (`_fast_update_character` @ `0x422c41`–`0x422ca6`) triples `base` first (`lea eax,[edi+edi*2]`) and then applies the same `(percent + 100) × amount / 100`. Each division drops the fraction. The percent is the character's `+0x7d8` (HPRegen, ability 123, summed from gear and the rest), and the step is skipped when it is 0. MMUD-Explorer's `CalcRestingRate` has the same order on both realms: divisor (500 on GreaterMUD, 750 on Stock), at least 1, `× 3` when resting, then `Fix(((percent + 100) × amount) / 100)`.
- **Resting on Paradigm: an HP gain every 5 s on the combat-round grid, three low then three high, counted from the command** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, report `paradigm-20261004-024314` and the same character's live program log: five rest sessions of a level 17 Gypsy, Health 60)*.
  - **The gains ride the server's round grid, whenever you lie down.** The first one comes on the next round after the `rest` command (0.4–4.9 s after it in the captures), then one every round. Rest takes the standing HP gain's place; nothing extra arrives on top.
  - **The amount runs in threes from the command:** three low gains, three high, three low, and so on — `+1 +1 +1 +4 +4 +4 +1 +1 +1 +4 …` in every session. A rest that is broken and started again begins at the low three, so resting again costs the high gains that were coming.
  - **What the numbers were:** for this character `(level + 20) × Health / 500` is 4.44. The low gain is `+1`, a third of that with the fraction dropped, and the same as the standing gain. The high gain is `+4`, the whole 30 s amount. Over 30 s that is 15 HP resting against 3 standing. (Reading the high gain as a third of a tripled resting rate gives the same number for any character: dropping the fraction of three times an amount and taking a third always lands on the amount with its fraction dropped.)
  - **A second character, wearing HP-regen gear, confirms the cycle and shows where the percent enters** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, report `paradigm-20261004-140923`: a level 28 Paladin, Health 71, a ring with HPRegen +25 and nothing else carrying it; 52 rest gains and 12 standing ones)*. `(level + 20) × Health / 500` is 6.82, so the amount before the bonus is 6. Standing it gained `+2`, `+2`, `+3` every 30 s, the `+3` on the mana pass. Resting it gained `+2 +2 +3 +7 +7 +7` every 30 s, counted from the `rest` command, first gain on the next round (3.6 s after it), through eight full cycles and into a ninth without exception.
    - **The full gain is the amount plus the percent of it, each with the fraction dropped:** `6 + 25 × 6 / 100` = 7. Scaling the unrounded 6.82 would give 8, so the amount is cut to a whole number before the percent, as on Stock.
    - **The low and standing gains are thirds of the amount before the percent** (`6 / 3` = 2), **and what the percent adds to the whole amount (1 here) comes on the last gain of each three**: the third low gain of a rest, and the standing gain that lands on the mana pass. **The same character with the ring off gained `+2 +2 +2 +6 +6 +6`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, report `paradigm-20261004-142359` and its live program log: 47 rest gains, seven full cycles and into an eighth)*, so the extra point on the third gain and on each full gain is the bonus and nothing else. The first character, with no bonus and an amount of 4, got `+1 +1 +1` and `+4`: a third that doesn't divide evenly just loses its fraction, and the point left over is never made up.
    - (Until this capture the percent was taken to scale the amount before it was split into equal thirds, from Stock's DLL and MMUD-Explorer and the user's expectation that the realms agree; that gave `+2 +2 +2`, one short per 30 s. Superseded 2026-10-04.)
  - **The rule that fits all three captures:** with `A = max(1, (level + 20) × Health / 500)` and `B = HPRegen% × A / 100`, fractions dropped, the full gain is `A + B`, the small gain is `A / 3`, and the three small gains are `A/3`, `A/3`, `A/3 + B`. `B` is the same term in the full gain and on the third small gain. It gives `1 1 1 / 4` for the first character (`A` 4, no bonus), `2 2 3 / 7` with the ring and `2 2 2 / 6` without it (`A` 6).
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`, where the rule runs ahead of the captures: a bonus worth more than one point (the rule puts all of it on the third small gain — `2 2 4 / 10` for an amount of 8 with +25% — where spreading it would give `2 2 3`), and an amount that isn't a multiple of 3 together with a bonus (the rule takes the third from the amount before the bonus: `1 1 2 / 6` for an amount of 5 with +25%).
  - **Mana is untouched by resting:** it kept its 30 s pass and its amount through every rest.
  - (An earlier note, 2026-09-30, had a rest tick every 10 s in cycles of three, two reduced ticks of a third each and then a full one; it was the user's unmeasured impression and is superseded 2026-10-04 by the timed captures. An older capture, 2026-09-27 at 0.1 s resolution, read a druid as +3 standing and +9 resting on a 10 s grid. MMUD-Explorer's source, checked 2026-09-30, has no Paradigm rest cycle: `CalcRestingRate` only switches the divisor (500 on GreaterMUD, 750 on Stock) and triples the amount when resting, and its exp/hr model uses one rest tick every 20 s on both realms, `SEC_PER_REST_TICK`.)
- **Meditating: a mana gain every 15 s on both realms, paying the base mana amount without `ManaRgn%`, while the 30 s passive tick keeps running alongside it** *(Stock [OBSERVED] DLL and [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user; Paradigm [OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, timed log of a level 49–51 Priest: 143 meditate stretches, 623 mana gains)*.

For 102 of those combined gains, the gain less the last standing tick before the stretch was exactly the meditate amount; the others differed by 26 to 45 and weren't traced (a mana-regen roll recast between the two would do it). Stock counts its 15 ticks from the command instead (the bullets above).

The `meditate` command wasn't logged, so the stretch doesn't show how soon the first gain follows it.

The meditate tick (`_fast_update_character` @ `0x422d33`–`0x422f24`, gated on the meditating flag) reads and writes mana only (`+0x602` against max `+0x600`); it never touches HP (`+0xb0`) or the HP-regen percent. The rest tick just before it (@ `0x422c06`) is the only fast-tick HP payer and is gated on the resting flag, and the two flags can't both be set: `rest` clears the meditating flag (@ `0x414884`) and `meditate` clears the resting flag (@ `0x4149d4`). So a meditating character's HP comes from the 30 s pass alone, which pays whatever the character is doing (the *Stock's passive tick* bullet above). The companion `wccmmpls.dll` has no regen or meditation code.

**Client use:**
- `RealmRegenProfile` gives `RegenTracker` its countdowns and the Exp/Hr simulator its cadence (see *Timing & rounds → The engine clock — one fast tick drives every timer*). On Paradigm the rest cycle anchors on the round grid; on Stock it counts from lying down. `RegenTracker` learns the per-tick amounts live.
- `HealthManager` never sends `rest` / `meditate` to a character already in that posture (lain down by hand, or left resting while the engine was switched off): it takes the rest under way as its own. A second `rest` restarts the count toward the next tick (Stock, the bullets in this topic; the user said the same of Paradigm, 2026-09-29).
- Character Info's HP Regen readout shows Paradigm as measured: the standing third and the whole amount as a rest's full gain, and with an HP-regen bonus the three low gains as they come (`+2, +2, +3`) (`CharacterCalculator.ParadigmHpRegenThird`). (Until 2026-10-04 its tooltip still described the superseded 10 s cycle and showed three times the amount as the full rest gain.)
- `SimCharacterBuilder.BuildRegen` (the Exp/Hr Estimator's character simulation) plays Paradigm as measured: mana whole every 30 s; standing HP a third of the idle amount, fraction dropped, every 10 s; resting a gain every 5 s on the round grid, three of that third then three of the whole idle amount, counted from lying down. The third is of the amount before the regen percent, and what the percent adds is paid on the last low gain of a run and on the standing gain that comes with the mana pass (`SimRegen.HpLowExtra`). A third is kept to at least 1 — `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`, since no capture has shown a character whose idle amount is under 3. (Until 2026-10-04 it played the superseded 10 s cycle, which paid `5 ×` the idle amount per 30 s; the measured cycle pays `3 × third + 3 × idle`: 15 against 20 for the captured character.)

### Poison prevents resting
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 (user; report `paradigm-20260817-092945`); meditate split by realm 2026-09-28 · Realm: differs*

- **How the poison itself ticks and stacks** is in *Spells, buffs & conditions → Poison and damage over time — ticks, stacking and cures*.
- **While poisoned you cannot rest.** A `rest` issued while poisoned does **not** put you into the `(Resting)` state — poison refuses / breaks it — so the position never becomes Resting and the resting recovery doesn't happen; you only get the slow standing regen.
- **Meditating while poisoned differs by realm.**
  - **Stock refuses it too** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p)*: both commands check the character's poison amount and refuse while it's above 0.
  - **Paradigm lets you meditate while poisoned** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*; only `rest` is refused.
  - (An earlier note, 2026-09-27, said neither works on either realm; superseded 2026-09-28 for Paradigm's meditate.)
- **The refusal lines are `You are too sick to rest!` and `You are too sick to meditate!`.** *(Wording [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p string table; meaning [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user: "you can't rest or meditate while poisoned".)*
- **Client use:**
  - An optimistic "resting" latch armed on the send (`HealthManager._restInFlight`) never confirms while poisoned, and the interruption latch can't clear it (it needs a confirmed Resting first). So the auto-rest engine must **re-attempt the rest once poison clears** (the poison falling edge drops the stale latch) — otherwise it sits standing below the rest floor forever, which is what report 092945 hit.
  - `HealthManager.NoteRestRefusedSick` reads the refusal lines: it drops the latch, holds the re-send while the poison is on record, and otherwise retries after 15 s, since the refusal can arrive before the poison shows up anywhere else.
  - On Paradigm a poisoned character with mana to recover meditates instead (`HealthManager.MeditatesWhilePoisoned`), so the pre-rest mana set swaps in as usual.

### Meditating with mana already full
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-27 (user) · wording [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p string table*

- **`meditate` with mana already full is refused with `Meditation will not help at this time.`** You don't start meditating.
- **Gear that changes max HP / mana changes it the moment it's worn or removed** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*.
- **Client use:**
  - `HealthManager.NoteMeditateNotNeeded` drops the unanswered meditate and records the current mana as the game's full mark while the client's max stays the same (the mark rises with any higher reading). Reaching it counts as rested and clears the mana gate.
  - A follower's `@ok` then waits for the Pre-rest set to come off (`HealthManager.SetPartyOkHold`): the Default set goes back on, a CR re-reads the pools, then `@ok` goes out (**Client policy**, user 2026-09-28). The hold is capped at 20 s.
  - Report `paradigm-20260928-223148`: the client read 423/448 when the game said 423 was full. The 448 was the client's mistake. An `exp` screen had re-applied the maxima from an older `stat` read with the Pre-rest set on (423), over the Default gear's real 398. The next swap then added +25 on top. Fixed: only a screen that showed Hits / the pool sets the maxima (`StatParser.LastCaptureReadHits` / `LastCaptureReadPool`).

### Rest basis — the Default-gear baseline
*Status: **Client policy** — CONFIRMED 2026-09-28 (user) · Realm: both*

- **Rest, heal and flee percentages resolve against the max HP / mana recorded from a `stat` screen taken with the Default gear set worn.** No other gear's screen, and no `exp` screen, changes it.
- **It only goes stale when the level changes, or when the Default set changes in a way that alters its max HP / mana bonus.** Then a `stat` goes out the next time the Default set is on and nothing is in progress; the old values stay in use until it lands.

**Client use:** `DefaultPoolBaselineKeeper` records and refreshes it (persisted as `CharacterProfile.DefaultPoolBaseline`). `AppServices.DefaultBasisMaxHp` / `DefaultBasisMaxMa` feed it to `HealthManager` and `CastingDirector`, falling back to `DefaultSetMaxPool`'s gear estimate before the first recording. The current-gear caps in `RestThresholds` still apply.

### Casting a spell interrupts resting / meditating
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 (user)*

- **Casting a spell on yourself (a self-bless, etc.) while resting or meditating breaks the rest/meditate state.** Position drops back to Standing, the same as taking a hit or moving. Reported as "meditate not re-engaging automatically after blessing while resting."
- **Client use:**
  - `HealthManager`'s confirm/interrupt latch (`_restInFlight` / `_restConfirmedByPrompt`) only recognized `PlayerPosition.Resting`, never `PlayerPosition.Meditating`. So a `meditate` send's confirmation step never fired, the interruption step's guard never tripped either, and the latch stuck `true` forever after a meditate got interrupted in place (no room move to fall back on and clear it via `NoteRoomChanged`).
  - Fixed by treating Resting and Meditating as the same "in a resting-family position" state for the confirm/interrupt check. `rest` was never affected, since its position always matched.
  - A rest broken off outside a fight is owed again until it is re-sent (`HealthManager._restResumeOwed`), so the recovery gate keeps clearing against the rest target, not the rest trigger, when the re-send is put off — a ShadowRest character sneaks first (report `paradigm-20261004-202253`: a buff ticked "cast while resting" stood the character up at 96/151, the re-rest waited for the sneak, and the gate cleared at the 77 trigger instead of the 121 target).

### What ends a rest
*Status: OBSERVED 2026-10-03 (`wccmmud.dll` 1.11p: every write that clears the resting flag, bit `0x400` of the user word at `0x6f4`, and the meditating flag, bit `0x100` at `0x7c8`) · Realm: Stock; Paradigm not recorded except where a linked topic says so*

- **`rest` sets the resting flag and `meditate` the meditating flag; these commands clear both.** Where one function serves several commands (`_handle_commands`), the command was read from the calls and strings around the clear, not traced line by line.
  - **Moving and fighting:** a move (`_move_user`); any attack command, `bash` and backstab included (`_cmd_any_attack`, `_cmd_bash`); attacking or being attacked, by a monster or a player; a monster's spell landing on you (`_monster_cast`).
  - **Doors and exits:** `open`, `close`, `lock`, `bash`, `picklock`, `search`, and `disarm trap` (cleared in the dispatcher just before `_cmd_disarm`).
    - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` A re-read of that dispatcher case on 2026-10-10 (@0x413f65–0x413fcd) has the clears on the other branch: a three-word line whose second word is `trap` goes to `_cmd_disarm` (@0x413f8c) and jumps past them, and every other line of that command clears resting, meditating, the sneak bit and the hidden byte (@0x413f99–0x413fb3) and calls `_ready_weapon`. `_cmd_disarm`'s own body (@0x468bed) writes none of them; what it calls wasn't traced. Does `disarm trap <dir>` end a rest on Stock? (The same question for the sneak is in *Movement & navigation → Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals*, the *What ends a hide on Stock* bullet.)
  - **Items:** `get`, `drop`, `give`, `use`, `eat`, `drink`, `light`, `ready` / `remove` gear, the `move` command.
  - **Shops and banks:** `list`, `buy`, `sell`, `stock`, `unstock`, `markup`, `deposit`, `withdraw`.
  - **Other:** `sneak`, `hide`, `track`, `rob`, `follow`, `drag`, `aid`, `share`, `train`, casting a spell (`_cmd_cast`).
  - Three more clears sit in the dispatcher beside the gang-rank calls (`_change_user_rank`); which commands they belong to wasn't traced.
- **Casting clears resting in the per-target cast routines as well** (`_cast_no_target`, `_cast_user_target`, `_cast_monster_target`); see *Casting a spell interrupts resting / meditating*.
- **A room command run from the room's text block does not clear either flag.** `_execute_input` hands an unrecognised command to `_perform_special_command` with no write to either flag before or inside it. That is the path a room action such as `pull winch` takes.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Winches exist on Paradigm (*Movement & navigation → Winch gates*), which is a different build. Does `pull winch` stand a resting character up there?
- **`look` does not end a rest.** `_cmd_look` writes neither flag.
- **Paradigm differs for gear and meditation:** see *Gear swaps interrupt resting, not meditating*.
- **A room spell's damage breaks a rest:** see *Resting in a room whose spell does damage*.

**Client use:**
- `DoorOpenManager`, `HiddenExitRevealManager`, `TrapDisarmManager` and `WinchManager` each hold their next bash / pick, `sea`, `disarm trap` or winch pull while the movement coordinator's `HealthRecovery` or `ManaRecovery` gate is up (`SetRestHold`, `NotifyRestHoldChanged`, wired in `AppServices` off `MovementCoordinator.GatesChanged`). **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-03): a try that would interrupt a rest waits until the rest hold is clear. The winch is held too, since Paradigm's answer isn't known.
- `LoopRunner.ParkClearedStepWhilePaused`: a trap, door, winch or hidden-exit reply that lands while the loop is paused takes the step out of flight, and the resume re-drives it (report `paradigm-20261003-111800`).

### Gear swaps interrupt resting, not meditating
*Status: see inline tags · Realm: Paradigm observed; rest rule from the user*

- **Wearing or removing gear stands a resting character up, and resting again restarts the rest timer from full** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)*: every `wear` / `eq` / `rem`.
  - Seen again on Paradigm *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-15, report `paradigm-20261015-202943`)*: `You are now resting.`, then `wear shungite pendant` → `You are now wearing shungite pendant.`, and the next prompt had no `(Resting)`.
- **Meditation isn't broken by a swap** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-29, report `paradigm-20260929-115648`: `(Meditating)` held through eight `wear` / `eq` / `rem` commands)*.
- **Client use:** the pre-rest set goes on before `rest` is sent — `HealthManager` asks `AutoEquipCoordinator.WearRestGearBeforeResting` and holds the rest while the swap streams. For `meditate` the gear follows the sit.
  - A `rest` the user types gets its gear only after the sit, so its wear stands them up: `AutoEquipCoordinator` sends `rest` again once the set has streamed (`HealthManager.ResendRestAfterGearSwap`), and that stand doesn't revert to Default (report `paradigm-20261015-202943`).

### Resting in a room whose spell does damage
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 (user); the room-spell classes [OBSERVED] 2026-10-10 (imported game data, Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p); the room cast [OBSERVED] 2026-10-10 (Stock 1.11p DLL) · Realm: both*

- **A room spell that does damage breaks rests** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user, of magma drip: "a room spell that does magma drip which breaks rests")*. The game re-casts a room's spell every six seconds or so (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Room-spell monster summons*), so a rest in such a room is broken on every cast.
  - **It breaks a meditation too** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: asked whether room damage breaks a meditation as it does a rest, "yes")*. (An earlier note asked this; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **A room that hurts only on a roll still allows resting** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "yes, they only break resting if the damage roll is what is chosen")*: the rest is broken on the casts where the damaging line of the table is rolled, and stands on the others. (An earlier note asked whether such a room should bar resting; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` The user said the first of magma drip (#115). Does any damage from a room's own spell stand a resting character up, however small (freezing cold #5242 does 1 to 4)? The client takes it that it does, and the user can untick any spell (the Client policy below).
- **How much a room's spell does** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL, `_room_cast_on_user` `0x47572f`)*:
  - One value is rolled between the two words at `spell+0xc0` and `spell+0xc2` (`0x4757f0`–`0x475815`: the lower of the two, plus a `genrdn` over their difference), read as the record's `MinBase` and `MaxBase`: magma heat #526 has 30 and 60, and report `paradigm-20261008-202210` saw 31 to 58 a hit. It is then cut by the percentage `_get_spell_random_modifier` (`0x43f608`) returns (`0x475818`–`0x47582a`: value × (100 − modifier) / 100). No level enters the roll: the per-level fields are not read here.
  - Each of the spell's ten ability slots takes that rolled value unless the slot has a value of its own (`spell+0xa8`, the `AbilVal-N` column), which is then used as it is (`0x475854`–`0x47586c`). Paradigm's fall below #5786 has `Abil 1` with value 35: a flat 35.
  - **A resist roll comes first for a spell whose byte at `spell+0xc6` is 2, or is 1 on a player with ability 51** (`0x475763`–`0x4757c4`): d100 against half the player word at `+0xc2`, capped at 97, and at or under it nothing is applied. Read as `TypeOfResists` and magic resistance (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Magic Resist (M.R.) and `TypeOfResists`*). Every damaging room spell in both sets has `TypeOfResists` 0, so none of them is resisted this way.
  - **The room's own spell is cast at no level** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL)*: `_room_cast_on_user` (`0x47572f`–`0x475948`) reads neither the spell's per-level bytes (`spell+0xf2` / `+0xf3`, `+0xf6` / `+0xf7`: `MaxInc` / `MaxIncLVLs`, `MinInc` / `MinIncLVLs`), nor its `Cap` (`spell+0xa2`), nor the player's level (`player+0x94`). Its callers are the periodic cast in `_medium_update_character` (`0x4228b4`), three sites in `_move_user` (`0x418822`, `0x418d72`, `0x419648`), and one each in `_add_experience` (`0x416b9b`), `_cmd_picklock` (`0x454ecf`) and `_cmd_disarm` (`0x468fbc`).
  - **A spell a textblock `cast`s is rolled at the character's own level** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL)*: `_perform_matched_action` (`0x470209`) runs the `cast` step as `_cast_no_target(spell, user, 1)` (`0x470334`), the routine a typed cast with no target uses, with the cast-success roll skipped for the flag (`0x44030e`–`0x440349`, `0x4405b7`). The level is the player's (`player+0x94`), lowered to the spell's `Cap` when that is above 0 (`0x4407bb`–`0x4407f0`); the max is `MaxBase + MaxInc × level / MaxIncLVLs` (`0x4407f3`–`0x440814`, `0x440853`) and the min `MinBase + MinInc × level / MinIncLVLs` (`0x44081e`–`0x44083f`, `0x440849`), each step left out when its `…LVLs` byte is 0; one value is rolled between them (`0x440860`–`0x44087f`). So ice fall #1142 (50 to 60, +4 / +7 a level, `Cap` 65), which the ice caverns and the cracked pit cast from their textblocks, grows with the character.
    - **The same on Paradigm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked whether a spell a room's text block casts (ice fall #1142) also grows with the character's level on Paradigm: "yes"; Realm: Paradigm)*. The settings tab keeps *more with level* on those rows.
  - **A monster's cast takes its level from the monster's attack slot** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL, `_monster_cast` `0x427cc3`)*: the word at `monster+0x148+slot×2` (`AttMax-N`, *Combat → Monster spell-attack damage — single cast, monster-owned energy*) multiplies the same two per-level bytes (`0x428191`–`0x4281f9`), no `Cap` is applied there, and slot −1 skips both steps. So one record does three things: chaos storm #212 (30 to 35, `MaxInc` 3 a level) is 30 to 35 as a room's spell, and more than that from monster #122 by its slot's cast level.

Only the spells set away from the default are stored, on the character tier beside the Health tab's rest settings.

  - **In such rooms the character heals and moves** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked whether a walk should stop and heal at some HP before going further into them: "it can heal and move, if healing spells configured")*. The rest-time heal (Settings → Health, *Heal (rest)*), which is otherwise cast only while resting, is cast standing while an HP rest is owed in such a room. The combat-time and emergency heals are unchanged. Nothing stops the walk to heal.
  - **A follower keeps following and asks in the next room it can rest in** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "yes")*: no `@wait` is sent from a barred room.
    - **Client policy:** a follower that comes into a barred room with a `@wait` already out (its deficit began in an ordinary room, the leader's wait window ran out and it walked on with the follower in tow), or under whom the room begins to bar, sends no second `@wait` there and releases the one that is out with `@ok`, as it does when Auto-Rest is switched off. The rest is owed for the next room that isn't barred, where the usual `@wait` goes out. (Before 2026-10-10 the room change re-sent `@wait` from inside the barred room and no `@ok` followed, so the party stood in the damage for the leader's whole wait window.)
  - **A rest given up because the room began to bar it runs no post-rest commands** (**Client policy**): the counter came off mid-rest, or the spell was ticked. Nothing was recovered, and the Post-rest chain (Settings → Health) is for a rest that ran its course.
  - Neither downtime rest is taken there: a follower beside a resting leader, a leader waited on by a member.
  - A loop's *rest up here* flag and a Rest-up event give way to it. Auto-Rest off and Sprint mode already rule resting out, and then nothing is deferred and the standing heal is not turned on.
  - (An earlier note asked whether a walk should stop and heal first and whether a follower should ask the leader to wait there; the user answered both 2026-10-10.)

- **Countered, the room is an ordinary room** (**Client policy**): a counter in effect makes the spell harmless to this character, and resting goes on as normal. How a counter has to be had follows from how it works: an item that negates the spell counts only while worn (*Movement & navigation → Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*); an item a textblock's `failitem` looks for counts while held, worn or not (*Movement & navigation → Room-spell hazard shape 2 — TextBlock action guarded by `failitem <itemNum>`*); a buff's source item counts while carried, since `AutoHazardCounterProvisioner` keeps the buff raised in those rooms (a lapse is not read). A room the client can't place on the map is rested in as before.

**Client use:**
- `RoomSpellDamageClassifier` reads each room spell of the active set into a `RoomSpellDamageReading` (class, damage range, share of casts, conditions, and the `RoomSpellDamageStage`s a timer ends in); `RoomSpellDamageIndex` holds them with their rooms and answers `BarsResting` from the stored choice or the class default. `AppServices.RoomSpellHurtingUs` is the spell on the current room when it bars resting (`RoomSpellBarsResting`) and `RoomHazardIndex.RoomHazard.IsCounteredNow` finds no counter in effect.
- `PeriodicDamageRoomSpellsSectionViewModel` is the Settings tab (`PeriodicDamageRoomSpellSettings.BarsResting` in the character's `Settings`); its room links go through `AppServices.NavigateToRoom`.
- `HealthManager.SetRoomSpellDamageProbe`: such a room skips both rest gates, HP and mana, like a do-not-rest room (`_skipRestDeferredRecovery` re-arms the rest on the room change), bars the opportunistic and leader-waited rests, and wins over `RestHereNow`. `RestDeferredByRoomSpell` / `HpRestDeferredByRoomSpell` say a rest is owed there; `CastingDirector.SetRestDeferredGate` reads the HP half as "resting" for the rest-time heal (`SelfHealPicker.Minor`).
- `HealthManager.NoteRoomChanged` settles a barred room on arrival, before its dragged-follower re-ask, and `Evaluate` releases a `@wait` that is out there. `HealthManager.NoteRoomPlacementChanged` (from `RoomTracker.StateChanged` when the room on either side isn't placed) asks again, so a rest put off for a room's spell doesn't stay owed after the room is left for one the map doesn't hold.
- The program log says once per room that a due rest is not being taken and why, where the put-off rest starts, and which spells a save in Settings changed; the bug report's *Combat weapon state* has a *Room spell and resting* line and the spells changed from the default.
- **A room spell's damage line is not a fight.** The test the round clock uses (`OffRoundDamageLines.IsOffRound`, *Timing & rounds → Combat round (5s) and the between-round cast cycle*) is handed, as `AppServices.IsRoomOrEffectDamage`, to everything that would take the line for a hit: `TickEngine` (no round), `CombatStateTracker.OnAnyCombatLine` (no in-combat flag, so no rest broken off in the bookkeeping and no swap to the fighting gear and back), `CombatManager.OnCombatLine` (no re-attack woken, no "room appears empty" Enter) and `RoundDamageTracker` (damage taken in a round already open, never a round of its own). Report `paradigm-20261009-120757`, 12:07:41 and 12:07:53: the heat in an empty room sent the Enter, put the client in combat and swapped gear twice.
  - **A monster in the room that casts the room's own spell as its attack makes the line a hit again:** `AppServices.MonsterHereCasts` (the room's roster against `MonsterCatalog`'s attack slots) is passed to `IsOffRound`, which then skips the room-spell match. The case in the data is chaos storm #212, the spell of seven Barley Fields rooms and a high druid's attack with the same text; the data summons the high druid elsewhere, so it is not known to happen.

### ShadowRest
*Status: CONFIRMED (user) · Realm: Paradigm (not present in stock)*

- **Some Paradigm races and classes have a ShadowRest ability; it is not a stock MajorMUD mechanic.** Resting with it doesn't break sneak or hide *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user: the flag can sit on the race or the class)*. In the imported game data it is **class-ability code 1103** on the Classes table (`AbilityNames` maps `1103 → "ShadowRest"`); a class row carrying that code in any `Abil-N` slot has the ability.
- **While hidden or sneaking, the character can `rest` (or meditate) and stay stealthed while resting in the room.** Monsters in the room **do not attack** the resting stealthed character. Normally a hostile in the room means you can't safely rest; ShadowRest lets a stealthed character rest right there without being engaged.
- **Some ShadowRest classes gain an HP-regen bonus while resting this way** (e.g. thief gets extra regen). The bonus is server-side.
- **No special messages mark the state.** The only observable sequence is a successful hide/sneak followed by `rest` — there is no "you shadow-rest" line. An `sn` sent while already resting is covered in *Movement & navigation → Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine* (*Sneaking and resting in place*).
- **Ideally used solo.** Resting while hidden un-targets you from party single-target heals/buffs (the same reason auto-hide is party-suppressed), so ShadowRest resting is a solo behavior.
- **Client use:**
  - The client's `RegenTracker` measures the actual regen rate off the stat line, so it needs no separate model of the bonus magnitude.
  - The client can't detect ShadowRest from the stream; it gates on the **class ability (code 1103) + the user setting** instead.

### Mana regeneration & the ManaRgn breakpoints
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 (against the engine's own reference formula); Stock re-checked against `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `_slow_update_character` / `_fast_update_character` 2026-09-28 · Realm: both (stock and Paradigm / GreaterMUD forms below)*

- **Passive (non-resting, non-meditating) mana regen ticks every 30 s (6 rounds)** and adds a whole-MP amount computed by one integer formula:

```
S (base stat) by magery type:  mage = INT ·  priest = WIL ·  druid = (INT + WIL) / 2 ·  bard = CHM ·  mystic = fixed 1
base = trunc( (level + 20) · S · (mageryLevel + 2) / 1650 )
tick = trunc( (ManaRgn% + 100) · base / 100 )        [stock]
tick = base + trunc( ManaRgn% · base / 100 )          [Paradigm / GreaterMUD — functionally equivalent for ManaRgn% ≥ 0; for a negative total they differ by 1, e.g. R=−31, b=5 → 3 on stock, 4 on Paradigm]
```

- **All four magery types, Bard included, use the same formula; only the stat differs** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, DLL jump table: type 1 INT, 2 WIL, 3 (INT+WIL)/2, 4 CHA; MMUD-Explorer has no realm split for any of them)*. The DLL reads the current stat values, the same ones `stat` shows.
- **`mageryLevel` is the class's magery tier (`Classes.MageryLVL`), a constant per class — NOT the character level.** It also drives max mana: `MaxMana = (mageryLevel · level · 2) + 6`. (A stock ability code 145 = "ManaRgn".)
- **`ManaRgn%` is the sum of every code-145 source** *(Stock [OBSERVED] 2026-09-28: `_update_dynamic_with_ability` adds code 145 to the character's mana-regen percent, as code 123 feeds the HP-regen percent)*. That is gear/quest `addability 145 N` bonuses (`+N ManaRgn`) **plus** a cast mana-regen roll spell's rolled magnitude. It is a **percent modifier on the tick, not flat mana**.
- **Breakpoints are emergent, not a table.** Because `tick` is truncated, it steps up by 1 MP only when `ManaRgn%` (or level / stat) crosses the integer threshold `(N·100/base − 100)`. Between thresholds, extra ManaRgn% does nothing.
- **Roll spells (nature tap / mana flux) carry a code-145 slot with stored value 0.** The magnitude is rolled per cast from the level-scaled range `Min/Max = base + trunc(inc/incLVLs · level)` (the same `SpellCalculator.AffectMagnitude` scaling every affect uses). So the worst roll = Min, best = Max, and the rolled value adds straight into `ManaRgn%`. This is why a reroll only helps when the range can cross a truncation breakpoint at the current level — otherwise it just burns mana.
- **Meditating** ticks every 15 s on both realms, and the meditate tick pays the unscaled `base`, leaving `ManaRgn%` out — see *Rest and meditate tick timing*. *(Previously a reverse-engineered 10 s model; settled 2026-09-27. Stock [OBSERVED] 2026-09-28: `_fast_update_character` pays the base every 15 fast ticks and never reads the regen percent; MMUD-Explorer skips `ManaRgn%` when meditating on both realms. Paradigm [OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, timed: a flat `+29` / `+30` across mana-regen totals from 70 to 360.)*
- **While meditating, every other meditate tick lands together with the 30 s natural tick**, so the jump you see is `base + natural` *(Stock [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user; Paradigm [OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, where it is exact because the meditate gains ride the mana grid)*.
- **The Paradigm standing tick, measured** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, timed log of a level 49–51 Priest whose mana-regen roll spell was recast through dozens of values with the gear held still)*: `trunc(base × (100 + ManaRgn%) / 100)` matched the full 30 s tick in all 141 combinations of level and mana-regen total seen five or more times (1,655 ticks, `ManaRgn%` 291 to 360), and every full tick within a combination was the same. `ManaRgn%` was the sum of the three values `abil 145` prints (`granted`, `worn`, `spells`). `base` was 29 at levels 49 and 50 and 30 at 51, which is `(level + 20) × WIL × 5 / 1650` with the Priest's Willpower of 140 *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-04, user: the character is level 51 with 140 Willpower)*: 71 × 140 × 5 / 1650 = 30.1 at level 51, and 29.3 and 29.7 at 49 and 50 for the same Willpower. So the level alone moved `base`, and the stat-side formula holds on Paradigm as written. The worn gear's ManaRgn summed to the `worn` value (240).
- **Unverified / modelled (not from the engine reference, don't hard-depend):**
  - the roll's *distribution* across `[Min,Max]` is treated as linear for "where on the range" purposes but is not proven uniform;
  - whether the live engine caps summed ManaRgn% is unknown. (Paradigm showed no cap up to 360 — the measured ticks above.)
- **Client use:**
  - `CharacterCalculator.CalcManaRegen` implements the formula; the Level Projection grid already relies on it.
  - The mana-regen breakpoint calculator uses only the CONFIRMED passive formula above.

### Rerolling a mana-regen roll spell
*Status: per-fact tags below (CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 user + screenshot; 2026-08-30 report `paradigm-20260830-110918`; 2026-09-09 user) · Realm: both (reading the roll differs by realm)*

- **Only roll spells are reroll candidates** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-08-28, user + screenshot)*. That means nature tap / mana flux / `prfl`, and kin — code-145 with stored value 0. A bad roll drags `ManaRgn%` down, so re-cast to chase a better one.
- **`CHSU` (chaos surge) is NEVER rerolled.** It's a *constant* mana heal-over-time (the mana analogue of HP regen), not a rolled `ManaRgn%` modifier; maintain it like a normal buff. A fixed (non-zero) code-145 spell isn't rerolled either. (`RegenSpellClassifier` already splits roll / fixed / HoT.)
- **Mana-regen roll spells are self-only casts** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-09, user)*. Mana flux and its kin **cannot be cast on others**; the caster always receives the roll whenever the slot fires.
- **The rolled value can be negative** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-08-30, report `paradigm-20260830-110918` — mana flux rolled `spells: -31`)*. So a "reroll below 0" gate is a normal setting: it chases any non-negative roll.
- **A roll spell confirms via the shared `ManaRegenerating` condition, not a spell-specific applied message** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-08-30, report `paradigm-20260830-110918`)*. So the applied-line path can't map the landing back to the specific spell (#406).
- **Reading the roll — Paradigm:** send **`abil 145`**. The output is three lines for `ManaRegen(145)`:

  ```
  granted: N      (innate)
  worn:    N      (gear/quest +ManaRgn bonuses)
  spells:  N      (what the mana-regen spell ROLLED — this is the value we gate on)
  ```

  The **`spells:` value** is the rolled magnitude (e.g. a priest's `prfl` rolling 32). Reroll if `spells:` < the min gate.
- **Reading the roll — Stock:** there is **no `abil 145`**, so the roll is read back off the next natural mana tick, using the formula in *Mana regeneration & the ManaRgn breakpoints* *(design 2026-09-28, from the Stock DLL and MMUD-Explorer)*:
  - The tick is truncated, so it pins the roll to a **band** (every roll that pays exactly that tick), e.g. base 12 and tick 18 → roll 50..58. Worn `ManaRgn%` is subtracted using the gear the client sees.
  - **Meditating:** a jump equal to the base is the meditate tick alone; a bigger one is `base + natural` (they share a prompt every other meditate tick).
  - **A tick that fills the pool** was cut short and is skipped.
  - **Gear-set swaps:** the gear-dependent inputs (worn `ManaRgn%` and INT / WIL / CHA) are taken from the gear worn when the tick lands. The `stat` screen's stats are corrected by the stat bonuses of the gear worn when it was read, and a tick within 3 s of a worn-list change is skipped *(**Client policy**, user 2026-09-28: a mana-regen gear set should raise the tick)*.
  - **A roll so bad the natural tick pays 0 shows no jump.** No natural tick within 40 s of the cast, with mana below max, reads as a 0 tick.
  - **Decision** *(**Client policy**, user 2026-09-28)*: the threshold is the **rolled percent on both realms**. Stock rerolls only when the whole band is below it; a band straddling it counts as good.
  - *(An earlier design judged Stock on a desired mana tick instead; superseded 2026-09-28. Saved Stock tick thresholds convert once to the smallest roll that pays that tick — **Client policy**, user 2026-09-28.)*
- **Client use:**
  - **Config per roll-spell slot:** a **max rerolls per cycle** and a **minimum gate**. Cast → read the roll → if below the gate, re-queue and repeat until at/above the gate or max attempts hit; then stop and wait for the spell's normal recast-within window before trying the cycle again.
  - **Self-only matching:** the reroll engine must NOT gate on a "cast on self" flag (a user can leave a slot's default whole-party flag on; the spell still only lands on the caster). `ManaRegenRerollSlot` therefore matches any configured roll-spell slot regardless of its target flags.
  - **Trigger timing:** the reroll cycle keys off the **cast** (we know what we cast), not the applied-line confirm: after the cast reaches the wire, send `abil 145` and read the fresh roll. Keying it on the confirm meant it never fired at all.
  - **Running out of mana mid-cycle PAUSES, it does not surrender** *(2026-09-01, report `paradigm-20260901-114223`: the reroller quit at 3/20 when a recast would breach the mana floor, stranding the spell at a bad roll)*. Each recast costs mana, so if the next one would drop under the buff mana floor the cycle SUSPENDS with its reroll counter intact and resumes the next attempt once meditation lifts mana back over the floor — so it spends its full reroll budget across rest instead of abandoning a bad roll at the floor.
  - **Built — Paradigm:** `ManaRegenReroller` sends `abil 145`, parses the `spells:` slice, rerolls below the per-slot threshold up to its cap.
  - **Built — Stock:** `ManaRegenReroller.OnManaTickObserved` / `JudgeNaturalTick` read the band via `ManaRegenBreakpointCalculator.RollsForTick`, from a `StockManaRollContext` that AppServices builds (level, stats, magery, worn ManaRgn%, the roll range, the meditate tick). `OnRecoveryTick` handles the 0-tick timeout. `AppServices.ConvertLegacyStockRerollThreshold` does the one-time conversion (`BuffSlot.RerollThresholdIsRoll`).

### Looking at a monster — coarse wound bands
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **`look <monster>` reveals a wound band, never a number.** The game only ever states the condition as one of **eight coarse wound bands**.
- **Monster look vs player look.** A player look prints a bracketed `[ Name ]` header and ends `He is unwounded.`; a **monster** look has **no header** — the monster's name is the first response line, prose follows, and the **last line** is `(It|He|She) appears to be <wound>.`. The `appears to be` phrasing is monster-exclusive (players read `is unwounded`), so it never false-matches a player look. The server echoes the typed command as its own content line (`look ca`) ahead of the name.
- **Each band is a fixed percentage window of the monster's max HP** (from game data), so `max HP × band` gives an absolute HP range. Validated live: a **70-HP cave worm** reading **heavily wounded** was **35–48 HP** (actual 38). Bands, percentage of max HP, lower bound inclusive:

  | Descriptor | % of max HP | 70-HP cave worm |
  |---|---|---|
  | unwounded | = 100 (full) | 70 |
  | slightly wounded | [85, 100) | 60–69 |
  | moderately wounded | [70, 85) | 49–59 |
  | heavily wounded | [50, 70) | 35–48 |
  | severely wounded | [30, 50) | 21–34 |
  | critically wounded | [20, 30) | 14–20 |
  | very critically wounded | (0, 20) | 1–13 |
  | mortally wounded | ≤ 0 (dead/dying) | ≤0 |

- **On Stock a monster never reads "mortally wounded"** *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p monster-look routine; [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*. The engine computes `pct = HP·100/max` (truncated) and checks only `< 20` very critically, `< 30` critically, `< 50` severely, `< 70` heavily, `< 85` moderately, `< 100` slightly, else unwounded. So 0 HP or below still reads **very critically wounded**. "Mortally wounded" is player-side wording (e.g. the `You may not do that while you are mortally wounded!` refusal).
- **Band → HP range.** For a band `[lo, hi)`: `Low = ceil(lo·M/100)`, `High = ceil(hi·M/100) − 1` — exactly the integer HP values that read as that band.
- **Why the range is worth having.** Against a **high-HP boss with fast regen / self-heal**, the per-round scroll outpaces any attempt to tally HP by counting damage lines, so the wound band is the only reliable read of where the boss's "HP gate" sits.
- **Client use:**
  - Implemented in `MonsterLookParser` → status-bar `TGT HP: min-max [~best guess]` and a terminal line `[<name>: <max> HP, <band>: min-max, ~<best guess>]` with the band shortened (Full / Slight / Mod / Hvy / Sev / Crit / V.Crit, user 2026-09-29); the best guess is `MonsterHpTracker`'s running estimate, pulled into the band (see *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster HP regen*).
  - Name→HP resolution goes through `RoomEntityClassifier.ResolveLookedMonsterNumber`, which prefers the monster variant actually in the room so shared names / adjective prefixes resolve to the right HP.

---

## Combat

How a fight runs on the wire: announcing and repeating attacks, what breaks combat, the attack-spell cascade, weapons and backstab, how monsters decide whom to attack, and how kills are recognised and attributed. Also covers the client's per-monster auto-combat overrides.

### Attack announce lines and round commits
*Status: CONFIRMED (user); room-spell and poised lines CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 (user)*

- **Any normal attack against an NPC is announced publicly.** The attacker sees `*Combat Engaged*`; everyone else in the room sees `<player> moves to attack <target>.` (the client's `moves to attack` regex requires the trailing period).
- **A backstab round is silent.** It emits no `moves to attack` line to other players, so the surprise opener doesn't tip off onlookers. The client therefore can't confirm its own backstab landed from a `moves to attack` echo (there won't be one); it uses the `surprise` swing line instead (see *Backstab*).
- **A round action is announced by ONE of two lines, melee OR spell.** A party member has "gone" for the round when the room shows *either* `<player> moves to attack <target>.` (melee/ranged) *or* `<player> moves to cast <spell name> upon <target>.` (a combat spell). Both count as that member's announce; a caster's turn produces the second form only.
- *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-21, user)* **A ROOM spell announces as `<player> moves to attack everyone in the room.`** — the melee "moves to attack" form with the wildcard target `everyone in the room`, NOT the single-target `moves to cast … upon …` form. Rooming is always a spell cast; physical attacks can't AoE. It matches the `moves to attack` regex with `target = "everyone in the room"` — a room-wide commit rather than a specific mob.
- **Paradigm-only: `<player> is poised to assault the room!`** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-21, user)* is shown when we ENTER a room where someone is ALREADY room-spelling: they've committed to rooming and the combat round hasn't fired yet. **Stock does not emit this line.** It is the "already-active roomer" counterpart to the fresh `moves to attack everyone in the room` commit.
- **An attack on a player tells the victim `<attacker> moves to attack you!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-05, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p, Stock; [CONFIRMED] the same day by the user for Paradigm too: the same line)*
  - A weapon attack (`_attack_user_user` @ `0x42bd26`): the victim gets that line, the rest of the room `<attacker> moves to attack <victim>!`, ending in `!`.
  - An attack spell aimed at a player (`_cast_user_target` @ `0x444712`): the victim gets the same line, the room `<attacker> moves to attack <victim>.`, ending in `.` like the announce for a monster.
  - Every caller of `_attack_user_user` passes its announce flag set (`_cmd_any_attack` @ `0x451090`, and both calls in `_restart_autocombat` @ `0x44c167`), so on Stock a player's attack on a player is always announced; the silent backstab round above is the monster-target path.
  - Other lines a victim of a spell can see: `<attacker> attempted to cast <spell> on you, but failed.` and `You resisted <attacker>'s <spell>.`
- **What Stock checks when an attack on a monster is typed, in order** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_any_attack` @0x451090, `_attack_user_monster` @0x42cfab; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  1. afraid: `You are too afraid!` (@0x4510ef; *Spells, buffs & conditions → Fear*);
  2. the target lookup (*Shared monster names — attacks and looks take the first*); an ambiguous result prints the "be more specific" list and stops, and no match makes the line "not a command" (*Attacking a monster that isn't in the room*);
  3. resting, meditating and the just-entered state are cleared, and hidden and sneaking too unless the attack is a backstab (@0x451370–0x4513a1);
  4. a `Protected` room (and not a sysop): the room's own text when it has one, else `You are overcome with a feeling of guilt and break off your attack.` (@0x4513a2–0x4513f5). The same refusal meets an attack on a player and a spell cast at a monster (`_cast_monster_target` @0x4473d0);
  5. `*Combat Off*` if already fighting, and the running attack is dropped (@0x4513fa–0x45141c);
  6. a Good or Lawful Good monster not already tied to you: the evil-points step, which can refuse (@0x42d15b; *Character stats & progression → How your alignment moves during play*);
  7. a monster carrying ability 158: `You are not using the required weapon to hit this monster!` unless the wielded weapon carries ability 158 with the same value; bare hands always fail (@0x42d1f4–0x42d219). The spell form is `You are not using the required spell to hit this monster!` (`_cast_monster_target` @0x447427). Nine monsters and five items in the 1.11p data carry it;
  8. the guard redirect (*Guarded monsters redirect attacks*);
  9. the hit-magic lines (*Weapons: "no effect" lines and the magical-weapon requirement*);
  10. `*Combat Engaged*`, the room's `moves to attack` line unless it is a backstab, the attacker's energy set to 0 (@0x42d4e3) and the attack queued for the round.
  - **Nothing swings at the command.** The first swing is at the next round, after the round has given the character its energy back (@0x421358); a round that finds less than a round's worth of energy queues the attack again without swinging (@0x42d04c–0x42d0a0).
  - **A refusal at steps 6 to 9 comes after step 5**, so attacking a monster you can't hit while fighting another leaves you out of combat: `*Combat Off*`, the refusal, and no `*Combat Engaged*`.

**Client use:**
- `PvpAttackWatcher` reads `<attacker> moves to attack you!` (`KnownPatterns.PlayerAttacksYou`) as an attack on us on a realm with PvP enabled, with a damage line that leads with a known player's name as the backstop. What it does about it is under *Damage lines* (the room-spell Client policy).
- Attack-last coordination (waiting until every other member has committed before our own `*Combat Engaged*` lands) must treat the melee and spell announce lines as equivalent per-member signals — keying only on `moves to attack` misses every spellcaster in the party.
- A `moves to attack everyone in the room` line counts as that member's round commit against the whole room, our target included. Never follow "everyone in the room" as a literal monster (there is no such mob).
- `<player> is poised to assault the room!` is also treated as a room commit for attack-last (we cast our room spell after the poised member, so ours lands last).

### Attack command words
*Status: `aa` rule CONFIRMED 2026-10-09 (user; no realm given); the rest [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`) · Realm: Stock for the DLL bullets*

- **`aa` is the bash command, in both of its uses** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "if aa is used to bash a door, there is nothing to stop, if aa is used to bash attack a NPC, break can stop it")*.
  - Used on a door, a bash is a single action with nothing to break off (the door form is in *Movement & navigation → Locked doors — picking, opening and bashing*).
  - Used on a monster or NPC, it is a bash attack: ongoing combat that `break` stops (*`break` — stopping an announced attack*).
- **On Stock `aa` parses to the same command as `bash`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_parse_command` @0x40e507 gives command 88 for `aa`, and entry 88 of the dispatcher (@0x413a1c) is `_cmd_bash`; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The other spellings of each attack word are in *Wire, prompt & command output → Command words and abbreviations*.
- **What each attack word starts on Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_attack` @0x451501–0x45155a, `_cmd_bash` @0x451d17–0x451d9d, `_cmd_smash` @0x45168f–0x4516d8, `_cmd_backstab` @0x451616; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. Each sets an attack type before the shared attack routine: 1 punch, 2 kick, 3 jumpkick, 4 backstab, 5 normal, 6 bash, 7 smash.
  - **`a <target>`** is a normal attack. Bare-handed with the Punch ability (29) it is a punch, and a backstab when sneaking or hidden: the same rule *Backstab* records for `pu`.
  - **`aa <name>` / `bash <name>`**, when the argument is not taken as a door bash (*Movement & navigation → Locked doors — picking, opening and bashing*), is the bash attack. It needs the bash ability (31) and a weapon in hand. The two refusal lines, and what a direction word aimed at no door does, are recorded with the door form (the *`bash <dir>` at an exit that is not a door* entry of that topic). The 1.11p `Classes` table lists ability 31 on fifteen classes, so for most characters the refusal that bites is the weapon one.
  - **`smash <name>`** needs ability 32, else `You don't know the first thing about smashing!`.
  - **`bs <name>`**: see *Backstab*.
- **A bare attack word attacks the last target again** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_any_attack` @0x451447–0x4514a9, `_cmd_bash` @0x451726–0x451759, `_restart_autocombat` @0x44c167; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The engine keeps each character's last target, attack type and spell after the fight ends: ending combat only takes the character off the round queue.
  - Bare `a` prints `*Combat Off*` if a fight was running and then re-attacks the remembered target with the remembered type, when the remembered action was a weapon attack (a remembered spell is ignored without a line). Bare `aa` / `bash` does the same with no `*Combat Off*`.
  - The remembered monster is no longer in the room: `You don't see your target here!` A remembered player is in another room, or hidden from you: `You do not see <name> here!` Nothing remembered: nothing is printed.
- **`kill` is not an attack on Stock.** `kil` and `kill` parse to a command whose handler does nothing and reports "not a command" (`_cmd_killblow` @0x451673; `tame` and `mesmerize` are the same kind of dead command, `_cmd_tame` @0x4528e3, `_cmd_mesmerize` @0x4528ea). The line then goes the way of any unrecognised one, so `kill rat` is spoken in talk fast (*Attacking a monster that isn't in the room*).

**Client use:**
- **One table, `AttackCommandWords`, is what the client takes for an attack word** (attack, bash under all its names, backstab, smash, the three strikes with `pur` / `purg`; and `break`). It is Stock's table on both realms, Paradigm's not being on record. Its two readers:
  - `OutboundAttackObserver`: a typed attack word is the user taking the round's attack.
  - `OutboundBreakObserver`: the user's attack ends their break hold (*`break` — stopping an announced attack*).
  - **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-10: "au, allout, force aren't used by players and i think never made it to anything in game that players can use. but it should be using the same list as the break hold.")*: both read the same list. `au`, `al`…`allout` and `forc` / `force` stay in it because the parser takes them; nothing depends on a player using them.
  - (Until 2026-10-10 `OutboundAttackObserver` had a list of its own: `a`, `at`, `att`, `aa`, `bash`, `sma`, `smash`, `bs`. The table's other spellings, `atta`…`attack`, `au`, `bas`, `smas`, `backs`…`backstab`, `al`…`allout`, `forc`, `force` and the strikes, were not in it.)
  - `sm` is not counted: smash starts at `sma` and `sm` is no command (*Wire, prompt & command output → Command words and abbreviations*); before 2026-10-09 it was in the list.
- A direction after the bash command (`bash`, `aa`, and its other names) is the door on that exit, not an attack (*Movement & navigation → Locked doors — picking, opening and bashing*).
- **A line that is a text exit of the room the character stands in is a move, not an attack, whatever its first word** (`Room.HasExitCommand`, asked by both readers; since 2026-10-10). `jump` is a spelling of jumpkick in the table, and rooms have text exits that start with it *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, game data)*: Stock 1.11p has one, room 8/559 (`go moat, dive moat, jump moat`); Paradigm 1.9.1 has about a dozen (`jump pool` on 15/1031 and 16/2632, `jump hole`, `jump down`, `jump boulder`, `jump pillar`, …). Typed there, or sent there by the walker, such a line neither takes the round nor lifts a break hold. Anywhere else, and with any other argument, the word is the jumpkick it spells.

### Player attack order and "Attack last"
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-28 (user) · Realm: both*

- **Player attack order = announce order, FIFO.** Players deal their damage in the order they engaged/announced their attacks — first to announce fires first. Party rank does NOT change this order.
- **Backstab is pre-emptive.** A successful backstab always resolves **first**, ahead of the normal order.
- **"Attack last" (client setting) therefore does two independent things:**
  - Resolves your action at the **end** of the round's order — the **mana/energy save**. In a party that *usually but not always* one-rounds a mob, a spellcaster set to attack last casts last, so if the mob is already dead its spell has no target and **never fires — energy/mana saved**; it only spends when the mob survives to the caster's slot.
  - **Raises** your monster-targeting odds (a positive modifier) (Paradigm: score modifier; Stock: lock re-point — see *Monster target selection — who it swings at once fighting*) — useful for a tank drawing aggro, a cost for a squishy caster.

**Client use:**
- **Attack-last re-fire waits for the announces to go quiet** (`CombatManager.ScheduleAttackOrderRefire`, `RefireSettle` 500 ms; **Client policy**). Party announces arrive on separate lines, and a member reacting to someone else's announce (an attack-after, another attack-last) lands a few hundred ms later, so the re-fire goes out once, after the last of them. Every qualifying announce that lands after ours is answered, with no per-round cap (user, 2026-09-28): party members for attack-last-party, anyone for attack-last-room. It used to fire on the next dispatch turn with a cap of one, which left an attack-after member swinging behind an attack-last one (user report, 2026-09-28).
- **An announce read before our last attack was answered isn't answered** (`CombatManager.ScheduleAttackOrderRefire`, `RefireAnswerWindow` 2 s; report `paradigm-20261013-153710`). The game prints lines in the order it handles commands, and answers each attack command with `*Combat Engaged*` (*Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)*), so an announce printed ahead of that answer was handled ahead of our attack, which already lands after it. Another MudPlay member's own re-fire crosses ours this way on every fight, and answering it was a third attack each time. An announce after our answer is still answered. The window lets a refused attack, which gets no `*Combat Engaged*`, stop blocking re-fires.

### Spell attacks auto-repeat; re-announcing a single-target spell is harmless
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-05 (user); stop conditions and re-announce rule CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 (user) · Realm: both*

- **A spell attack command AUTO-REPEATS server-side every round, exactly like a weapon swing — on ALL realms.** You announce the spell once (type its cast-code + target); the next combat tick it fires, and it keeps firing each round while the target is present and mana suffices, with NO re-announcing. A spell attack is functionally identical to a physical attack — announce once, the server repeats it; the client adds its own gates (`MinManaPerCast`, `MaxCasts`, `MinEnemies`). See also *Timing & rounds → Combat spells: engaged once, auto-repeat per round*.
- **The auto-repeat stops on** *(2026-09-21, user)*: `break`; moving rooms; the room clearing; the target dying (single-target); or any non-swing action (a cast or an equip) with its `*Combat Off*` (see *Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)*).
- **Re-announcing a SINGLE-TARGET spell the server is already repeating is HARMLESS — it costs no mana and does NOT double-fire** *(2026-09-21, user)*. Mana is spent **each time the spell fires**, not when it is announced *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*: a 500-energy spell that fires twice in a round costs its mana ×2; if the target dies before the second fire, that cast never goes out and its mana isn't spent. The announce itself is free. Re-typing the cast-code (e.g. `fbal`) just re-postures the same auto-repeat: the server still fires it once that round (or, if mana is short that round, postures without firing and tries again next round).
- **This corrects an earlier note** that claimed re-announcing "double-fires / wastes mana" — it does not, for a single-target spell.
- **What an attack command sent during a fight prints**, a repeat of the running one included, is in *Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)* (the *A new attack command sent while a fight is running* bullet).
- **Room spells are the exception — do NOT re-send one while it is channeling** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-23, report `paradigm-20260923-103938`)*: re-sending the same room spell breaks the running channel and starts a fresh one, wasting the round (see *Room-attack spells: cast bare, persistent channel*). This newer rule supersedes the 2026-09-21 "harmless" note for room spells.
- **The hazard for a single-target spell is targeting, not mana.** Re-announcing a **single-target** spell at a mob that just died would re-aim at the corpse. A **room spell is cast bare** — no target — so it has no corpse hazard, but it still must not be re-sent while channeling.

**Client use:**
- The client CAN safely re-announce a single-target combat spell for ordering purposes — this is how **attack-last** works for a caster: re-announcing our attack after the party's commits re-posts our action so it lands last, with no extra mana cost. A room spell must not be re-sent while it is channeling. The single-target re-announce guards on the target still being our live current target.
- The client re-announces when the best action must change, AND for attack-last ordering:
  - **Target dies** → announce at the next target.
  - **`MaxCasts` rounds elapsed** → switch to the next cascade action. Scope: **per-target** for the single-target slots (normal / alternate attack spell, single-target debuff); **per-room** for the two AoE slots (multi-attack, area debuff).
  - **Attack-last re-fire** → re-announce our current action after a party member's round commit, so ours lands last (a harmless re-posture for a single-target spell; never re-send a channeling room spell).

### Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)
