- The block clears on room change, on a target-not-here / no-effect reply, or when a room re-display no longer lists the priority (`CombatManager.JudgeGuardBlockByRoster`). A kill can't clear it: a guard's death and the priority's both reach the client as exp + `*Combat Off*` (*Kill detection and monster-kill message order*), so a kill while the block stands asks for the room (`CombatManager.NoteUnattributedDeath`, even inside the 3 s re-display cooldown once the last re-display has been read) and its re-display decides. While that re-display is coming (sent for this kill, or sent earlier and not read yet), the guard retry waits for a room read newer than the kill, for at most 2 s (`GuardKillJudgeWait`); a one-shot timer then sends the retry, since no further `*Combat Off*` may come. With none coming (a dark room) the retry goes out at once, as before: in the dark the kill's roster removal drops the priority's slot whichever of them died, so the client roster can't tell, and a retry at a corpse is cleared by its "You don't see" reply.
  - **A room the kill emptied has no `Also here:` line in its re-display** (the `ForceAoeMultiKillReparse` note, report `paradigm-20260827-081208`), so `JudgeGuardBlockByRoster` never hears of it. A display that finishes after the kill with no `Also here:` read since it (`CombatManager.NoteRoomDisplayed`) ends the block.
  - (Until 3.183.24 the block cleared on the priority's death line, which was retired with the rest.)
- Without this, killing the last guard emits a *Combat Off* with the chief alive but unengaged, and auto-combat stalls until the user manually attacks (`aa b`) — the reported symptom.

### Monster `Align` values and your alignment-title ladder
*Status: `Align` values CONFIRMED (matches `LookupEnums.MonAlignmentNames`); band thresholds CONFIRMED by user 2026-09-27 (Paradigm help screen) and [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p (Stock) · Realm: both, Fiend's threshold differs*

- **Monster `Align` values** (the Monsters-table `Align` column, int 0–6): `0` Good · `1` Evil · `2` Chaotic Evil · `3` Neutral · `4` Lawful Good · `5` Neutral Evil · `6` Lawful Evil.
- **Your alignment-title ladder** (good → evil, from the who column): Saint → Good → Neutral → **Seedy → Outlaw → Criminal → Villain → Fiend**. The last five (Seedy and worse) are the **"Evil bucket."**
- **Your alignment is a number — evil points (EP): negative is good, positive is evil.** Each title covers a range; the published numbers are where the title changes over *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user, from Paradigm's alignment help screen; Stock [OBSERVED] in `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p's band function, EP a signed 16-bit value)*:

  | Title | Paradigm | Stock |
  |---|---|---|
  | Saint | -201 and below | -201 and below |
  | Good | -200 to -51 | -200 to -51 |
  | Neutral | -50 to 29 | -50 to 29 |
  | Seedy | 30 to 39 | 30 to 39 |
  | Outlaw | 40 to 79 | 40 to 79 |
  | Criminal | 80 to 119 | 80 to 119 |
  | Villain | 120 to 299 | 120 to 209 |
  | Fiend | 300 and up | 210 and up |

  (An earlier note gave single values `Saint -201 · Good -100 · Neutral 0 · Seedy 40 · Outlaw 80 · Criminal 120 · Villain 180 · Fiend 300`, CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 from capture `paradigm-20260827-144553`; superseded 2026-09-27 — they weren't the thresholds.)
- **Saint isn't reached in normal play.** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user.)* A sysop has to enable or award it; players normally cap at -200, Good. Stock's own drift toward good stops at -200 (see *Character stats & progression → How your alignment moves during play*), and the DLL's `You will have to complete a quest to regain your Saint status.` points the same way.
- **The ladder is otherwise the same on Stock and Paradigm** — Paradigm shows your exact number where Stock shows just the band title.
- **"Lawful" is NOT its own band.** It's a user-set flag that forbids the character from ever committing evil acts, and it's treated as **Good** for all alignment math. *(An earlier note gave it Good's value as -100; the Good band is -200 to -51.)*
- **Lawful is permanent.** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user.)* A lawful character can't engage in evil acts and can never shed the flag — only rerolling a new character gets rid of it.
- **The finer evil titles (Villain / Fiend) matter mainly for item-equip gating** on items in that range — a separate system from the exit gate.
- **Gear uses its own buckets:** on Stock, Seedy wears gear as Neutral (see *Items, inventory & equipment → Item wear restrictions (ability-code flags)*). The "Evil bucket" above is for aggro.

**Client use:**
- `AlignmentBucket` collapses the ladder to Good / Neutral / Evil for item filtering (`ItemEquipFilter.GearBucketForWord`: Seedy → Neutral on Stock); the criminal / guard layer needs the finer title.
- `AlignmentBands` keeps one value per title — where it takes over — for the exit gates; only their order matters there.

### Monster aggression — who opens on you unprovoked
*Status: CONFIRMED (Layer 1 alignment auto-aggro; Layer 2 criminal/guard behaviour; guard identification)*

- **A monster is hostile (attacks without being engaged first) as a function of the monster's `Align` and your character's alignment title.** Two independent layers stack.
- **Layer 1 — alignment auto-aggro (every monster, straight from `Align`):**
  - `Align` **1 / 2 / 5** (Evil / Chaotic Evil / Neutral Evil) — **opens on everyone**, every title.
  - `Align` **0 / 3** (Good / Neutral) — **never** aggros anyone.
  - `Align` **6** (Lawful Evil) — "honor among the wicked": opens on **Saint / Good / Neutral / Seedy** and spares **Outlaw and worse** *(Stock [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p monster pass, [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*. The engine checks your EP, not the title bucket: a monster already fighting you keeps going, otherwise it skips you at **EP ≥ 40**. The separate free-attack path (a swing at you as you move) uses **EP ≥ 80** (Criminal and worse); that path is the parting attack in *Movement & navigation → Refused ("bonked") moves*, the order of checks. *(An earlier note said it spared Seedy and asked about Saint; superseded 2026-09-27.)* **The same on Paradigm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*.
  - `Align` **4** (Lawful Good) — **never aggros by alignment**; the only Align-4 aggro is the guard subset via Layer 2.
  - So the only alignment-driven aggro that depends on *your* alignment is Align-6 (spares Outlaw+); 1/2/5 are unconditional, 0/3/4 never bite on alignment alone.
- **Layer 2 — criminal / guard system** (the guard subset of Align 4; runtime reputation, NOT in the monster table). Keyed on **your title**, enforced by **guard** NPCs plus special actors:

| Your title | Guards | Extra actors |
|---|---|---|
| Saint / Good / Neutral *(a Saint, where one exists, is treated like Good — [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)* | ignore | — |
| Seedy | ignore | bad deeds done *to* you are ignored (you lose guard protection, but guards don't aggro) |
| Outlaw | **attack on sight**, but spare your life | — |
| Criminal | **slay on sight** | — |
| Villain | **slay** | bounty hunters also attack |
| Fiend | **slay** | bounty hunters + archons / gods smite you with lightning |

- **Identifying a guard from imported data.** The game's monster-`Type` field distinguishes an ordinary NPC from a law-enforcing *guard*, but that distinction is **not exported into the MDB we import** — the imported `Type` only carries Solo / Leader / Follower / Stationary (0–3), never the guard value. So guard-ness can't be read off the type.
  - **The reliable proxy:** a monster that **casts spell 583 (`jail`)** is a guard, and it attacks us when our title is **Outlaw or worse**. Detection = the monster references spell `583` in any of its castable-spell fields (`AttHitSpell-*`, `MidSpell-*`, `DeathSpell`, `CreateSpell`).
  - In the shipped set that flags the guardsmen (#13/#14/#905/#538), Sheriff Lionheart (#40), and elite guardsman (#757).
  - **The engine's own marker is the monster's group:** group 5 is named `Guard` and group 37 `Angel` in the DLL, and neither is in the MDB (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*; [OBSERVED] 2026-10-03, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p and `wccknms2.dat`, Stock). Group 5 holds Sheriff Lionheart, Templar and elite guardsman, but also the woodelves, storm giants and Pastor Lander; group 37 holds guardsman and bounty hunter. *[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]: whether group membership, rather than the `jail` spell, is what makes a monster attack the evil-titled.*
  - This is a **partial** list — other mobs aggro the evil-titled without casting `jail` (e.g. Templar is a guard yet has no `jail`); those get added here as they're recognised.
- **A monster that opens on you unprovoked is an enemy, not a neutral** — e.g. storm giants. The client models those as the `Enemy` relationship (see *Neutral monsters and kill-on-sight*).

**Client use:**
- **Hostile-in-room test.** For each monster in the room, read its `Align`: hostile if `Align ∈ {1,2,5}` (always), or `Align == 6` and our title is Seedy or better, or the monster is a **guard** (casts `jail` 583 — the guard proxy in this topic) **and** our title is Outlaw-or-worse. Our own title comes from the stat screen / who line (`AlignmentTracker` / `PlayerStats`).

### Neutral monsters and kill-on-sight
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-15 (user)*

- **A neutral monster never attacks you on sight / never attacks first.** "Neutral" here means any monster that doesn't open on you (see *Monster aggression — who opens on you unprovoked*), not only `Align` 3. It attacks **only if you've attacked it** and it's still alive — and once provoked it **keeps attacking every round until it dies**, even if you `break` and sit there.
- **So a room of un-engaged neutrals is safe to rest in.** The moment you engage one, *that* one is hitting you back (no resting mid-fight), but the others stay passive until you turn on them.
- **A monster that *does* open on you unprovoked is an enemy, not a neutral** — e.g. storm giants; see *Monster aggression — who opens on you unprovoked*.

**Client use:**
- The per-monster overlay `Relationship` (`Enemy` / `Neutral` / `Friend` / `Flee` / `Hangup`) drives auto-combat. `Enemy` = engage on sight; `Neutral` = leave alone.

The sighting stays open, and the roster issued when the fight ends (`PvpFight.ActiveChanged` posts `RoomEntityClassifier.ReemitCurrent`) or when the Enemy leaves is answered then. Once the room is confirmed, a re-display or an arrival resolves against the room stood in. No shipped overlay seed sets `Hangup`.

(An earlier note said `Flee` had no response of its own and nothing started a run from a `Flee` monster; superseded 2026-10-09.) It is a client response only: nothing here says how either monster behaves in the game.

What came of it is reported as a `FleeOutcome`.

An engine held by a fight or a rest is running. Only this flee asks: the low-HP, hit-and-run and PvP flees take a paused engine over as before.

And *(user, 2026-10-10)*: "if we dont have flee backwards on (the checkbox text is: go backwards if running) we should flee forward and the loop wont get stuck... if we have it on we will just keep bouncing and its something the user needs to fix themselves." No guard is built. A walk-to whose destination is the monster's room bounces the same way with the box ticked.

A walk already re-planned to its destination from where any run landed (`AutoWalkManager.ResumeAfterRecovery`). Unchanged: a hit-and-run, a failed backstab's run and a PvP flee (`FleeFromPlayer`) walk a loop back to the room they left whichever way they ran (`LoopRunner.StartFleeReturn`, report `paradigm-20260929-221352`), and so does every run made `Backward`. (An earlier note here marked the user's "it'll skip forward over the room" as in conflict with the loop walking back after any flee; settled 2026-10-10.)
  - **A forward run starts with the next step, not the one just walked.** `IRecoverableEngine.PeekPlannedDirections` leaves out the step at the engine's index when its move has landed and the index has not been advanced, which is how it stands whenever the engine was paused before the arrival (a fight in the room, or a flee held for that move and started as it confirms: `HealthManager.NoteRoomChanged` runs ahead of the engines' own arrival handlers). `LoopRunner.InFlightStepHasLanded`; the same test in `AutoWalkManager.PeekPlannedDirections`. Before 2026-10-10 a forward flee from a room entered that way set off with the direction it had come in by. A later leg of the same run, planned while a flee already holds the engine, starts after the step that leads into the room the tracker stands in (`LoopRunner.FirstStepLeadingTo`; the walker looks down its own path), since the earlier legs walked steps the index knows nothing of.
  - **A flee ends when it is cut off** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: "this needs to be fixed before it merges. if we died, the flee needs to end". `HealthManager.EndFlee` clears every piece of flee state and logs one `[Health]` Info line with the reason. It is called on `RoomTracker.PlayerDeathObserved` ("died"), on `ProfileService.ProfileLoaded` / `ProfileClosed`, by Reset States (`CancelFlee`), and from the disconnect handler in `MainWindowViewModel`. On a disconnect a loop is stopped and restarts by its own reconnect resume, but a walk lives through it, so where the engine the flee paused is still the active one the retreat only stops where it stands and the walk is handed back at the first game prompt of the next stay (`HealthManager.NoteInGamePrompt`, from `WirePromptScanner.PromptObserved`); `PlayerState.HasPromptData` is not dropped on a disconnect, so the resume in `Evaluate` is held until then. `LoopRunner.SendBacktrackMove` sends nothing through a stopped loop. A run from a `Flee` monster that was held for a move in flight is also dropped at the landing if the user paused the walk or loop meanwhile.
  - **All autos off is the master switch** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: "when i say all auto's off, i mean the master switch is off", and with it off "none of our auto systems should respond". `MonsterRelationshipWatcher.AnswerFlee` asks for no run while `AutoModeController.KillSwitchEngaged`, which stays true when a single auto is turned back on by hand after the switch was pressed. Only the `Flee` response was held to the master switch for this ruling; the `Hangup` response's all-off rule (the sub-bullet **All-off mode** in the `Hangup` policy in this topic) and the other engines are as they were. Self-defence has no test of the master switch of its own: it follows Auto-Combat (`CombatManager.Fighting`), one of the autos the switch turns off, for a `Flee` monster as for a `Neutral` one.

There is no all-off option for a flee, and `GeneralSettings.AllowHangupInAllOffMode` does not apply to it. Under either hold the sighting stays open, as it does at the board's menu and while the PvP side has the roster.
  - **No hang-up in its place.** The Health tab has no flee that ends in a hang-up (that is a PvP action only), so when no run can start nothing is sent: no walk or loop running (`FleeOutcome.NoEngine`), one the user has paused (`Paused`), no way out (`NoRoute`), a party follower (`Follower`: a follower never flees, *Party → Following the leader: follow / drag movement*; no `@heal` either, which asks for HP), a hang-up or wimpy jump sent within `EscapeRepeatWindow` (`Escaping`), or a flee already under way (`AlreadyRunning`). Those are the sighting's one answer and are not tried again inside it, so a walk started beside the monster is not turned round by the next roster. A character at 0 HP or below (`Down`) is asked again at the next roster. A run started while a PvP flee is staying away uses `CombatSettings.RunDistance`, not the PvP flee's length, and the stay-away stands.
  - **A run decided while a move is in flight** waits for it to land (the `Also here:` line of the room being entered is read before the move is confirmed) and then asks whether a `Flee` monster is on the roster of the room it landed in, in place of the held flee's usual hostile check: a `Flee` monster is not counted a hostile (`CombatStateTracker.HasHostileMonster` counts `Enemy` only).

Where none went out and none is owed (`EscapeOutcome.HangupsDisabled`, `AllOff`, `NotSent`, or the minute after a reconnect) the `Flee` monster is answered as if alone. With Disable Hangups on *(user, 2026-10-09)*: "it would only run from the flee monster if a navigation engine was running (walk to, loop, auto lair) otherwise it'd fight, and if it was idle, and disable hangups was on, it would fight both". So the `Flee` monster is run from when a walk or loop is running; with none running neither is answered on sight and both are fought back when they attack (the `Hangup` one by **Fought back when no hang-up is coming** in the `Hangup` policy in this topic, the `Flee` one by **Fought back when no run is coming** below).
  - **"pvp actions win"** *(user, 2026-10-09)* is applied to `Flee` as to `Hangup`: no run starts while `PvpFight.IsActive` or `PvpResponder.IsAnswering` the roster, and the monster is answered when the PvP side is done.
  - **Fought back when no run is coming** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: asked whether a `Flee` monster that attacks when no run can start should be left alone or fought back, the user answered "fight back". `CombatManager.OnAttackedInSelfDefense` leaves a `Flee` monster out unless `MonsterRelationshipWatcher.NoAnswerComing` says no run is coming: no walk or loop running (`FleeOutcome.NoEngine`), one the user has paused (`Paused`), no way out (`NoRoute`), a party follower (`Follower`), Auto-Heal and Auto-Rest both off (`EngineOff`), or the master switch off. It is also said once the run that answered the sighting is over (`HealthManager.IsFleeInFlight` false) with a `Flee` monster still on the roster: the run's first move was refused (`HealthManager.NoteMoveBlocked`), or a second `Flee` monster stood where the run landed, its display read while the run was in flight (`AlreadyRunning`); no second run is chained from there. It is not said while a run is under way or held for a move to land, after an escape (`Escaping`), for a character that is down (`Down`), or while the hang-up, the PvP actions or the board's menu have the roster. It is self-defence only, under self-defence's own gates (`CombatManager.Fighting`, and not during a walk-to in motion, `SetSelfDefenseTravelGate`): `MonsterEngagement.IsEngageable` never picks a `Flee` monster on sight, exactly as it does not pick a `Neutral`. (An earlier note said a `Flee` monster was never fought back, run or no run; superseded 2026-10-09.)
  - **The seeds stay** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: "keep both as flee". Both shipped overlay seeds set `Flee` on the gigantic black ooze (#63) and the huge gruesome creation (#191), so this applies to them until the user changes their relationship.
  - **Client use:** `MonsterRelationshipWatcher.AnswerFlee`, `AnswerHangup` and `NoAnswerComing`, `HealthManager.FleeFromMonster`, `HealthManager.IsNavigationPausedByUser`, `FleeOutcome`, `CombatManager.SetNoAnswerComingProbe`, `IRecoverableEngine.ResumeAfterFlee` and `PeekPlannedDirections`, `LoopRunner.TakeStepsRunForwardAsWalked`; the `[MonsterFlee]` log lines and the bug report's **Flee-relationship monster** line (`MonsterRelationshipWatcher.LastFleeSighting`, `BugReportBuilder`).
- The **KillOnSight** flag (Monster edit dialog, shown only for `Neutral`) makes auto-combat **engage a neutral like an enemy** — but because neutrals never open on you, the *other* un-engaged neutrals still don't block resting, so between kills the engine rests/meditates (only when below the rest trigger) before turning on the next one.
- **Hand-attacking a passive neutral.** If *you* hand-attack one (a manual swing or combat cast), it turns hostile per the mechanic above, so the client marks that instance user-engaged and the auto-combat engine **takes over finishing it** — treating it like an enemy until it dies (and holding the walker in the room) instead of stopping the moment you engaged it. It's keyed per-instance by name and pruned once the mob is gone, so it never leaks onto a freshly-arrived same-named passive neutral; the *other* un-engaged neutrals stay passive and rest-safe. `Enemy` monsters are unchanged.

### Shared monster names — attacks and looks take the first
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-29 (user) · Realm: both*

- **Monsters in a room are told apart by their name prefixes** (`large orc`, `nasty orc`). When two carry no prefix, or the same one, **an attack or a `look` at that shared name goes to the first monster of that name in the `Also here:` line**.
- **How Stock picks the target of a typed attack** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_find_action_target` @0x4699fc; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **Monsters are scanned in room-slot order, and the first match wins.** A typed string equal to a monster's whole name returns that monster at once, before players are looked at (@0x469af6–0x469b54).
  - **Several monsters matching is never "ambiguous".** The ambiguity that prints the "be more specific" list is raised only when more than one thing matched and the result is not a monster (@0x46a0bf–0x46a0d2).
  - **An attack by name goes to a monster that isn't charmed first.** The first pass skips charmed monsters (@0x469a9b) and a second pass takes only those (@0x469c02–0x469c5a), so a charmed monster is reached only when no other monster matched.
  - **Players are matched on the first typed word only**, in the same room, skipping yourself and hidden players you can't see (@0x469db6–0x469e61). A player match replaces a monster match and, with a monster also matched, makes the result ambiguous. An exact player name returns at once.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` The typed text seems to match when it is a prefix of the name starting at any word of it (`orc`, `lar` and `large o` would all fit `large orc`), and when the whole text fits nothing its last word is dropped and the scan repeated, so `a orc 2` would attack the first orc: the routine has no numbered form. Both rest on what the host's string helpers do, which wasn't traced. Does `a lar` attack a `large orc` on Stock, and does `a orc 2`?

**Client use:**
- `MonsterHpTracker` credits damage at a shared name, and a look's band, to the first instance; a death removes the first, an arrival joins at the end.

### Monster target selection — who it swings at once fighting
*Status: Stock CONFIRMED (stock DLL source, user-provided); Paradigm CONFIRMED (user writeup, Paradigm only; matches the Paradigm developer's write-up shared by the user 2026-09-27); realm split CONFIRMED 2026-09-26 (user) · Realm: differs — see bullets*

- **Distinct from *whether* a monster opens on you:** once a monster is in a fight it picks **one target per beat**, and the two realms use different engines.
- **Stock** *([CONFIRMED] — stock DLL source, user-provided)*. A stock monster attacks a single **locked target** at a time (not everyone it has aggroed). Each beat:
  1. **Locked target present** → hit it again (the lock clears if that player left / died).
  2. **No lock → spread pick** among the aggroed players in room / terminal order: each rolls `genrdn(0,100) < 50 − 5 × (hits they're already taking this beat)`; **first to pass** is hit; if none pass, the **last eligible** player is hit (fallback). The mob drifts toward whoever *isn't* already piled on — a player taking ≥10 hits this beat hits a 0% threshold and is skipped by fresh rolls.
  3. **After swinging it rolls `genrdn(1,100) < Follow%`** (Monsters `Follow%`; the roll is 1–99, so Follow% `F` passes `(F − 1)` times in 99 — never at 1 or below, always at 100): pass → **lock** onto the just-hit player; fail on an **aggressive** align (∉ {0,3,4}) → **clear** the lock and re-spread next beat; fail on a **passive** align ({0,3,4}) → **keep** the lock.
  - **The mirror roll when a *player* hits the mob re-points the lock to that attacker** — the "attack last" behaviour. Follow% is the stickiness dial.
  - **Special groups** (the monster's group number, not the imported `Type` column — *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*)**:** group 37 (`0x25`, the engine's `Angel`) monsters never manage a lock this way; a group 5 (`Guard`) monster only acquires a lock when currently untargeted. (An earlier note called these an engine-internal type, with `0x25` as "summoned"; superseded 2026-10-03 — the field is the group copied at spawn.)
  - **Carve-out:** an evil NPC won't spread onto a fellow-evil player (`EvilPoints > 39`).
- **Paradigm** *([CONFIRMED] — user writeup, Paradigm only)*. Paradigm rewrote target selection into a **weighted lottery** with no locked-target mechanic. Each player scores from a base **150**: `+ (10 − Charm/5)` (higher Charm lowers the score), `+` party position (frontrank 60 / midrank 30 / backrank 0; **solo = frontrank 60**), `+` recent aggro (last hitter **+30 × players-in-fight**, everyone else **−5 × players-in-fight**), **floored at 50**. The monster rolls a weighted lottery over the summed scores — bigger score = bigger slice, never a guarantee, never impossible.
- **Charm and party position have no effect on stock target selection** — they are Paradigm-only.
- **Targeting depends on the realm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)* — the two models above never share a formula, and the Monster Aggro calculator shows each one.
- **Paradigm, in plain terms:** a hostile NPC picks its target by **chance**; hidden **modifiers** make a party member more or less likely to be chosen — never guaranteed, and the modifier values aren't visible in game:
  - **Party rank** — **frontrank** raises the odds of being targeted, **backrank** lowers them (midrank between).
  - **Attacking last** raises the odds; **attacking first** lowers them.
  - These stack: a **frontrank member attacking last** is the most likely target; a **backrank member attacking first** the least — but it's still a weighted roll.
- **On Stock, rank doesn't matter** for who gets targeted; "attacking last" works through the lock re-point and Follow% stickiness above, not a score.
- **Stock rank does change your combat stats** *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `_move_player_to_fighter`; [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*:
  - **back rank:** accuracy −10, defence +15;
  - **front rank:** net accuracy +5, defence +5 (it takes the front bonus, +15 accuracy / −10 defence, and then the back-rank adjustment too);
  - **middle rank or solo:** no change.
  - Paradigm's rank effects differ and aren't captured yet (user, 2026-09-27).
  - **Fighting blind, or in light above 900, takes 10 off both of those values on Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_move_player_to_fighter` @0x42b16a–0x42b18c; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: accuracy −10 and defence −10, on the same two fighter values the rank adjustment writes (@0x42b14a–0x42b166). The blind test is the blind condition's status bit (`+0x6f5 & 0x10`); the light test is `_get_light_level` above 900, the too-bright case of *Movement & navigation → Light sources*.

**Client use:**
- Surfaced in the **Monster Aggro** calculator (Workshop → Calculators), which shows the loaded set's model: `StockAggroCalculator` (acquisition → spread pick → Follow% stickiness) or `ParadigmAggroCalculator` (weighted lottery).

### Per-monster overlay automation (client policy)
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-10 (user design); count-field reading is a client interpretation, [NEEDS CONFIRMATION]*

Client-side automation policy for the Game Data → Monster overlay flags — not engine behaviour, but how the client's auto-combat interprets the per-monster overrides.

- **DontBackstab — a flagged monster is never the backstab opener.** On the opening (armed) round the target picker **prefers the highest-priority non-flagged** actionable monster to backstab. A flagged monster is only chosen when **every** actionable monster in the room is flagged, in which case the room is **still cleared** — the opener just falls through to a normal attack instead of `bs` (never skip the room over the flag).
- **Override Attack / Override pre-attack — a per-monster attack that substitutes for the global Combat-tab choice for that species only.** The **Override Attack** field takes EITHER:
  - a **`Spells.Number`** (resolved to the `Spells.Short` cast-code) — routed through the *Normal Attack Spell* rung with its mana floor + per-room cast cap; OR
  - a **raw command verb** ("attack", "bash") sent **verbatim** as the attack verb, forced over the whole spell/weapon flow, with **no** rung gating (the server auto-repeats it like any attack command).
- **The editor disambiguates on save.** A positive integer is the spell id; other text is checked against the active set's known spell **cast-codes** — a match (e.g. "turn") resolves to that spell's Number and takes the **gated spell rung** (a user who types the code they'd cast in-game gets mana/cap gating, not a raw command). Only text matching no spell stays a raw command — this is what lets `attack` persist; an earlier int-only parse silently dropped it.
- **The pre-attack override stays spell-only** and occupies the *Single-Target Debuff* rung.
- **Gate bypass.** When an override is set the client **bypasses the effectiveness gates** (observed "no effect" immunity, SpellImmu level-block, and ≥100% elemental resist) — the rationale is that a user who hand-picks the attack for a specific monster has done the due diligence that it works. So a forced command is **never** second-guessed by the *Attack-command "no effect" fallback*. The **physical constraints still apply** for the spell-id form: the rung's mana floor, the once-per-target guard (pre-attack), and the override's own per-room cast cap.
- **Count = per-room cast cap (spell-id form only).** The override's configured count is the cap; the overlay documents **null = 0**, so a spell set with **no positive count is treated as inactive** and the client falls back to the global slot (likewise if the number doesn't resolve to a known cast-code). The command form carries no count — it's active whenever the text is non-blank. This "null/zero count ⇒ fall back to global" reading is the client's interpretation of the ambiguous count field — **[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]** if override behaviour is ever questioned.
- **0-mana stand-down.** At literal 0 mana nothing that costs MA can land — the server silently **no-ops** a cast or a mana-costing command with **no error line** to react to (an earlier build kept re-sending a forced `turn` every round while the player stood there getting hit until a regen tick). So at 0 mana the client marks spells unavailable (the chooser collapses to Backstab/Physical) and, for a forced command that resolves to a spell cast-code, falls back to the physical weapon; a genuinely free verb (bash/kick) still fires since it costs no MA. Re-evaluated each round, so it resumes the instant mana ticks back up.

### Combat round output order — damage lines precede the prompt, so HP lags a round
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-05 (user + report `paradigm-20260904-214056`); per-line redraw OBSERVED 2026-09-28 (report `paradigm-20260928-131549`) · Realm: Paradigm (Stock not recorded)*

- **A combat round's server output arrives as a burst: damage / hit / miss lines first, then the round's prompt** (`[HP=.../MA=...]`) — and **only the prompt carries the post-round HP/MA**. So between "the hit landed" and "the prompt parsed," the client's `PlayerState.Hp` still holds the *previous* round's value.
- **Paradigm redraws the statline after EVERY line of the burst, carrying the HP as of that hit.** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, raw wire in report `paradigm-20260928-131549`)* Each hit line is followed by `ESC[79D ESC[K` + `[HP=<before>/MA=..]:` + `[HP=<after>/MA=..]:`, e.g. `The ogre skeleton claws you for 53 damage!` → `[HP=414/MA=303]:` → `[HP=361/MA=303]:`. So mid-burst HP is not stale but **partial** — it keeps falling until the last line; only the final prompt is the round's settled HP.
- **A between-round cast sent mid-burst is processed after the round's output.** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, report `paradigm-20260928-131549`)* The command echoes on the burst's final prompt (`[HP=127/MA=671]:gdhe`) even though the client picked it on a partial `241`, so picking once HP settles costs no game time.

**Client use:**
- **Client encoding (load-bearing).** The between-round cast heartbeat, `TickEngine.CombatTickElapsed`, is fired *by the damage lines themselves* (`RecordCombatTick`, debounced to the round's first combat line) as well as by the 5 s timer fallback. So a damage-line-driven tick runs `CastingDirector.OnCombatTick` → `Evaluate` **during the burst, before the round's prompt refreshes HP** — the between-round decision sees stale HP.
- **The incident** (report `paradigm-20260904-214056`): a round chunked the player 254 → 117, but the tick fired the between-round decision while HP still read 254, so it spent the round's one slot on a due **armour buff** (looked safe at "254") instead of a heal; the player died two rounds later. The program log's `Buffing fired ... hp=254/257` is the *stale* read — matching the pre-burst prompt — while the wire shows the buff landing at `[HP=117/MA=286]`.
- **Fix (v3.50.10).** `TickEngine` flags whether the tick in flight is damage-line-driven (`LastCombatTickWasDamageDriven`); on such a tick `CastingDirector` held the non-heal survival categories (cure / buff / debuff) so the round's slot isn't spent on unconfirmed HP. (That fix left heals eligible as "safe on the stale read"; superseded 2026-09-28 — see the next bullet.)
- **Burst-settle hold (v3.118.7, report `paradigm-20260928-131549`).** Heals were not safe on a partial read: the tick picked `gdhe` at a partial 236 (54%), spending the round's one slot, and the burst ended at 72 (17%) with the Emergency heal (`mgra`, < 50%) locked out for a round; a reactive pass at a partial 362 also fired `grhe` and a second tick re-fired it (`You have already cast a spell this round!`). `CastingDirector` now stamps a burst on a damage-line tick and on every HP drop, and holds **every** between-round cast until HP has been quiet for `BurstSettleWindow` (400 ms), then a scheduled settled pass picks on the final HP. The one exception: an **Emergency heal already due** on the partial read fires at once (HP only falls inside a burst, so that tier can't turn out wrong) — unless a due cast the user ranked above it exists, which then waits for the settled pass. The timer-fallback tick and out-of-combat heartbeat are HP-fresh, so they're unaffected.
- **The drop is stamped inside `Evaluate` (v3.143.23, report `paradigm-20261004-054304`).** The party self row (`PartyManager.SyncSelfFromPlayerState`) subscribes to `PlayerState` before `CastingDirector` and its `HpPercent` change runs a pass, so the old stamp in the director's own HP handler came too late: `gdhe` went out on a partial 273/520 (52%), the burst ended at 160 (31%), and the `mgra` that followed drew `You have already cast a spell this round!`. `Evaluate` now stamps any HP drop itself (`NoteHpReading`), whichever subscriber calls it.
- **The burst's damage-line tick is read after the burst's prompts** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, program log in report `paradigm-20261004-054304`)*: the prompt scanner runs ahead of the line extractor, so the round's `CombatTickElapsed` arrives just after any cast those prompts fired. That cast was run by the server after the round and took the slot, so `NotifyRoundComplete` keeps a slot spent within `BurstSettleWindow` of a damage-line tick instead of freeing it for a second, refused cast.

### Damage lines — who hit whom
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-09-28 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` strings and the `wccmsg2` message table) · Realm: Stock — Paradigm not recorded*

- **Every damage line ends `for N damage!`, but nothing else about its shape is fixed.** The rest is the engine's own melee wording, a monster attack's own verb phrase, or a spell's message.
- **The engine's melee lines** (hardcoded in the DLL):
  - `You %s %s for %d damage!` — your hit;
  - `%s %s you for %d damage!` — a hit on you;
  - `%s %s %s for %s damage!` — what everyone else in the room sees, including a party member's hit;
  - `critically %s` is prefixed to the verb on a critical.
- **Each monster attack and each spell carries its own three lines** in the message table: line 1 to the attacker / caster, line 2 to the victim, line 3 to the room.
  - Monster attack phrases run to several words: `The %s claws you with its pincers for %d damage!`, `The %s bites your ankle for %d damage!`.
- **Many spells show the caster the same text the room sees.** E.g. message 139: line 1 `Dark flame sears %s for %d damage!` and line 3 `Dark flame sears %s for %s damage!`.
  - So such a line doesn't say who cast it: yours reads exactly like a party member's.
  - Line 2 to the victim names no caster either (`Dark flame sears you for %d damage!`).
- **A victim can be named first:** `%s is scorched for %d damage!`, `%s's life is drained for %d damage!`.
- **A room spell's caster line names the room, not a victim** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user; report `paradigm-20260929-063213`)*: `A hellish storm of fire and brimstone scorches your foes for %d damage!`, `A storm of raw energy blasts your foes for %d damage!`, `You summon a %s which drains your enemies for %d damage!`, `You cast swarm on the room for %d damage!`. **Every foe in the room when it's cast takes about that amount**, each adjusted by its own magic resistance, which no line shows. Only the caster sees the number: the room gets `A hellish storm of fire and brimstone scorch the room!`, and a victim `… scorches you for %d damage!`. The singular `… your foe for %d damage!` wordings are usually a single target, **but the wording alone doesn't decide it** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-06, report `paradigm-20261006-051627`, Paradigm)*: spirit horde (`spir`, spell 287, `Targets` 12) cast bare printed `You scatter some ashes in a sweeping motion!` then one `A horde of shrieking spirits ravages your foe for %d damage!` per cast, and its second cast dropped all ten slimeworms in the room at once. The spell's `Targets` field says whether it hits the room. (An earlier note said every singular wording is a single target; superseded 2026-10-06 for room-scoped spells.)
- **An attack spell can show its caster a flavour line first, then the damage line right after it** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-06, user)*: mana storm (`msto`, spell 281) prints `You make a complex gesture!` on a successful cast, then its damage line, which on both realms is `A swirling mana storm engulfs your foe for %d damage!` (user, 2026-10-06: Paradigm's is the same as Stock's; not yet seen in a capture). Spirit horde does the same with `You scatter some ashes in a sweeping motion!` *([OBSERVED] report `paradigm-20261006-051627`)*. The message seed's caster slot holds the damage line; the flavour line isn't recorded. On Stock the room sees `A swirling mana storm engulfs the room for %d damage!`. (The Paradigm seed had the gesture in mana storm's caster slot, and Stock's had a stray slot glued after "mana storm" in both its caster and witness lines; the user called both strays, corrected 2026-10-06.)
- **Each spell names one message-table entry for its damage lines, and ability 120 names the flavour entry** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-06, Stock 1.11p `wccspel2.dat` + `wccmsg2`)*. The spell record's message number isn't in the imported Spells table. Read from the file:
  - mana storm 281 → message 563 (`A swirling mana storm%s engulfs your foe for %d damage!` / `A swirling mana storm engulfs you for %d damage!` / `A swirling mana storm%s engulfs the room for %s damage!`), flavour 564 (`You make a complex gesture!` / `%s makes a complex gesture!`);
  - spirit horde 287 → 571 (`A horde of shrieking spirits ravages your %sfoe for %d damage!`), flavour 572;
  - dragonfire 288 → 577 (`A withering blast of dragonfire sears %s for %d damage!` / `… sears you for %d damage!` / `… sears %s for %s damage!`, the `%s` being whoever is seared), flavour 578 (`You make a complex circling gesture!`);
  - dragonfire 263 → 517 and 265 → 534, both with no caster line, `The %s breathes %s on you for %d damage!` / `The %s breathes %s on %s for %s damage!`; dragonfire 266 (room) → 535, `The %s sweeps the room with %s for %d damage!` to the victim and nothing else; dragonfire 1117 → 3240 (`You breath %s on %s for %d damage!`); mana storm 257 → 463 (`%s casts %s on the room for %d damage!` only); soul rip 211 → 3087, flavour 3086.
  - **An area spell's caster and room lines carry one extra `%s`** (`your %sfoes`, `%sthe room`, `mana storm%s engulfs`). It printed as nothing in the spirit horde capture (report `paradigm-20261006-051627`), and the user called mana storm's a stray (2026-10-06), so the message seed leaves it out. What the engine can put there isn't recorded.
  - **Client policy:** the Paradigm seed's dragonfire 288 and 266 follow these Stock entries (user, 2026-10-06); Paradigm's own table hasn't been read.
- **Elemental fury prints four cast lines, one for each elemental spell it casts** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-06, user)*. The game data chains them through ability 151 *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-06, Spells table on both realms; wording from Stock `wccmsg2`)*: elemental fury 716 (`Shards of stone slice %s for %d damage!`, message 2038) → elemental lightning 718 (`Lightning strikes %s for %d damage!`, 2039) → elemental fire 719 (`Fire burns %s for %d damage!`, 2040) → elemental ice 720 (`Ice freezes %s for %d damage!`, 2041). Its flavour line is message 2037, `You summon the power of the elements!` (the room sees `%s makes a mighty gesture!`). On Paradigm the four lines read the same (user, 2026-10-06: the Paramud MegaMUD message file is the right wording for Paradigm; it lists all four under elemental fury). `Lightning fries %s for %d damage!` is the staff of the elements' line (elemental lightning 417), not fury's.
- **Fireball, song of shockwave and thunderclap show the caster a line that names no victim** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-06, Stock `wccspel2.dat` + `wccmsg2`; Paradigm from the Paramud MegaMUD message file, which the user confirmed 2026-10-06 as the right Paradigm wording)*:
  - fireball 120 → message 99: `The fireball explodes, %scausing %d damage!` / `You take %d damage from the explosion!` / `An explosion rocks %sthe room for %s damage!`;
  - song of shockwave 275 → 604: `A shockwave ripples %sthrough the room for %d damage!` / `A shockwave strikes you for %d damage!` / the same ripples line to the room;
  - thunderclap 775 → 2156: `A massive thunderclap blast your %sfoes for %d damage!` on Stock (`blast`, as the table spells it) and `A massive thunderclap blasts your foes for %d damage!` on Paradigm / `A massive thunderclap blasts you for %d damage!` / `A massive thunderclap ripples through the room!`.
  - fireball 243, the monsters' one → 1395: `You take %d damage from the explosion!` to the victim and no other line.
  - song of draining 101 → 8515: `You sing the %s to %s, draining %d hit points!` / `%s sings the %s to you, draining %d hit points!` / `%s sings the %s to %s!`. Both MegaMUD files also list `%s sings the song of draining to %s, draining %d hit points!`, kept in the seed as a second witness wording.
  - **Paradigm dragonfire 5023 is the monsters' copy of Stock's 288** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-06, Spells table)*: the same base numbers (100 / -50, level 30), the same flavour message (578) and the same monsters cast it (186, 343, 385, 510, 567 …), while Paradigm's learnable 288 is cast by monster 2830 only. Which damage lines 5023 prints on Paradigm isn't known (user, 2026-10-06). **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-06): the seed gives it the lines of the Stock spell it copies, 288's `A withering blast of dragonfire sears you for %d damage!` / `… sears %s for %s damage!`, and no caster line, since nobody learns it.
  - The MegaMUD files also list `%s take %d damage from the explosion!`, `A shockwave strikes %s for %d damage!` and `A massive thunderclap blasts %s for %d damage!` under the same spell names; when those print isn't recorded.
- **A spell that isn't learnable is a monster's** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-06, user)*: mana storm spell 257 shares the name with the learnable 281. We never cast it, so its caster line is never ours, and since it is an area spell aimed at us we only ever see its target line (`%s casts mana storm on the room for %d damage!`), never a witness line.
- **Another player's room spell prints a sourceless room line, right after the caster's announce** *([OBSERVED] report `paradigm-20260929-161536`, Paradigm)*: a party druid's acid tempest showed `Midnight summons a powerful tempest into the room!` immediately followed by `An acidic tempest blows through the room for %d damage!` — the number is on the room's line, though the seed's witness text (`An acidic tempest blows through the room!`) has none. **Every foe in the room takes that amount** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)*, as with our own room spell.
- **A room spell also hits players in the room who aren't in the caster's party** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)* — it matters in PvP. **Client policy:** the round ledger doesn't model PvP yet; a room spell is spread over the room's monsters only.
  - **Being in the caster's party is the only thing that spares a player, and room debuffs hit them the same way as room attacks** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-05, user · Realm: realms with PvP enabled)*.
  - **A party that was just broken up is exposed** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-05, user)*: the portal at the top of the pyramid to the dao lord splits the party (see *Movement & navigation → CMD-driven room teleports split the party*), and the dao lord usually has 3–4 monsters with him. A room attack cast on arrival hits the people who were in the party a moment ago; it is only safe once they have rejoined.
  - **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-05; all built — see **Client use** at the end of this list):
    - Only the combat-round room attack can be pulled back. The between-round room debuff is one cast: once it has fired the damage is done, so it has to be held before it goes out.
    - A Friend or Neutral player who walks in while the room attack is repeating means break and swap to the single-target attack until that player is in the party.
    - A full party (six, see *Party → Party size bounds*) can't take them, so the room attack stays held for as long as they are in the room.
    - A Neutral player who attacks us becomes an Enemy, and the PvP settings' action (hang up, flee or fight) applies from then on. The change is saved on their record.
    - A Neutral player who enters our room and starts a room attack counts as attacking us: Enemy, and respond.
    - The other way round is not an attack: when we walk into a room where a Neutral player is already room-attacking and get hit, they are not marked Enemy. Other clients don't tell Friend, Neutral and Enemy apart or stop a room attack for a newcomer. (On Paradigm an already-running room attack shows as `<player> is poised to assault the room!` on entry — see *Attack announce lines and round commits*.)
    - The same holds when we are already standing in their room and they start a room attack there (a monster walks in): it is their room, so no flip.
    - In both of those cases we leave the room rather than stand in the blast: one room forward along the loop, not back. This covers a Friend's room as well as a Neutral's, when they aren't in our party.
    - With PvP enabled (the realm, or the PvP settings), we don't wait to find out: walking in on a non-party player whose class has room attack spells, we move out of their room at once. A player whose class isn't known yet is treated the same way. On a walk-to that means carrying on to the next room of the route; moving by hand, the client does nothing.
    - **Which classes room-attack** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-05, imported game data, Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p: spells with an area-attack target (9 / 11 / 12) that cost energy, by each class's magery type and level; the user named druids and mages as the main ones, gypsies and bards sometimes, the same day)*: **Mage** (from level 11; 17 such spells on Paradigm, 16 on Stock), **Druid** (from 12; 10 / 8), **Gypsy** and **Warlock** (from 11, the same list; 10 / 8), **Bard** (from 19; 2 / 1), **Ranger** (swarm only, from 12). The Priest, Cleric, Missionary and Paladin area spells are all between-round casts, and the Mystic has none.
    - **How to tell on Stock that such a player is rooming** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-05, user — the threshold players usually use)*: their class can room-attack and the room they are in holds **three or more monsters**. This guess is for Stock only: Paradigm says so outright with the `poised to assault` line, and the client goes by that there. Warlocks and Rangers count as room-attack classes for it, with the others listed above.
    - Stock gives no notice on entry, so there a running room attack is only known from its next round's room line or its damage *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-05, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p)*: the DLL has no `poised to assault` string; `%s moves to attack everyone in the room.` is printed once, by `_cast_no_target` when the caster commits, to whoever is in the room then; and `_display_room_desc` marks a listed player only with the evil-record `*` (see *Robbing players (`rob`)*, The evil record), never with a combat state.
    - What our client does in their place — a Friend or Neutral walks into our room attack — is send `break`.
    - That flip must not come from a room attack after a party split: a Neutral we were partied with, whose party a teleport broke up, can catch us (or be caught by us) in a room attack that was never aimed at them.
    - A Friend isn't flipped or attacked back, unless a PvP-tab checkbox ("Flip a Friend to Enemy if they attack you", off by default) says to treat a Friend who attacks us like a Neutral who does.
    - **An Enemy holds and breaks the room attack like anyone else outside the party** *(user, 2026-10-05: in a party and rooming, a Neutral and an Enemy walk in — send `break` to stop the room attack, then attack the Enemy if we are set to kill enemies, or flee or hang up, whatever is set)*. The Enemy is answered by their PvP response, aimed at them; a room spell is never how they are attacked. *(An earlier note exempted an Enemy whose response was Attack; superseded 2026-10-05.)*
    - A room spell slotted as the normal or alternate attack, or set as a monster's override, is held the same way as the room-attack slots.
    - "Their room" is decided by who was listed in the first room display after our move. Anyone first seen later (an arrival line, a later re-display) came in after us.
    - **Client use:**
      - `PvpRoomSafety.RoomAttackHeldBy` names the first player in the room who is outside our party (`PartyState.HasMember`), whatever their relationship, on a realm with *PvP is enabled on this realm* ticked. While it names someone, `CombatManager.BuildContext` offers the chooser no room attack and no room debuff (`AllowNukes`) and blocks a room-scoped spell in the single-target rungs (`WithRoomScopedHeld`).
      - `CombatManager.BreakRoomAttackForBystander` sends `break` when that player turns up while a room attack is repeating; the `*Combat Off*` that answers it re-dispatches the round, which then picks a single target.
      - **Party split** *(user, 2026-10-05)*: a client with room attacks that was in a party recognises the party breaking up and holds its room attacks until the party is recovered or a user-set time has passed (`PvpSettings.PartySplitHoldSeconds`, 120 s by default). `PartySplitTracker` stamps each member who leaves the roster and clears them when they are back; `PvpRoomSafety.RoomAttackHeldBy` holds while anyone is out, in the room or not, and `PvpAttackWatcher` uses the same stamps for the room attack that isn't an attack.
      - **A player with no record** *(user, 2026-10-05: `who` lists every player online, nobody can hide from it; the entered-the-realm line names arrivals; the top list can build records too; a fresh realm needs spam protection)*: `PvpStrangerLookup` sends one `who` when a capitalised one- or two-word name in the room can't be placed, or `<name> just entered the Realm.` names someone unrecorded. At most one `who` per 30 s, a name not asked about again for 5 min; one outstanding `who` answers for every name seen before its list is read. Until then the name counts as a player for the hold (`SetStrangerProbe`); `RoomEntityClassifier.ReclassifyUnknown` turns it into a player in the room when the record arrives. A top-list capture now creates records for names that had none.
        - **Client use:** the same name rule (`PlayerObservation.LooksLikePlayerName`, a client heuristic, not engine data) counts such a name in Session Stats → Players Seen on every realm, with no `who` sent (`PlayerSightingTracker.NoteAlsoHere`; user, 2026-10-16; report `paradigm-20261013-173152`).
      - `PvpAttackWatcher` marks a Neutral who attacks us Enemy (`PlayerDatabase.SetRelationship`, their own PvP response kept) and raises `Attacked` for every attack. A Friend is marked only with `PvpSettings.FlipFriendToEnemyIfAttacked`. A room attack counts only from a player whose arrival line we saw since our last move (`PvpRoomSafety.ArrivedAfterUs`), and not while that player is out of our party inside the party-split hold (`PartySplitTracker.LeftRecently`). An attack aimed at us counts whoever it comes from. A party member's is ignored. With PvP not enabled for the realm nothing is marked and the program log warns once.
      - `PvpResponder` carries out the response to an Enemy seen in the room or attacking: the player's own response, else Settings → PvP's action. Hang up goes through `HealthManager.HangUpForPvp` (the `@panic` escape); a flee goes to the chosen favourite room (`PvpFleeWalk`: walked in Sprint Mode, we stay there, and the come-back wait counts from arriving — user, 2026-10-05) or backwards along the running walk or loop (`HealthManager.FleeFromPlayer`) a user-set number of rooms, with Flee then hang up hanging up as soon as those rooms are done *(user, 2026-10-05)*; the gang is told with `bg` (*Talk & chat channels → Gang channel speak verb (`bg`)*) when an Enemy is seen, when a player attacks us and when we attack one *(user, 2026-10-05)*; which of the three are sent, and the least time between two of the same line about the same player (60 s by default, 0 for every time), are user settings; a PvP dial-back enters the realm or waits at the menu by `PvpSettings.ReconnectEntersRealm`. How long a flee stays away, the hang-up delay counted from the flee starting, and one response per player per 30 s (10 s for an attack) are the client's choices, 2026-10-05; what MegaMUD's "If forced to hide, wait" does is not known and nothing is built for it.
      - `PvpFight` is the fight with a player. **Anything usable on a monster is usable on a player, except a spell that only takes monsters, such as the charm spells (`cded`, enslave)** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-05, user)*; in the data those are `Targets` 4, and a room-scoped spell can't be aimed at a name. The attack is a PvP combat spell (Settings → PvP) while its max casts and mana floor allow, else the combat profile's: its normal attack spell, its alternate, then the normal attack command (`AppServices.PvpAttackCommandFor`). A PvP between-round spell (`EnergyCost` 0) is cast at the start and again each time its duration at our level has run out (`SpellCalculator.Duration` × 3.04 s), one a round *(user, 2026-10-05: a spell that lasts 5 rounds is used every 5 rounds; a combat spell every round while conditions apply; no combat spell configured means the combat profile)*. For its length the running walk or loop is stopped and `AppServices.CombatSuppressedInCurrentRoom` stands the combat engine down, so a monster in the room is not fought; `PvpFight.ActiveChanged` re-emits the room roster at both ends, which clears the engine's state after the `break` that stopped a room attack and has it pick the room up again afterwards. It ends when the player leaves, on the game's `You do not see <name> here!`, on a refusal, on our death or a disconnect. **The chase** *(user, 2026-10-05)*: step the way they went as soon as they go; when that was missed, guess their trajectory (the way they were heading, else the room's only other way out, never back); at a crossroads with a door, a door that just opens is tried first and a few rooms looked into behind it before coming back for another way, while a door that needs a key, an action, strength or picklocks is passed over; give up after a user-set number of rooms without sight of them (the user's range: 5–10; default 8) and return to what was interrupted. `AppServices.PvpChaseExits` offers only plain exits and `Door` exits with no stat requirement; how many rooms in (default 3), the wait with no way to follow (default 20 s) and the walk back not counting against the limit are the client's. A player's departure line (`RoomDepartureWatcher.PlayerDeparted`) also takes them off the room roster now, which is what lifts a room-attack hold when a bystander walks out.
      - `PvpRoomSafety.LeaveRoomReason` is the leave rule: a resident outside our party who showed the Paradigm `poised` line or announced `moves to attack everyone in the room.`, or on Stock a resident whose class can room-attack (`KnownSpellCatalog.RoomAttackFromLevel`; a known level below it clears them, an unknown class or level doesn't) in a room with three or more monsters. `AppServices.CombatSuppressedInCurrentRoom` adds it to the loop's own "do not attack" gate while a walk or loop is running, so the engine treats the room as one to walk through.
    - Inviting such a player to the party is left to the per-player invite settings that already exist; nothing new invites them.
- **A spell can chain to a second one whose line follows the first** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user; report `paradigm-20260929-063213`)*: necromantic bolt (#1008) chains to `nebo secondary` (#1246, ability 151): `You fire a necromantic bolt at small dark sprite for 350 damage!` → `small dark sprite's life is drained for 95 damage!`. The drain both damages the target and heals the caster.
- **Some Paradigm spells' seeded caster line was wrong or on another record** *(report `paradigm-20260929-063213`; user 2026-09-29)*:
  - arcane assault (`aslt`, #5083) lands as `Pure energy rips through %s, ravaging them for %d damage!`, several times a round, after the emote `You mutter an ancient phrase and point at %s!`. (The seed said `Potent energies streak through …`; superseded 2026-09-29.)
  - the mage's dragonfire (`dfir`, #288) record holds only the emote `You make a complex circling gesture!`; its damage line `A withering blast of dragonfire sears %s for %d damage!` is on the same-named record #263.
- **A monster attack that names only the attacker is the victim's own view** — the victim is you. Message 2431: line 1 `The %s releases a bolt of force from its palm for %d damage!`, line 2 (the room) `The %s releases a bolt of force at %s for %s damage!`. *([OBSERVED] Paradigm too, report `paradigm-20260928-231609`: `The mad wizard throws a flask, which explodes for 5 damage!` with HP 91 → 86.)*
- **Damage to you with no attacker named:** `You are poisoned for %d damage!`, `You combust for %d damage!`, `Your blood is drained for %d damage!`. These are conditions or effects on you — nobody dealt them (the client counts them as damage taken only, report `paradigm-20260929-003750`). The only `Your ... is` damage lines are blood / life / soul drains; every other `Your ...` damage line is your weapon or spell hitting something.
- **Area effects name no one:** `An earthquake rocks the room for %d damage!`.
- **A weapon proc's line names only its victim and follows the hit that set it off** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-29, report `paradigm-20260929-043055`, Paradigm)*: `You cut angry feral ogre for 11 damage!` → `angry feral ogre takes 3 damage from the cold!` → `Flames burn angry feral ogre for 15 damage!`; `Tristian shatters angry feral ogre for 47 damage!` → `angry feral ogre's life is drained for 12 damage!` → `A magic missile streaks out at angry feral ogre for 19 damage!`. It fires only on a connected swing (see *Spells, buffs & conditions → Item-cast spells — how a `CastsSp` fires (on-use vs combat proc)*). **Client use:** `RoundDamageTracker` credits a caster-less hit on a monster to whoever landed the last hit on that same monster within a second.
- **Other damage wordings** in the Stock message table, without `for N damage` *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-29, `wccmsg2`)*:
  - `You take %d damage from the flames!` / `You take %d lightning damage!` / `You take %d damage!` (also after a sentence: `The %s opens, and then snaps shut tightly. You take %d damage!`);
  - `%s takes %d acid damage!` / `%s takes %d damage from the cold!` — often the **caster's own view** of a spell, naming only the victim;
  - `…, causing %d damage!` / `…, causing you %d damage!` / `… upon the room, doing %d damage!` / `A counterstrike at you does %d damage!`;
  - `You fall to the ground with a thud, taking %d damage!`.
  - Heals share the word but aren't damage: `healing %d damage`, `is healed of %d damage`, `regenerating %d damage`; so do `…, but your armour absorbs the damage!` and `You resist the poison, and take only partial damage!` (no number).
- **Falls** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user; spells from the message seed and TBInfo)*: `You fall to the ground with a thud, taking %d damage!` is the failed-jump message (spell `drops`, #321; Paradigm also #5487) — used on the slum warehouse rooftops. `You take %d damage from the fall!` is the `level 1`–`level 5 fall` spells (#689, #707–#710), cast by the map-12 `jump pit` / `jump shaft` / `enter pit` room commands after the drop.
  - **Seeing either fall line usually means you didn't land in the room you were heading for** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)*. **Client use:** `MovementRefusalDetector` → `RoomTracker.NoteFell` drops the move's predicted landing and goes Suspect, so the next room display is resolved from scratch (and Paradigm asks `rm` when no engine is driving); a running walk or loop replans through its recovery gate.
- **`A bolt of lightning from the heavens strikes you for %d points damage!`** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user · Realm: Stock)*: only with evil punishments turned on, or a sysop's punish command. Nobody in the room dealt it.
- **`You sing the %s, causing %d damage to your foes!`** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)*: the bard's **song of blasting**, an area spell that hits every hostile in the room.
- **The smash penalty** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-29, user)*: `You smashed %s to the ground!` · `You are smashed to the ground!` · `%s is smashed to the ground defenseless!` · `The %s is smashed to the floor defenseless!` are the secondary effect of a smash landing — the penalty applied to whoever was smashed. No damage.
- **The engine also has** `%s's just glanced off of %s's armour.` · `%s just dodged an attack from %s.` · `%s just missed an attack against %s.` *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-29, `wccmmud.dll` strings; where they print isn't recorded)*.

**Client use:**
- `DamageLineAttributor` names each side by matching the room roster, the party and "you" inside the line, not by grammar, across all the wordings above; damage nobody dealt (a condition, a fall, the heavens' bolt) counts only as taken. `CombatLineClassifier` labels those lines `Damage (you)` and the smash penalty `Smashed (you)` / `Smashed (other)`. `RoundDamageTracker` keeps the per-round ledger; a caster's-eye spell line counts as ours only when it matches one of our class's spells and we cast within the last few seconds; a victim-only proc right after a hit goes to that hitter.
- Our room spell credits every monster in the room with the full amount (`RoundDamageTracker`, `DamageLineAttributor` naming a "your foes" / "your enemies" line ours); another player's room line goes to the player whose announce came right before it, spread the same way (`RoundDamageTracker.AnnouncedBy`, report `paradigm-20260929-161536`) and lowers every monster's HP estimate (`MonsterHpTracker.NoteAreaDamage`). A chained spell's line adds to the cast it follows in Session Stats (`SpellLineMatcher.FollowUp`); that covers every spell down the chain, so all four of elemental fury's lines are its own. A spell whose own record carries no damage line is recognised by its same-named records' wordings (`AppServices.OwnSpellLines`).
- A room spell's landing line counts as one cast toward its slot's Max casts on the wording alone, with no monster name required (`CombatManager.OnAttackCastConfirmed`, `ApplyConfirmedAttackCastToCap`; report `paradigm-20261006-051627`: Multi-attack 1 capped at one cast never handed over to Multi-attack 2). A single-target spell's line must still name the monster the round is on. Either way the cast confirms on any damage wording recorded under the spell's name, not only its own record's line (`AppServices.AttackSpellMatchersFor`): Paradigm hail of stones (spell 5080) has no caster line on its own record.
- The round ledger spreads one of our spells over the room when the game data scopes it to the room (`Targets` 3 / 5 / 9 / 11 / 12), whatever its wording says (`SpellLineMatcher.HitsRoom`, `CombatSessionTracker.MatchesOwnRoomSpell`), and keeps a no-caster spell line ours for as long as the engine has that spell repeating, not just for the seconds after the cast was sent (`CombatManager.IsRepeatingSpell`; report `paradigm-20261006-051627`: spirit horde's damage went to nobody, and its second round to an unknown dealer).
- The ledger feeds Settings → Combat "Show combat round totals" (issue #245), Session Stats (`CombatSessionTracker.OnAttributed`: our procs, spells, per-round damage and blows taken), the Wire Inspector's Classified `[Ledger: …]` tags and the bug report.

### Kill detection and monster-kill message order
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-23 (bug-report captures); exp-line and AoE rules CONFIRMED 2026-08-15 (user); fight-over rule CONFIRMED 2026-09-08 (user); where a room spell's `*Combat Off*` comes OBSERVED 2026-10-10 per realm (inline)*

- **A kill prints in a fixed order:** the monster's **death line** (e.g. `The toad croaks in agony, and collapses wetly.`) → `You gain N experience.` → `*Combat Off*`, all in the same server flush.
- **`*Combat Off*` is not a reliable death signal on its own.** Non-sustaining attacks (thrown weapons, KAI pummel, a party member's throws) emit an off/engaged bounce **every strike**, so a `*Combat Off*` fires many times per fight with no death.
- **The "exp + Combat Off within a window" fallback death is a *weak* heuristic** — only trust it for monsters whose specific death line isn't in the data (historical — per-monster death lines were retired in v3.16.0; the exp line followed by `*Combat Off*` is the kill signal). Because a specific death line always precedes its exp, an exp that lands right after a specific death belongs to that already-attributed kill and must not also arm the fallback. Otherwise, with identical-exp mobs dying every few seconds (a swarm), the prior kill's exp stays inside the window and the next fight's non-death `*Combat Off*` fires a phantom fallback death on it, a beat before the current mob actually dies. A `*Combat Off*` that answers an echoed command is such a non-death Off and is told apart by its place on the wire: *Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)* (the *A new attack command sent while a fight is running* bullet and the Client use under it).
- **The exp line is the earliest reliable per-kill signal during combat** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-08-15, user)*. Every kill grants exp, and the exp line lands **before** the kill's `*Combat Off*`. So while engaged with a target we've attacked, a `You gain N experience.` line means that target just died — recognize the kill on the **exp line**, not the later `*Combat Off*`. Waiting for the Off let the round's **alternate** attack corpse-cast: `lbol` kills → `mmis <corpse>` → "You don't see X here!" (report `paradigm-20260814-230258`). This is generic — the exp line is identical for every monster.
- **AoE clears the whole room as a burst of exp lines** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-08-15, user — "20 targets dead in 1 spell"; no realm was named)*. One room spell prints a `<flavor>` + `You gain N experience.` **pair per monster it kills**. So exp-line count = kill count. Where the `*Combat Off*` comes differs by realm *(Realm: differs)*. (The 2026-08-15 entry had "then a **single** `*Combat Off*` at the end" for every realm; that is Paradigm's shape for an emptied room, superseded for Stock 2026-10-10.)
  - **Paradigm: one `*Combat Off*` after the last pair when the spell empties the room, and none when a monster survives** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10 (capture; report `paradigm-20261010-145330`; Realm: Paradigm))*. `hsto` killed all four brute zombies in a room: four `The brute zombie keels over like a hewn tree!` / `You gain 16250 experience.` pairs, then one `*Combat Off*`. Fifteen seconds later it killed three of four: three pairs, then the prompt and no `*Combat Off*`. A round before that it had killed one of four, again with none, and fired again at the next round with nothing re-sent.
    - So after a partial room-spell kill on Paradigm the next `*Combat Off*` belongs to something else, and the exp lines are still fresh when it comes.
  - **Stock: a `*Combat Off*` after every kill's exp line, the caster's channel going on regardless** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`; Realm: Stock)*. Each monster the room cast kills goes through `_check_kill_monster` and then `_distribute_experience(caster, exp, -1, monster, …)` (`_cast_no_target` @0x441aa6 → @0x441af3, @0x4423a1 → @0x4423fa, @0x4428c6 → @0x442913). In `_distribute_experience` the killer takes the same branch as a player targeting the dead monster, whatever its own queued target and whether or not it is on the round queue (@0x44ca6e–0x44ca84): `_add_experience` (@0x44ca8c), `_kill_autocombat` (@0x44ca97), `_display_autocombat_broken` (@0x44caa2). `_display_autocombat_broken` prints `*Combat Off*` for any valid player number, with no test of whether a fight was running (@0x44bd75–0x44bd9d). So a room spell that kills three prints death line, exp line, `*Combat Off*` three times over. The next round is queued all the same: *Room-attack spells: cast bare, persistent channel*.
  - **Stock: nothing but a prompt comes between a kill's exp line and its `*Combat Off*`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, same DLL)*: `_add_experience` prints `You gain %s experience.`, then the prompt, and returns (@0x416a9a–0x416ab3), and the two calls after it print nothing ahead of the Off. In report `paradigm-20261010-145330` the kills read (a room emptied by `hsto`, a single-target kill) show the same on Paradigm: the `*Combat Off*` on the wire line after the exp line.
  - **Stock: a room caster's share of another player's kill is an exp line with no `*Combat Off*`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, same DLL)*: a player on the round queue with no queued target, which is the entry a room cast makes (`_engage_autocombat(caster, -1, 0xffff, …)` @0x4446f1–0x444701), standing in the room of the kill, gets `_add_experience` alone (@0x44caac–0x44cafd). It is the "no attack target" share of the Stock bullet after this one.
- **Stock: a kill's experience is split among the players fighting that monster, not among the party** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_distribute_experience` @0x44c990; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The function reads no party field.
  - The share is `exp / N`, a whole-number division, and at least 1. N is the killer plus every other player who is in auto-combat (`_is_inside_autocombat`) and either has that monster as their attack target (@0x44c9d1–0x44c9f1), or has no attack target and stands in the room of the kill (@0x44c9f3–0x44ca39).
  - Each counted player gets the same share (`_add_experience(player, share, 1)` @0x44ca86, @0x44caf2), whatever their level. A party member who isn't attacking isn't counted, and a player outside the party who is attacking is.
  - The killer and everyone targeting that monster then have their combat ended (`_kill_autocombat`, `_display_autocombat_broken` @0x44ca94–0x44caa2); a player counted for having no target keeps theirs. For the killer this runs whatever it was attacking with, a room spell included: the *AoE clears the whole room* bullet of this topic.
  - A textblock's `addexp` is not split: *Quests → Quest experience — `addexp`*.
- **Paradigm: a party member who isn't attacking gets no experience from a kill, as on Stock** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (report `paradigm-20261009-122342`; Realm: Paradigm), one kill)*. In the capture our attack had been stopped five and a half seconds earlier (a typed `eq`: *Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)*) and none was sent since; the party killed the monster, and our screen showed its death line and no `You gain N experience.`. The kills before and after it, with our attack engaged and no damage of ours landing, each printed `You gain 6000 experience.`. How Paradigm divides the experience among those who are attacking is not recorded.
- **"The fight is over" = `*Combat Off*` AND an empty hostile roster** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-08, user)*. `*Combat Off*` is the message that marks us no longer engaged, **on Stock and Paradigm alike** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*. It has three causes: the monster died (then a death line and an exp line come with it), we typed `break` (the monster is still alive), or a between-round spell interrupted our attack. (Those are the usual three; everything that prints it on Stock is listed in *Non-swing actions break combat (casting, equipping)*.) As above it also fires on every cast and once per strike for non-sustaining attacks, so on its own it says nothing about whether anything is still alive. The usable pair is that line **plus** a room re-display showing no engageable monster left.
- **Death messages are arbitrary per-monster flavor** — no shared keyword (a scan of 1035 seed death lines: `…a tortured squeak`, `…to the ground`, `…without a sound`, `…a thousand pieces`, `…an agonized bellow`, `…in a heap`, most with no death word) and no distinctive colour (they render default/white). So a monster death **cannot be recognized by wording or colour generically** — the exp line is the generic signal, and our own targeting (`CombatManager.CurrentTarget`) names the mob.
  - **The giant hellhound (#1250, Paradigm) dies with `The massive demonic beast stumbles and collapses!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (reports `paradigm-20261009-120757`, `paradigm-20261009-122342`; Realm: Paradigm))*: after every `<adjective> giant hellhound` kill in the two captures. The behemoth hellhound (#693) beside it dies with `The behemoth hellhound lets out a monstrous wail, then dies.`. Stock 1.11p has no monster #1250.
  - **Client use:** the Paradigm message seed carries that line as a record linked to monster #1250 (`WitnessMessage`, user 2026-10-09), so `MessageCandidateWatcher` doesn't stage it when no experience line follows it (a kill made while not attacking). Nothing acts on the line.

**Client use:**
- `CombatStateTracker` combines `*Combat Off*` with the room observation: it clears the Combat gate only on that observation, and its idle-stall watchdog sends a bare CR to force a re-display when a final kill produced none.
- Anything asking "may I leave this room now?" — the Auto-Lair engage phase is the first — must read the gate, never the raw line.
- The per-monster `DeathLine` data was **retired** (v3.16.0): every kill is recognized from exp + `*Combat Off*`, and the dead slot is refreshed by the forced room re-display. No per-monster death message is maintained anywhere.
- **The arrival settle defers on an exp line read inside its window** (`CombatManager.OnArrivalSettleElapsed`, since 3.183.24). With no target of ours the exp line drops nothing and stamps no death, yet it is still a kill in our fight or our room (the *A kill made in another room never prints `You gain N experience.` to you* bullet), so the settle asks for the room re-display rather than engage an accumulated roster that may still list the corpse. The defer first keyed on a monster's death line (report `paradigm-20260916-141344`), which no longer comes; a kill with a target of ours still defers through the death it stamps.
- **A kill made by our own room spell is a death on its exp line** (`CombatManager.NoteRoomSpellKill` → `RoomSpellKill` → `MonsterDeathWatcher.NoteRoomSpellKill`; report `paradigm-20261010-145330`). **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-10: a kill is counted when it happens)*. Such a kill has no `*Combat Off*` of its own on Paradigm while anything in the room survives, and a room emptied by one spell has a single Off for all its kills, so the exp + `*Combat Off*` pairing counted an emptied room as one death and a partial kill as none.
  - **Counted on the exp line when all three hold:** a room attack of ours is running in the room (`_roomChannelSpell`); that spell's own damage line was read within 2 s before the exp line (`RoomSpellKillWindow`, stamped by `OnAttackCastConfirmed`), so the exp belongs to a round the spell landed in; and this round's exp lines since the room was last read don't outnumber the monsters it listed (`_expGainsSinceRosterRead`), so there are never more such deaths than the roster held.
    - **The monsters counted are every monster the room listed, neutral ones included** (since 2026-10-10; before, only the ones the engine would attack): a room attack kills a neutral standing in the room like the rest (the Stock target rule is in *Room-attack spells: cast bare, persistent channel*), and one hostile with two neutrals gave two deaths for three kills.
    - **Only the spell's own damage wording stamps it as landed** (since 2026-10-10). Before, with a room spell announced, any hit or miss line starting `You ` that named the monster the round was anchored to stamped it too, a monster's own hit on us among them, and an exp line behind one was counted as the spell's kill.
  - **Never twice.** The exp line is spent when the death is raised, so the `*Combat Off*` the game prints after it (Stock after every kill, Paradigm after the last of a room) finds nothing to pair with. `MonsterDeathWatcher` reads each exp line ahead of `CombatManager` (router tie-break) so that holds whichever was built first.
  - **Left to a `*Combat Off*`, as before:** an exp line past the listed count (a monster the roster never held); an exp line in a round the spell's damage line wasn't read in, or for a spell whose damage wording isn't on record; an exp line with no roster of the room on record; every kill made with no room spell of ours running. The first three are logged and shown in the bug report (`CombatManager.RoomSpellKillSummary`).
  - **The death names nobody.** It carries the exp gained and the kinds of monster the room listed (`MonsterDeathEvent.RoomSpellRoster`); the engaged target is only the monster the round was anchored to. What each reader of a death does with it:
    - lair-timer kill (`LairTimerStore.NoteKill`, which needs only the room), session kill count, kill sound, the Wire Inspector's death tag: once per kill;
    - drop re-look and summon-on-death re-scan: when any listed kind could drop a flagged item, or summons on death;
