  - **Engulfed.** `engulfs` (#234, `HoldPerson`) prints `You are engulfed!` and ends with `You are freed!`; `engulf in flame` (#262, damage only) prints `You are engulfed in flames!` and ends with `The flames enveloping you die down.`
  - **Client policy:** `ConditionTracker` matches an applied text anywhere in a line, so the longer line also latched the shorter text's records: Confused from the zap, a hold from the flames, each with a wear-off that never comes (reported from play, 2026-10-04: the zap showed the wrong condition and "it just sat there" after it ended). An applied text that matches only inside a longer applied text the line also holds is now left out (`IsPartOfALongerMessage`); a longer text that adds only punctuation (`You are blind` / `You are blind!`) is the same message. About ten such pairs exist per realm; these two are the ones where a flag changes. This rule compares applied texts with each other; a cast line that holds an applied text is the next bullet's. (An earlier note said only applied texts are compared, and gave `You are poisoned for N damage!` as a spell's own cast line off which the condition is rightly read; in both seeds that line is poison hits', which carries no poison; superseded 2026-10-11.)
  - **Client policy:** a wear-off line also clears its flag when its own record wasn't the one latched (an applied line and the wear-off the game prints can sit on different records that share a flag), and the aggregate flags are recomputed whenever the active set moves. `ConditionEnded` still fires only for a record that was latched, since the self-buff recast timers consume it.
- **One spell's cast line can hold another spell's applied line** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11: report `paradigm-20261011-165726` (Paradigm), the Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p `Spells`, `Rooms` and `Monsters` data, and both message seeds · Realm: both, the report Paradigm)*:
  - **Freezing water.** The Underwater Passage rooms (`6/1139` and on, 70 rooms on each realm) carry room spell #511 `freezing water`: `Targets` 8, `Dur` 0, damage 1 to 4, abilities 1, 144, 151 → 512 and `115` = 66, the same row on both realms. Each cast prints `You are freezing cold!`, and the spell has no Confusion (71) and prints no wear-off. It EndCasts `holding breath` (#512), which ends in `drowning` (#513): *Movement & navigation → Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*. Paradigm's freezing cold (#5242) prints the same line: *Timing & rounds → Combat round (5s) and the between-round cast cycle*.
  - The line holds `You are freezing`, the applied text of glacial mist (#1042) and galacial mist (#1336), both Confusion (71) at 10, of the ice storms (#1363 and, on Paradigm, #5027; #135 on Stock, whose Paradigm record reads `You are freezing!`) and of freezing (#1015, the end of a blizzard, #771 and Paradigm's #5019). Their wear-off is `You are no longer freezing`.
  - **Three more such pairs, in both seeds:**
    - `You are poisoned for %d damage!` is poison hits (#588: `Dur` 0, abilities 1 and 144, no Poison (19); the on-hit spell of the green slime, #468) and holds `You are poisoned`, the applied text of way of the cobra (#299, Poison). **It is a damage line, not a poisoning** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user: "is a damage line, poison lines dont actually tell us how much damage they do in game via their visible lines, only in the game data")*: a poison's own visible lines never give its damage figure, which is only in the game data;
    - `You are chilled for %d damage!` is cold hits (#587, the same shape) and holds `You are chilled`, the applied text of the frost sceptre's chill touch (#176);
    - `You are mesmerized by the hypnotic movements!` is hypnotic hands (#300), a confusion whose own applied line is `You are confused!` (*Confusion is a single state — generic onset and wear-off lines*), and holds `You are mesmerized`, the applied text of mesmerize (#1391) and strut (#1109).
  - **Client policy:** every record whose applied text sat inside the line latched: in the Underwater Passage rooms the two mists set Confused on each cast, with no wear-off ever to come, which held navigation and had the party told to wait (report `paradigm-20261011-165726`). An applied text that matches only inside the cast, target or witness line of a record for a DIFFERENT spell is now left out (`ConditionTracker.CastLineOfAnotherSpell`). A line is the record's own, and still latches it, when any record carrying that line is the record itself, is linked to one of the same spells, or has the same applied text (web entangle's `You are entangled in sticky strands of webbing.` entangles as the other entangles' `You are entangled` does; mesmerize's `You are mesmerized by the movements!` latches mesmerize and strut), or when a record carrying that line has every condition flag this record has, this record having at least one: the line's own spell really brings that condition on. So hypnotic hands' line still latches mesmerize and strut, all three being confusions, as it did before (the two seeds latch and end the same records on `You are mesmerized by the hypnotic movements!` → `You are confused!` → `The effect of hypnotic hands wears off.` as they did without this rule), and its own applied line need not be waited for (*Confusion is a single state — generic onset and wear-off lines*). Freezing water, poison hits and cold hits carry no condition, so their lines latch nothing: 7 record pairs on 3 lines in each seed. (An earlier version of this rule had no condition test and held hypnotic hands' line back as well; superseded 2026-10-11.)
    - **A record switched off in Game Data (Disabled) still owns its lines** (**Client policy**, plan of 2026-10-12): it applies nothing itself, but its cast, target and witness lines still keep a shorter applied text inside them from latching. Before, switching off the `freezing water` record brought the Underwater Passage bug back.
- **Who can have cast a spell is in the data** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, the Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p `Spells`, `Monsters` and `Rooms` data; items, textblocks and exits 2026-10-16, the same sets' `Items`, `TBInfo` and `Rooms` data · Realm: both)*:
  - The `Spells` column `Casted By` lists a spell's sources as `Monster #N`, `Room M/R`, `Spell #N`, `Item #N` and `Textblock #N(P%)`; an empty one holds a NUL. It is cut off at 250 characters (107 spells on Paradigm, 46 on Stock, ending `+`), and leaves out casters even where it is not cut, so each kind is read from the table that holds it:
    - **monsters:** the `Monsters` table (attack-slot spell, on-hit spell, between-round spell, death and spawn spell) is the whole list of monster casters;
    - **rooms:** a room's own `Spell`;
    - **exits:** an exit cell's `(Cast: pre-N, post-M)` and `(Spell Trap: N)` (*Movement & navigation → Cast-on-walk exits and random teleports*); 26 spells on Paradigm, 23 on Stock. Clean room #5841 is the spell of Paradigm's `17/10691` and also the pre-cast of its east exit, and the column names the room once;
    - **items:** every `CastsSp` (43) slot, on use or as a proc (*Item-cast spells — how a `CastsSp` fires (on-use vs combat proc)*); 337 spells on Paradigm, 224 on Stock. A `LearnSp` (42) slot is no cast: it teaches the spell (*Learning a spell from a teaching item*), so its caster is a player who learned it, as with `Learnable`. The column misses 55 item `CastsSp` slots on Paradigm and 23 on Stock: the starhammer (#1245, `%Spell` 33 → `CastsSp` 420) casts Stock's blazing comet #420, whose list is `Monster #537` alone. `Learned From` misses two taught spells on Paradigm (#24 by item #121, #279 by items #540 and #1374) and one on Stock (#279);
    - **textblocks:** every `cast N` step of the `TBInfo` table (*Textblock directives — the Stock interpreter's list*), room commands among them; 158 spells on Paradigm, 133 on Stock. A `learnspell N` step teaches, as an item's `LearnSp` does. Items and textblocks teach 291 spells on Paradigm and 239 on Stock;
    - **other spells:** an enchantment's on-hit spell (ability 43) and a temporary grant (`GiveTempSpell`, 160); 15 spells on Paradigm, 1 on Stock.
  - Read that way, every `Monster`, `Item`, `Textblock` and `Room` entry of a list that is not cut off names a row of its own table that carries the spell, on both realms.
  - `Room M/R` is also said of a spell cast by one of that room's exits or commands (holding breath #512 lists `6/1138`, whose own spell is none). `Spell #N` is said of an EndCast (151) and also of a spell that only takes this one off (stop drowning #515 on holding breath and drowning: abilities 122 / 153), of an enchantment's on-hit spell (ability 43) and of random tables.
  - **31 `Spell #N` entries on each realm are explained by no table** (2026-10-16). Each names a spell whose only EndCast (151) has the value 0, from a spell inside that spell's `MinBase`–`MaxBase`: random dmg #964 on #977–#981, evil random #988 on #984–#987, pris effect #1052 on #1064 and on. Not every such range is listed: Paradigm's shock #781 (`MinBase` 100, `MaxBase` 200) is named by none of #100–#200. `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Does an EndCast of 0 cast one spell, picked at random, from the spell's `MinBase`–`MaxBase`?
    - **Client use:** the list is the only record of such a tie, so `SpellCasterIndex` keeps open a spell whose cut-off list may have lost one: a spell inside the `MinBase`–`MaxBase` of any spell with an EndCast of 0. On Paradigm that is magma drip #115 and free #164, inside shock's 100–200; on Stock no cut-off list falls in such a range.
  - Glacial mist (#1042) is learnable (`Learnable` 1, class 13, from NPC #244); galacial mist (#1336) and the ice storms #1363 / #5027 are cast by monsters alone; ice storm #135 and blizzard #771 are learnable. All six are `Targets` 12 (Full Attack Area) on Paradigm, and the five of them Stock has (#5027 is Paradigm's) are 12 there too *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-17, Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p `Spells`)*.
  - **A party member's glacial mist doesn't affect us; only a player outside the party on a PvP realm, or an NPC that casts it, does** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-17, user: "if a player in our party used mist, it wouldnt affect us anyway. only players outside our party on a pvp realm, or NPC's that cast it, would affect us" · Realm: both)*. **It holds for every hostile spell** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-17, user, asked whether it covers every learnable hostile spell, the single-target ones included: "Yes, all hostile" · Realm: both)*: a party member's hostile spell (curse, hold, blind, confusion, area attack) never reaches us, and an outside player's reaches us only on a PvP realm. Heals and buffs are not covered; they still affect us. It agrees with *Combat → Damage lines — who hit whom*: on a PvP realm a room attack or room debuff hits every player in the room outside the caster's party.
  - **A spell or a line reaches you only from the room you are in** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user, asked whether a spell's applied line can land from a caster that is not in your room at that moment: "no, monsters or players can only affect you with spells/lines, IF they are in your room. same with room spells, room spells cannot trigger on you unless you are in its room."; Realm: not stated)*. (Filed under *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster movement lines* until 2026-10-16.) **Client use:** which of the records one applied line matches are latched (`KeepWhatCouldBeCastHere`, the **Client policy** of *Who can have cast a spell is in the data*).
  - **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-11: "it should also be able to discriminate spells being cast based on monsters in the room, spells they have available and what spells the room casts as well, for the freezing water fix")*: **when one applied line matches several records, a record nobody here can have cast is left out.** A record's spell is in reach when the room's own spell is it or ends in it (an EndCast chain), or a monster the client has in the room casts it or a spell that ends in it. A record is out of reach when every caster of every spell it is linked to is a monster or a room and none is here; a spell that is cast by an item, a textblock, an exit or another spell's enchantment or grant, a monster's death or spawn spell, tied to another spell otherwise than by an EndCast, or listed with no caster, is never out of reach. Neither is a spell an EndCast reaches from a spell with a duration: it lands when that spell ends (*Health, resting & recovery → Resting in a room whose spell does damage*, the holding-breath timer), when its caster may be gone (1 spell on Paradigm, deadly spores #522 after cloud of spores #581, `Dur` 1; 3 on Stock, #522 and the two after burrows #946, `Dur` 20: burrows deeper #947, `Dur` 200, and death's door #948). From a spell with no duration it lands at once and keeps that spell's casters. A cut-off `Casted By` no longer counts against a spell, since the tables give its casters, save the EndCast-of-0 tie above: 711 of 2,104 spells are cast only by monsters or rooms on Paradigm and 362 of 1,379 on Stock (636 and 333 when a cut-off list kept a spell open and items, textblocks and exits came from that list alone; superseded 2026-10-16). A learnable spell, one an item or a textblock teaches among them, is the next bullet's. Out-of-reach records are left out only when another of the matched records is in reach; with none in reach all latch as before (a hidden monster, a room not seen). The room counts only while the position is confirmed (`CastReach.Standing`). Wear-off lines are read as before.
    - **A learnable hostile spell is in reach only of a player outside the party in the room on a PvP realm** (**Client policy** on the user's rulings of 2026-10-17 above): a spell with `Learnable` 1, a `Learned From`, or a teacher in the `Items` or `TBInfo` table (an item's `LearnSp` slot, a textblock's `learnspell` step: *Who can have cast a spell is in the data*), and an enemy scope, `Targets` 4 (Monster), 8 (Monster or User), 9 (Divided Attack Area) or 12 (Full Attack Area) (`BuffClassifier.IsEnemyScope`, the client's existing buff-versus-enemy split), is cast by its monsters and rooms and by players (`SpellCasterIndex.Casters.PlayersAtFoes`). The player half is out of reach off a PvP realm (Settings → BBS, the realm's PvP box), and on one while the roster is known whole and lists no player outside the party; a name the roster can't place leaves it unknown (`CastReach.StrangersSeen`). A learnable heal or buff (`Targets` 0 / 1 self, 2 one player, 10 / 13 the party) is never out of reach: it lands on the character from anyone, the character included. Before, every learnable spell was never out of reach, and an ice storm cast with no mist caster in the room latched Confused through glacial mist. (An earlier version of this bullet applied it to `Targets` 8 / 9 / 12 only, pending the second ruling; superseded 2026-10-17.) Every learnable hostile spell is also taught by an item or a textblock (glacial mist #1042 by NPC #244's `learnspell`, ice storm #135 and blizzard #771 by items' `LearnSp`), and only note of destruction #279 is taught with no `Learnable` or `Learned From`: 143 learnable hostile spells on Paradigm, 123 on Stock. 156 spells on Paradigm and 136 on Stock are cast only by monsters, rooms and such players.
      - In both sets every learnable curse, hold, blind, confusion, cloud and attack has an enemy scope *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-17, Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p `Spells`)*. Two learnable spells that may be hostile carry `Targets` 0 (User), the scope heals share: song of ugliness (#1389, both realms: Charm −5) and, on Stock, glitterdust (#147: a Stealth ability, `Targets` 8 on Paradigm). The scope can't tell them from the heals, so they stay never out of reach.
    - **A monster's or a player's absence rules its spell out only while the roster is known whole** (`RoomEntityClassifier.RosterIsWhole`): the room is not dark, the character is not blind, every name listed is a monster of the set (for the player half: a monster or a player), and the roster comes from a read of the room (its `Also here:` line, or a walked-into room whose display listed nobody) with nothing since that may have added someone it doesn't name. That is: an arrival line that names nobody the pattern can lift out (a follow, a directionless spawn: *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster movement lines*), an arrival under a name the set has no monster for, a summon line, a combat line with nobody on the roster to fight, a dark advance, the roster emptied as stale, or a watched cast line whose `{source}` names someone the roster doesn't list (`ConditionTracker.CasterNamed` → `RoomEntityClassifier.NoteCasterNamed`; a caster has to be in the room). The next read of the room makes it whole again. (Found in review, 2026-10-11: with an ancestral guardian listed and a banshee floated in after the character, her wail was read as the guardian's and its hold was not latched. Found in review of 2026-10-12: Paradigm's `The {source} rears its head, and shrieks in fury!` is shriek #191, the rocs' and gryphons' confusion, and #5138, Mother Ungol's, which is none; with Mother Ungol listed, a gryphon that came in unlisted and shrieked had its confusion left out.)
    - **The spell's own cast line speaks first.** A record whose cast line was just seen outranks the records sharing its applied text whose line was not (`OutrankedByAnnouncedCast`), and only what that leaves standing is asked who could have cast it. A cast line all of them share (the three plagues') says nothing of which, and who is here still decides.
    - **What stops the character moving, fighting or seeing is never ruled out by who is in the room** (**Client policy**, 2026-10-11): a record flagged MovementPrevented, AttackPrevented or Blinded always latches. A caster has to be in the room (*A spell or a line reaches you only from the room you are in*, the user's statement of 2026-10-11), but a few monsters follow in with no line (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster movement lines*, the user's statement of 2026-10-11), so the roster can never be proven whole; the narrowing is kept to the conditions that cost less when missed (Confused, Poisoned, Diseased, Fear, none).
    - So in the freezing family the monster-only records are left out when another's caster is here, and glacial mist (#1042) and freezing (#1015, through the learnable blizzard #771) are left out too unless a player outside the party is in the room on a PvP realm, or one of their monsters is: an ice storm cast by the ice sorceress latches no Confused. (An earlier note said glacial mist, being learnable, is never left out, with the question this ruling answered; superseded 2026-10-17.)

### Confusion is a single state — generic onset and wear-off lines
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-14 (user); single-state clear CONFIRMED 2026-07-28 (report `paradigm-20260728-173036`); five message forms CONFIRMED 2026-09-02 (user)*

- **`The effects of confusion wear off!` is a shared, generic wear-off** reused by many different confusion sources — a lot of confusion spells and monster effects emit the same line. The onset `You are confused!` is likewise generic. So from the wire alone the client cannot tell *which* of those confusions is on the character: most confusion sources share the generic onset, and a single wear-off line ends it.
- **Most confusion sources share the generic onset; some (convulsions `You are in convulsions!`, form of the monkey) have their own onset and wear-off** — see *Convulsions — custom fumble line, repeated move fumbles, seed onset fix* and *Form of the monkey — self-buff that confuses the caster*.
- **A few effects append their own specific wear-off** (e.g. `The effect of hypnotic hands wears off.`) rather than the generic line, but they still share the generic `You are confused!` onset. They are therefore not independently distinguishable from text alone.
  - **The onset line does not always follow the spell's own line at once** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user, asked whether hypnotic hands always prints `You are confused!` after its own line: "not always immediately, but if thats a stock spell record, check the DLL's paradigm will behave the same way")*.
  - **On Stock a monster's spell prints its cast line and its onset line in one output, or neither** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p; Realm: Stock)*. `_monster_display_spell_success` (@`0x425a5c`) prints to the target, in order: line 2 of the spell's `StartMsg` (120) message with the monster's name (@`0x425b5f`), the spell's own message (@`0x425bb0`), then line 3 of its `DescMsg` (115) message (@`0x425bd1`), and the prompt. For hypnotic hands (#300: 120 = 595, own message 594, 115 = 593) that is `<monster> weaves an intricate pattern in the air!`, `You are mesmerized by the hypnotic movements!`, `You are confused!`. Its caller `_monster_add_cast_spell_to_user` (@`0x425ea6`) calls it when the spell takes one of the target's ten slots, or lengthens the one it already holds (@`0x425f04`, `0x425f51`); when the target already carries the spell with as long or longer left it returns without printing any of the three (@`0x425ee6` → `0x425f10`). Nothing in the two routines prints the cast line and holds the onset line back; what delays it in the user's play is not found there.
  - **Client use:** `ConditionTracker` takes hypnotic hands' own line for a confusion at once and does not wait for the onset line (*Condition Effects flags derive from the linked spell's ability codes*).
- **Records that share an applied line are aliases of one effect and must be cleared as a group** — when any of them wears off, all of them end. Keying each record's clear solely to its own end text strands the flag whenever a sibling with a specific wear-off never sees its matching line. *(2026-07-14)*
- **Any confusion wear-off clears confusion entirely** *(CONFIRMED 2026-07-28, report `paradigm-20260728-173036`)*. More than one record can hold `Confused` at once: a specific source (a monster confuse spell with its own wear-off line, matched by a user-defined message entry incl. caster/target/witness cases) plus the generic `fumble` record, which also carries `Confused` so a confuse whose *set*-line was missed is still recognised. When ANY real confusion wears off you are no longer confused, so **every** latched `Confused` source clears — not just the record whose wear-off fired. Clearing only the wearing-off record (or its applied-line aliases) strands the flag: a death-dog shriek that wore off left the co-latched `fumble` still holding `Confused`, keeping the nav ConfusionGate stuck.
- **A confuse spell surfaces up to FIVE distinct message forms** *(CONFIRMED 2026-09-02, user)*. From the target's point of view: (1) a caster→you cast line, (2) a third-party witness line, (3) an **applied** onset, (4) a **wear-off**, and (5) a per-action **fumble**. The applied/wear-off pair sets and clears the `Confused` state; the fumble line (carrying `LastActionFailed`) fires on each swallowed command and has no wear-off pairing of its own — it clears with the effect via the single-state confusion clear. (The catalogue's `fumble` RECORD does list an end text, but that is just the generic confusion wear-off — see *Confusion fumbles — actions fail and must be re-sent*.)
- **Client use:**
  - `ConditionTracker`'s applied-line alias group-clear implements the shared-applied-line rule.
  - `ConditionTracker` clears every active `Confused` record when a `Confused`-carrying record's wear-off matches.
  - The parked game-data remodel plans to fold the fumble wordings into a shared table, like monster prefixes, plus an "is a confuse spell" checkbox on the message record — so a confuse record then needs only the standard spell lines, not a hand-built fumble entry.

### Confusion fumbles — actions fail and must be re-sent
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-14 (user; report `paradigm-20260714-093614`); any-action + move revert CONFIRMED 2026-09-01 (user + report `paradigm-20260901-080223`); re-send of every client command CONFIRMED 2026-09-09 (user + report `paradigm-20260908-211659`)*

- **Confusion does not block attacking (or acting) outright — each action you send can fumble.** The game consumes the command and it does **not execute** — surfaced as `You fumble in confusion!` (self) / `<name> fumbles about dazedly!` (others). The catalogue's `fumble` record carries the `LastActionFailed` flag (and `Confused`), and the record's end text is the generic confusion wear-off `The effects of confusion wear off` — the fumble line itself has no wear-off pairing.
- **A fumbled action is lost; to actually perform it you must re-send the same action.** Confusion can fumble several actions in a row; how many depends on the severity of the confusion.
  - **When to re-send an attack** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user)*: while trying to start a fight and fumbling, keep sending; `*Combat Engaged*` means the attack finally went through, as long as the target is in the room. Once a fight is under way, a fumble should not make the client interrupt it with a fresh attack. A between-round cast interrupts it regardless, and that can't be helped. **Client policy:** re-send a fumbled attack only while not engaged; every other client command is re-sent as before, in a weapon fight and a spell fight alike.
- **A fumble can prevent ANY action, not just combat, and the fumble line can be customized per confuse source** *(2026-09-01)*. Most confusion sources surface the generic `You fumble in confusion!`; `convulsions` customizes it (see *Convulsions — custom fumble line, repeated move fumbles, seed onset fix*). Either way the just-sent command is consumed and never executes.
- **The fumble line always appears as the direct reply to the command it swallowed**, never as unprompted ambient text *(2026-09-01)*.
- **Each confusion source picks its fumble wording through ability `101` (ConfuseMsg); without one the engine falls back to `You look around stupidly and do nothing!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p + imported Spells data for Stock; Paradigm's spells carry the same ability `101`, but its fallback wording is [NEEDS CONFIRMATION] — does a Paradigm card-void or rainbow2 fumble print this line?)*.
  - A command fumbles when your Confusion (ability `71`) value is above a roll of 0–99. The engine then prints line 1 of the ConfuseMsg message to you and line 2 (with your name) to the room, and adds an action delay of 1. *(Re-read [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_check_confusion` @0x420cb2–0x420dcb; an earlier note had the roll as 0–100; superseded 2026-10-09.)*
    - **Several confusions don't add: the highest Confusion value counts, and the highest ConfuseMsg number picks the wording** (`_get_user_ability_value` keeps the largest value for abilities `71` and `101`, @0x43d085–0x43d12b). They are two of the seven abilities that take the highest value instead of a sum; the whole rule for an ability total is in *Items, inventory & equipment → Abilities of carried items*.
    - A source whose ability `71` has `AbilVal` 0 uses its cast's rolled value: Stock convulsions #951 fumbles at a rolled 10–30%, mesmerize #1391 at 25%.
    - **At a value of 100 every checked command fumbles**, since the roll never reaches 100.
    - **A fumble always prints a line on Stock**: the source's message, or the default pair when the source has no ConfuseMsg or its message record doesn't exist. The only way to an empty line is a message record whose first line is blank.
  - With no ConfuseMsg on the source (or a missing message), it prints `You look around stupidly and do nothing!` to you and `<name> looks around stupidly and foams at the mouth!` to the room.
  - Most confusions carry message 8489, the generic `You fumble in confusion!` / `<name> fumbles about dazedly!`. Many have their own, e.g. stun `You are stunned!`, sleep `You are fast asleep.`, fear `You are too afraid to do that!`, stinking cloud `You retch uncontrollably!`, petrification `You struggle, but you are solid stone and do not move.`
  - **The room wording of the stinking cloud message is `<name> retches uncontrollably!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-04, capture `unrecognized-lines-20261004-122235`: `short orc warrior retches uncontrollably!`, a monster; realm not recorded)*. The user describes it as flavour text shown when a monster or player takes damage from stinking cloud, and probably other abilities *(2026-10-04)*. [NEEDS CONFIRMATION] — is it printed when the cloud damages the victim, or when the victim's action fumbles (line 2 of the ConfuseMsg, as the Stock routine above prints for a player)? The client only recognizes the line; nothing acts on it.
  - The fallback applies to spells with ability `71` and no `101`: on Stock hypnotic hands #300, card-void #502/#976, convulsions #951, rainbow2 #1163, blink #1225, mesmerize #1391; on Paradigm only card-void #502/#976 and rainbow2 #1163 (Paradigm gives hypnotic hands, convulsions, blink and mesmerize their own messages).
  - **Client use:** both seeds list the fallback line in those records' `ConfuseFumbleLine` (plus convulsions). `ConditionTracker` indexes every Confused record's fumble lines, so the line is recognized whichever confusion is active.
  - **Client use:** the three room wordings on record are `KnownPatterns.OtherFumbled`, recognized so they aren't staged as unrecognized lines; nothing subscribes.
- **Where Stock rolls the fumble** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_execute_input` @0x4502d9, and the attack and cast routines; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **On every typed command, before it is dispatched**, `break` included. A fumble returns without running the command. Whether a prompt follows the fumble line wasn't found on that path.
  - **Exempt:** an empty line (bare Enter), the bare word `x`, anything typed during the exit wait, and a command that goes into the typed-ahead queue (whether it is rolled when it later runs wasn't traced).
  - **Again inside the action routines:** a player's attack on a player (@0x42c17b), each round of an attack on a monster (@0x42d59b), and every cast routine (@0x43ff88, @0x44477c, @0x44717a, @0x44929a). So a typed cast is rolled twice, a typed attack once, and each round of a running fight once more.
  - **A fumbled round does not end the fight on Stock.** The swing or cast is skipped, the energy zeroed and the same action queued for the next round (@0x42d5b0–0x42d5c5, cast form @0x444791–0x4447ae), with no `*Combat Off*`. So on Stock a fight that fumbles a round needs no re-send; the *fumbled action is lost* rule of this topic, recorded from Paradigm reports, is about the command that was typed, which is lost on Stock too.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` The client takes a fight that has printed `*Combat Engaged*` to go on until `*Combat Off*`, a fumbled round included, and so sends no fresh attack for a fumble in it. That is recorded for Stock in the bullet before this one and not for Paradigm: does a Paradigm fight ever end on a fumbled round with no `*Combat Off*`?
- **A fumbled move has to REVERT its pending step or the tracker strands** *(2026-09-01)* — the unreverted move got wrongly matched against later unrelated text and stranded a tier-3 recovery backtrack indefinitely (no timeout watched its landing).
- **Implication for auto-combat:** an attack command (`aa` / `a`) that fumbles is consumed without hitting, so the engine must **re-issue its last attack** when it sees a fumble rather than assume the swing landed. Otherwise the monster goes unattacked until the user manually re-sends — the reported symptom of "monsters in room but not attacking unless I manually send attack commands" (report `paradigm-20260714-093614`).
- **The re-send covers EVERY client-sent command, not just a weapon swing — but only the CLIENT's own commands, never what the user typed** *(2026-09-09)*. A fumble eats whatever command was just sent; to perform it you re-send the same command. The client does this generically for anything IT sent — weapon swing, attack spell (immediately, not deferred to the next round tick), item use, door bash, and so on — because a user fighting confused shouldn't have to hand-repeat each eaten action. A command the **user typed** is never auto-repeated (re-sending a manual command is the user's call).
- **Client use:**
  - `MovementRefusalDetector` recognizes the fumble lines as movement refusals, reverting the pending move immediately. The lines aren't hardcoded — they come from each Confused MessageRecord's `ConfuseFumbleLine`, checked via `ConditionTracker.IsConfuseFumbleLine`.
  - Every fumble fires `ConditionTracker.ActionFailed` (on a `LastActionFailed` record OR a `ConfuseFumbleLine` match). The handler is `CombatManager.HandleFumble`, which decides in this order: (1) `CombatManager.OnActionFailed` re-sends the weapon swing WITH its engage-verification bookkeeping when the swing hasn't been answered yet, and that ends it; (2) the engine's own attack in a fight already engaged is left alone (`CombatManager.AttackAlreadyEngaged`: the weapon line last sent, or a cast of the announced attack spell); (3) anything else is re-sent by `EngineSendGate.ReplayLastClientCommand`, the last command that passed through the engine send gate. "Engaged" is `*Combat Engaged*` seen since the last attack the engine sent, with no `*Combat Off*` since; the bug report carries it as *Engaged since last attack*. (An earlier line had the handler call `OnActionFailed` and fall through to the replay with no engaged test, so a fumble mid-fight re-sent the swing or the attack cast; superseded 2026-10-09 by the *When to re-send an attack* rule of this topic.)
  - User-typed input bypasses that gate (it flows straight to `SendUserInput`), so it's never in the replay buffer.
  - A bare **movement** step is skipped by the replay (the fumbled-move revert already recovers it, and a second send would double-step).

### Convulsions — custom fumble line, repeated move fumbles, seed onset fix
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-01 (user + report `paradigm-20260901-080223`); CONFIRMED 2026-09-02 (report `paradigm-20260902-113201`); CONFIRMED 2026-09-05 (report `paradigm-20260905-183956`); default fumble line OBSERVED 2026-09-28 (Stock DLL)*

- **`convulsions` customizes the fumble line to `You convulse violently!` (with its own onset `You are in convulsions!`)** *(CONFIRMED 2026-09-01)*. Its wear-off (`AppliedEndsWith`) is `Your body returns to normal.`.
- **Convulsions can fumble several consecutive moves in a row, well inside a handful of seconds** *(CONFIRMED 2026-09-02, report `paradigm-20260902-113201`)*. The per-move revert is correct, but `LoopRunner`'s bounded recovery budget (3 attempts) was shared between genuine desyncs and these fumbles — three convulsion bonks on the same room burned the whole budget in under 10 seconds and permanently failed the loop, leaving the character standing there Confused with nothing left running.
- **The correct onset is `You are in convulsions!`** *(CONFIRMED 2026-09-05, report `paradigm-20260905-183956`)* — confirmed live in both this report and `paradigm-20260901-080223`. The shipped `convulsions` message record's `AppliedMessage` was wired to the wrong line, so the 2026-09-02 recovery-budget exemption never actually engaged for a real convulsions episode:
  - Both bundled seeds (`Messages.paradigm.seed.json` and `Messages.stock.seed.json`) had `AppliedMessage: "You look around stupidly and do nothing!"` on the merged `convulsions` record — that's one of the fumble wordings (correctly still listed in `ConfuseFumbleLine`), not the condition's own onset line.
  - Since that fumble text never actually appears as ambient onset text in a session, the record's `AppliedMessage` never matched, `ConditionTracker` never added it to `_active`, and `IsConfused` stayed false for the whole convulsions duration — so `LoopRunner.EnterRecovery` charged every fumble-caused block against `MaxRecoverAttempts` same as a real desync, burning the budget in under 20 seconds and permanently failing the loop.
  - The onset had previously been found and hand-corrected by the user in a per-set `messages.json` override that predates the realm-flavored split — a one-time legacy-messages migration (since removed; historically `DataMigration.RetireLegacyMessagesOnce`) retired that override to `.bak` during the split since the shipped seed never carried the same correction, silently reintroducing the bug.
- **`You look around stupidly and do nothing!` is the engine's default fumble line, and Stock convulsions uses it** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p + imported Spells data)*. Stock convulsions #951 carries no ConfuseMsg (ability `101`), so it fumbles with the default; Paradigm's #951 carries its own message (8640), and live Paradigm convulsions fumble with `You convulse violently!`. See *Confusion fumbles — actions fail and must be re-sent*. (An earlier note held this wording as an unconfirmed third convulsions line from a messages.md export; superseded 2026-09-28.)
- **Client use:**
  - `MovementRefusalDetector` recognizes BOTH `You fumble in confusion!` and `You convulse violently!` as movement refusals, reverting the pending move immediately; it also recognizes the default `You look around stupidly and do nothing!` (same revert mechanic), so a move fumbled that way doesn't strand the tracker. These lines are no longer hardcoded in the detector — they come from each Confused MessageRecord's `ConfuseFumbleLine` via `ConditionTracker.IsConfuseFumbleLine`.
  - `LoopRunner.EnterRecovery` reads `ConditionTracker.IsConfused` (wired via `SetConfusedCheck`) and doesn't charge an attempt against `MaxRecoverAttempts` while it's true — the reroute/resend still happens every time, it just isn't bounded by the same budget a real mapping problem is.
  - Both bundled seeds' `convulsions` record now has `AppliedMessage: "You are in convulsions!"`; `AppliedEndsWith` (`Your body returns to normal.`) was already correct. No code change — `ConditionTracker` and `LoopRunner` already behaved exactly as designed once fed the right onset text.

### Form of the monkey — self-buff that confuses the caster
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-02 (user)*

- **`form of the monkey` inherently confuses the caster for the buff's whole duration.** While the self-buff is up (onset `The spirit of the monkey inhabits your body!`), each action has a chance to fumble as `You are distracted!`.
- **There is no separate wear-off for the confusion** — it ends when the **form itself** wears off (`The spirit of the monkey has left your body!`). **Client encoding:** the `form of the monkey` message record carries `Confused` (set on the form's onset, cleared on the form's wear-off, which triggers the single-state confusion clear); the separate `You are distracted!` record carries `LastActionFailed` (+ `Confused` as the missed-onset fallback) to drive the per-action re-send.

### Knockdown — a movement-preventing hold
*Status: CONFIRMED (report `paradigm-20260714-002413`)*

- **A knockdown is a movement-preventing (held) status.** The hit lands as `You are knocked off your feet, and land with a heavy thump!` (third-person `{s} is knocked flat!`).
- **While down, the standing status is `You are flat on your back!`** — which is also what the server prints as the **move refusal** when you try to walk while knocked down (a bonk, no room redisplay).
- **It clears with `You get back on your feet.`**.
- **`knockdown` (#318) is AC −10, Dodge −20, Accuracy −5 and HoldPerson for 12 s, so you take more damage while it lasts — roughly a 1–2% effect** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-30, user)*. The grimhound's trample carries it as a hit spell (see *Combat → Monster on-hit procs (`AttHitSpell-N`) are physical attacks, not casts*).
- **Client use:**
  - `MovementRefusalDetector` matches the `You are flat on your back!` move refusal.
  - `LoopSimulator` applies a hit spell's AC / Dodge / Accuracy change for its duration, and neither walks on nor flees (the Health run trigger waits) while a HoldPerson hit spell is on (`Held`).
  - The applied/clear pair maps to the `MovementPrevented` flag, so the local hold (`SelfHeldResponder` → `HeldGate`) holds our own loop for the duration exactly as a confused leader's does. A held leader or solo character has no leader to send `.@held` to, so the local `HeldGate` alone pauses the loop.
  - The automatic `curp` / freedom can be set to wait until the fight is over — see *One between-round spell per combat round*.
  - **Client policy:** a move that lands in its predicted room (walked or follow-dragged) drops a latched `MovementPrevented` flag, since a held character can't move and a held follower isn't dragged (see *Party → A follower who can't move is left behind*). `RoomTracker.MoveConfirmed` → `ConditionTracker.ClearFlag` covers a wear-off line that never arrived (report `paradigm-20261003-161904`).
