  - Above 900 the whole display is replaced by the single line `You are blind!`, with an exclamation mark (@0x46bd68): a room too bright to see in. *Moving while blind* has the same wording as the onset of blindness. The blind condition itself (`+0x6f5 & 0x10`) makes `_can_see` print `You are blind.` (@0x46bd19). Fighting in either state costs accuracy and defence (*Combat → Monster target selection — who it swings at once fighting*, the rank and blind bullets).
  - **The Stock string has no full stop at its end**: `The room is %s - you can't see anything` (also noted under *Wire, prompt & command output → Message catalogue (lines the client parses)*). The first bullet of this topic quotes the very-dark line with one; that wording came from MMUD-Explorer's message list, which took it from Stock *(user 2026-10-09: "we got the dark lines from MME which took them from stock i believe")*, so for Stock the DLL string is the one to trust. `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Whether Paradigm prints the full stop; a Paradigm capture of a dark room settles it. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`.)

**Client use:**
- The tracker keeps position by projecting the sent direction onto the current room's graph edge (`RoomTracker.NoteDarkRoomEntered`): when the pending move resolves to a known neighbour it advances there; when the edge is unmapped it holds the last position (stays Pending) rather than guessing.

### Moving while blind
*Status: CONFIRMED (capture 2026-07-11)*

- **A move made while *blinded* succeeds but starves the room display, printing only `You are blind.`** — same shape as the dark-room case, but it's the player who can't see, not the room. A blinded player who sends a move gets no name, no `Obvious exits:`, no description — just the single line `You are blind.` (period) — yet the move **traverses** (party followers are dragged in the sent direction).
- **Three lines mention blindness — distinguish them:**
  - the **onset** `You are blind!` (exclamation, applies the Blinded flag);
  - the **move-succeeded** `You are blind.` (period, starves the display);
  - the **refusal** `You can't see well enough to move.` (a bonk — the move did *not* happen, caught as an impairment refusal).
- **Verified from a live capture:** `:s` → `You are blind.` → `Suijin walks into the room from the north.` (the party followed south) with no room render; the map had frozen at the source room until this path landed.

**Client use:**
- Only the period form drives dead-reckoning: `RoomTracker.NoteBlindMove` advances along the pending move's mapped edge just like `NoteDarkRoomEntered`, but leaves `IsInDarkRoom` untouched (carried light can't cure blindness, and the dark-room attack-line combat path must not switch on).

### Light sources
*Status: CONFIRMED (verbs; bare-CR redisplay user 2026-08-11; visibility user 2026-07-24; burnout line capture 2026-07-11)*

- **`use <item>` readies a light (torch, lantern); `rem <item>` removes it.** Lights follow the same trade-places rule as `eq` — `use`-ing a new light swaps out the current one (if usable), **on Paradigm only** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "the swap is paradigm only")*; Stock refuses the second light (next bullet).
- **Stock refuses a second light instead of swapping** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_light` @0x46728e–0x467297; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. With a light already lit, lighting another answers `You already have something lit!` and nothing changes, so on Stock the lit one has to be `rem`'d first. The swap in the bullet before this one is Paradigm's *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user)*. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **Stock: `use <light>` is `light <light>`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_use` @0x460efc and `_cmd_light` @0x46713b; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_cmd_use` hands any `ItemType` 6 item to `_cmd_light`, which checks in this order:
  - you can't use the item: `You may not light that item!`
  - it isn't a light: `You cannot light %s!`
  - a light is already lit: `You already have something lit!`
  - success: `You lit the %s.`, and the room sees `%s lights %s %s.` (your name, a word not read, the item).
  - A light with no uses left answers `You must recharge that before you may light it again.` (@0x46739d).
- **Stock: one light at a time, and it is not a worn slot** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_light` @0x46728e, `_display_inventory_items` @0x439c0b; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The lit light is a pack item the player record points at, not one of the 20 worn slots. `i` lists it as `<name> (Readied/<N>)`, where `<N>` is its uses divided by 10, rounded down, so it reads 0 for the last nine uses.
- **Stock: a lit light burns one use per medium character update** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_medium_update_character` @0x422906; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_background_medium` runs that update every 3 fast ticks, and both intervals are constants in the DLL (*Timing & rounds → The engine clock — one fast tick drives every timer*), so a lit light burns a use about every 3 seconds. (An earlier note said the update's length is a sysop timer and isn't in the DLL, and left the burn rate unrecorded; superseded 2026-10-09.)
- **Stock: `rem <light>` on the lit one answers `You have removed %s and extinguished it.`**, and the room sees `%s removes %s!` *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_remove_armour` @0x41cede–0x41cf70; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. A light that isn't the lit one answers `You do not have %s lit.` Unlike taking off armour or a weapon, it does not break combat.
  - **The line is its own string, not the plain removal with words added** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`, string pushed @0x41cf50)*: `You have removed torch and extinguished it.` What Paradigm prints for taking off a lit light is not recorded.
- **Stock: a `drop` or `hide` of a light can take the lit one, and that puts it out** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_remove_item_from_inventory` @0x41b2c8, called by `_cmd_drop` @0x4666f9 and `_cmd_hide` @0x466e6f; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*.
  - **The removal takes the first pack slot holding that item number** (@0x41b317–0x41b321), so with a lit torch and a spare it is the one in the lower slot that goes, lit or not.
  - **When the item is a light (`ItemType` 6, @0x41b32a) and that slot is the lit one, the light is put out**: the lit slot (player byte +0x6ba, which `_cmd_light` sets @0x4672e8) is set to 0xff (@0x41b334–0x41b340) and the light's IlluTarget (54) value comes off the player's lit-light value (@0x41b347–0x41b356). Nothing is printed at that step.
  - **The lit light has no "only when the last copy goes" protection.** That rule covers the readied weapon (@0x41b39b–0x41b3cd) and the 20 worn slots (@0x41b3d3–0x41b41d) only.
  - **Client policy** for a light flagged for auto-discard: *Items, inventory & equipment → Item batching: Paradigm counted commands vs Stock one-per-command*.
- **Stock: a bare `light` prints the room's light band** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_light` @0x467194; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: `The current light level is %s`, with no full stop, e.g. `The current light level is dimly lit`. The band can be read without moving.
- **Stock: how the light level is built** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_get_light_level` @0x41f09e; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `light = the room's Light + your Illumination (13) total + for every player in the room, you included, (that player's lit-light value + RoomIllu (14) total)`, capped at 900, and then your BlindingLight (53) total is added on top. The lit-light value is the IlluTarget (54) of the light a player has lit.
  - So **another player's lit torch or RoomIllu lights the room for everyone in it, and Illumination (13) helps only its owner.**
  - **Bands** (the words `light` and the dark-room line print): below −200 `pitch black`; −200 to −151 `very dark`; −150 to −101 `barely visible`; −100 to −1 `dimly lit`; 0 to 199 `Regular Light`; 200 to 899 `Daylight`; 900 and up `You are blind!`.
  - **You can't see when the level is below −150** (`_can_see` @0x46bd46), so only `pitch black` and `very dark` appear in the dark-room line (*Dark rooms — no name, no exits, traversal inferred from no bonk*), or when it is above 900, which only BlindingLight on top of the cap can reach.
- **`use <light>` only grants the ability to see — it does NOT re-display the room** *(CONFIRMED, user 2026-08-11)*. After lighting in a dark room you must send a **bare carriage return** to redisplay:
  - if the light now lets you see, the full room prints (name / exits / `Also here:`, revealing any monsters that were standing there unseen);
  - if it's still too dark, the "can't see" dark message prints again.
- **The bare CR is the ONLY way to discover a *standing* (non-attacking) monster in a just-lit room** — the dark display never listed it, and `DarkRoomCombatWatcher` only catches a monster that *swings* (its attack line).
- **A readied light is visible to other players** *(CONFIRMED, user 2026-07-24)* — an onlooker sees the lit source the way they see worn gear, so it counts as "shown," not hidden.
- **A readied torch burning out prints exactly `Your torch flickers and goes out.`** *(CONFIRMED, capture 2026-07-11)* — one line, period-terminated, no name/exits. (An earlier note gave the line as `Your <item> flickers and goes out.` for every light; superseded 2026-10-09 for Stock, where the line is the item's own, as the bullet after this one records. The capture's realm isn't recorded.)
  - It is the *only* signal the light is gone: the inventory `i` dump still lists the item as readied until the next dump lands, so the display lies about a light that no longer exists in the meantime.
- **Stock: the burn-out line is per item** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_medium_update_character` @0x42294b–0x422a62, with the 1.11p item records and message table; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. At 0 uses the light goes out and, unless the item is flagged to be kept, leaves the pack. If the item names a message, its first line goes to you and its second to the room; if it names none, you see `%s is no longer lit!` and the room sees `%s's %s just went out.`; if it names a message that doesn't exist, nothing is printed.
  - **The flag that keeps a burnt-out light in the pack is the item byte `+0x42a`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, same routine, the test @0x422942 ahead of the removal @0x42294d)*, the byte that behaves as the data's `Retain After Uses`. No `ItemType` 6 row has `Retain After Uses` set in the Stock 1.11p or the Paradigm 1.9.1 Items table *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, game data: 10 and 12 rows)*, so in the data as it stands every light that burns out is gone from the pack.
  - **Paradigm: what a burn-out does to the item is not recorded.** **Client policy** (2026-10-10): the client applies Stock's rule on both realms: the light is no longer lit, and it is gone from what is held unless its record is `Retain After Uses`. `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` On Paradigm, does a light that burns out leave the pack?

  | Item | Line to you |
  |---|---|
  | torch (175) | `Your torch flickers and goes out.` |
  | lantern (176), brass lamp (286), marsh light (692) | `Your lamp runs out of oil, and goes out.` |
  | moon-lamp (1153) | `The light in the moon-lamp flickers, and goes out.` |
  | light ball (1085) | `Your light ball disappears out of existance.` |
  | scaled lantern (1233), glowing pearl (1234) | `scaled lantern is no longer lit!` / `glowing pearl is no longer lit!` |
  | Eternal Fire (935), incense (284) | nothing (their message numbers, 66 and 121, don't exist) |

**Client use:**
- Auto-light must send the bare CR after readying the light or it walks past passive mobs (the "lights a torch but doesn't re-check the room" report).
- The `@inv` remote report (carried items an onlooker can't see) deliberately excludes the readied light, reporting only the pack + key ring.
- Lighting a light doesn't end a sneak or a hide: `_cmd_light` clears only the rest, and a light's IlluTarget is applied without a cast (*Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine*, the `use <item>` bullet of *What ends a sneak*). So `AutoLightProvisioner`'s `use <light>` is never held for sneak keeping and marks nothing broken; its `rem` is held (`SneakKept`). A light that casts a spell (incense, which carries no IlluTarget) is marked like any other casting item (`ItemUseStealthRule`).
- On a burn-out line the inventory takes the light off what is held at once (`InventoryManager.NoteLitLightBurnedOut`, subscribed to `KnownPatterns.LightBurnedOut` ahead of the auto-light handler): a light the last `i` read listed as lit comes off the lit slot, and one lit since (Stock's `You lit the <item>.`, whose copy is still in the pack list) is taken out of the pack; either goes back in only when its record is `Retain After Uses`. Before 2026-10-10 the lit light stayed listed until the next `i` read, and a death in between recorded a light that no longer existed. A light lit since the last read on Paradigm, whose lighting line isn't recorded, can't be told from the rest of the pack and waits for the next read.
- The auto-light path latches on a burn-out line (`AutoLightProvisioner.OnReadiedLightExpired`, `KnownPatterns.LightBurnedOut`) to discount the stale readied value and re-ready a carried spare once the room's "can't see" line confirms it went dark. (The latch is kept beside the inventory's own clearing: with the lit slot cleared it changes nothing, and it still covers a snapshot the provisioner is handed that hasn't been.) The pattern reads the torch's `Your <item> flickers and goes out.`, and the other lines of the *Stock: the burn-out line is per item* table in this topic: `Your lamp runs out of oil, and goes out.`, `The light in the moon-lamp flickers, and goes out.`, `Your light ball disappears out of existance.` and the default `<item> is no longer lit!`. Anchored full-line so a mob-flavour "flickers" elsewhere can't false-trigger. (An earlier line gave the pattern as `^Your .+ flickers and goes out\.$` alone, which on Stock matched the torch only, so a burnt-out lamp was never relit; superseded 2026-10-09.)
- `AutoLightProvisioner.ReadyLight` sends `rem <lit>` before `use <new>` on both realms, so Stock's refusal of a second light is not met in the ordinary swap. `You already have something lit!` is one of the fixed replies the unrecognized-line watcher skips (*Wire, prompt & command output → Fixed command replies (refusals and housekeeping notices)*); nothing acts on it.
- `InventoryManager` reads `You have removed <item> and extinguished it.` ahead of the plain removal (`RemovedLitLightRegex`, `UnreadyLight`): the light stops being listed as lit and is a pack copy again, under one notice. Until 2026-10-10 the plain pattern read the item as `<item> and extinguished it`, added a pack entry of that name and left the light listed as lit. A plain `You have removed <item>.` naming the light listed as lit, with nothing worn by that name, is handled the same way, so the light is not listed twice whatever the realm prints.
- `InventoryManager.RemoveHeld`: a copy that leaves (dropped, hidden, sold, handed over) with no pack entry to take it from, while the light listed as lit has that name, was the lit one, and it stops being listed as lit. With a spare and the lit one both held the spare is taken off first, since which the game took can't be told. The lit light was otherwise cleared only by a full `i`, so auto-discard, which counts it as a pack copy, sent a second discard for a light already gone.

### Monsters in dark rooms
*Status: CONFIRMED (attack-line engage; name dedupe 2026-07-21, user; late populate 2026-07-22, user)*

- **A monster in a dark room is invisible to the room display but still attacks — engage it by the name in its attack line.** With no `Also here:` line (the dark room prints only the "can't see" line, see *Dark rooms — no name, no exits, traversal inferred from no bonk*), the only evidence a hostile shares the room is its incoming attack line: a miss `The <monster> <verb> at you`, in dark cyan *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "always dark cyan as far as i know")*, or a hit `The <monster> <verb> you for N damage!`, in bright red (`ESC[1;31m`) *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10: all 46 such lines matched in 19 Paradigm captures; Realm: Paradigm, Stock not seen)*. The colours' home is *Wire, prompt & command output → Message catalogue (lines the client parses)*, the two *Incoming mob attack* rows. (An earlier form of this bullet said the attack line was rendered in dark cyan, hit and miss alike; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - The `<monster>` token is the monster's real name, so `a <monster>` (e.g. `a cave bear`) attacks it exactly as if it had been listed under `Also here:`.
  - Attacking a monster that **isn't** in the room draws `Your command had no effect.` (with talk slow on — see *Combat → Attacking a monster that isn't in the room*) — the signal that the target is gone (retract it and stop swinging).
- **In a dark room, a distinct display name is a distinct enemy — dedupe reveals by name, never by monster record** *(2026-07-21, user)*.
  - A mob can swing more than once per round and the dark room re-emits its attack line every round, so four `The cave lizard swings at you` lines are **not** four lizards — the client collapses same-name reveals to one entity.
  - But `cave lizard` and `small cave lizard` (e.g. we're on one, a partner announces the other) are **two separate enemies**, even if they share a Monsters-table record — so the dedupe keys on the **name string**, not the resolved monster number; collapsing by record would drop a live mob.
  - Two genuinely same-named mobs can't be told apart in the dark, so they read as one until the first dies — the survivor's next swing re-reveals it and combat re-engages. Over-count is thus impossible and under-count self-heals.
- **A dark room's monsters can populate *after* entry, not only at the moment you arrive** *(2026-07-22, user)*. A room that reads empty on arrival (no attack line yet) can still have a hostile reveal itself a beat later via its first swing.
  - Empirically a reveal often lands at 0ms (synchronous with entry — over a 1-hour hunt all 334 populated rooms revealed at 0ms), but that is area/condition-dependent, **not** a guarantee: the delayed-populate case is real.

**Client use:**
- The client injects the attack-revealed monster into the room's entity list so auto-combat engages it (`DarkRoomCombatWatcher`).
- The dark-room settle window (`DarkRoomSettleGate`, ~1.0s per dark advance) must hold before the walker moves on — it's the only late-reveal guard for a room that looked empty at entry. It is a justified safety buffer, not dead time: do **not** trim or short-circuit it on the strength of an all-synchronous sample. (See *Per-hop movement speed* for its realm-coupled cost.)

### `look <dir>` — peeking an adjacent room
*Status: CONFIRMED (closed-barrier case 2026-09-08, user + report `stock-20260908-205441`)*

- **`look <dir>` peeks the adjacent room with a full room display, but the player never moves.** Looking into an exit (`look north`, `l e`, `peer …`) renders the neighbouring room exactly like walking in would — its title, its `You notice … here.` item/cash survey, and its `Also here:` monster/player list — yet the player stays put.
- **It is a *preview*, not an entry**, so any room-entry automation keyed on the room display (auto-get items, cash pickup, combat engage) must be suppressed for it — otherwise the client fires `get`/attacks at a room it isn't standing in (the reported bug).
- **The player's *own* room is unaffected:** walking in for real re-renders the room outside the window and the automation runs normally.
- **A closed door/gate blocks the peek** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-08, user + report `stock-20260908-205441`)*. `look <dir>` at an exit whose barrier is **shut** renders no room — the server answers *"The door is closed in that direction!"* instead.
  - **On Stock that wording is `look`'s alone** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_look` @0x45204d, @0x4520f8; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: `_move_user` never prints it. A refused move through a shut door prints one of the lines in *Refused ("bonked") moves*, and a `look` at a wall prints `There are no exits to the %s!` (`There are no exits upwards!` / `downwards!`; `_cmd_look` @0x45209e–0x4520c8), not the move's `There is no exit in that direction!`.
  - The obvious-exits line flags it ahead of time (`closed door north` / `closed gate north`), so a peek that must read the neighbour has to **open the barrier first, then look**.

**Client use:**
- The client arms a short suppression window on sending the look (`RoomTracker.NoteLookSent`); the display consumers that run *before* the `Obvious exits:` line poll `IsPeekSuppressed()` to skip the peeked room, and the window is consumed when `NoteRoomObserved` fires on the exits line.
- `AutoPartyManager.OnRoomAlsoHere` is one of those consumers: players a peek lists stand in the next room, so they are neither invited on sight nor taken as arrived by a party reform. Before 2026-10-08 a reconnect reform spent its invite on a peeked listing and got `You don't see <name> here.` (report `paradigm-20260923-092317`). A reform still waiting for members asks for another redisplay of its own room when a listing is passed over, since the one it sends may be what was passed over.
- `IsPeekSuppressed()` lets one display through while a peek is armed: that of a move sent before the look, once the game has echoed that move. The server answers in order, so that display is the room just entered and the peek's follows it (`e` then `l e` typed quickly). A move not yet echoed leaves the peek reading in force, since it may be a step the game never answered.
- The Warped Asylum look-sweep opens the barrier then looks (its rooms gate siblings behind bashable doors); before #346 a shut door on a peek direction failed the whole maze solve out.

### Room display parsing — the room title is positional, not just bright cyan
*Status: CONFIRMED (user; report `paradigm-20260829-154032`)*

- **Bright cyan is not uniquely the room title — an engine-side palette can remap spell/ability text to it.** A player running a palette that shifts spell/ability lines from dark blue to bright cyan makes every `<player> invokes the way of the monkey!`-style broadcast render in the **same bright cyan as room names**, deterministically (not an occasional fluke).
- **Such a line can arrive in the arrival burst immediately *before* the real title**, so colour can't tell an ability line from the title under that palette.
- **The room display is one contiguous block** — title → `Also here:` → `Obvious exits:` — so async player broadcasts land before it, never between the title and the exits line. The title is therefore the **last** bright-cyan line before `Obvious exits:`.
- **A miss or a dodge never shares the title's colour: those print dark cyan** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "always dark cyan as far as i know")*. The statement and its capture are in *Wire, prompt & command output → Message catalogue (lines the client parses)*, the *Incoming mob attack — miss* row.
  - **Client use:** `CombatLineClassifier` reads no miss or dodge off a bright-cyan line, so a title printed while a fight is on (the room read again, or a step taken with combat still engaged) is left untagged in the Wire Inspector's Classified pane, and a title that leads with a monster's name (`Dire Wolf Lair`) is not that monster's attack under a break hold (`MonsterAttackLine.IsBy`; report `paradigm-20261010-215619`).
- **Stock: the order of one room display** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_room_desc` @0x436f5d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  1. the can-see test (`_can_see`); when it fails, its one line is the whole display (*Dark rooms — no name, no exits, traversal inferred from no bonk*);
  2. the room name, in bright cyan (@0x4370d4);
  3. in a `Colliseum` room while the arena switch (`0x4790e8`) is off: `NOTE: This room is *not* a death-free zone right now!` and `Treat this room as you would any other combat zone.` (@0x4370f3–0x437123);
  4. the long description, only when the caller asks for it (@0x43713d);
  5. `You notice … here.` (`_display_items_in_room` @0x4363a9): coins first, highest denomination first, then the visible items, joined with `, `. The whole line is left out when the floor is empty (@0x436c19–0x436c1f);
  6. `Also here: `: players first, in user-slot order, then the room's monster slots 0–14, joined with `, ` and ended with a full stop (@0x437201–0x437610). The line is left out when nobody is listed;
  7. `Obvious exits: ` (`_display_visible_exits` @0x43584d);
  8. `The room is barely visible` or `The room is dimly lit`, when the light level is below 0 (@0x437643–0x43765c).
- **Paradigm shows the same order for the lines the client reads, and likewise prints no floor line for an empty floor** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, reports `paradigm-20261009-082958` and `paradigm-20261009-185106`; Realm: Paradigm)*: room name, `You notice … here.`, `Also here:`, `Obvious exits:` (e.g. `Tagesh Highlands, Southern Road` / `You notice 2 silver nobles here.` / `Also here: <player>, <player>.` / `Obvious exits: east, west`), and rooms with nothing on the floor go from the name straight to `Also here:` or `Obvious exits:`. A `sea` answers with the floor line alone (report `paradigm-20261009-164508`: `You notice 2 magma key, 2 black star key here.` after each `sea`).
  - **Client use:** a room's floor is read before the exits line that confirms the room, on both realms. `DeathRecoveryManager` reads the arrival's own floor at the room change (`FloorWasJustRead`): Stock's loose pile in `OnRoomChanged`, Paradigm's corpse in `CorpseOnArrival`. `RoomTransition.Displayed` says whether a room display decided a transition: an arrival, a re-display of the room the character stands in (both rooms the same), the first display after a reconnect, a booked landing its own display corrects. It is false for a dark or blind move, a manual locate, a saved room at load, a move the game refused and a landing booked ahead of its display.
- **Stock: an `Also here:` entry** *(same source)*. A player is the name, then `*` when the engine's evil-mark test passes, then `(Hidden)` with no space before it; a hidden player is listed only for a viewer with the see-hidden status bit (`0x6f5 & 0x20`; @0x4371c3–0x4371d9). A monster gets ` (Charmed)` when it is charmed and tied to the viewer (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Spell targeting: monster type tags*).
- **Stock: the `Obvious exits:` line** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_visible_exits` @0x43584d, `_visible_exit` @0x4357de, `_secret_visible_exit` @0x43577b; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The entries are joined with `, ` and the line ends with no full stop. With no visible exit it reads `Obvious exits: NONE!!!` (@0x436376–0x43638d). By exit type (the codes are in *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*):
  - `Key` (2): `closed door <dir>` when its state isn't 0, else `open door <dir>`.
  - `Door` (7): `closed door <dir>` for state 1 and for state 2, so a shut door and a locked one read the same; `open door <dir>` for state 0. `Gate` (11): `closed gate <dir>` / `open gate <dir>`.
  - Up and down use `above` and `below`, and a door or a gate there reads `closed trap door above` / `open trap door above` (and `… below`) (@0x43631b–0x436333).
  - `Hidden` (6): listed only once found by a search (flag 4) or opened by its actions (flag 8). The text is line 1 of the exit's label message with the direction word, else `secret passage <dir>`; the built-in strings vary in their capitals (`Secret passage north`, `secret passage East`). A hidden exit with only the passable flag (1) can be walked but isn't listed.
  - `Trap` (9): a plain direction, unless its state is 2 (a lever trapdoor). `Timed` (16): a plain direction, and only while open.
  - `Text` (10) and `Remote Action` (12) exits aren't listed.
  - A plain direction word carries the filler letter and backspace of *Wire, prompt & command output → Direction words on the wire: a filler letter and a backspace*; the door, gate and passage forms are whole fixed strings and don't.

**Client use:**
- The room-name detector anchors on **position**: `RoomDisplayParser` keeps the nearest bright-cyan line to the exits, not the first in the block.

### Rooms the data leaves unnamed
*Status: mixed; tags on each bullet · Realm: both (counts differ)*

- **Some rooms have no name in the imported Rooms table** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, game-data lookup, `Rooms.json` `Name` null)*:
  - Stock (`data-v1.11p`): 140 rooms.
    - 134 on map 15: the gang-house rooms. Eighteen of them each host a `Gang Shop #<n>` (`Shops` rows numbered between 125 and 145, `ShopType` 11). Paradigm's data has all 134 under names, 49 different ones (`Silver House Room` and `Blue House Room` 12 rooms each, `Black House Room` 11, `White House Room` and `Gold House Room` 10 each, and others such as `Orange House Vault`, `Orange House Shop`, `Entrance Orange House Room`). *Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences* counts these 134 among the Stock rooms Paradigm has under another name.
    - 6 on map 1: `1/2431`–`1/2435` and `1/2603`.
  - Paradigm (`data-Paradigm-1.9.1`): 16 rooms. The same 6 on map 1, and 10 on map 5 (`5/246`, `5/1091`–`5/1099`).
  - What the map 1 and map 5 rooms are isn't recorded: nothing here says they are gang-house rooms.
- **Each gang-house room's name is defined by the sysop, and the rooms of one house can all have different names** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user; Realm: both)*. The user's words: "each gang house room name is sysop defined, they can all be different and its the same on paradigm but paradigm ships the ganghouse rooms named with their MDB". So the Paradigm set carries names where the Stock set has none, and a board's own names can differ from them.
- **A gang's house name can change whenever the sysop edits it, and the change typically only shows after a cleanup has run** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user)*. With each room named on its own, a rename can be of one room at a time. When exactly a change shows, other than "typically after a cleanup", is not recorded.
- **The printed name of a gang-house room is the same for every character on the realm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user)*. It does not depend on who is looking.
- **Stock: where the title line comes from** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_room_desc` @0x436f5d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The routine prints the room record's own name field (record `+0x105`, format `%s\r`, @0x4370cd–0x4370d9) for every room alike; no routine that names a gang-house room apart was found. One branch replaces that line: when the record's text at `+0x13a` reads `FILE DESCRIPTION` and its field at `+0x181` is not empty (@0x43708c–0x4370ac), the text is read from a file through `_display_desc_from_file` (@0x439598), whose failure message is `Can't display gang house file %s` (@0x43966b). What that file holds, and which rooms have it set, was not traced. Guards and emblems are in *Items, inventory & equipment → Gang houses and guard emblems*.
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-11: "learned room names are per realm on a BBS"; "we shouldnt be writing in the game data file"): a name learned for such a room is kept per realm of a BBS, filed under the game-data set whose room numbers it goes by, and the game data files are never written. A name seen on one realm is not put on the map of another.
- **Client policy:** the client treats every room the data leaves unnamed the same way, taking the name it prints and taking another when it prints another. The user's statements above are about gang houses; for the map 1 and map 5 rooms the client's handling is its own choice, not a recorded mechanic.

**Client use:**
- `RoomTracker` adopts a predicted neighbour that has no name when the display's exits are all exits of that room, and takes the printed name (`MatchesPredictedNameless`, `TryMatchNullNameNeighbour`; `NameLearned` asks the user whether to keep it).
  - Because the name can change, a room the data leaves unnamed that already bears a learned name is matched the same way when the display has another name (`MatchesPredictedRenamed`, `ArrivesInRoomTheDataLeavesUnnamed`): adopted on its exits, the new name replacing the old on the map, the user asked again. Only with a move in flight that predicts the room, since the rooms of one house can share a name and exits. (An earlier form also re-learned with no move in flight, `TryRelearnRenamedRoom`; removed 2026-10-11, it renamed the room stood in from another room's display.)
  - Never for a room the data names. Whether a display that fits is the arrival is weighed by the walk (`ReadUnnamedArrival`, 2026-10-16). **Client policy** (a weighting of the client's, not an engine fact): the room one step along the move just sent is taken to be the one shown, so a room of that name anywhere else on the map doesn't count against it, and a room renamed to a name the data has elsewhere (a `Kitchen`) is re-learned. The rooms the walk leaves open are the room being left and its other neighbours. With the move echoed (*Movement on the wire — command echo, failure lines, and what actually moves you*), the display is the arrival; before the echo, a display one of those rooms could have shown is that room's and is held. With no echo seen on the statline, a neighbour the data names that could have shown the display as its own (`RoomGraphManager.NamedInDataCouldShow`: the same name, every exit shown is one of its exits, and every exit its exits line always prints is shown, by the Stock `Obvious exits:` bullet of *Room display parsing — the room title is positional, not just bright cyan* and the look-alike bullet of *Wire, prompt & command output → Hang-up / lost carrier*; Paradigm's exits line is not recorded beyond those) is taken to be the one shown, for a room with no name as for one that bears a name (for one that bears a name, the room being left counts too when the data names it, as it did under the earlier check), and is left to the name re-anchor; the same holds with no move in flight (`TryMatchNullNameNeighbour`). A `look <dir>` into such a room answered before the step is dropped as the look's (`ObservationLooksLikePendingMoveOutcome` asks `ReadUnnamedArrival`). (Until 2026-10-16 a room bearing a name was held to every room the data names with the printed name and exits covering the ones shown, `DataNamesRoomShowing`, and was confirmed in that room elsewhere on the map; a room with no name was held to nothing, and took a peeked neighbour's name. For a short while on 2026-10-11 the earlier check was on the nameless rule as well; taken off the same day, it confirmed the tracker in another room on every visit to a house with such a name. The printed-exits floor is what keeps that case learned: the street's display always shows its way north.)
  - A display that fits the room being left while the move has not been echoed is a redisplay of that room, not the arrival (`LooksLikeSourceRelook`, the test the plain predicted-neighbour match makes). With no echo seen on the statline that test, by timing, is made for a room bearing a name only, as before; with one, for a room with no name too. A room being left that the data leaves unnamed and that hasn't been shown since we came to it (put there by hand, or come back into the game in it) may be shown under a new name: before the echo, a display under another name that fits its exits is held as its own (`MayBeSourceUnderAnotherName`), and one that fits only it, before the step is echoed or on a statline with no echo, leaves the tracker Pending rather than Suspect (logged at Info: with no echo, a step that landed somewhere unexpected waits there instead of going Suspect). With no echo seen, a display that fits it and the room ahead is still taken for the room ahead.
  - With no echo seen, a display held as a re-look of the room being left may have been the arrival in a room that looks the same. When the next display for that move fits the room a second move queued behind it leads to, the held display is taken as the arrival and named from, and the new one is read for the second move (`TryTakeHeldArrival`); before, the new display was taken for the room ahead, which took the name of the room beyond it. Only for a room the data leaves unnamed, and never across a teleporting exit. Not when a named neighbour, or the room being left when the data names it, could have shown the held display. And, when the held display is under another name than the room ahead bears, not when the new display shows the room ahead under the name it bears (its own arrival, the held display a re-look), nor when the new display could be the room ahead under a new name and the room beyond isn't shown under the name it bears. The bug report shows the held display (**Display held as a possible re-look**) and whether a command echo has been seen on the statline (**Command echo seen on the statline**).
  - Coming back into the game inside a renamed room, the tracker is unsure of its place until the first move, and the room keeps its old name until it is next walked into.
- `RoomGraphManager` notes which rooms the data left unnamed when the graph is built (`IsUnnamedInData`), renames one in place with its name indexes (`LearnRoomName`, `ApplyStoredNames`), takes the session's learned names off on a change of realm (`WithdrawLearnedNames`), and does not put a stored name back over one learned since (`_learnedOverStored`).
- `LearnedRoomNameStore` keeps the names in the realm's folder (`AppPaths.RealmLearnedRoomNamesFile`) and puts them on the map each time it is built and each time the realm changes. `RoomNameIndex.NameOf` gives the learned name to the lists that label rooms from the Rooms table.

### Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine
*Status: commands OBSERVED (the client issues these) · equip-before-sneak CONFIRMED · sneak lines OBSERVED (parsed by the client)*

- **Commands** *([OBSERVED])*: `sn` — attempt to sneak. (Hiding is `hid` — see *Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals*.)
- **Equip before sneak** *([CONFIRMED])*: equipping / removing gear breaks sneak, so any gear change for an approach must be sent **before** the `sn`, never after. The correct approach order is **equip → sneak → move**.
- **Sneak state machine** *(lines all [OBSERVED])*:
  - `Attempting to sneak...` (alone, no suffix) — no failure **noticed**. Either the sneak took and a move made now carries it into the next room, or it failed and your Perception roll missed that (see *The rolls* below). Only the next room's `Sneaking...` proves it. *(An earlier note called this the server ACK that the sneak took; superseded 2026-09-30 by `_cmd_sneak`, Stock.)*
  - `Attempting to sneak...You don't think you're sneaking.` — a failure you noticed; the attempt didn't take. Resend `sn`.
  - `Sneaking...` — emitted on each room entry while sneak holds; post-move confirmation you arrived unseen. On Stock the engine prints it when the move command is accepted, ahead of that move's roll: see the `Sneaking...` bullet under *The rolls* in this topic.
  - `You make a sound as you enter the room!` — loud loss of sneak. You enter seen, so a backstab opened in that room would fail. *([CONFIRMED] user, 2026-09-26; report `paradigm-20260926-222210`.)*
  - `You may not sneak right now!` — a **combat cooldown**: you can't sneak for a few seconds after being in combat or attacked, and a retry shortly after works. It's also the refusal while a monster that could attack you shares the room (the *NPCs and sneaking* rules in this topic). *([CONFIRMED] user, 2026-09-26; report `paradigm-20260926-233357`. An earlier note called it a hard block with no auto-retry; superseded 2026-09-26.)*
- **The rolls** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-30, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `_cmd_sneak`, `_move_user`, the stealth-chance routine at `0x46cc43`; Stock only, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **The stealth chance** starts from your Stealth (`0x5fa`; *Character stats & progression → Stealth base*), then:
    - −10 over 66% encumbrance, or −5 over 33% (field `0x708`, set by `_get_encumbrance_percent`);
    - ×⅔ while a status bit (`0x6f5 & 0x80`) is set — not identified;
    - **−1 for each other player and −1 for each monster in the room**;
    - clamped to 0 and a cap: 95 for `sn`, 100 for a move.
  - **`sn` rolls 0–100 under the chance.** On a fail you roll 0–100 under your **Perception**: pass and you see `You don't think you're sneaking.`; fail and you see the same bare `Attempting to sneak...` a success prints.
  - **Every sneaked move re-rolls** (0–101 under the chance, counting the room you're leaving), unless you have ability 186 (PerfectStealth), which always holds.
    - **Held:** `_move_user` prints nothing for a roll that holds. (An earlier note said you arrive with `Sneaking...`; superseded 2026-10-09 by the `Sneaking...` bullet in this list.)
    - **Lost:** the sneak is gone. You hear `You make a sound as you enter the room!` only if a 0–100 roll under your **Perception** passes; otherwise the loss is silent. The room you left sees `You notice %s sneaking out to the %s%s.` (`sneaking out upwards` / `downwards`), and the room you enter `You notice %s sneak in from the %s%s.` (*Observing another player's failed sneak into your room*) *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_move_user` @0x419159–0x41924f)*. (An earlier note wrote the departure line `You notice <name> sneaking out <dir>.`, without `to the`; superseded 2026-10-09.)
  - **`Sneaking...` is printed by `_cmd_move`, when the move command is accepted** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_move` @0x468a1e–0x468a44; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. It goes out if the sneak flag is set at that moment, before the move delay is charged and before the roll, which `_move_user` makes when the delay runs out (@0x417947–0x417997). For a follower's move `_move_user` prints it itself (@0x417742–0x417769). So on Stock the line says the sneak flag was set when the move was accepted, not that this move's roll held.
    - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` On Stock, does a move whose roll is lost silently (no `You make a sound as you enter the room!`) still show `Sneaking...`, with the missing `Sneaking...` only appearing on the move after it? The code order says so; no Stock capture of a silent loss is on record. Paradigm's order isn't recorded: its captures in *Movement on the wire — command echo, failure lines, and what actually moves you* show `Sneaking...` between the echo and the landing display, which fits either order.
- **Sneak breaks *silently* when you move into a room that doesn't re-emit `Sneaking...`** *([OBSERVED])* — no failure line, the stealth is just gone. On Stock that's a lost move roll whose Perception roll also failed (see *The rolls*); since Stock prints `Sneaking...` ahead of the roll, the room that shows without it may be the one after the loss (the `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` under *The rolls*). `Sneaking...` arrives between the move and the new room's display, and the old room's `Attempting to sneak...` doesn't carry over. A room shown without it is a guaranteed backstab failure *([CONFIRMED] user, 2026-09-27; report `paradigm-20260927-014325`)*.
- **NPCs and sneaking** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-30, user)*:
  - **Only a monster with see-hidden stops a sneak you already have.** Other monsters don't break it; on Stock each just takes 1 point off a move's re-roll *([OBSERVED]; see *The rolls*)*.
    - **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-07; report `paradigm-20261007-143049`): a sneak a see-hidden monster broke counts as broken by it until the character is sneaking again, wherever it has gone meanwhile. With *Clear hostiles when sneak broken by see-hidden monster* on, `CombatStateTracker` carries the break from room to room (`SneakBrokenBySeeHidden`). The character stops in the first room that meets the Min/Max monster window, the see-hidden room itself included, and clears all of it; a room outside the window is walked through with the break still on, as is a room it was carried into by a move already sent. A fresh `sn` answered cleanly ends the break (`NoteSneakRegained`), and the route behaves as the settings say again. It is not a failed sneak: *Clear hostiles when sneak fails* being off doesn't let it walk on exposed. (Until 2026-10-07 the clear belonged to the see-hidden room only and ignored the window there.)
    - **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-07): the clear has a tick for each kind of company, *While solo* and *While in a party* (`CombatSettings.SeenHiddenClearWhileSolo` / `SeenHiddenClearWhileInParty`, both on by default; `CombatStateTracker.SeeHiddenClearApplies`). A character in a party, leading or following, with the party tick off keeps running as if the option were off.
  - **You can't re-sneak in a room with NPCs.** Once your sneak is broken, `sn` won't take until you're in a room without them. On Stock, `_can_sneak` refuses `sn` with `You may not sneak right now!` before any roll, when a monster in the room could attack you (`_monster_could_attack`), when someone in the room is attacking you, or while a combat timer (`0x6f0`) runs *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p)*.
  - *(An earlier, realm-unrecorded note said any NPC in the room prevents a sneak from taking; restated 2026-09-30 as the two rules above.)*
- **What ends a sneak** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p: the 34 functions that clear the sneaking flag; treated as true on both realms — **Client policy**, user 2026-09-28)*. Where a function serves several commands, the command was read from the code and text around the clear, not traced line by line.
  - **Fighting:** any typed attack command other than a backstab (`_cmd_any_attack`); `bash`; attacking a monster; a monster attacking you; PvP attacks.
    - **A backstab command leaves the sneak and the hide in place when it is typed** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_any_attack` @0x45138a–0x4513a1: the two clears are skipped for attack type 4; Realm: Stock)*. The attack itself then ends them (the *attacking a monster* entry of this list). The command's other steps are in *Combat → Attack announce lines and round commits*. (An earlier note said any attack command, backstab included; superseded 2026-10-09.)
  - **Casting any spell** (`_cmd_cast`, which also clears hidden) — see *Casting breaks both Sneak and Hide*.
  - **Actions:** `aid`, `drag`, equipping (`_cmd_equip`), `ready` / `remove` gear, `give`, `search`, `rob`, `picklock`, `open` / `close` / `lock` a door, `disarm`, `follow`, the `move` command (moving an object).
  - **Shops and banks:** `buy`, `sell`, `stock`, `unstock`, `markup`, `deposit`, `withdraw`.
    - Where the clear sits *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`; Realm: Stock)*: `buy` and `sell` once in a shop room (@0x453a3a–0x453a42, @0x453c61–0x453c69), `deposit` and `withdraw` in a bank with an amount given (@0x4685d5–0x4685dd, @0x46878b–0x468793), and `give` with four or more words (@0x467784–0x46778c). `list`, `bankbook` and `appraise` have no such clear.
  - **Party and social:** `invite`, `share`, **saying something** (plain room speech) and **yelling**, and a social *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_execute_input` @0x450a93 / @0x450b46 / @0x450cb2, `_handle_ljn_actions` @0x46069b; Realm: Stock)*. Each of these clears the hidden state as well.
  - **Resting or meditating** — starting either ends it, except on Paradigm for a race or class with the ShadowRest flag, whose rest keeps it *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)* — see *Health, resting & recovery → ShadowRest*.
  - **Room commands:** textblock / CMD actions (the "pull lever" kind).
  - **Movement:** a move attempt that fails ("You can't seem to move anywhere!", too stunned); moving while dragging something; a loud entry (`You make a sound as you enter the room!`). Also walking into a wall, which prints `You are no longer sneaking.` (*Refused ("bonked") moves*), and paying a toll (*Toll exits*) *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, `_cmd_move` @0x468b43–0x468be5, `_move_user` @0x417e38)*.
  - **Being spotted:** by a monster with see-hidden, or by a Gaunt One player who has finished their level-15 race quest *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*.
  - **Other:** `quit`, `suicide`; `sneak` itself resets the flag before it re-tries. Also `break`, which prints `You are no longer sneaking.` when it ends one (*Combat → `break` — stopping an announced attack*) *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` @0x414446–0x41447f; Realm: Stock)*.
    - **`sn` throws away the sneak you have before it tries for a new one** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_sneak` @0x454641; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. It clears resting and meditating (@0x454660, @0x454669) and then the sneak bit (@0x454672), and only after that asks `_can_sneak` (@0x45467e) and rolls (@0x454765–0x45477f); a pass sets the bit again (@0x454749, @0x454781). So an `sn` sent while already sneaking is a fresh roll against the stealth chance of *The rolls* in this topic, not a free top-up, and one that is refused (`You may not sneak right now!`, `You must wait before you may do that!` @0x4547c7) or fails its roll leaves the character not sneaking. It never writes the hidden byte. Past `_can_sneak` it also stops auto-combat (`_kill_autocombat` @0x4546f2).
  - **Being counted as a target of someone else's spell cast with no target** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_count_valid_targets` @0x43f3a7; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_cast_no_target` calls it straight after its own clear (@0x4402e2), and it walks every player slot: for each player `_is_valid_target` accepts (@0x43f416) it clears that player's sneaking and resting bits (mask `0xfbfb`, @0x43f51c), resisted or not, unless the spell's record Type (`+0xc4`) is 3 (@0x43f512). It does not write the hidden byte. So another player's room or area spell of Type 0, 1 or 2 that takes you as a target ends your sneak and your rest, and a Type 3 (`General`) one does not. The Type names are in *Spells, buffs & conditions → Elemental resistance — flat, deterministic, pre-emptable*; which spells carry which Type isn't in the imported Spells table. **Not built on:** the client has no handling for it.
  - **`use <item>` whose spell has no target ends a sneak, a hide and a rest, when the cast goes through** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_use_no_target` (@0x44a827–0x44a82f) calls `_cast_no_target(spell, user, 1)`; unless that third argument is 2, `_cast_no_target` (@0x4402a9–0x4402be) clears the sneaking and resting bits (mask `0xfbfb` on the word at `+0x6f4`) and zeroes the hidden byte `+0x5f6`, only after its early refusals have passed. `_cmd_use` reaches the same routine at 0x460f31, 0x46108a and 0x4610ad. `open <container>` ends them the same way (*Items, inventory & equipment → Chests and chest loot tables*, the `open <item>` bullet). The user's ruling: "follow what the DLL says" *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user)*, so on Stock a `use <item>` whose spell has no target ends a sneak, a hide and a rest when the cast goes through. (An earlier note said `use` is not on the list; superseded 2026-10-10. That list was built from the functions that clear the sneak bit alone, and this clear takes two bits at once. A second note the same day said the `use` routines for a spell that takes a target were not read; they are read below.)
    - **None of the item commands clears the sneak bit or the hidden byte itself. The only clears on their paths are inside the cast routines, and nothing is printed at any of them** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_use` @0x460d5c, `_cmd_light` @0x46713b, `_cmd_eat` @0x4673c3, `_cmd_drink` @0x467574, `_use_no_target` @0x44a630; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. What those commands clear of their own is resting and meditating: `_cmd_use` for a light (@0x460f06, @0x461029), for a key (@0x461054, resting only), after a use that reports success (@0x46114d) and for a `read` of something not carried (@0x4611b9); `_cmd_light`, `_cmd_eat` and `_cmd_drink` on entry (@0x467157, @0x4673df, @0x467590).
    - **So a use clears them only when it reaches a CastsSp (43) slot** (`_use_no_target`, @0x44a66b–0x44a935; what each ability does is in *Items, inventory & equipment → Equip → use → restore swap for a readied buff item*, the bullet on a `use` and the item's abilities). The ability slots are walked in order. Heal (18), HealMana (150), IlluTarget (54) and AlterLightDuration (55) are applied on the spot and LearnSp (42) teaches its spell (`You read %s and learn the spell %s.`), all without a cast. A `%Spell` (114) slot ends the walk when the routine's third argument is not 11 (@0x44a6ac–0x44a6b9; `_cmd_use` passes its command number, 0x16 or 0x6e for `read`, or for a key a direction below 10; *Spells, buffs & conditions → Item-cast spells — how a `CastsSp` fires (on-use vs combat proc)*), so a swing proc is never cast by a `use`. The first CastsSp slot reached casts its spell and the routine returns that cast's result at once (@0x44a7ec–0x44a847): a slot after it is not run. The key step that follows the walk (@0x44a93b–0x44ac0f) clears nothing.
    - **`use <item> <word>`** (`_cmd_use` @0x460f54–0x461135): the word is looked up as a target.
      - A player: `_use_player_target` casts with `_cast_user_target(spell, user, target, 1, 1)` (@0x44ae01–0x44ae0e), which clears the caster's sneaking and resting bits and hidden byte (@0x4448db–0x4448fa) once its early refusals have passed (confusion, 0 HP, `Your spell fails!`). It clears the **target's** sneaking and resting bits too (@0x4448ee), unless the spell's record Type (`+0xc4`, the field named in *Spells, buffs & conditions → Elemental resistance — flat, deterministic, pre-emptable*) is 3.
      - A monster: `_use_monster_target` casts with `_cast_monster_target(spell, user, monster, 1)` (@0x44b0a4–0x44b0ad), which clears the same three (@0x4475dd–0x4475e6) after its refusals: `You may not cast that spell on a monster!`, `%s is not in this room!`, `You are not of a high enough level to cast that spell.`, the protected-room refusal and `You are not using the required spell to hit this monster!`.
      - An item: `_use_item_target` casts with `_cast_item_target` (@0x44b1f7), which writes none of the three. A spell name: `_use_spell_target` does nothing.
      - A word that names nothing: the use runs with no target (@0x46101f–0x4610ad).
    - **A light** (`ItemType` 6) goes to `_cmd_light`, which runs the item's abilities through the same `_use_no_target` (@0x4672c5) and lights it when that reports success. Every light in the imported data but one carries IlluTarget (54) and no CastsSp, so lighting one clears nothing; the exception on both realms is incense (284), which casts spell 118 (`Targets` 1) *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data, Stock 1.11p and Paradigm 1.9.1)*.
    - **A key** (`ItemType` 7) with a direction runs `_use_no_target(item, user, direction)` (@0x46108a). Keys do carry abilities in the imported data, but none the use-walk acts on *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data)*: ability 119 on 83 of Stock's 88 keys and 95 of Paradigm's 105, 183 on 19 / 27, 149 on 8 / 6, 184 on one each, and 188 on one Paradigm key. None is Heal, LearnSp, CastsSp, IlluTarget, AlterLightDuration, `%Spell` or HealMana, so using a key clears only the rest. (An earlier line here said no key carries an ability; corrected 2026-10-10.)
    - **`read <item>` is the same routine** (`_cmd_use`, entered with command 0x6e; only the word `read` in full, `rea` being `ready`: `_parse_r_command` @0x411d4a–0x411d6b). A learn-spell scroll (LearnSp) clears nothing; a scroll that casts (CastsSp) clears as a `use` does. A `read` of something not carried is handed to `_cmd_look` (@0x4611b4–0x4611d5).
    - **`eat` and `drink`** run `_use_no_target` on the food or drink (@0x467523, @0x4676d4): every food in the imported data casts a spell with `Targets` 1, and so do 32 of Stock's 34 drinks and 39 of Paradigm's 41, so eating and drinking end a sneak and a hide. The exceptions *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data)*: the small vial (1608, both realms) carries no ability at all; Stock's grey potion (1662) casts spell 1132 with `Targets` 8, which a `drink` is refused for before the clear; Paradigm's dice (3373) casts spell 5050 with `Targets` 6, which is cast with no target and so clears like the rest. (An earlier line said all but one drink cast `Targets` 1; corrected 2026-10-10.) The words are `eat` only, and `dri`, `drin`, `drink` (`_parse_command` @0x40f611, @0x40ef82); light is `lig`, `ligh`, `light` (@0x410be4).
    - **Refusals that come before the clear, so the sneak and the hide stand:** from `_cmd_use`, `You don't have %s.`, `You may not use that item!`, `You must have that item readied to use it!`, `You must be wearing that item to use it!` and `There are no more uses in %s.`; from `_cmd_light`, `You may not light that item!` (@0x467255) and `You already have something lit!` (@0x467297), both ahead of its `_use_no_target` call, and `You cannot light %s!` for an item that isn't a light; from `_use_no_target`, a spell the user can't use (silent, @0x44a815–0x44a85d); from `_cast_no_target`, the protected-room refusal for an attack spell (`You are overcome with a feeling of guilt and break off your attack.` or the protection's own line, @0x440149–0x440207) and `You must specify a target for that spell!` (@0x44020c–0x4402a4).
    - **Refusals that come after the clear, so both are gone all the same:** `Your spell has no effect in this room!` (@0x4402e2–0x440309), and the shortfalls tested at @0x4404d6–0x440515: `You have already cast a spell this round!` / `You have already invoked a power this round!`, `You do not have enough mana to cast that spell.` and `This spell is too powerful for you to control.` (printed @0x444545–0x4445f0).
      - **Paradigm: assumed the same, not observed** (user, 2026-10-10: "assume paradigm is the same"). A `use` refused there with `You have already cast a spell this round!` (*Items, inventory & equipment → Deck of cards (Gypsy)*) is taken to have ended the sneak before the refusal, as on Stock. No Paradigm capture or source shows where its clear sits.
    - **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-10: "follow what the DLL says"): the client treats this list as it treats the rest of the topic's, as true on both realms.
  - Not on the list: `get` / `drop`, `look`, telepaths, gossip and other channels — none of these clear it in the DLL.
- **Sneaking and resting in place** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-02, user)*:
  - **Stock: a sneak and a rest don't share a spot.** `rest` ends the sneak (see *What ends a sneak* in this topic), and sending `sn` while resting breaks the rest (user: "on stock, sneaking while resting, breaks the rest"). So a rest isn't broken to sneak unless HP is past rest-max (user: "if i manually typed rest, it shouldnt break the rest to sneak unless we were above our rest max hp").
  - **Paradigm with ShadowRest: sneak, then rest.** The rest keeps the sneak, so that order is fine (user: "its fine to send a sneak then rest because of shadowrest") — see *Health, resting & recovery → ShadowRest*.
  - **Paradigm: `sn` while resting does not break the rest.** For a ShadowRest character it is believed to start the ShadowRest if the rest wasn't one already (user: "i believe it puts us into shadowrest if we werent previously") *([NEEDS CONFIRMATION]: does an `sn` sent mid-rest turn the rest into a ShadowRest?)*.
  - Whether the sneak holds through the rest for a Paradigm race or class **without** ShadowRest is not recorded; the client leaves such a rest alone, as on Stock (**Client policy**).

**Client use:**
- The backstab loadout is applied in the walker's pre-move step, ahead of the `sn`, rather than raced at room-clear (because of the equip-before-sneak rule).
- `StealthManager.TakeSneakBrokeOnEntry` → `CombatManager`: with *Run if backstab fails* on, a loud entry runs instead of opening with a plain swing.
- Auto-Sneak stands down while the pack holds an item that takes Stealth to nothing (a log raft): see *Items, inventory & equipment → Abilities of carried items*.
- `StealthManager` holds movement (`SneakCooldownGate`) on `You may not sneak right now!` while Auto-Sneak is on. It retries `sn` every 2 s and releases once sneaking, or after 15 s. Not when a monster is in the room or following us: then no hold, the walk goes on unsneaked.
- **A follower's arrival lands a few milliseconds after the new room's display** *([OBSERVED] backscroll 2026-10-04 14:50, Paradigm: room shown at .305, `spirit assassin moves into the room from the southwest.` at .311)*, so a room that "looks empty" when the arrival `sn` is decided isn't. **Client policy** (2026-10-04): a monster arriving within 1.5 s of our room change marks us **followed** (`StealthManager.NoteMonsterArrival`, from `RoomEntryWatcher.ArrivalObserved`); while followed no `sn` goes out (arrival, pre-step or cooldown retry) and no step stops to cast. It lifts when we leave a room nothing followed us into, when a kill empties the room (even inside the window: a backstab dropped the follower 0.5 s after arrival and the kept flag sent the next step out unsneaked, report `paradigm-20261004-180252`), or when a fight ends any other way after we've stood in the room longer than the window. Before this, every step of a chase sent `sn` twice and each refusal stood the walk still under attack.
- `StealthManager.SneakEntry` → `SessionActivityTracker.NoteSneakEntry`: Session Stats' **Sneak %** counts a room entry as held on `Sneaking...` and as lost on `You make a sound as you enter the room!` or a silent loss.
- `StealthManager.IsStealthedHere` (the backstab gate) counts a sneak only once the new room has confirmed it. `ReadyToMoveSneaking` holds a planned step until a sneak settles (`SneakSettleGate`, retries up to 15 s).
- **Sneak keeping** (`Game.Stealth.SneakGuard`; **Client policy**, user 2026-09-28). The client holds its own sneak-ending automation in four cases:
  - **A backstab is owed or unresolved here:** hold until it fires.
  - **Our sneaked move is in flight:** hold until it lands.
  - **Sneaking past NPCs we won't fight** (auto-combat off, or the room suppressed): hold until a room with no NPCs, since a re-sneak won't take with one there. There the held actions go out and we re-sneak.
  - **ShadowResting beside a monster** (*Utilize shadowrest*, Auto-Sneak on or off): hold until the rest reaches rest-max (`SneakHold.UntilRested`; user, 2026-09-30, report `paradigm-20260930-193005`). A monster attacking ends the ShadowRest, and the hold with it.
  - **Held:**
    - automatic gear swaps (`EquipmentManager.HoldGear`), re-run when the hold lifts;
    - room search;
    - auto-light `rem` and the room-light spell;
    - in-between spells, heals included;
    - a hazard counter's `use` inside its refresh window (the desert waterskin; user, 2026-10-10), which is sent by the same between-round pass and held the same way until its last call (*Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*, the Client policy bullets);
    - optional rests (a rest the gates call for goes out anyway);
    - invites and say-channel chatter, queued at the engine send gate.
  - **Not held:** walk steps the route can't skip (doors, traps, room commands, winches, hidden-exit search) and their `.@party` / `.@trap` relays, plus `.@panic` (the leader's hang-up call; followers just hang up). A hazard counter's `use` at its last call (the buff off or inside its last 15 s, with a countered room here or next) is not held either: it keeps the character alive in the room being entered, so it goes out and the sneak is spent (**Client policy**, user 2026-10-10, asked what to do when no empty room turns up before the buff runs out: "yes it should use it anyway, at this point its more important to just use it, clear the room and continue, if thats the options they have set"). (An earlier line here had every hazard `use` go out unheld; superseded 2026-10-10 by the window in *Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*.)
    - Everything the walker and the loop send goes out as a route step (`EngineSendGate.WrapEngineSender(…, routeSteps: true)`), whatever its wording. Some room commands are spoken passwords, which read like say-channel chatter: `say gazmuldduhaz:checkability 134 9:remoteaction 1188 2008 0 0` opens the hidden exit north of `12/1188`, and `say courage` / `say bravery` / `say love` / `say time` teleport in map 17 (7 `say`-keyed room commands on Paradigm 1.9.1, 8 on Stock 1.11p; `speak` is an alias on `12/1188`). Until 2026-10-07 the send gate took the walker's `say gazmuldduhaz` for later while it sneaked past the stronghold guards, and the move behind it met `There is no exit in that direction!` (report `paradigm-20261007-225617`).
  - **Health-gate flee:** while fleeing on the run-if-below HP / MA gates (`HealthManager.IsGateFleeing`; not a hit-and-run or failed-backstab run), the emergency heal isn't held, and the re-sneak waits until it has gone out (`StealthManager.SetSneakHoldForHeal`).
  - **Marking the sneak broken:** any command on the "What ends a sneak" list sets the sneak broken (`StealthManager.NoteSneakBroken`), so the next move re-sneaks. That covers the client's own sends (the send gate, the walker's room-command hook) and lines the player types (`AppServices.NoteSentForSneak` → `StealthManager.NoteCommandSent`, from `SendUserInput`; report `paradigm-20260928-163051`: a typed `sea` left the client believing it still sneaked, so every buff stayed held). A hand-typed cast re-sneaks like an engine one (`StealthManager.ReSneakAfterCast`).
    - **Item commands** (`us` / `use`, `read`, `eat`, `dri`…`drink`, `lig`…`light`; 2026-10-10): `ItemUseStealthRule` marks the sneak broken only when the use casts, per the `use <item>` bullet of *What ends a sneak* in this topic. It finds the item among what is carried, worn and on the key ring (`ItemChargeTracker.HeldMatching`), reads its kind and its first cast slot from the game data (`ItemCastSpells.ReadCasts`), and for a use with no target tests the spell's `Targets`. A torch, a key, a learn-spell scroll and a swing-proc weapon leave the sneak alone; so do `eat` on something that isn't food and a spell that needs a target. Until this the client took no `use` for sneak-ending, so after a waterskin, a potion or a ration it went on believing in the sneak and the next move went out unsneaked.
    - **Which item the words name:** the longest run of leading words that names something held (`use iron key n` tries `iron key n`, then `iron key`, then `iron`; `ItemChargeTracker.HeldMatching`). When that run fits more than one held item, or the name is one several item records share (the game data has a `poisoned shuriken` that casts on use and one that doesn't), the sneak counts as broken if any of them would break it. (Until 2026-10-10 only the first word was matched and the first hit taken: `use iron key n` beside an iron ration read as the ration, and `use healing potion <name>` beside healing herbs read as the herbs.)
    - **Where it can't tell, the sneak counts as broken:** a word after the item, which may name a player or a monster; an item not found in the pack (`use`, `eat`, `drink`, `light`; an unfound `read` is taken for the look it is in the engine and leaves the sneak alone, which the user accepted on 2026-10-10) or not in the game data; and the refusals only the game sees (not worn or readied, no uses left, an item the character may not use, a protected room). The client does not watch for those refusal lines to take the mark back. Both mistakes cost something. Counted broken when it wasn't, the `sn` that follows throws away a sneak the character still had and rolls again (the `sn` bullet of *What ends a sneak*). Believed in after it has gone, the next move goes out with no `sn` at all, which is the worse of the two.
    - **Each verdict is logged** at Debug under `Stealth`, the ones that leave the sneak alone included: the command, the item it was read as, what that item casts, a word after it, and `sneak intact` / `sneak ended`.
    - **What a verdict costs:** nothing when there is no sneak or hide to end (`StealthManager.NoteCommandSent` asks the rule only in Sneaking, Hidden, or with either being attempted), and a dictionary read otherwise: `ItemUseFactsIndex` maps a name to every item record that bears it, built once per game-data set (`GameDataCache.Derived`). Each sent command is judged once: a typed line from `SendUserInput`, the client's own from the send gate after it has gone out, a replayed one included (`EngineSendGate`). Residual misreadings left in: an item picked up as the command goes out and not yet in the pack list is read as a held namesake sharing its first word, and a run of words that fits inside another held name (`net r` in `gold signet ring`) is read as that item, the match being a substring.
    - **The same mark drops a hide, on both realms** (`StealthManager.NoteSneakBroken(what, endsHide)`; *Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals*, the *What ends a hide on Stock* bullet and its Client use): every command on the client's list but `disarm`, `follow` and `move`. Nothing hides again; with Auto-Sneak on and nothing driving the moves, the in-place re-sneak takes over.
    - **An item cast by the cast engine** (`ItemCastSequencer`'s `use`, then `CastingDirector.CastFired` → `ReSneakAfterCast`) is marked on the `use` and re-sneaked by the cast path, with one `sn`: `ReSneakAfterCast` stands the in-place re-sneak down once its own `sn` is out.
    - **A hazard counter's `use`** (the desert waterskin, `AutoHazardCounterProvisioner`) is marked like any other, and the `sn` behind it is the held kind, answered before the next step: sent by the between-round pass it is followed by `ReSneakAfterCast`, and the step's own last call is asked ahead of the sneak check (`AppServices.HazardLastCallBeforeStep`, in both engines' ready checks). So the wire reads `use waterskin`, `sn`, both answers, then the move: the step waits for the `use`'s own answer as well, on `MovementCoordinator.HazardBuffGate` (*Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*). (Until 2026-10-10 the `use` went out from the approach hook, behind the sneak check, and its `sn` left in one burst with the move, unanswered.)
    - **A `use` that is itself the move** (a token, `TokenRouteCoordinator`; an item-use teleport route step) is marked as it goes out, so the landing re-sneaks once on arrival. It is no longer read there as a sneak lost on the way in: no `SilentSneakLost`, nothing counted against Session Stats' Sneak %, and `TakeSneakBrokeOnEntry` stays false for that landing, so *Run if BS fails* and *Clear hostiles when sneak fails* aren't armed by it. For a token that changes nothing in play (user, 2026-10-10): a token can't be used in a room with monsters and lands where no hostile monster is (*Item-use teleports*).
  - **Re-sneaking in place when nothing drives the moves** (report `paradigm-20261002-004148`): an engine
    re-takes a broken sneak at its pre-move hook; a player walking by hand has no such hook, and the
    arrival re-sneak is refused in any room with an NPC, so in a tunnel with a monster in every room a
    broken sneak never came back. With no walk, loop or auto-lair running, `StealthManager` re-sneaks
    where the character stands: 700 ms after `NoteSneakBroken` (so a burst of commands finishes first),
    at combat end (`NoteCombatEndedStealthReset`), and when Auto-Sneak is switched on. A hand-typed move
    also sends `sn` ahead of itself (`NoteTypedMove`, off `OutboundMovementObserver.MoveSent`), since the
    report shows `sea` typed about a second before the next step.
  - **The in-place re-sneak yields to a rest** (*Sneaking and resting in place* in this topic; **Client
    policy**, user 2026-10-02): while the character is resting or meditating with a pool short of rest-max
    (`HealthManager.RestingShortOfRestMax` — the engine's rest or one typed by hand), no `sn` goes out;
    `StealthManager.ReSneakInPlace` looks again every 2 s and sneaks once the rest has topped off. With
    ShadowRest utilized (`HealthManager.UsesShadowRest`) the `sn` goes out over the rest, the engine's or
    a hand-typed one, since on Paradigm it leaves the rest standing.
  - **An `sn` answered after a later sneak-ending command** (same report): `sn` then `sea` leaves the
    character not sneaking, but the `Attempting to sneak...` for that `sn` arrives after the `sea` was
    noted. `StealthManager` ignores that answer instead of reading it as sneaking.
  - **Stopping to cast** (report `paradigm-20260928-165844`): a sneaked walk is always mid-step, so a held buff / heal / cure never finds a gap. When one is due (and affordable), the step in the next NPC-free room waits on `SneakCastGate` (`StealthManager.ReadyToMoveSneaking`, from `CastingDirector.HasSneakHeldCast`); the arrival `sn` waits too, the cast goes out, and the re-sneak after it sends us on. Capped at 7 s per room.
  - **After the backstab** (report `paradigm-20260928-165954`): when the backstab round settles with the target still up, a cast held for the opener goes out before the re-announce, and its `*Combat Off*` resume re-attacks (`CombatManager.SettleBackstab`).
  - **Ordering:** pre-move gear now goes out before the `sn`.
  - **Replies:** while stealthed, a reply to an @-command said aloud goes back by telepath.
  - **ShadowRest (Paradigm):** a race or class with it sneaks before it rests when *Utilize shadowrest* is ticked (`HealthManager.SneakingBeforeShadowRest`), and its rest doesn't mark the sneak broken.
  - **A cast during a rest** (a buff the rest window lets out) ends the sneak. It is re-taken only when the user utilizes ShadowRest on a race or class that has it; otherwise the next `rest` would end the fresh sneak, so it waits for the next move's pre-move sneak (`StealthManager.SetReSneakSkipForRest`; **Client policy**, user 2026-09-30, report `paradigm-20260930-184343`).
- **Loop simulator** (`LoopSimulator`; **Client policy**, user 2026-09-30, report `paradigm-20260930-114254`): a simulated sneak **always holds** on a move, because Paradigm's rolls aren't recorded and the report's character held 296 of 299 entries. A see-hidden monster in the room still breaks it, and so does an attack, a cast or a rest. It is re-taken with **no cooldown** on the way out of a room with nothing alive in it; the report shows `Sneaking...` in the same second as a one-stab kill.

### Observing another player's failed sneak into your room
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-12 (user)*

- **`You notice <name> sneaking in from the <dir>.`** — you *perceived* another player entering your room while sneaking (their sneak failed against you).
- **This line is always a player, never a monster** — monsters do not sneak-enter with this wording.
- **Wire colour is not a reliable kind hint here** — the realm may paint the line the monster hue (yellow).
- **`[CONFLICT — ask the user]` The Stock DLL words the arrival notice `You notice %s sneak in from the %s%s.`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_move_user` @0x419159–0x41924f; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*, with `You notice %s sneak in from above%s.` / `You notice %s sneak in from below%s.` for the vertical pair; the last `%s` is the drag suffix. The DLL has `sneaking` only in the departure form shown to the room being left, `You notice %s sneaking out to the %s%s.` This disagrees with the `sneaking in from` wording in this topic, which carries no realm. Question: is `You notice <name> sneaking in from the <dir>.` Paradigm's wording, or was it written from memory? (User 2026-10-09: unsure; "if we have recorded confirmed wording it might be from paradigm". A capture on either realm settles it.)

**Client use:**
- `SneakArrivalNotice` captures the bare `<name>` and `RoomEntryWatcher` classifies it Player unconditionally. It reads both wordings in this topic, `sneaking in from` and the Stock DLL's `sneak in from`, with `from above.` / `from below.` and the ` (Dragging <name>)` suffix before the full stop (the Stock wording added 2026-10-09; the conflict over which realm prints which stays open).
- The generic `RoomEntryArrival` pattern carries a `(?!You notice )` guard so it doesn't also grab `"You notice <name>"` as a null-numbered Monster — which previously held the combat gate open and froze the loop.

### Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals
*Status: CONFIRMED (hide lines from paired two-character POV captures)*

- **Sneaking and hidden are distinct stealth states and either one enables a backstab.**
  - *Sneaking* lets you **move** silently and open on a target you approach, but does **not** remove your name from the room's `Also here:` line — others still see you listed there.
  - *Hidden* removes your name from `Also here:` (you're invisible in the room) but you **cannot move** while hidden.
  - A **player** has to `search` the room to reveal (unhide) you; **monsters do not search rooms**, so a monster that walks into a room you're hidden in never reveals you — it just becomes a backstab target.
  - A monster's passive **see-hidden** ability is a separate thing: it reveals a stealthed character to the whole room on sight, defeating the opener (see *Combat → Backstab*).
- **Command** *([OBSERVED] — the client issues it)*: `hid` — attempt to hide.
- **The bare verb hides the player; with an object it stashes the object** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*.
  A plain `hide` (or its shorthand `hid`) is the player hiding themselves; `hide <N> <item>` stashes the
  item in the room, where it can't be seen again until someone actively searches for it (see *Items,
  inventory & equipment → Hiding items in a room (stashing)* and *Money, banks & shops → Hiding coin in a
  room (stashing)*).
- **Hide state machine** *(lines all [CONFIRMED] — from paired two-character POV captures)*:
  - `Attempting to hide...` (alone, no suffix) — the attempt fired and the server ran a hide check, but the outcome is **NOT reported to you**. This line is **ambiguous**: it means "a check happened," not "you are hidden." You cannot tell success from failure off this line alone.
  - `Attempting to hide...You don't think you are hidden.` — explicit hide **FAILURE**. This is the only self-observable failure signal.
    - **Stock prints a space before the suffix:** `Attempting to hide... You don't think you are hidden.` *([OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p string table; [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-27, user)*. `UserHideFailed` accepts either form; matching only the unspaced one missed every failed hide on Stock.
