- **Skill roll** *(issue #455)*: a **`testskill <skill> <amount> <failTB>`** in the same block is a per-use **skill roll** (like the winch's `testskill strength`) that can fail even for the right class. A failed roll leaves the asker put — sometimes with no fresh room render at all, so no tracker transition comes.

**Client use:**
- The navigation engine models only the **ungated** greet teleport as a routable exit (GreetTeleportResolver → `RoomGraphManager.BuildGreetTeleportEdges`, a `Direction.Teleport` edge whose command is `ask <noun> <keyword>`); gated keywords are skipped because the client can't verify the gate and a failed transport would strand the walker.
- Three directive kinds on a greet chain are NOT treated as "unverifiable, skip": `class N`, `testskill`, and `price` (`GreetTeleportResolver` parses it and sums repeats — see *Money, banks & shops → Repeated `price` directives add up*).
  - The client does NOT model the skill-roll odds; instead the walker treats a greet teleport as a **verify-and-retry** step: after asking, it checks it actually landed in the destination and, if not, **re-asks until it arrives.** The class gate guarantees only a class that CAN eventually pass the roll ever reaches the step, so the retry converges.
- Ordinary CMD teleports — chime / boat / item-cast — stay fire-once; only the `ask`-transport edge, `RawHint` `"greet teleport"`, gets the retry watchdog.
- **Fares:** `GreetTeleportResolver` sums the line's `price` directives into the transport's `FareCopper`; the graph stamps it on the synthesised Teleport edge (`RoomExit.FareCopper`) and `MovementFilter` gates it like a toll: on your own purse, and for a party you lead on `PartyTollGate`, which asks every member at the step and funds or closes it (*Movement & navigation → Gating a party's route through toll and level exits*). (An earlier note had it gated on the poorest party member's `@wealth`; superseded 2026-10-10.)

### Boat travel — the sea captain's `secure passage to <place>`
*Status: CONFIRMED (user 2026-07-20) + OBSERVED from Paradigm-1.9.1 data · Realm: Paradigm*

- **A sea-captain dock `CMD` ferries a party across water via `secure passage to <place>`.** This is a *specific, more elaborate application* of the CMD-teleport-splits-party mechanic (see *CMD-driven room teleports split the party*): a dock room's `CMD` points at a TBInfo block listing one `secure passage to <place>` verb per reachable port.
  - Typing the verb at the dock CMD-teleports **only the caster** onto a ship, so it splits the party exactly like `ring chime` — the leader `.@party`-relays the verb, every member fires their own copy, and the party **re-forms at the destination port** (re-invite/wait, same arrival-ordering rules).
  - The NPC behind it is the **old sea captain (#2344)** standing in the dock room.
- **Boat passages are Paradigm only: Stock has none** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-11, user: "the boat passage is paradigm only, there are no boat passages in stock")*.
  - *[OBSERVED] 2026-10-11 (game data):* `data-v1.11p` has no TBInfo block with a `secure passage to` line among its 2,326, so no room `CMD` is a dock and its room graph holds 0 sailings.
  - *[OBSERVED] 2026-10-11 (game data):* `data-Paradigm-1.9.1` has two such blocks, `4986` and `5012`, with 5 `secure passage to` lines between them. They are the `CMD` of `14/759` and `14/702`, and its room graph holds those 5 sailings (the dock table in this topic).
- **Per-member gating — the captain rejects an individual, not the party.** Each `secure passage` line carries an independent **minlevel** *and* a **fare** (price). Every member is gated **individually** on both: a member below the minlevel, or without the fare on hand, is refused *at the captain* and **left behind on the dock** while the rest sail. So the pre-flight check is per-member, mirroring the toll gate: route the party to a port only when the **poorest / lowest** member clears both bars.
  - **Fare is in copper** (the base coin unit), so it folds into the same `@wealth` pre-flight gate as tolls — a member needs `price` copper-value on hand. (Contrast: a `(Toll: N)` exit is `N` **gold** = `N*100` copper; a boat `price` is already copper.)
  - **`checkability <flag> <rank>`** (optional, present only on talkiran below) is a **quest-flag / rank** gate the client does **not** read *for boat routing* — attunement (e.g. MerchantCaptain rank 3) is the user's responsibility. If a member routes to that port un-attuned the captain rejects *them*; the client never boards and **fails out** (see the **Transit + fail-out** bullet in this topic). (The client *does* read live quest-flag values elsewhere — the login quest-completion sync, see *Quests → Quest-flag values (`abil` / `sys god abil`)* — but never uses them to decide boat passage; attunement stays the user's call.)
- **TBInfo Action format** (verified verbatim off `data-Paradigm-1.9.1`, TBInfo #4986 / #5012, each reached from the dock room's `CMD`). One newline-separated line per port; colon-separated directives:

  ```
  secure passage to <place>:[checkability <flag> <rank>:]minlevel <L> <failMsgId>:price <copperFare> <failMsgId>:random <tbId>:text <msgId>
  ```

  - `random <tbId>` points at a **weighted-random TBInfo table** (a `Textblock(rndm)`), whose lines read `<roll>:cast <boardSpell>:cast <tripSpell>`.
  - Both `cast`s fire in order: **`boardSpell` (5415 "board ship")** random-teleports the caster into a ship room (`Abil 140` val 0 over `MinBase..MaxBase` = rooms **14/715–723**, `Abil 141` = map 14); **`tripSpell`** starts the buff-locked voyage.
- **Arrival-room resolution is a spell EndCast chain** (uses the `140/141/151` mechanics — `140/141` documented in *Cast-on-walk exits and random teleports*, the `151` EndCast chain in *Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*): follow `tripSpell` down its **`Abil 151` (EndCast → follow-on spell)** chain — `trip 1 → trip 2 → trip 3 → disembark to <port>` — to the terminal **`disembark`** spell, whose **fixed `Abil 140` room + `Abil 141` map** is the arrival `RoomKey`.
  - Each trip leg carries `Abil 29` (buff-lock) so the player can't act mid-voyage; the final `<port> landing` spell is a cosmetic message.
  - Worked chain (albion): random `#4987` → `cast 5415`+`cast 5416` → `5416 → 5418 → 5419 → 5417 "disembark to kingsport"` (`Abil 140`=702, `Abil 141`=14) → arrival **14/702**.
- **Verified Paradigm-1.9.1 dock table** (discovered data-driven, *not* to be hardcoded — scan every room's `CMD` TBInfo for `secure passage to` lines and resolve as above):

  | Dock room | Port | Verb | Minlevel | Fare (copper) | checkability | Arrival room |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 14/759 "Blackwater Harbor, Wharf" | albion | `secure passage to albion` | 50 | 2,000,000 | — | 14/702 (Kingsport Harbor) |
  | 14/759 | terra fuego | `secure passage to terra fuego` | 50 | 2,000,000 | — | 14/1812 (Shoreline, Sandy Beach) |
  | 14/759 | terra ista | `secure passage to terra ista` | 60 | 5,000,000 | — | 14/1813 (Cliffside Beach) |
  | 14/759 | talkiran | `secure passage to talkiran` | 65 | 6,000,000 | `211 3` (MerchantCaptain rk 3) | 14/15000 (Tal'kiran Shore) |
  | 14/702 "Kingsport Harbor, Wharf" | port blackwater | `secure passage to port blackwater` | 1 | 2,000,000 | — | 14/759 (Blackwater Harbor) |

- **Transit + fail-out.** After the verb: board → random ship room (14/715–723) → buff-locked trip legs → disembark teleport to the arrival room. A member the captain rejected (minlevel / fare / attunement) **never boards**.

**Client use:**
- The client **suppresses engines** during the voyage and waits for the arrival room to render.
- A rejected member is detected as *no teleport into a ship room within a short window of firing the verb*, which is the fail signal.
- A sailing whose fare the crosser's own purse doesn't cover is not set out for, even as the only crossing: the walk fails naming the sailing, its fare and the purse (`AutoWalkManager`, `PaidCrossingDescriber.DescribeBoat`). One gated on level still sails as the only crossing, with a warning.
- **A party's fares** (user, 2026-10-10: the boat ride counts as a toll): the verb is held at the dock while every member's purse is asked, a short member is handed the difference when funding is on, and otherwise the sailing is closed to the party for the trip and not set out for (`PartyTollGate.BeforeSailing`; the rules are in *Gating a party's route through toll and level exits*). (An earlier note had a sailing gated on a follower's purse still sail as the only crossing, with a warning; superseded 2026-10-10.)
- The words a captain refuses a fare with are a message number on each `price` step whose text isn't recorded for either realm, so a refusal at the dock is read only by the fail signal above, and raises no doubt about the purse.

### Jail `bribe guard` — cell-hop helper with an escalating toll
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-30 (user) · Realm: Paradigm*

- **In the jail rooms (Paradigm `1/541–545`, `14/1326–1333`) the `bribe guard` command casts a jail-teleport** — it moves the player between cells so a jailed player can reach their gear when they can't bash / picklock the cell door or lack the jail key.
- **The TBInfo `Action` lists six escalating `price` tiers** — `100 / 1000 / 10000 / 100000 / 1000000 / 10000000` copper (1 Gold → 10 Runic).
- **The guard charges the largest tier the player can currently afford**, capped at 10 Runic per bribe: carry 11 Runic → charged 10 Runic; carry 8 Runic → charged 1 Runic (the next tier, 10 Runic, is unaffordable). The escalating cost *is* the catch.
  - **Why it isn't a sum** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*: the trigger reads its effects **top-down** — if you can afford a `price` it moves on to the next one, until it reaches one you can't afford, and then fires the previous (last affordable) tier. Contrast the identical repeats on an NPC transport line, which add up (*Money, banks & shops → Repeated `price` directives add up*). The client models the two shapes separately: `GreetTeleportResolver` sums, the room-CMD requirement reader takes the highest affordable tier.
- **This tiered multi-`price` shape is unique to bribe guard among room-`CMD` commands**; ordinary paid services (`roll dice`, `buy <spell>`, `summon <x>`, `secure passage`) carry a single `price <copper> [failTextblockId]`.

**Client use:**
- Only the ceiling is meaningful to surface, so the room tooltip renders it as "bribe guard — costs up to 10 Runic (takes the most you can afford)".

### Room-entry hazards — what counts as a movement hazard
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-25 (user)*

- **A room's entry spell (`Rooms.Spell`) is a hazard only when its unprotected effect actually damages the player, kills the player, or forces/prevents their movement** (a teleport/transfer out). For the navigation router's purposes a hazard is something to route around, gate behind a counter item, or warn on.
- **Not hazards:** a monster summon on entry, an alignment shift (`addevil`/`addgood`), a flavor `message`, or quest-item placement — you can still walk in freely, so the router must treat the room as ordinary.
- **This holds even when the room-entry spell carries a `failitem` "counter".** E.g. Blackwood Forest (`Spell 1040`) only summons a monster + shifts alignment + prints a message, so despite its `failitem 185` ("manhole"), it is **not** a movement hazard.
- **Real hazards** damage (a `Damage`/`EndCast` ability, or a TextBlock `cast` of a damaging spell), gate on a survival buff (`checkspell`/`failspell` — the desert heat, the drown chain), or `teleport`/`transfer` you out (the sea/ice/pit rooms).

**Client use:**
- Encoded in `RoomHazardIndex` — see the harm gate in `BuildHazard`.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09: "a room spell that does magma drip which breaks rests, means we should heal but not actively try to rest in a room like this, because it'll kill us if we dont have heals")*: no rest is started in a room whose spell is set to bar resting (by default the spells that damage on every cast), counter or no counter in the game data, unless the counter is in effect. The rule, the rooms, the setting and the code are in *Health, resting & recovery → Resting in a room whose spell does damage*.
- **Client policy** (report `paradigm-20261004-204354`): only a route the user picked may cross a hazard room without its counter. A through-gates walk nobody picked (a stash transfer, a bank run, a trainer trip, a sell detour) plans with `MovementFilter.SuspendAcquirableGatesButUncounteredHazards`: the room stays closed unless the counter is carried or the walk will obtain it (`HazardProvisionProbe`, the walk-start announce list). The route picker's commits pass `pickedRoute` to `AutoWalkManager.WalkTo`. Before this, a stash transfer planned as if every gate item were carried, took the Silver River — whose counter is any one of three boats, which the walk-start announce provisions for nobody — and walked in unprotected.

### Protective-item gates — exit-gated vs room-spell-gated
*Status: CONFIRMED (encoding fully decoded off the stock v1.11p data set)*

- **Some rooms harm you on entry unless you carry (or wear, or drink) a protective item — either exit-gated or room-spell-gated.** There are TWO gate locations (exit vs room-spell) and, within room-spells, THREE distinct protection encodings (*Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*, *Room-spell hazard shape 2 — TextBlock action guarded by `failitem <itemNum>`*, *Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*).
- **A. Exit-gated** — the exit string itself carries the modifier; already parsed:
  - `Item: (item#)` → `RoomExit.KeyItemId` + `RoomExitHint.Item`. Traversal needs the item in the pack. Examples: `6/79 → 6/80` needs *rope and grapple* (item 191); `6/1549 → 6/1550` needs *climbing harness* (item 930).
  - **An `Item:` exit takes across only the member holding the item** *([OBSERVED] report `paradigm-20261007-183903`, Paradigm)*. The Elder Darkwood Grove stone arch, `7/87` SE → `7/140` `(Item: 474)`, darkwood ring: the leader, carrying two rings, crossed with `You rub the darkwood ring, and are swept through the arch!` and the two followers, carrying none, stayed behind (`Fujin is no longer following you.`, `Boost is no longer following you.`, `Your party has been disbanded.`). A second ring in the leader's pack carried nobody. Each follower handed a ring then crossed on their own move. So a party of N needs N copies, one in each pack.
    - **Everyone holding the item crosses together; a member without it is refused at the exit and stays in the room** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-07, user)*. So a leader who walks through takes along exactly the followers who hold one, and the rest drop out of the party there. (An earlier note asked whether followers holding the item cross with the leader's move or only by their own command; superseded the same day.)
    - **Client use:** before a walk the user starts is planned, a leader with followers asks the party for its count of every such gate item on the way that the leader holds (`AppServices.CountPartyGateItemsAsync`, `@have` through `PartyInventoryProbe`; a joined member who doesn't answer counts as holding none, and one invited but not yet joined is not asked or counted). While the leader's live count plus the members' reported count is under one each, the item's exits are closed to the plan (`MovementFilter.PartyShortOfItemProbe`), so the route card names the item and the count. Picking the gated route forces the missing copies; `PartyPathItemGate` hands them out and its `Provisioned` reopens the gates. The count is dropped when the roster changes. Only a walk the user starts takes this count before planning; the members' answers behind it are handed once to `PartyPathItemGate` (`AppServices.TakeCardCount`): to the first walk that asks about that item within two minutes, normally the walk the card starts, which then doesn't ask again. A card closed without a pick drops them.
    - **Client policy:** at walk start `PartyPathItemGate` asks the party who holds each ticked or ordered gate item on the route, for any walk, so the leader can hand spares out. The walk stands still for that count only when the answer could send it somewhere else first: its journey has a fetch order and no errand (Auto-Lair, a bank run, a sell trip) owns the walker. Such a walk sets off when the answers are in, "just in case it needs to plan a detour to a shop to buy needed items" (user, 2026-10-09; report `paradigm-20261009-011133`). A leader carrying more than its own quota of the item is held as well, on any walk: the count is what hands the spares out, and the gate takes across only those holding one. Every other walk goes on while it is counted; a PvP flee makes no item announce and asks nothing. The hold is `MovementCoordinator.PartyItemCountGate`; it ends with the probe's reply window (`PartyInventoryProbe.QueryWindow`, 4 s) and has a cap of its own 2 s past that. A journey asks about an item once: later legs and re-plans reuse the answer until the leader's own copies change, a hand-off is made, the roster changes or the answer is two minutes old. A trip resumed after a sell detour, a flee or a comeback is a new journey (`AutoWalkManager.ResumeJourney`) and asks once more. An item whose trade was agreed on a route card is fetched without asking.
    - **Client policy:** "if a member doesnt answer an @have count, assume they dont have it and fetch them one" (user, 2026-10-09). A joined member who doesn't answer is in the pool holding none, for the route card's count and for `PartyPathItemGate` alike: both read it from the same result (`PartyInventoryProbe.PartyItemResult.Unanswered`). The leader's shortfall includes their copies, and the hand-off gives them theirs: the leader's own `give <item> to <name>`, or `/<holder> @do give <item> to <name>` to a member who answered with a spare. A silent member counts as holding none at every count, except for what the leader handed them (the next bullet). (An earlier rule left a member who didn't answer out of the gate's pool; superseded 2026-10-09. An earlier note said the client does not read the reply to that give and never learns that a silent member holds a copy; superseded 2026-10-09 by the next bullet.)
    - **Client policy:** a gate item the leader's client handed to a member is remembered until the party changes (user, 2026-10-09). Asked: "Silent party member at a gate that needs an item each: a member who never answers `@have` is fetched a copy on every trip. Remember "already gave them one" until the party changes? The cost is that a failed hand-over isn't retried." Answer: "yes".
    - **Client policy:** a copy the leader's trip fetched for a member to cross with isn't auto-discarded before it is handed over (user, 2026-10-16; report `paradigm-20261016-031735`, where a keep-1 discard dropped the rope bought for the member, so a rope was bought again every trip). `AutoDiscardManager` keeps the trip's count (`PartyPathItemGate.CopiesToCarryFor`) while it stands.
      - **Remembered:** the leader's own `give <item> to <name>` sent by `PartyPathItemGate`, once the giver's line naming that item and that member comes back within 30 seconds (either wording in *Items, inventory & equipment → Giving items and coins to another player (`give`, `share`)*). A give with no such line is not remembered, and neither is a relayed `/<holder> @do give …`, whose line goes to the holder and not to the leader. A give the user types is not remembered either, unless its line arrives while one of the client's own gives of that item to that member is still waiting: it then stands for that one, and either way the game has said the member was handed the item. The wait ends after the 30 seconds, or at once on one of the Stock refusal lines of that topic (`<name> refuses your offer.`, `<name> cannot accept your offer.`, `You may not give that item away!`, which names nobody and ends the oldest wait). Paradigm's refusal wording is not on record, so a give refused there waits out the 30 seconds. (An earlier note said flatly that a give the user typed is not remembered; superseded 2026-10-09.)
      - **Credited:** at a later count, for the route card and for the walk alike, a member who doesn't answer is taken to hold what they were handed, up to the per-person quota (nothing can be asked of a silent member, so a spare of theirs can't be sent on). A member who answers is taken at their word, and the answer replaces what was remembered, up or down.
      - **Forgotten:** for one member when they leave the roster, or when the `par` asked after a gate crossing no longer lists them as following (the `par` Client policy below); for everyone when the party disbands, this character stops leading it, the client disconnects, another character is loaded, or the user presses Reset States. A member joining forgets nothing. Never saved to disk.
      - **An item with a limited number of uses** (Items `UseCount` above 0, or no item record to read; see *Items, inventory & equipment → Item charges (`Uses` / `UseCount`)*) is remembered only for the journey it was handed over on, and no longer than the leader's own crossing of an exit whose key item it is. The client assumes such an item may be used up by its gate and doesn't count uses. In the Paradigm 1.9.1 and Stock 1.11p Rooms and Items tables the `Item:` exits with a limited-use item are the room ticket (924), bloodstone orb (807), amber talisman (815) and greasy leather bracelet (817), each `UseCount` 1, plus the magical quartz rod (996, `UseCount` 9999), the smoky black talisman (657, Stock) and the demonic idol (3544, Paradigm); the darkwood ring (474), rope and grapple (191), climbing harness (930) and mine pass (942) are `UseCount` -1 *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, game data)*. The crossing also drops the trip's standing count of that item when it forgot a hand-over, so the trip's next leg asks the party again, and a walk's end drops a limited-use hand-over whose journey is over.
        - **`UseCount` at or below 0 does not always mean the item is kept** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, game data: `data-Paradigm-1.9.1 (room commands)` and `data-v1.11p (room commands)`, Rooms / Items / Spells / TBInfo)*. The chess pieces white pawn (1933), black knight (1934), white bishop (1935), white queen (1936), black king (1937) and black rook (1939) are `UseCount` -1, and each is the key item of one `Item:` exit among the map 17 `Marble Room` squares (`17/3067` N `(Item: 1933)`, `17/3070` E `(Item: 1934)`, `17/3073` S `(Item: 1935)`, `17/3065` W `(Item: 1936)`, `17/3061` N `(Item: 1937)`, `17/3076` N `(Item: 1939)`). Room-entry spells take them:
          - spell 1372 `chess pieces` (17 rooms in the Paradigm set, 16 in the Stock set; its own record carries ability 148 with value 0, and TBInfo 4326 names it in `Called From`: `Spell #1372`) runs `failitem 185:takeitem 1933`, and the same line for 1934, 1935, 1936 and 1937;
          - spells 1267 `fortress trigger` (TBInfo 4173), 1305 `meadow trigger` (4192), 1306 `cloud trigger` (4194), 1307 `fire trigger` (4196) and, in the Paradigm set only, 5833 `tower trigger` (10211) each carry `takeitem 1933:random <N>` and the same line for 1934, 1935, 1936, 1937 and 1939.
          - The client does not read these chains for this rule, so a chess piece handed over is remembered until the party changes although a room may since have taken it. What then happens is under *The accepted cost*.
      - **The accepted cost:** a hand-over that was confirmed and then didn't stick is not made again until one of the events above. The loss itself brings one of them about after a single crossing, on either realm: a member credited with a copy they no longer hold is refused at the exit and is out of the leader's party (the `Item:` exit bullets of this topic). Where the game tells the leader (Paradigm prints `<name> is no longer following you.`), `PartyManager.OnLeftBehind` takes them off the roster and their hand-overs go with them; with auto-invite on the leader goes back for them (`PartyComebackManager`). Where it tells the leader nothing, the `par` asked after the crossing shows it (the next Client policy). Either way the next count takes them as holding none and fetches a copy, so the cost is one party split per lost copy. (An earlier note asked whether a Stock follower refused at an `Item:` exit is dropped from the leader's party, and said that if they stayed listed a wrongly credited member would be left behind on every trip; the user answered 2026-10-09, see *Party → A follower who can't move is left behind*, and the `par` check covers it.)
    - **Client policy:** a credited member's hand-over is dropped after a gate crossing only on `par`'s word (user, 2026-10-09). Asked whether a member's credit should be dropped when the leader crosses the gate and the member isn't in the arrival room: "yes, but before forgetting them we check PAR, that will tell us if they're in our room or not, as another member in our party, that is actively in our par, has to be in our room." The rule it rests on is in *Party → Co-location and the `Also here:` line*.
      - **When:** the leader's arrival through an exit with a key item is confirmed by the room display, and a member is taken to hold that item on a hand-over alone, having never answered a count of it. Not for a member who answers `@have`, and not for a limited-use item, whose hand-over the crossing has already forgotten.
      - **What is sent:** one `par`, however many members are credited, through `PartyPoller.RequestPar`. It goes out on both realms, and with auto-heal off or every `par` trigger in Settings → Party unticked, since it asks who is in the party and not how hurt they are. It is not sent with the master switch off, while disconnected, out of a party or in the trainer menu; the credit then stands. The poll timer counts from it, so the timer's own `par` doesn't follow back to back.
      - **The answer** is the first `par` reply read after the crossing, whoever asked for it. A member it lists as following keeps the credit. One it leaves out is taken off the roster by that same reply (`PartyManager.ReconcileMissingFromPar` acts on the first reply that omits a member), and one it lists as `[Invited]` stays a row; either way their hand-overs are forgotten and the trip's standing counts dropped, so the next count takes them as holding none.
      - **No walk back is started from it.** A member a `par` reply drops is stamped for the re-invite-on-return window only; going back for a member is the left-behind path (*Party → A follower who can't move is left behind*).
    - **Client use:** `PartyHandOverMemory` holds it (`NoteGiveSent` from `PartyPathItemGate.Redistribute`, `OnItemGivenAway` from `InventoryManager.ItemGivenAway`, `OnGiveRefused` from `InventoryManager.GiveRefused`, `Reconcile` from `PartyPathItemGate.QueryHoldingsAsync` and `AppServices.CountPartyGateItemsAsync`, `OnGateCrossed` and `SilentHoldersOf` through `PartyPathItemGate.OnGateCrossed` from `RoomTracker.StateChanged`, `ForgetEndedTrips` from the walker's Stopped / Failed / Finished events, `KeepOnly` from the roster's `CollectionChanged` and from `PartyPathItemGate.OnPartyListRead` on `PartyManager.ParReplyRead`, `Clear` from the rest). The bug report lists it as *Gate items handed to party members (remembered)*, and a `par` asked after a gate as *Members par was asked about after a gate, reply not read yet*.
  - `Level: X to Y` → `MinLevel`/`MaxLevel`. Example: `12/2369 → 12/2371` needs level 50+.
  - A level-restricted *action* can also be `CMD`-driven (TBInfo), not a Spells hazard — e.g. `17/2854` (`CMD:4328`), a min-level gate expressed as an action chain, not `Room.Spell`.
- **B. Room-spell-gated** — the room carries a cast-on-enter spell (`Room.Spell` = a record number into the Spells table). 3981 rooms carry an entry `Spell` but only ~82 distinct spell numbers are used, and most are benign (light/ambiance/message). The hazardous ones use one of three shapes: (1) direct damage negated by `NegateSpell`, (2) TextBlock guarded by `failitem`, (3) TextBlock guarded by a buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`).
- **Routing takeaway:** a room is *safe to route through* if, for its `Room.Spell` hazard, the player satisfies the protection — holds a `failitem` item, wears/holds an item that `NegateSpell`s the damage/timer spell (or its EndCast follow-on), or carries the buff-source item for a `checkspell` gate. Otherwise the node is hazardous: avoid it, or offer acquire/ask, same as an item-gated exit.
- **Detecting a hazard therefore needs:**
  - (i) read `Room.Spell`;
  - (ii) walk its `Abil/AbilVal` for a direct `1`(Damage) or `151`(EndCast) chain, and for `148`(TextBlock) parse the TBInfo `Action` for `failitem` / `checkspell` before a `cast`;
  - (iii) resolve protective items via Items `NegateSpell-N`, `failitem` item ids, and `checkspell` buff-source `CastsSp` items.

### Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`
*Status: CONFIRMED (lava/volcano via game data, Paradigm 1.9.1; Misty Bog by user, report `paradigm-20260829-203409`) · Realm: Paradigm*

- **The entry spell has `Abil 1` (Damage) directly, and may chain a death-timer via `Abil 151` (EndCast → follow-on spell).** Protection is a worn item whose `NegateSpell-0..9` list (an Items.json field) contains the spell number; held in the pack it does nothing, on either realm (the `NegateSpell` bullet below). (An earlier wording here said "held/worn"; superseded 2026-10-10.)
- **Worked example — the underwater/frozen passage:**
  - `6/1139` `Spell:511` "freezing water" = `Abil-0 1`(Damage) + `Abil-2 151`(EndCast→**512** "holding breath", `Dur 25`). Spell 512 in turn `151`(EndCast→**513**) — that is the **death timer**: hold-breath runs 25 ticks, then 513 drowns you.
  - `8/647` Black Moat `Spell:453` "black water" = `Abil-0 1`(Damage), constant chip each entry.
  - Protection: **gnomish fish-helm (item 929)**, `NegateSpell = [512, 513, 514, 453]`. Worn, it negates the drown chain (512/513/514) and the black-water damage (453). You still take the minor direct 511 chip but never drown.
  - **Timer cancel on exit:** the `6/1139` up-exit is `(Cast: pre-516, post-0)` → spell **516** `151`(EndCast→**515** "stop drowning"), and 515 `153`(KillSpell) **512** & **513** — leaving the water cancels the drown timer. (`Cast: pre-N` = cast spell N *before* moving through the exit.)
- **The lava / volcano biome is this same shape** *([CONFIRMED via game data, Paradigm 1.9.1])*.
  - `Spell:526` "magma heat" (`Abil-0 1` Damage, a leaf spell — no EndCast chain) covers ~1000 rooms (Lava Tube / "salamander tubes", Magma/Molten River, Jagged Obsidian Field, Volcano Magma Tunnels, etc.); `Spell:218` "temple of fire fire" covers the Temple-of-Fire / Volcano-heart rooms.
  - Both are negated by **either** the **magma amulet (item 487)** or the **phoenix feather (item 1000)** — each has `NegateSpell = [526, 218]`, and they're the only two items that do.
  - **The phoenix feather protects only while it is worn** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-08, user: a lot of the volcano's rooms "require wearing a phoenix feather to protect from magma heat"; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "phoenix feather has to be worn to negate, sunstone wristband does not"; [OBSERVED] report `paradigm-20261008-202210`, Paradigm)*. In `Infernal Cavern` (`16/10109`, `Spell:526`) a character carrying the feather with another neck piece on took `You are seared by the flames for 48 damage!` about every 6 s (31 to 58 a hit) for as long as it stood there; with the feather worn (`phoenix feather (Neck)`) no such line came, over stretches of 35 s and 23 s in the same room, and the line was back 3 s after the feather came off. In report `paradigm-20261009-122342` the line came every 6.05 s with the feather carried, last at 12:23:17.306; the feather went on at about 12:23:21 (`Eq phoenix` → `You are now wearing phoenix feather.`) and none of the four lines due in the 21 s to the end of the capture came.
  - **An item's `NegateSpell` list is asked of what is worn, and of nothing else** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL, Realm: Stock; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, Realm: Paradigm, asked whether any Paradigm item negates a room spell from the pack: "paradigm is the same as stock")*. It is the feather's mechanism, not the feather's own rule. On Stock:
    - `_room_cast_on_user` (`0x47572f`), which applies a room's spell to a player in it, calls the routine at `0x43e3db` with the player and the spell's number (`0x4757d2`) and applies nothing when it answers yes (`0x4757dc`).
    - `0x43e3db` walks the 20 slots at `player+0x62c`, loads each slot's item (`_get_item_data`) and compares the ten numbers at `item+0x36c` with the spell's (`0x43e3ee`–`0x43e42a`). `player+0x62c` is the worn array: `_user_is_wearing` (`0x41c815`) scans the same 20 slots and `_wear_armour` (`0x41c846`) writes them.
    - It reads nothing else: not the pack (`player+0xd8`, 100 entries), not the key ring (`player+0x334`, 50), and not the single slot at `player+0x624` that `_remove_item_from_inventory` unequips separately (`0x41b39b`; read as the wielded weapon), so a wielded item's list is not asked either.
    - The same routine stands in front of a spell a textblock `cast`s (`_perform_matched_action` `0x4702db` → `_cast_no_target` `0x43ff1f` → `_count_valid_targets` `0x43f3a7`, the call at `0x43f42f`: the wearer `resists your spell!`), a player's spell at another player (`_cast_user_target`, `0x4451ec`) and a monster's (`_monster_cast` `0x427e80`, `_monster_count_valid_targets` `0x425ff6`).
    - So on Stock every `NegateSpell` item counters by being worn, the magma amulet, the fish-helm and the boots included, and an item with a `NegateSpell` list and no wear slot would counter nothing.
    - **Paradigm is the same** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "paradigm is the same as stock")*. Its server is not this DLL, so the addresses above are Stock's alone; the rule is the user's word there, and the feather's reports bear it out. The client applies it to every `NegateSpell` item on both realms.
    - (An earlier note asked whether every `NegateSpell` item with a wear slot has to be worn or whether it was the feather's own rule, and a later one whether any Paradigm item negates a room spell from the pack; settled for Stock from the DLL and for Paradigm by the user, both 2026-10-10.)
- **Misty Bog swamp damage** *([CONFIRMED by user, report `paradigm-20260829-203409`])* — `Spell:485` (the bog zone's entry spell) is negated by **either** the **swamp boots (item 925)** or the **trollskin boots (item 1232)** — both share `NegateSpell = [485, 5682]`, an any-of group exactly like the lava amulet/feather pair.
  - A player who equips a *different* group member they already own (swamp boots) is just as protected as one wearing the sourced item.

**Client use:**
- `RoomHazardIndex` already indexes the lava counters (one any-of group {487, 1000}), so the router treats lava like any protectable hazard: avoid unless the player carries a counter. By severity, lava sits with the river as *survivable* damage, while the desert is *grave* (see *Hazard severity — survivable damage vs grave*).
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-10: "phoenix feather should be worn, or magma amulet if no phoenix feather, before stepping into magma drips that are prevented by it. and put the default piece(or whatever set is equipped) back on once we're no longer about to enter a room spell that needs the feather")*: **a carried item that negates a room's spell is put on before the step into the room, and its slot is given back afterwards.** `RoomSpellCounterWear`, through `EquipmentManager.ClaimSlot` / `ClearSlotOverride` (the per-slot claim the Location rules use, so the gear sets skip the slot meanwhile and the set in force is what it returns to).
  - **Which item** *(order confirmed by the user, 2026-10-10: "yes")*: the hazard's `NegateSpell` group (`RoomHazard.NegatingItems`), less what this character can't wear by class, level or alignment (`ItemEquipFilter.CanEquip`). With several carried, one that fills a free place before one that pushes a piece out; then the one that leaves the most armour counting what it pushes out: armour class, then damage resistance, then the lower item number. The feather and the amulet negate the same two spells from the same slot *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, both sets: `NegateSpell` 526 and 218, `Worn` 8)* and differ in `ArmourClass` / `DamageResist` 10 / 1 against 0 / 0, so the feather goes on first, as the user ordered. One already worn is left alone.
  - **Where it is on** *(user, 2026-10-10: "the counter should stay on while inside the room that it is needed, and be put on when we're next to a room where it is needed. if we exit a room where its needed but are within 1 room in any direction of the hazard, it should stay on.")*: in a room whose spell it negates and in any room with an exit into one, read from the exits of the room stood in; on when the character arrives next to such a room, off when neither holds, the same whether or not something is moving the character. The move-ready check of the walker and the loop (the step held on `MovementCoordinator.CounterWearGate` until the game answers, 3 s at most for a wear that draws no answer, one such hold per step) and the wear ahead of a typed compass step (`RoomTracker.ManualMoveObserved`) are the backstop for an arrival that had no such room next to it first: a teleport, a leader's drag, an exit the map can't follow. (An earlier rule kept it on within 5 steps while moving and 1 step otherwise; superseded 2026-10-10.)
    - **One step of the plan keeps it on** *(user, 2026-10-10, asked whether the counter should stay on while the next planned step is again next to the hazard: "stay on while the next planned step is again next to the hazard")*: where it would come off, it stays on when the moving engine's next planned step (`PeekPlannedDirections(1)`, followed through the room's exit) lands in or next to a room it is for. It keeps a counter on and puts none on. Known consequences of a look one step deep: a corridor with such a room off every second room is walked with one wear and one restore, one with such a room off every third room still swaps at each, and with no engine plan (typed moves, a follower being led) the plain rule applies.
    - **A counter of ours taken off by other hands is left off for that room** *(user, 2026-10-10, asked whether one taken off by hand where it is needed should be left off for that room and put on again in the next room that needs it: "yes")*.
    - **The look-ahead for the sneaking-past case is 3 planned steps** *(user, 2026-10-10: "thats fine")*.
  - **Sneaking** *(user, 2026-10-10: "it should try to wear the counter in an empty room is auto-sneak is on and auto-combat is off, if auto sneak is on and auto-combat is on, wear it before the hazard rooms where appropriate.")*: a wear ends a sneak (*Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine*). With Auto-Sneak on and Auto-Combat off the next `RoomSpellCounterWear.EmptyRoomLookAhead` (3) steps of the moving engine's own plan are read, and the counter goes on in a room with no NPC (`CombatStateTracker.HasRoomNpc`, the test `SneakGuard` holds a command on) when one comes up before the hazard; with none it goes on next to the hazard anyway; the pre-move `sn` re-sneaks. With Auto-Sneak on and Auto-Combat on, or Auto-Sneak off, there is no look-ahead and the wear goes out through a sneak `SneakGuard` is keeping. The ruling is about the wear, which has the room's damage at stake. **Giving the slot back never goes out through a sneak hold**, in any combination: it waits for `SneakGuard` (and, sneaking past things, for a room with no NPC), the item stays owned until the commands have gone out, and the release is decided again when the hold lifts, so an item needed again by then stays on. (An earlier rule sent the wear through a kept sneak always; a later build sent the restore through one with Auto-Combat on, which cost the backstab opener in the first room clear of the hazard; both superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **What is on and what was pushed out:** the game's `You are now wearing %s.` reaches the router's handlers before the inventory's worn list is patched, so a confirmed wear is the manager's own knowledge until the list agrees. The piece pushed out is the one named by the `You have removed %s.` line that comes ahead of the wear line while the wear is out; none means a free place was filled. The piece restored is the current set's for that slot, else the piece pushed out, else nothing (`rem`). On a finger or a wrist the restore is `rem <counter>` then `eq <piece>`, because an `eq` into a full pair evicts whichever piece the realm picks (*Items, inventory & equipment → Named-item uniqueness and paired slots (finger / wrist)* covers which).
  - **A wear that puts nothing on** is paired with its answer through the equipment manager's own list of wears out (the game answers gear commands in the order sent), so a refusal that names no item goes to the oldest unanswered wear, a gear set's or the counter's. `You may not wear that item!` and `%s may not be worn!` set the item aside until a level-up, a change of alignment or a stat-screen read (a read that finds the alignment unchanged lifts nothing: a refused wear asks for that read itself, and lifting on it sent the wear again and again); `You have no more room to wear that item!` until a worn piece comes off; `You do not have %s left unequipped.`, `You are already wearing %s and it may not be removed.` and no answer in 3 s until the next full inventory read. An item set aside opens no room to a route. A wear the locked `EngineSendGate` would drop is not sent, claimed or waited for.
  - **A slot a Location rule holds:** with the same item, shared (one wear, given back when both let go); with another piece, the counter takes it and the rule's piece goes back on when the counter lets go.
  - **Not covered:** the crystal ward (user, 2026-10-10: "no"), Paradigm item 3701, whose `NegateSpell` list is the four class filters #1325, #1326, #1327 and #1337 *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, `data-Paradigm-1.9.1`)*. Those four spells turn a class away with a teleport and do no damage, and `RoomHazardIndex` holds no hazard for any of them on either realm, so the wear, which reads its items from that index, never dresses for them.
  - **Not** with the setting off (Settings → Periodic Damage Room Spells, on by default, character tier) or the master switch off (user, 2026-10-10: "with the master switch off, it shouldnt automatically swap gear"); the room stood in is settled when the switch comes back on.
- `RoomHazardIndex.RoomHazard.IsSatisfiedBy`, what a route is planned on, counts a carried negating item only when it is worn or the client will wear it (`MovementFilter.NegatingItemUsableProbe` → `RoomSpellCounterWear.WillWear`: the setting on, the master switch on, the character able to wear it, the item not set aside after a wear that put nothing on). Standing in an uncountered hazard room, an exit into a room whose hazard shares a counter with it is not shut for the hazard (`MovementFilter.SharesHazardStoodIn`), so a re-plan from the middle of such rooms still finds a way on. Such a plan may run on through rooms of that hazard to its destination and need not step out and go round: accepted for now (user, 2026-10-10: "yes thats fine for now"). (Before 2026-10-10 a carried, unworn feather read as protected to the planner though nothing wore it: report `paradigm-20261008-202210`.)
- `RoomHazardIndex.RoomHazard.IsCounteredNow`, the test behind resting in such a room (*Health, resting & recovery → Resting in a room whose spell does damage*), asks the `NegateSpell` group of what is worn and every other group of what is held. `DescribeCounters` words each group the same way (`(worn)`, `(held)`, `the buff from … (used)`) for Settings → Periodic Damage Room Spells.
- A gear swap leaves a worn counter on while the character is in the hazard's room or one next to it: `EquipmentManager.KeepRoomProtection` withholds the `rem` and the set's own item for that slot (both slots of a paired family), fed by `AppServices.WornRoomHazardCounters`; a Location rule ending inside the hazard leaves the item on too (`ClearSlotOverride`). Report `paradigm-20261008-202210`.
- The route picker/walker only ever resolve to *sourcing* one representative item from a multi-item group (whichever the acquisition pipeline can actually reach — here, trollskin via a shop). The client's path-item tracking accepts **any** member of the any-of group, so equipping a different group member counts as protected (fixed for report `paradigm-20260829-203409`, when tracking was still pinned to the one item it originally chose).

### Room-spell hazard shape 2 — TextBlock action guarded by `failitem <itemNum>`
*Status: CONFIRMED (ice cavern by user 2026-08-10, reports `paradigm-20260810-201953` / `-202239`) · Realm: both (Silver River `failitem` guards differ)*

- **The entry spell has `Abil 148` (TextBlock → a `TBInfo.Number`); the TBInfo `Action` is a colon-separated command chain.** A leading run of `failitem N` tokens before a harmful `cast <spell>` means **"if you HOLD any listed item N, abort the chain (safe); if you hold none, fall through to the damage cast."**
- **Worked example — Silver River:** `Spell:753` → `Abil-0 148`(TextBlock **2750**). TBInfo 2750 `Action` (stock): `failitem 690:failitem 691:failitem 1181:message 2096:cast 754`. Items 690 *log raft* / 691 *wooden skiff* / 1181 *silverbark canoe* are the boats; holding any one aborts before `cast 754`. *(DATA-VERIFIED: Paradigm's TB 2750 adds a fourth guard, `failitem 3609`; stock doesn't.)*
- **`failitem` and `checkitem` look through everything the player holds, worn or not** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p DLL, `_perform_matched_action` `0x470209`, Realm: Stock; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, Realm: Paradigm: "paradigm is the same as stock")*. On Stock, both steps (`checkitem` at `0x470f35`, `failitem` at `0x47100c`) compare the item number with the 100 entries of the pack array (`player+0xd8`, loops at `0x470f7a` and `0x471051`) and then the 50 of the key ring (`player+0x334`, `0x470f9b` and `0x471072`). Neither reads the worn array (`player+0x62c`).
  - **A worn item is still in the pack array:** `_wear_armour` (`0x41c846`) writes only the worn slots, and `_remove_item_from_inventory` (`0x41b2c8`) clears a worn slot only when no other copy of the item is left in the pack array (`0x41b3d5`–`0x41b408`). So wearing an item doesn't take it out of a `failitem`'s sight.
  - So an item that counters through `failitem` only has to be held: the boats, the rope and grapple, the climbing harness (which has a wear slot, `Worn` 10) and the sunstone wristband (`Worn` 14; *Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*). This is the other half of *Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*, where the list is asked of what is worn alone: which of the two an item needs follows from which of the two it counters by, not from whether it can be worn.
- **Not every `failitem` is a hazard:** `failitem` is used 139× across TBInfo — many are quest "don't re-give" guards like `failitem 622:giveitem 622`; only the ones ending in a harmful `cast` are hazards.
- **Ice cavern (Frozen Cavern) up/down slide** *([CONFIRMED by user 2026-08-10, reports `paradigm-20260810-201953` / `-202239`])* — the descent rooms (`10/276`–`10/295`) cast `Spell:1144` "ice cavern level 1" / `Spell:1145` "level 2", which check for a **rope & grapple** (item **191**): hold it and the slide is safe, lack it and you're **teleported down and take heavy damage**.
  - In the data the entry spell's TextBlock is **9407** (`failitem 191:failitem 930:random 9408`; `9408` does the `teleport … cast 1142` damage). The room-hazard machinery already handles this `failitem` shape — but see the encoding gotcha next.
- **DATA ENCODING GOTCHA — a TextBlock spell's TB number is NOT always in `AbilVal`.** Most room-entry hazard spells put the `TBInfo.Number` in the `Abil 148` slot's `AbilVal` (e.g. desert 683 → 2653, river 753 → 2750). But a **large class** (~40 spells: the ice cavern 1144/1145, blackwood 1040, graveyard 1126, bone dock 1152, fungus 1205, the highlands/farms 5500-series, caverns 5788/5789, …) leave `AbilVal-0 = 0` and stash the TB number in the spell's **`MinBase`/`MaxBase`** instead (ice cavern 1144 → MinBase `9407`).

**Client use:**
- `RoomHazardIndex.WalkSpellChain` now falls back to `MinBase`/`MaxBase` when the Abil-148 `AbilVal` is 0 — before that fix every one of these hazards was invisible to the router, so no protection was ever offered (the ice-cavern route picker never surfaced).
- `SpellTextBlock` holds that fallback for every reader of a room spell's block: `RoomHazardIndex`, `RoomSpellTeleportClassifier` and `RouteExpResolver` (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Room-spell monster summons*).

### Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin
*Status: CONFIRMED (user; `failspell` 2026-07-28, report `paradigm-20260728-201619`; sunstone possession 2026-08-27, report `paradigm-20260827-112011`) · Realm: differs (Paradigm `failspell`, stock `checkspell`)*

- **A TextBlock action guarded by a buff check — `checkspell` OR `failspell`** (a buff check, not an item check).
  - `failspell S T` *([CONFIRMED by user 2026-07-28])*: "if buff S is **not** active, the damage fires."
  - `checkspell S T` **also branches to T when buff S is ABSENT** — T is the damage branch, not a safe one
    *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-26 — deduced from the data plus confirmed rules; Stock not yet seen live)*. Stock's
    T for the desert (TB 2654) is `failitem 1180:cast 712:random 2655` / `checkitem 1180:random 2655`: it
    casts the thirst damage (712) unless you hold the sunstone. Since the waterskin buff is confirmed to stop
    that damage, 2654 can only be the no-buff branch. (An earlier note here defined `checkspell` as "if buff
    S is active, branch to T (safe)" — wrong.)
  - Either way the survival model is identical — the room punishes you unless buff S is up. The client's
    `RoomHazardIndex` already reads both directives' T as the buff-absent branch.
- **Worked example — Scorching Desert** `12/853` `Spell:683` → TextBlock **2653**: `failspell 711 2654:random 2655` on **Paradigm 1.9.1** — **`failspell`, not `checkspell`** — but `checkspell 711 2654:random 2655` on **stock v1.11p** *(DATA-VERIFIED — the directive differs by realm)*. The client's hazard parser first handled only `checkspell` and so walked the Paradigm desert unprotected (report `paradigm-20260728-201619`).
  - Map 12 also has a `failspell 711` variant on `Spell:684`.
  - Buff 711 "waterskin" (`Dur 600`) is conferred by **using** the *waterskin* (item 283, `Abil 43` CastsSp→711, 3 uses).
- **On Paradigm the desert's damage is done by a follow-on spell cast on a character without the waterskin buff** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "the desert rooms spell damage is done by a follow on spell if they dont have a waterskin buff"; Realm: Paradigm)*. The room spell itself carries no damage figure: desert spell #683 and desert spell 2 #684 have only the TextBlock ability (148 → 2653 / 2658) and the description ability (115), with `MinBase` / `MaxBase` 0.
  - **The link from the room spell to that follow-on is not in the Paradigm data** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, `data-Paradigm-1.9.1`, Spells and TBInfo)*: TB 2653 / 2658 are `failspell 711 2654` / `failspell 711 2659`; the set has no TBInfo 2654 or 2659 and no spell of those numbers; no textblock in it has a `cast 712`; no spell names 711 or 712 in an ability slot. Desert damage #712 (`Abil 1` Damage, `MinBase` 5, `MaxBase` 20) is in the Paradigm Spells table with an empty `Casted By`. On Stock the same record's `Casted By` is Textblock #2654 and #2659, the blocks `checkspell 711 2654` / `2659` run.
  - **The follow-on is desert damage #712, 5 to 20 a cast** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked whether the Paradigm follow-on is #712, desert damage, 5 to 20 per cast: "yes"; Realm: Paradigm)*. Its line is the thirst prompt seen on Paradigm (the trigger messages at the end of this topic). (An earlier note asked this; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **Client use:** `RoomSpellDamageClassifier` reads a `failspell` whose block the set lacks as damage on every cast with no figure, except behind a room spell in its table of follow-ons the user has named (`ConfirmedFollowOns`: #683 and #684 → #712), where it reads that spell's record. So Settings → Periodic Damage Room Spells lists #683 and #684 on Paradigm ticked, with Damage *5–20* and Comes *every tick: desert damage is cast on a character without the waterskin buff* (*Health, resting & recovery → Resting in a room whose spell does damage*). The table is the user's word and not the data's: an entry is added on a confirmation only.
- **The desert spell does two things — damage AND a random teleport — and the two protections are NOT equivalent** *([CONFIRMED by user 2026-07-28, report `paradigm-20260728-201619`])*.
  - The waterskin buff (711) only stops the **damage** portion; it does not stop the random teleport.
  - The **sunstone wristband** (item 1180) prevents the **entire** interaction (damage + teleport), so **if you have the sunstone you don't need a waterskin at all.**
  - **The sunstone grants desert immunity by POSSESSION** *([CONFIRMED by user 2026-08-27, report `paradigm-20260827-112011`]; [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked whether every item that cancels a room spell has to be worn: "no, phoenix feather has to be worn to negate, sunstone wristband does not")* — it can be worn, but the player only needs to *have* it (carried or worn), matching the `failitem` "if you HOLD the item" mechanic. Why the two items differ is the mechanism: the wristband is a `failitem` item (*Room-spell hazard shape 2 — TextBlock action guarded by `failitem <itemNum>`*, where the Stock DLL reads the pack), the feather a `NegateSpell` item (*Room-spell hazard shape 1 — direct damage, negated by an item's `NegateSpell-N`*, where it reads what is worn).
  - In the data the wristband is a `failitem 1180` guard sitting one-to-two `random` hops below the `failspell` (e.g. `2653 → random 2655 → random 2700` and `2658 → random 2660`), guarding the sandstorm/sinkhole casts (713/714/743) — which are the only desert damage that fires above `maxlevel 19`, i.e. what actually hits a high-level character. (Its `NegateSpell` covers only 713; the reliable signal is the `failitem`, not the negator.)
- **Protection is duration-based, not carry-based** *([CONFIRMED by user])*. `use waterskin` applies buff 711, which lasts its listed `Dur` in spell rounds like any cast buff — `use` applies it engine-side exactly as casting `bless` would *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*: 600 × 3s = **30 min** (see *Timing & rounds → Spell round (3s) and durations*; an earlier note said "600 = 10 min game-time", which was wrong). You are protected only **while the buff is up** — carrying the item alone does nothing. If you're still in a desert/hazard room that needs the buff when it **expires**, you must `use waterskin` **again** to re-apply it.
  - **The buff's length doesn't depend on level, and is the same on both realms** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data, Stock 1.11p and Paradigm 1.9.1, Spells #711)*: `Dur` 600 with `DurInc` 0, `DurIncLVLs` 0 and `Cap` 0, so 600 spell rounds for any character: 1800 s at the nominal 3 s round, about 1824 s at the 3.04 s round observed on Paradigm (*Timing & rounds → Spell round (3s) and durations*).
  - **Its line is the spell's caster line; it has no applied or wear-off line of its own** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, both realms' message data, the record linked to Spells #711)*: `CasterMessage` `You take a swig of water from your waterskin.`, with `AppliedMessage` and `AppliedEndsWith` empty.
  - **Nothing in either data set removes it by number** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data)*: no spell carries RemovesSpell (122) with 711. The buff's own abilities are AC (2) with value 0 and DescMsg (115) 66. Paradigm has three spells with DispellMagic (73) on AC: primordial echo (5140), restore body (5770) and reverse time (5837). They do not reach it: each is a monster's spell on itself (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Cure-spell identification — which spells REMOVE each ailment*, the DispellMagic bullets; an earlier `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` here asked whether they strip the buff, settled 2026-10-10 from the Stock DLL and the spells' records at the user's direction). No line of theirs is read for the buff; the thirst line stays the correction for anything the clock misses.
  - **What ends it early: dying, or a room that purges buffs (negate magic)** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked what ends the buff early besides death: "dying or walking through a room that purges buffs, negate magic"; Realm: both)*. In the data *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data, both sets)* negate magic is spell #310, DispellMagic (73) with value 0; it is the room spell of 12 rooms on Stock and 16 on Paradigm, and two more room spells carry the same ability: nanati dispel #891 (3 rooms) and draka tomb #1115 (1 room). Negate magic is also cast by textblocks ahead of a teleport: every Paradigm transport-token block (TBInfo 3281–3285, 3362, 5436: `…:adddelay 10:cast 310:teleport …`) and a few room commands (TBInfo 9295 `go portal` / `enter portal` / `go mirror portal` / `enter mirror portal`, `enter tapestry` 9498, `enter portal` 9649, Paradigm's `go courtyard` 5791). Two more dispels of value 0 are cast by room commands: portal dispel #645 (`touch ruby`, TBInfo 4011) and opaque field #213 (`sit throne`, TBInfo 4285, 2 rooms; `go arch` / `enter arch` / `go field` / `enter field`, TBInfo 5001, 4 rooms). On Stock one room spell reaches a dispel through its textblock and not its own abilities: hydra boss check #1361 (1 room, TBInfo 4120) casts portal dispel #645, DispellMagic value 0. **A dispel cast by a room command ends the buff as well** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, asked whether the dispels cast by a room command or by a room spell's textblock should end the tracked buff too: "yes")*. Room spells that only remove other spells by number (stop drowning #515, on the desert's own map 12, removes 512 and 513) take nothing off the waterskin buff.
  - **The waterskin is the only counter of this kind in either set** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, imported game data)*: the one buff a room's `checkspell` / `failspell` asks for that an item casts. Item 283, `ItemType` 5, 3 uses, CastsSp 711; asked for by room spells 683 (902 rooms on Stock, 936 on Paradigm) and 684 (43 rooms on each).
- **Each `use` consumes one charge; a fresh waterskin carries 3 charges** *([CONFIRMED by user])* (the item's `Uses` field). When a waterskin is spent, you need another one — so players typically carry **2–3 waterskins** into the desert. Provisioning must therefore stock enough total charges to cover the expected time in the hazard stretch, not just "one waterskin."
- **Routing model:** carry the source item(s), `use` on entering the first hazard room to raise the buff, and **re-`use` whenever the buff lapses while still inside a hazard room**, consuming a charge each time; when charges run out mid-stretch and no spare waterskin remains, halt rather than walking a room unprotected.
- **Client policy — the hazard counter item is not used with the master switch off** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: "with the master switch off, it shouldnt automatically swap gear". With `AutoModeController.KillSwitchEngaged`, `AutoHazardCounterProvisioner` sends no `use`, no re-raise and no "I'm out of …" say, and does not halt the walk; the skips are counted under "Hazard counter item". Back on, a follower standing in a hazard room drinks at once (`AppServices.OnMasterSwitchChanged`). Nor is a refresh offered to the cast pass while it is off.
- **Client policy — the buff is tracked quietly and raised again shortly before it wears off, not sooner** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: "for the waterskin hazard, specifically with auto-sneaking on... it should look for an empty room to use the waterskin to re-apply the buff. but the buff should be quietly tracked and \"recast\" before it wears off but not too soon before it wears off or we'll be using a lot more waterskins than we should be." The numbers are the client's:
  - **On since:** the moment a `use` of ours goes out, set again when the buff's line shows, which also starts the clock for a `use` typed by hand. **Lasts:** the spell's `Dur` × 3 s, 1800 s, the nominal round being the shorter of the two.
  - **Forgotten** on a death (*Death & corpse recovery → Death wipes all effects*; a hang-up death worked out at the login too, `RoomTracker.PlayerDeathInferred`), on entering a room whose own spell strips the buff (`RoomBuffStripIndex.StripsBuff`: a DispellMagic in the room spell's chain or in a spell its textblock casts, or a RemovesSpell naming the buff), on sending a command of the room that casts such a spell (`RoomBuffStripIndex.CommandStripsBuff`, asked from `AppServices.NoteSentForRoomCommand` for every command sent, typed or the client's own), on a token use (`TokenTracker.TokenUsed`; user, 2026-10-10, asked whether a token use should forget the buff: "yes"), on a profile load and on a change of game-data set. Unknown counts as off when a hazard room is next. The room command is judged when it is sent, and no line of the game's is read for it: a line's steps run left to right (*Room-command refusals*), so a cast written ahead of its conditions lands whatever comes of them (Stock's `enter portal:cast 310:failability 127:…`), and one behind a condition that failed did not, in which case the buff is only forgotten early. The cast pass's own strip-room gate (`RoomBuffStripIndex.StripsBuffs`) is not widened with these: it asks what the room spell does of itself. (An earlier note here said a dispel cast by a textblock was not seen; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **A dropped link pauses the clock; it does not forget the buff** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: "yes, buffs survive disconnects, relogs.. .etc... we should have buffs that we're tracking persist between sessions.. BUT for each buff we're tracking, as soon as we've disconnected all timers need to be paused until we're back in the game, then they all resume." The clock stops at the disconnect (`AutoHazardCounterProvisioner.Pause`, from the same handler as `CastingDirector.PauseBuffTimers`) and runs on with the time it had left at the first in-game prompt (`Resume`, on `PromptScanner.PromptObserved`); nothing is sent in between, by any road: a thirst line that shows on the way back in, ahead of that prompt, counts the buff as off and its `use` waits. A buff whose own line shows in that stretch starts then, and the time away is not added to it. What it had left is kept across a client restart with every other buff on the character (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Buff timers across a disconnect*; an earlier note here said it was not kept, superseded 2026-10-10). (An earlier note here said a dropped link forgets the buff, so a reconnect in the desert cost a charge; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **With Auto-Sneak on, the refresh window is the last 60 s** (`AutoHazardCounterProvisioner.RefreshWindowSeconds`): twelve 5 s combat rounds, room to finish a fight, find a room with no NPCs on a sneaked walk and get the round's one between-round cast, at the cost of a thirtieth of a charge when the refresh goes out at the window's start. **With Auto-Sneak off there is no window**: nothing is searched for, so the refresh keeps to the last call, by the "not too soon" of the ruling.
  - **Only where it matters:** standing in a room the buff counters, or, with Auto-Sneak on, with one within the next 5 planned steps of the walk or loop (`LookaheadSteps`). With Auto-Sneak off nothing is looked ahead for: the first `use` goes out at the hazard's edge, on the step's last call. Elsewhere nothing is refreshed, whatever the clock says.
  - **No walk has to be running** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: asked whether the tracked refresh should also run for a character standing in a countered room by hand, "if auto master toggle is on, yes, if off, no". With no walk, loop or leader the cast pass keeps the buff up by the same clock and windows; the "I'm out of …" say and the halt stay a walk's (and a follower's say).
  - **The last call is the last 15 s** (`ForcedLeadSeconds`; also the buff off or unknown): three rounds, one for a cast already made this round, one for the `use`, one for a retry. Then the `use` goes out where the character stands: at the step into a countered room, on a follower's arrival in one, or from the cast pass while standing in one.
  - **The step waits for its `use` to be answered** (`MovementCoordinator.HazardBuffGate`): until the buff's line or a refusal, three seconds at most, so it goes in with the buff on. With Auto-Sneak off nothing else held it, and it went in on the heels of a `use` that might be refused.
  - **Known and left as they are:**
    - a `use` the game ignores with no line at all is believed on for its full length, until the thirst line corrects it; on a walk that line then reads as out of charges, and halts;
    - at the last call the cast pass drinks for the room stood in even when the next step leaves the desert;
    - the hazard `use` does not consult the lair-entry buff hold (`LairEntryDebuffHold`): at a lair's doorstep in the desert it takes the round's cast ahead of the pre-attack debuff, which is right for a survival item.
- **Client policy — with Auto-Sneak on the `use` waits for a room with no NPCs, and goes out anyway at the last call** *(user, 2026-10-10)*: the first half is the ruling above; asked what to do if no empty room turns up before the buff runs out: "yes it should use it anyway, at this point its more important to just use it, clear the room and continue, if thats the options they have set". Inside the window the `use` is held exactly as a held buff is (*Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine*, Sneak keeping): the walk stops in the next room with no NPCs, the `use` goes out, the re-sneak is answered, and the walk goes on. A `use` forced over a kept sneak is reported as a sneak lost in that room, so *Clear hostiles when sneak fails* clears the room when it is ticked and the room is inside the Min/Max window, and otherwise the walk goes on unsneaked as after any lost sneak. With Auto-Sneak off nothing is waited for and the `use` goes out at the last call only.
- **There is NO wear-off message for the waterskin buff** *([CONFIRMED by user])*. So routine refresh cannot be reactive — the client **must TIME it** (predictively re-`use` a margin before the buff's `Dur` would expire; this is the PRIMARY refresh). The lapse prompt below is only a **reactive backstop**: when the timer's estimate is off and the buff drops early, the room re-emits the prompt and the client fires **exactly ONE** `use waterskin` to re-raise — not a client-side wear-off reaction (there's no such line), but a correction to a mistimed timer.
- **Lapse / sandstorm spells are derivable from the checkspell chain.** `checkspell 711 2654` — the token's second int (2654) is the buff-ABSENT target TB; that block's `cast` is the lapse-damage spell. In the desert that's **spell 712 "desert damage"** (its CasterMessage is the thirst prompt); **spell 713 "desert sandstorm"** is the separate random-chance teleport, not a lapse signal.
  - Stock's TB 2658 → 2659 has the same shape. On **Paradigm**, TB 2654 and 2659 don't exist, so the thirst damage and sandstorm don't come from that branch there; holding the sunstone (not wearing it) still prevents **both** the thirst damage and the desert teleport *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)* — see the possession bullet above.
- **Trigger + confirmation messages** *([CONFIRMED by user])* — all in the Messages game-data table, so match by record number, not hardcoded realm text. **These lines are plain text with no `{s}` placeholder**, so they're matched by literal case-insensitive substring, not the caster-message regex:
  - Desert lapse prompt — drink now (Spells#712): `You suffer in the desert heat... you need water, soon!` The game's own signal that the buff has lapsed while still in the hazard. Fire ONE `use waterskin` on this line.
  - Self re-`use` success (Spells#711): `You take a swig of water from your waterskin.` Confirms a charge burned and buff 711 re-applied. A `use waterskin` that draws no such line before the NEXT lapse prompt means charges/waterskins are exhausted → halt, don't walk on unprotected.
  - Witnessing a party member drink: `<name> takes a swig of water from a waterskin.` How the leader observes a follower successfully re-buffing (each member reacts to their own desert prompt).

**Client use:**
- `RoomHazardIndex.ScanTextBlock` parses both `checkspell` and `failspell` into the same buff-counter, guarded on an item actually casting the buff (so a `failspell` on a buff no carried item raises is ignored).
- A `failitem` guard found by chasing a buff-gate's `random`-linked failure branch is folded into the SAME requirement group as the buff source, so having **either** the waterskin **or** the sunstone clears the desert for routing. This mirrors how the river raft/canoe `failitem` guards (top-level, not nested) let a boat-carrier route the river.
- The `BuffCounter` also carries the immunity guards, so the buff-refresh provisioner **skips the `use waterskin` entirely** when a sunstone is held (carried or worn) rather than spending a pointless charge (report `paradigm-20260827-112011`).
- The client resolves the lapse prompt via the Messages record linked to Spells#712, so it tracks the active set rather than hardcoded realm text.
- **`use waterskin` ends a sneak and a hide** (it casts spell 711, `Targets` 1; *Sneaking — commands, equip order, and the sneak state machine*, the `use <item>` bullet of *What ends a sneak*), and `AutoHazardCounterProvisioner`'s `use` is marked like any sent command (`AppServices.NoteSentForSneak`).
- **Who sends the `use`** (2026-10-10, the two Client policy bullets of this topic):
  - **Inside the window, the between-round cast pass** (`CastingDirector.SetClientUseSource`, asked `AutoHazardCounterProvisioner.DueNow` on every pass and sending through `FireDue`). It is not a buff slot: it answers to neither Auto-Heal nor Auto-Bless and is due only where its hazard is. It shares the sending with the slots: one between-round cast a round, an emergency heal ahead of it, held while `SneakGuard.Holds` (`HasSneakHeldCast` then stops the walk in the next room with no NPCs; the hold is dropped the moment the `use` is no longer due or went out by another road, whether or not a pass runs), and followed by `CastFired` (the fight resumes on the `*Combat Off*`, `StealthManager.ReSneakAfterCast` takes the sneak again and holds the step for the answer).
  - **At the last call, the step itself** (`OnApproachingRoom`, asked from both engines' ready checks ahead of the sneak check, and still from the approach hook), a follower's arrival (`OnArrivedInRoom`), the cast pass while standing in a countered room (`MustGoNow`), and the lapse prompt on a walk. Each reports `UseSent`, so the cast pass counts it as the round's cast.
  - **A sneak spent by a forced `use`** raises `SneakSpentHere` → `CombatStateTracker.NoteSilentSneakLoss`, the entry the sneak-failed clear already listens on. Only when the character was sneaking or hidden at the send (`SneakGuard.Holds` and `StealthManager.IsStealthed` together): the guard alone also holds for any move in flight with Auto-Sneak on, and a sneak that had already failed is not one the `use` lost.
- **A `use` the game turns away** is read for 5 s behind our own send, in the Stock engine's wording (*Items, inventory & equipment → Equip → use → restore swap for a readied buff item*): `You have already cast a spell this round!` puts the clock back and the `use` is tried again next round; `You don't have …` and `There are no more uses in …` naming the item, and `You may not use that item!`, set the item aside until the count carried is seen to differ (more, fewer or none: it is checked on every look, the cast pass's once a second included, so a spent one sold and a fresh one bought is caught at none) or the buff's line shows. An item the client's charge count reads as empty (`CarriedChargeReadout.RemainingForName`) is not sent at all. Nothing is sent or stamped while the engine send gate is up. One `use` goes out per window: the send itself stamps the buff as on.
- **"Next round" holds for both roads.** A `use` inside its window is offered to the cast pass again, and the pass keeps to a cast a round. One that could not wait (the step's last call, a follower's arrival, the thirst line) is owed to the pass from the refusal on: due wherever the character stands, sent when the pass has the next round's cast, and not sent by the step or the thirst line meanwhile. A step that was waiting on it waits on, six seconds at most, then for the answer to the `use` the pass sent. (It was sent again at every ready check: with Auto-Sneak on, a `use` and a fresh `sn` per refusal.)
- **The lapse prompt is read on both realms.** On Stock the lapse spell comes from the data (`checkspell 711 2654` → `cast 712`). Paradigm's data lacks the buff-absent block, so the link from its two desert room spells (#683, #684) to desert damage #712 comes from the one list of follow-ons the user has named (`RoomSpellDamageClassifier.ConfirmedFollowOn`, which `RoomHazardIndex.BuildHazard` asks), resting on the user's confirmation (2026-10-10: asked whether the Paradigm desert's follow-on spell is #712, desert damage, 5 to 20 a cast, "yes") and used only where the data names no lapse spell. The line is matched by the wording of the Messages record linked to Spells#712, `You suffer in the desert heat...` in both seeds, as a substring.
- **The lapse prompt counts the buff as off**, whatever the clock said (`AutoHazardCounterProvisioner.HandleThirst` → `NoteBuffAbsent`). On a walk, ours or a leader's, the one `use` goes out at once; over a kept sneak it reports the sneak spent; where the item was already refused or reads empty it says "I'm out of …" and halts in place of asking again. With nothing moving the character the line sends nothing itself and the cast pass's refresh is due where it stands.
- **Program log** (`HazardCounter`, Info): `due: …`, `waiting for a room with no NPCs …`, `used …`, `forced: …`, `refused: …`, `buff tracking reset (…)`, `buff … taken off by …`, `buff … is off: the room's lapse line showed …`, `buff clock paused …`, `buff clock resumed …`; the step's wait shows as the `HazardBuff` gate's own assert and clear. **Bug report:** *Hazard buff* under Sneak keeping (on since, runs out, the window, what a due `use` waits on, a round refusal being waited out, a step held).

### Hazard severity — survivable damage vs grave
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-02 (user + game-data trace, Paradigm 1.9.1) · Realm: Paradigm*

Among protectable hazards, a further split governs whether the navigator may offer to **cross it unprotected** (walk in and eat the effect on the user's say-so):

- **Survivable damage** — the unprotected outcome is only a `Damage` hit: a direct `Damage` ability, OR a TextBlock `cast` of a spell whose own chain is `Damage`-only.
  - Example: the **Silver River** (`Rooms.Spell 753`) → TB `failitem 690/691/1181/3609` (any raft; the `3609` guard is Paradigm-only — stock's TB 2750 has `690/691/1181`) `: cast 754`, where spell **754 "battered"** is a plain `Damage` spell. You just take the hit and keep walking, so "cross unprotected — take the damage" is a legitimate choice (survivable = can't displace you or start a death timer; it can still kill a weak character — see *Teleport vs walking route choice*).
  - Lava / magma heat, `Spell 526`, is the same shape — a direct `Damage` ability.
- **Grave** — the chain reaches an `EndCast` death-timer, a `teleport`/`transfer` (forced relocation), or a `checkspell`/`failspell` buff-gate (drown / suffocation / desert-heat-death). These can END or DISPLACE you, not just hurt you, so the counter is the only safe way past — the navigator must **never** offer to cross them unprotected.
  - Conservatively, ANY `EndCast` or buff-gate is treated as grave.

**Client use:**
- Encoded as `RoomHazard.IsSurvivableDamage`; classifier `RoomHazardIndex.IsSurvivableHazardDamage`.

### Crystal Lake: the sea room spells
*Status: the chances [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (game data: `data-Paradigm-1.9.1` and `data-v1.11p`; reports `paradigm-20261009-123349`, `paradigm-20261009-135049`, `paradigm-20261009-135314`); that it teleports that often, boat or no boat, and what the lake is for CONFIRMED 2026-10-09 (user); the galleon's rooms, that nobody loops the teleport rooms, that the other lake rooms need no raft, who may enter the lake, the Weald room's terms and Stock's coast CONFIRMED 2026-10-10 (user) · Realm: both, differing on the coast*

- **A raft or skiff does not keep Crystal Lake from teleporting you, and nobody should walk into its room-spell area** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user; Realm: both)*. Asked whether a boat leaves a character under level 50 teleported about two casts in three, the user answered: "yes it does teleport that often, any character on stock or paradigm, should never enter the room spell area of crystal lake, even with a raft, unless they're trying to goto the pirate ghaleon in which case, they grab their raft, sit in the room spell and wait til they get teleported.... under level 50's, it happens real fast, lvl 50's and above, can take a very long time."
  - So the teleport **is the way to the pirate galleon**: take a raft, sit in a sea room, and wait. Under level 50 it comes fast; at level 50 and over it can take a very long time.
  - **The pirate galleon is the `Ancient Galleon` at `17/981`–`17/985`** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: asked whether it is, "yes")*, the five rooms the with-boat teleport table `9396` lands in (below).
  - **Nobody loops the lake's teleport rooms, and the lake's other rooms need no raft** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: both)*: "no one loops crystal lake because each sea spell has a teleport, so its not feasible to loop. no user walks on those teleport rooms specifically, unless they're trying to goto the ancient galleon, and you can walk around in the non teleport rooms without a raft."
  - That holds at level 50 and over with a boat too: asked whether the lake should stay ordinary ground for such a character, the user referred back to the same answer. And a route card offering a raft to shorten a route: "if it involves crystal lake, no".
  - **Who may enter the lake** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: both)*: "only typed moves should enter the lake unless the user points to the bloodwood weald teleport room or the ancient galleon".
  - **The Bloodwood Weald's room takes level 50 and a boat, both** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: Paradigm)*. Asked whether the walk pointed at that room (the lake room carrying `5258`, below) needs a raft and level 50 together or either one: "both lvl 50 and raft or skiff together".
