Earlier the same day: "no navigation system should try to walk to this room as a means to teleport to the bloodwood weald if the player is under level 50 and doesn't have a log raft/skiff", and that it applies "only on paradigm until they decide they want to remove that room spell from that room".
  - **On Stock the coast is the way to White Forest, and the Isle of Bones is never walked to across the lake** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; Realm: Stock for the coast, both for the isle)*. Told that the data puts a sea spell on 581 of Stock's 611 lake rooms, coast included, that the shortest walk from White Forest to town passes 15 of them and that there is no spell-free way, and asked whether automatic walks may use those coast rooms on Stock: "on stock it is ok". Before that: "they can reach the white forest by hugging the coast and the isle of bones is reached from inside the library as part of the 5th alignment quest, you dont walk directly there across the lake, ever... it has a teleporting exit if you try to walk onto it."
- **Most of Crystal Lake's rooms cast a room spell that can teleport whoever walks in.** `Rooms.Spell` is `1076` "sea 1", `1077` "sea 2" or `1078` "sea 3": 116 / 149 / 125 rooms on Paradigm 1.9.1 (390 in all, on map 17; all named `Crystal Lake` but two of the `1077` rooms, `Damp Cave Entrance` and `trina`), 181 / 194 / 206 on Stock 1.11p (581 in all, on map 17; all `Crystal Lake` but one `Crystal Lake, Near Docks` on `1076`). Each spell's ability 148 names its textblock: `9358`, `9359`, `9360`. Their row in the table of *Room spells that teleport* gives the chain in brief; the detail is here. The spell is cast on entering and again on the room spell's tick while the character stays, so the chances below are per cast, not per entry (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Room-spell monster summons*).
- **Some Crystal Lake rooms carry no spell at all**, and a walk crosses the lake through them untouched, with no raft (the user's statement above; the data agrees). Of the rooms named `Crystal Lake…` on map 17, 222 of Paradigm 1.9.1's 610 carry no sea spell (216 `Crystal Lake` with `Spell 0`, 4 `Crystal Lake, Inlet`, 1 `Crystal Lake, Near Docks`, and 1 `Crystal Lake` carrying `5258` `bloodwood weald temp`) and 30 of Stock 1.11p's 611 (26 `Crystal Lake`, 4 `Crystal Lake, Inlet`, all `Spell 0`). No exit of a lake room names a boat in either set: the only `(Item: 690)` / `(Item: 691)` exits are the two `(Item: 691)` at `The Silver River, Rapids` on map 1. The one Paradigm lake room with `5258` teleports on a roll too (*Room spells that teleport*). *[OBSERVED] 2026-10-10 (game data, Paradigm)*: room `17/1457` is reachable only through `1078` sea 3 rooms (all 8 of its exits lead to them, and all 8 entries to it come from them); no exit leads from it into the Bloodwood Weald (its teleport is a room spell, not an exit, so no planner uses it); and all 158 `Bloodwood Weald` rooms are reachable on foot from `1/1` with no sea room, so walks to the Weald go on foot. *[CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10 (user; Realm: Paradigm)*: "no navigation system should try to walk to this room as a means to teleport to the bloodwood weald if the player is under level 50 and doesn't have a log raft/skiff". On Paradigm 1.9.1 the lane `17/1014` → `1051` → `1050` → `1049` → `1056` → `1068` → `1067` → `1066` → `1065` → `1064` → `1062` → `1041` → `17/1026` is as long as the way through the `1076` rooms `17/1015`–`17/1025` beside it.
- **The three textblocks differ only in their last two lines** (`9361` for sea 1, `9362` for sea 2, `9363` for sea 3):
  - `failitem 690:failitem 691:random 9357`
  - `maxlevel 49:checkitem 690:random 9445`
  - `maxlevel 49:checkitem 691:random 9445`
  - `minlevel 50:checkitem 690:random 9361`
  - `minlevel 50:checkitem 691:random 9361`
  - Items `690` *log raft* and `691` *wooden skiff* are the only boats named: a silverbark canoe (`1181`) does nothing here.
  - Read by the rules in *Room-command refusals* (`failitem`, `checkitem`, `minlevel`, `maxlevel`), the line order in *Cast-on-walk exits and random teleports* (the first line whose action succeeds ends the scan) and the roll-table rule in *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Room-spell monster summons* (a roll of 0–99 runs the first line whose number is above it: *Textblock directives — the Stock interpreter's list*). Those were read from the Stock engine; the user's answer above confirms the outcome on both realms.
  - **These are the only room spells in either set whose textblock has a line for the holder of its `failitem` item** (a `checkitem` on the same item), and both level bands of it lead on to a teleport. The river (`2750`), the ice cavern (`9407`, `9410`), the cracked pit (`4077`) and the desert stop at their `failitem`: hold the item and nothing happens.
- **With no boat: teleported on 7 casts in 10.** `9357` is `30:addexp 0` / `100:random 9383`, and `9383` is a table of `teleport <room> 17` lines: 89 different rooms on Paradigm 1.9.1, nearly all `Crystal Lake` (with and without a sea spell), plus `Crystal Lake, Inlet`, `Crystal Lake, Near Docks` and `White Forest, Landing`.
- **With a boat at level 49 or under: still teleported on about 2 casts in 3.** `9445` is `25:random 9363` / `50:random 9357` / `100:message 2906:random 9396`. Half the roll is `9396`, five equal bands of `teleport 981 17` … `teleport 985 17` (the `Ancient Galleon` rooms); a quarter is the no-boat table `9357`. That is 0.50 + 0.25 × 0.70 = 67.5% (67.55% on Stock), against 70% with no boat.
- **With a boat at level 50 or over: hardly ever.** Every branch is behind `nomonsters`, so nothing fires with a monster in the room.
  - sea 1, `9361`: `30:addexp 0` / `100:nomonsters:random 9388`; `9388` is `50:addexp 0` / `53:message 2906:random 9396` / `70:message 3071:summon 904:summon 904` / `100:message 2909:summon 891:summon 891:summon 891:summon 891`. The Galleon on 0.70 × 0.03 = 2.1% of casts.
  - sea 2, `9362`: `40:addexp 0` / `100:nomonsters:random 9389`; `9389` only summons. No teleport.
  - sea 3, `9363`: `50:addexp 0` (Stock: `10:addexp 0`) / `100:nomonsters:random 9390`; `9390` summons, and on 3 rolls in 100 goes to `9394` (`5:message 2906:random 9396` / `10:random 9390` / `75:random 9388` / `100:random 9389`). About 0.1% (Stock 0.2%).
- **Message `2906`, printed with the Galleon teleport, reads `You suddenly find your self aboard an ancient sea vessel!`, and the room is told `%s just vanished with no trace!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p message table `wccmsg2`; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. (An earlier note said the text was not recorded; superseded 2026-10-10. An earlier note asked whether a boat really leaves a character under level 50 teleported two casts in three; confirmed by the user 2026-10-09, above.)
- **With the sea rooms closed, 111 dry rooms on Stock and one on Paradigm can be reached only across them** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, game data `data-v1.11p` and `data-Paradigm-1.9.1`, through the client's room graph, every exit gate ignored, counted from `Bank of Arlysia` `17/2435`)*.
  - **Stock: White Forest and nothing else.** 108 `White Forest` rooms, `White Forest, Landing` `17/1641`, `White Forest, Shrine Entrance` `17/1745` and `Pristine Shrine` `17/1746`. The only way in is the sea room `17/1062`, whose north exit leads to the Landing (`Spell 0`); the Landing's room command `9556` (`say tree:message 2986:teleport 1642 17:message 2987`, and the same for `tree`, `say trees`, `tress`) leads on to `17/1642`, whose south exit leads back to the Landing. From the bank the crossing with the fewest sea rooms passes 8 (from `Crystal Lake, Near Docks` `17/1124` to `17/1062`), 25 steps to `17/1642`. **The way out needs no sea room:** `Pristine Shrine` has a greet teleport to `Arlysia, Outer Wall` `17/515`, 44 steps from `17/1642` to the bank.
  - **Paradigm: the one room `17/1457`** (above). White Forest there is reached by the lake's spell-free rooms, 25 steps from the bank with no sea room.
  - **The Isle of Bones is not among them on either realm: the library reaches it**, as the user said. From the bank, 64 steps with no sea room: the north door of `Library Steps` `17/1791` (`Key: 1536 [or 1000 picklocks/strength]`, the jagged bone key), the Library and its Inner Sanctum, `Monstrous Den` `17/2019` (a room-command teleport to `Filthy Room` `17/2020`), a greet teleport from there to `17/1759`, and so onto the island. `Island of Bones` `17/1752` east is `go stairs` / `go path` / `go steps` down to `17/1315`, one of 17 spell-free `Crystal Lake` rooms that ring the island and have 59 plain exits to and from sea rooms.
  - **The island's "teleporting exit"**: `17/1752` west to `17/1753` is `Cast: pre-0, post-1231`, and 12 `Island of Bones` rooms carry `1231` `island spell`, whose textblock `9511` is `maxlevel 49:random 9383`: a character of level 49 or under is put through the lake's no-boat landing table (`9383`, every band a teleport) at each cast. `17/1753` carries `1235` `face rgen` (textblock `9693`: the same line, and `minlevel 50:nomonsters:failroomitem 1686:failroomitem 1687:summon 945`).
  - (An earlier note, 2026-10-10, counted 151 Stock rooms from `1/1` over exits and room-command teleports alone: White Forest's 111, 14 `Island of Bones` rooms plus 8 bone-cavern rooms (6 `Bone Strewn Cavern`, `Bone Cavern`, `Bone Room`), the 17 spell-free `Crystal Lake` rooms and `Isle of Shadow`, 39 of them lair rooms; it left the Paradigm count unsettled and asked whether a level 50 character with a raft should cross to White Forest and the Island of Bones automatically. The greet teleports put the island on the land side, and the user's answers above settle the rest; superseded 2026-10-10.)
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10): **only typed moves enter a sea room, but for two crossings: to a place the map reaches no other way (Stock's White Forest), and to the Bloodwood Weald's room on a route card.** As built:
  - The rule is keyed on the data, not on the spell numbers: a room-entry hazard whose textblock teleports the holder of its own `failitem` item. In both sets that is `1076`, `1077` and `1078` and nothing else, so it closes Paradigm's 390 and Stock's 581 sea rooms listed above. The other room spells that teleport on a roll (*Room spells that teleport*: the desert `683` / `684`, `1257`, Paradigm's `5258`, `5788`, `5789`) are untouched: the desert keeps its waterskin and sunstone, and the rest were never hazards to the router.
  - The boat is no counter for routing: no route card offers one for the lake, none is fetched, bought or asked of the party, and one already in the pack opens no sea room by itself (it is half of what the two crossings below ask).
  - A walk whose way there crosses sea rooms has no route, the user's as much as the client's, and no card: its failure says in one line that only typed moves go into them. A sea room is never a destination. A character standing in a sea room is always planned out, by the nearest way out that leads on to the destination. (A card that offered any such crossing on the user's pick was built on 2026-10-09 and removed on the user's 2026-10-10 rule.)
  - **A place the map reaches across the sea rooms and no other way is walked to and from, by any walk, with no card.** "No other way" is judged on the map alone, every exit gate set aside, sailings and portals counted, so a key or a level never turns a place into one; and the walk takes the crossing with the fewest sea rooms, then the fewest steps (the user's "hugging the coast"). In the data that is Stock's White Forest, 8 sea rooms from the bank, and nothing else; the Isle of Bones is never crossed to on either realm (its greet and room-command teleports on dry land are ways in, so the map is not cut off there). On Paradigm it opens no destination; a character already in `17/1457` is planned out as one in a sea room is: across its 2 sea rooms by the same crossing, with level 50 and a boat, and with no route out without them, an automatic walk's as much as the user's. A walk of this kind writes one `Walker` Info line at plan time: how many sea rooms it crosses, the first and the last, and why it was allowed. When another gate stands on the way (an item, a key) the walk's route card lists those sea rooms and says the character has what the crossing asks.
  - **The Bloodwood Weald's room is offered on one route card, to a walk the user starts with that room as its destination.** It is told from the data: a room that itself teleports on arrival (`RoomSpellTeleportIndex` class red) and that the map reaches only across the sea rooms; Paradigm's `17/1457` is the only one. The card says what it is, crosses by the fewest sea rooms (2 from the bank side), and fetches nothing. A walk the client starts is never planned there.
  - **Both crossings ask level 50 and a log raft or wooden skiff, together.** For the Weald's room that is the user's rule above. **For Stock's White Forest it is the client's own policy** (2026-10-10, until the user says otherwise): the user said only "on stock it is ok"; the terms were added because the data gives about 70 casts in 100 a teleport without both and about 2 with. The level is read from the sea textblock's own `minlevel 50:checkitem …` line, the boat from its `failitem` items. With either missing there is no route, and the failure names what is missing. A level or pack not read yet counts as missing.
  - A loop has no exception, boat or no boat: its legs are planned like any route, so they go round the sea rooms, and a loop with a waypoint in one is refused at start with the reason. (A boat exception for a recorded loop's legs was built on 2026-10-09 and removed on the user's 2026-10-10 answer.)
  - The lake's rooms without a sea spell are ordinary ground: they are no hazard, need no raft and are not avoided. Which room is which is read from the room's spell, never from a list of rooms.
  - A "walk to the galleon" (take a raft, stand in a sea room, wait) is not built: "bench this for now, will revisit later, players usually do this manually" (user, 2026-10-10). A walk pointed at the galleon has no route and says so. A move the player types is not planned and is untouched.
  - (An earlier policy here, 2026-10-09 and never approved, counted a boat as protection from level 50 by a "halves the chance" threshold; withdrawn the same day on the user's ruling.)

**Client use:**
- `RoomHazardIndex.TeleportsHolders` reads the holder lines into `RoomHazard.TeleportsCounterHolders`, and `MovementFilter.HazardCounterProtects` is false for such a hazard.
- `MovementFilter.IsHazardEntryBlocked` then keeps the room closed to every plan, boat carried or not: live (walk-to, a loop's approach, Auto-Lair travel, the automatic trips), with uncountered hazards kept, and under `SuspendAcquirableGatesButUnprotectableHazards` (on `IRoomFilter`, so the loop runner's nearest-room probes, the lever detour and the toll probes use it too). It opens only for the rooms a route card's pick agreed to and for the all-gates-open search that names a failed walk's reason. It doesn't wait for the inventory to be read, since nothing carried changes it. `MovementFilter.IsClosedToRoutes` is the public "is this room one no route enters" probe.
- `BfsMapper.FindCrossing` makes the two crossings: `IsCutOffByClosedRooms` for "the map has no other way", `IRoomFilter.CrossingTerms` (`RoomHazard.CounterHolderMinLevel` and the hazard's items) for the level and the boat, fewest closed rooms first. `BfsMapper.FindPath` falls back to it for any walk unless the destination `TeleportsOnArrival`; `RouteChoicePlanner.CrossingCard` calls it for that destination, from the route picker alone.
- `LoopRunner.RefusalFor` refuses a loop with a waypoint in such a room (`Start refused: …`, raised as the loop's failure), and `RouteChoicePrompt.StartLoopAsync` asks it before walking to the loop.
- `BfsMapper.FindPath` → `FindPathOutOfClosedRooms`, on `IRoomFilter.IsClosedToRoutes`: from inside, out by the fewest sea rooms, then on.
- `RouteChoicePlanner.Evaluate`: beside a free route, the "acquire, then go" route is planned with `SuspendAcquirableGatesButUnprotectableHazards`, so no boat is offered (report `paradigm-20261009-123349`: 84 steps round against 82 through 11 sea rooms; the walk now takes the 84 with no card). A sole route is planned with the sea rooms kept closed (reports `paradigm-20261009-135049`, `paradigm-20261009-135314`: the loop walk to `17/9781` needs only the jagged bone key, and was planned through 8 to 13 sea rooms and asked for a log raft, for a way no shorter); ordinary hazard rooms are crossed and their counter asked for. (An earlier build also went round every other uncountered hazard, at any length; withdrawn 2026-10-10.) `RouteRequirement.NoProtection` and `RouteChoice.UnprotectedRoomNames` mark any card whose route enters the sea rooms: the Weald room's card, and a rule-C crossing to a place only the lake reaches when another gate on its way puts a card up. `CrossingGoalSpell` is set on the Weald room's card alone, and is what tells the dialog to say "to reach the room whose spell … teleports you on". `AutoWalkManager.NoteLakeCrossing` writes the plan-time log line for a crossing.
- `AutoWalkManager.DescribeClosedRooms` words the failure of a walk with no route for the lake; `AppServices.HazardAnnounceItems` provisions nothing for such a room.
- `RouteChoicePlanner.HazardDetour` feeds the bug report's "Hazard rooms the direct route goes round".
- `HealthManager.BuildFleeSteps` cuts a flee's route at the first step into a room `IRoomFilter.IsClosedToRoutes` keeps routes out of (`HealthManager.IsClosedToRoutes`, wired to `MovementFilter.IsClosedToRoutes`), and `HealthManager.AwayFromThePlan` / `AnotherWayOut` never pick an exit into one. A flee builds its own retreat, so the route filters do not reach it. The room the character already stands in does not count.

### Room spells that teleport
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (game data: `data-v1.11p`, `data-Paradigm-1.9.1`); the colour rule is Client policy (user, 2026-10-09) · Realm: both*

- **A room spell (`Rooms.Spell`) reaches a teleport in one of three ways** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, game data: both sets)*:

  | 1375 `solo trainer key check` | 2 / 2 | yellow | condition | TBInfo 4327 `class N:takeitem 1975:teleport <room> 17:message 837`, room 3250, 3304 or 3325 by class |
  | 5085 `under level teleport` | — / 1 | yellow | condition | TBInfo 3360 `maxlevel 79:random 3361`; 3361 is `100:teleport 1041 8` |
  | 5258 `bloodwood weald temp` | — / 1 | red | roll, with a condition | TBInfo 3457 `nomonsters:random 3470`: `70:addevil 0`, `100:cast 5259` (`bloodwood weald`: `140 = 0`, 3449–3595) |
  | 5788 `cavern 1`, 5789 `cavern 2` | — / 34, 32 | red | roll, with a condition | TBInfo 10167 `random 10168` (10169 / 10170 for 5789): `85:addevil 0`, `100:maxlevel 19:cast 5786` (5787) (`fall below`: `140 = 0`, `141 = 12`, `Targets 8`) |

  - The other placed room spells reach no teleport: 56 of Stock's 82 and 132 of Paradigm's 159, leaving out `sys j` below. The Paradigm `baenglen portal` (5624), `farnholme portal` (5676) and `talgarn portal` (5686) only summon, and every `… scatter` spell but `dao scatter` carries ScatterItems (157) and no textblock.
  - **One spell can't be read to the end:** `sys j` (943, one room in each set) → TBInfo 4042 `checkspell 935 4043:addevil 0`, and neither set has a TBInfo 4043. Nothing else on its chain teleports. Paradigm's desert blocks name a missing 2654 and 2659 the same way (*Room-spell hazard shape 3 — buff check (`checkspell` / `failspell`): the desert waterskin*), but those spells reach a teleport anyway.
  - The two sets agree on every spell they both place.
  - **`cavern 1` / `cavern 2` cast a spell the Stock engine would refuse.** `fall below` (5786 / 5787) is `Targets 8`, and Stock's `_cast_no_target` turns away a spell with that target (the `cast` bullet of *Textblock directives — the Stock interpreter's list*). Those rooms are in Paradigm's data only, and Paradigm's engine is not that DLL. `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Does a character under level 20 standing in a Paradigm `cavern 1` / `cavern 2` room get dropped to the rooms below, as the data reads?
- **Whether the teleport can be resisted** is in *Spells, buffs & conditions → Magic Resist (M.R.) and `TypeOfResists`* (the room-spell bullet); that a textblock `cast` makes no cast roll is in *Textblock directives — the Stock interpreter's list*.
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-09): the Navigation map's by-teleport overlay colours a spell room by its spell. The user first asked for red, yellow and green by "a teleport", "a chance to teleport" and "no teleports", and then settled which is which in two sentences, in this order: "if the teleport is a random chance or has a condition the room should be yellow, only if the teleport is guaranteed, should it be red", and, on seeing the table, "move the random chance teleports to red as well". As built, each way to a teleport is a path, and a path is read by what it passes:
  - **red** when a path has nothing in the way of its teleport, or has a roll in the way, whatever conditions it also passes. The rolls: a `random` table with a band that doesn't teleport or with numbers that stop short of 100 (the roll is 0–99: *Textblock directives — the Stock interpreter's list*), a `testskill`, an EndCast with an EndCast% of 1–99;
  - **yellow** when every path to a teleport passes conditions only: `minlevel`, `maxlevel`, `checkitem`, `failitem`, `takeitem`, `nomonsters`, `monsters`, `needmonster`, `class`, `race`, `goodaligned`, `evilaligned`, `checkability`, `testability`, `failability`, `price`, `checkskill`, `flag`, `test_tournament`, `roomitem`, `failroomitem`, `clearitem`, and both sides of a `checkspell` / `failspell` (the block it names and the rest of its line);
  - **green** when it reaches none;
  - **the flat spell purple, and `(teleport unknown)` in the tooltip, never green,** when no teleport was found and part of the chain couldn't be read: a spell or textblock the set lacks (`sys j`), a block with a `LinkTo` continuation, a chain more than 16 steps deep. A teleport found elsewhere on such a spell stands.
  - Only the steps ahead of a `teleport`, `cast` or `random` on its line gate it. Each line of a block is taken as a path of its own: that an earlier line didn't run is not counted as a condition on a later one.
  - A `random` table whose every band reaches a teleport without a roll of its own is not a roll, so the two ice-slide spells are the same colour. Were such a table's bands to carry different conditions it would read yellow, though it is a roll for a character meeting only some of them; no table a room spell reaches is built that way.
  - A resist roll is not counted: it is the character's own Magic Res against the spell, and only the three class filters could roll one.

**Client use:**
- `RoomSpellTeleportClassifier` reads the class of one spell; `RoomSpellTeleportIndex` holds it for every room spell of the active set and, on a set change, logs the four counts and each spell it couldn't read in full.
- The Navigation map's **Spells** chip mode `SpellDisplayMode.ByTeleport` paints it (`MapControl`), and in that mode the hover tooltip's `Room Spell:` line names it (`RoomTooltipBuilder.Build`).

### Door and gate barriers in the room display
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-14 (capture, report 091244)*

- **A lever-raised gate renders in the live room display as a *gate*, not a *door*.** At `1/1331` the
  `Obvious exits:` line reads `closed gate north, south, east, west`; after `pull lever` ("you hear the
  loud nearby rumbling of a gate") it becomes `open gate north, …`.
- **The barrier noun on the wire is "gate", and the open/closed prefix carries its live state exactly
  like a door's.** Treat "gate" and "door" as the same door-type barrier class for display parsing.
- **A door in your room changing because of someone else prints a line naming its direction.** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_open` / `_cmd_close` / `_background_update_exits`; the same on Paradigm per the user 2026-09-28. The "just closed" form captured on Paradigm, report `paradigm-20260928-110224`: standing at 1/2150 with `open door north` showing, the line named north, and the next `n` got `The door is closed!`.)*
  - Opened or closed **from the other side**: `The door to the %s just opened.` / `The door to the %s just closed.` (`The %s to the %s just …` for a gate). The engine sends it to the room on the far side of the door, so the direction is an exit of the room you're in.
  - Opened or closed **by someone in your room**: `You see %s open the door to the %s.` / `You see %s close the door to the %s.` (gate forms too).
  - **Re-locked by the engine's periodic exit reset:** `The door to the %s just locked!` / `The gate to the %s just locked!`
    - A key exit relocks with the door line. A door or gate whose pick / bash modifier is above 0 never relocks *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_background_update_exits` @0x44f45e; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*.
- **A timed exit opening or shutting prints `The exit to the %s just opened!` / `The exit to the %s just closed!`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-09-28, Stock 1.11p `_background_update_exits`; the same on Paradigm per the user)*. The user's read: it's what you see standing in the exit's room when someone else works the remote actions, or when a timed exit (the pyramid's room-spell doors) shuts again. (An earlier form of this bullet gave the same two lines to an action-opened exit, a lever's hidden passage; superseded 2026-10-09, see the next bullet.)
- **Both of those strings belong to the `Timed` exit (type 16) alone** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_background_update_exits` @0x44f5eb and @0x44f670; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: they are what a timed exit prints when it has no line of its own. A hidden exit opened by its actions prints the exit's own message to its room, or `A concealed passage opens to the %s.` when it has none (@0x46cb24–0x46cb8d), and the reset that shuts it again prints nothing in that branch (@0x44f6c9–0x44f893; *Multi-action exits and levers*). The user confirms it *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09: the line has not been seen for a lever-opened exit; "what you found is correct")*. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **Client use:**
  - `RoomDisplayParser.ParseExits` strips an `<open|closed> <door|gate>` prefix off each exit token,
    feeding the open ones into `OpenDoorDirections` so the walker skips the door-open FSM on an
    already-raised gate.
  - `RoomTracker.NoteNamedDoorClosed` (via `MovementRefusalDetector`) clears that direction from
    `OpenDoorDirections` when nothing is moving, so the next move opens the door first
    (report `paradigm-20260928-110224`); with a move in flight that way it also reverts the move.
    `NoteNamedDoorOpened` marks one open the same way; the "You see …" and "just locked!" lines use
    the same two paths. Mid-move (another direction) all of them are ignored: the line could be about
    either room.
  - `RoomTracker.NoteNamedExitChanged` adds or removes the direction from the room's shown exits
    (standing still only). `RoomTracker.ShownOpenExits` (shown, and not a shut door or gate) lets
    `SpecialExitDispatch` and the walk planner (`RemoteActionPathExpander`) cross a lever exit that is
    already open instead of re-pulling its levers or detouring to them.

### Multi-action exits and levers
*Status: CONFIRMED (timed window, fire-and-forget); CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 (user; relative order, nesting); CONFIRMED 2026-07-28 (capture, report 180730 — supersedes report 195552; redundant levers) · per-fact tags inline*

- **[CONFIRMED] A `(Hidden, Needs N Actions, {any|specific} order)` exit unlocks by issuing the listed
  command(s) from the named room + exit direction.** The action room can differ from the room the exit
  lives in (the "cross-room" case): e.g. pull a lever in room A to open an exit in room B.
- **[CONFIRMED] Repeating the action on an open exit does not close it** *(2026-10-05, user: pushing the
  brick or the stone a second time)*. A repeat is wasted, not harmful.
- **[CONFIRMED] Once opened, the exit stays open for a timed window of roughly 3–5 minutes that is NOT
  encoded anywhere in the game data.** Long enough to walk from the action room to the exit room and
  cross without racing a re-lock.
- **[CONFIRMED] Specific-order across rooms is tolerant of walk time.** For "Needs 2 Actions, specific
  order," performing action #1 (in its room) stays satisfied through the same ~3–5 min timer; you then
  walk to action #2's room and perform it, which opens the target exit, and *that* exit then stays open
  another ~3–5 min. No tight contiguous-run requirement.
- **[CONFIRMED] Confirmation is unmatchable — each action is fire-and-forget.** Each unlock action
  **does** produce a visible server response, but the wording is **different per action** and those
  TextBlocks are **not shipped in the game data**, so the client cannot await a known confirmation
  string. Send the command, don't wait for a specific reply, then proceed to the next step / the
  cardinal.
- **[CONFIRMED, user 2026-08-17] A "specific order" gate tracks ONLY its own sequence levers, in
  RELATIVE order.** For `Needs N Actions, specific order`, the gate only requires that ITS OWN actions
  fire in relative order (#1 before #2, #2 before #3, …). Pulling a lever for a *different* exit (e.g.
  the entrance lever of an alcove you must open to reach the next sequence lever) between two of the
  gate's ordered steps does **not** reset the sequence. So the client may interleave: open alcove *i*,
  pull sequence-lever *i*, repeat — the sequence stays valid.
- **[CONFIRMED, user 2026-08-17] Nested action gates can chain, and persistence covers the compound
  walk.** This lets the walker solve *nested* lever vaults (a lever whose room is itself behind another
  action-gated exit). An opened action-gated exit stays passable for the same minutes-long window, and
  opening several nested gates and re-crossing them all lands well inside it — so a multi-gate compound
  detour is safe.
  - **Grounding example (data-Paradigm-1.9.1): the 6/861 tomb vault → 6/924.** Descent
    `6/861 →D→ 6/922 →D→ 6/923 →D→ 6/924`; `6/861` D needs 4 ordered levers, in alcoves 6/919 / 6/921 /
    6/920 / 6/918. Each alcove is behind its own `Needs 1 Actions` entrance gate whose lever sits in a
    freely-walked Ancestral Tomb room (6/889 / 6/917 / 6/903 / 6/875) — genuinely one level of nesting.
- **[CONFIRMED, capture 2026-07-28 report 180730 — SUPERSEDES the earlier report-195552 "both needed"
  claim] Two guardroom levers with identical commands on one gate are REDUNDANT alternatives — one pull
  raises it.** Some `Door` exits are raised not by a same-room verb but by a `pull lever` performed in
  one or more *other* rooms — the game data annotates the door exit with an
  `Action[#N] [on the {dir} exit of room M/R]: pull lever` cell per lever room. At the Newhaven castle
  inner gate `1/1331 N`, the two guardrooms `1/1345` and `1/1339` each carry a lever, and
  **both cells carry the identical command list and a bare `Action` (StepNumber 1)** with **no `Needs N`
  modifier** on the door.
  - Scrollback proves one suffices: the exits line went `closed gate north` → `open gate north` after
    the *first* `pull lever` and stayed open through the redundant second pull. So same-command,
    same-StepNumber levers on one exit are interchangeable — pulling either raises it. (An earlier run
    misread a failure as "both must be pulled"; this direct capture retracts that.)
  - A **genuine** multi-step gate is one whose data declares an explicit `Needs N Actions` modifier or
    distinct `Action#1`/`Action#2` StepNumbers — those pull every step.
  - A same-room lever variant also exists (`1/1375 S`, the courtyard, whose lever is on this room's own
    W slot — one action, no remote detour).
- **Stock: what the engine's action handler does** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `Remote Action` handler @0x46c573, called from `_execute_input` @0x4507ae; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. An exit action is a `Remote Action` exit (type 12 in *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*). Its phrases and its action message are rows of the message table, not a textblock.
  - **The action message is printed first, whatever state the target is in**: line 2 to the room (@0x46c5e5–0x46c63b) and line 1 to the actor (@0x46c643–0x46c66c), before the handler looks at the target exit (@0x46c672). So an action answers with the same line every time. The pyramid's stone block is the worked case (*Great Pyramid puzzle climb*).
  - **A hidden target opens when all its blocked bits are clear** (@0x46ca8a–0x46cafc): the exit is queued for the exit reset with count 1 (`_add_exit_to_list(room, map, dir, 1)` @0x46cb0f), and the exit's room is told the exit's own "opens" message, or `A concealed passage opens to the %s.` when it has none (@0x46cb24–0x46cb8d). Repeating the action on an open hidden exit runs that branch again: the reset is queued again and the line is broadcast again. That agrees with the repeat rule in this topic.
  - **The open window is the exit-reset queue.** Count 1 is 5 minutes, and the queue's order can stretch it (the re-arm note in *Exit traps — search and disarm*). The reset gives an action-opened exit its blocked bits back, and that branch prints no line (`_background_update_exits` @0x44f6c9–0x44f893).
  - **`[CONFLICT — ask the user]` A door or gate target is toggled on every action** (@0x46c6bb–0x46c7d0): state 0 (open) becomes 2 (locked) and any other state becomes 0, then the far side is toggled from its own state, and the relock is queued on both sides. By that code a second pull of a lever on an open gate locks it again. The redundant-levers capture in this topic (report 180730, realm not recorded) has the gate staying open through the second pull. Question: which realm was that capture on, and does a second pull shut a lever gate on Stock? (User 2026-10-09: unsure.)
  - **A trap target in state 2 (a lever trapdoor) pushes every player and every monster in the target room through the exit** (@0x46c7dd–0x46c8ab; the monsters' side is in *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*).
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` **Specific order on Stock.** The handler ignores action *n* while the blocked bit of action *n+1* is still set (action 1 tests bit `0x20` @0x46c972, action 2 tests `0x40` @0x46c992, and so on), so the highest-numbered action is the first one it accepts. Whether the engine's action number (the exit's second parameter divided by 10) is the game data's `Action#N` wasn't traced. Question: on Stock, must a specific-order gate's levers be pulled from the highest `Action#N` down? The relative-order rule in this topic (user, 2026-08-17) has #1 before #2.
- **Client use:**
  - A walk resumed after a pause carries on from the step it stood at even when the go-act-return detour comes back through that room later (`AutoWalkManager.TryReconcileIndexAfterResume`, `RoomBeforeStep`). Matching the later visit skipped the detour and its action. Report `paradigm-20261007-202509` *([OBSERVED], Paradigm)*: the Ancient Darkwood Tree's `9/1343` S → `9/1413` is `(Hidden/Needs 1 Actions, any order)`, opened by `turn statue` in `9/1412` (Small Statue), which answers `You grasp the ivory statue, and it turns easily on its base.`; until then `s` in `9/1343` answers `There is no exit in that direction!`.
  - Walker takeaway: walk-to-action-room → send the command(s) in `StepNumber` order → walk-back to the
    exit's room → send the cardinal. The generous open window makes normal walk distances safe; do not
    gate on a data-supplied timer (there isn't one) or on parsing a confirmation line.
  - `RemoteActionPathExpander` opens nested gates recursively (open the inner door, then cross), bounded
    by a nesting-depth cap + a lever-cycle guard; past those it clean-fails. This is fully generic off
    the exit graph — no per-area code (the Asylum + Pyramid remain the only bespoke area solvers).
    A 400-step backstop caps one exit's assembled detour. [OBSERVED, game data 2026-09-30] The Darkened
    Tunnels gate `15/477 N` (2 ordered levers in `15/604` / `15/730`, the way to the new master assassin
    at `15/416`, both realms) needs a ~232-step detour once the 1000-picklocks doors are routed around;
    the earlier 200 cap stopped the walk at the shut exit (user report, 2026-09-30).
  - A lever `Door`/`KeyLocked` exit carrying action cells is promoted to `MultiActionHidden` at
    graph-build; the required-action count is the number of DISTINCT StepNumbers (same-StepNumber levers
    count as one), and the path expander pulls one cheapest alternative per StepNumber — so a redundant
    pair pulls once, a declared multi-step gate pulls all.

### Room-command reveal exits
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 (user + game-data trace) · Realm: Paradigm (1.9.1)*

- **Context:** one of two exit shapes beyond ordinary cardinals / doors / CMD-teleports that the walker
  can route through, both on the route to the Necromancer (9/1431, phoenix-feather quest). (The other is
  the item-use teleport — see *Item-use teleports*.)
- **A room-command reveal is a lever whose opener is the room CMD.** A hidden exit
  (`(Hidden/Needs N Actions)`) whose unlock isn't an exit `Action` cell but a `remoteaction` in the
  **room's CMD chain**.
- **Canonical: 9/1012 "Crumbling Ruin, Entrance" CMD 1422 =
  `clear rubble:testskill strength 0 …: remoteaction 1012 … 0`** (synonyms `move`/`push` ×
  `rubble`/`mound`/`rock`; the trailing `0` = the N exit). You type `clear rubble`, the N passage to
  9/1013 opens.
- **The reveal is one-directional.** Only the closed side (9/1012→N) needs it; the reverse
  (9/1013→S→9/1012) is a normal always-open exit.
- **The opened exit stays open a few minutes.**

### `testskill` obstacle checks
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-18 (user + game-data trace) · Realm: Paradigm (1.9.1)*

- **`testskill <stat> <difficulty> <failTextblock>` is a stat check with a random roll.** Found in a
  room-CMD / greet / spell action chain: the game rolls a die in a range tied to the difficulty and
  compares it to the character's `<stat>`.
  - Roll **under** your stat → the check **passes** and the chain's follow-on action fires (a
    `remoteaction` reveal, a `teleport`, etc.).
  - Roll over → the **fail action** runs (jump to `<failTextblock>`), which often lands you somewhere
    unintended.
  - Example that DOES roll: the Slums slaver-rooftop `jump` exits carry `testskill agility` and can drop
    you into the wrong room on a miss.
- **Difficulty `0` is the special case: it never actually checks anything — the action always fires.**
  So `clear rubble:testskill strength 0 …:remoteaction …` behaves like a plain lever/reveal, not a
  gamble.
- **Stock: the roll** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `testskill` helper @0x46f53a–0x46f875; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `testskill <skill> [<modifier>] <failTextblock>` passes when your value is at least `genrdn(0, cap) + modifier`; on a failure it runs the textblock and fails the line.
  - The caps: 150 for `agility`, `strength`, `intellect`, `wisdom`, `health`, `charm` and `magicresistance`; 175 for `spellcasting`, `stealth`, `thievery`, `traps`, `picklocks` and `tracking`; 110 for `perception`; 100 for `current_hp`, and for a skill word the engine doesn't know, whose value is 0.
  - **A modifier of 0 still rolls on Stock**: `testskill strength 0 <tb>` rolls `genrdn(0,150)` against Strength (@0x46f83e–0x46f84e). The difficulty-0 rule in this topic is recorded for Paradigm; by this code a `clear rubble`-style reveal can miss on Stock.
  - `checkskill <skill> <N> <msg>` is the form with no roll: it passes when your value is at least N, and otherwise prints the message. The Stock data doesn't use it.
- **Client use:**
  - A room-command reveal whose chain has a `testskill` ahead of its `remoteaction` is carried as a step that rolls (`ExitAction.Rolled`, set by `TBInfoActionResolver.EnumerateRemoteActions` and `RoomGraphManager.InjectRoomCmdRemoteActions`), whatever its difficulty. The engines send the keyword and then the move; when the move bonks, the roll missed, and `AutoWalkManager.TryResendRolledReveal` and `LoopRunner.TryResendRolledReveal` send both again, up to `SpecialExitDispatch.RolledRevealRetryCap` (10) times for the step, before the ordinary blocked-step handling takes it. Each re-send is logged, and the count is in the bug report. It needs no realm switch: where the roll never misses, the bonk never comes (user, 2026-10-09: "yes"). Same-room reveals only; a lever (an `Action#` cell) carries no roll, and a winch is `WinchManager`'s. (An earlier line said the walker treats a difficulty-0 `testskill` reveal as a deterministic action with no fail-handling; superseded 2026-10-09, since on Stock a modifier of 0 still rolls.)
  - A non-zero `testskill` exit is NOT auto-traversed as a sure thing.

### Room-wide search during and after combat
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-27 (user; report `paradigm-20260727-185836`); start-room search from report `paradigm-20260909-055045`*

- **You can't search while you're engaged in combat — on every realm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*. Engaged means you've sent an attack, physical or spell, at a monster or player. A room-wide `search` (`sea`) sent then is refused with `You may not search while attacking!` on both realms *(Stock [OBSERVED] `wccmmud.dll` 1.11p `_cmd_search`; Paradigm [CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user)*.
- **Out of combat it's a quick command→reply** (just the ~150 ms network latency, no server-side delay).
- **A search always turns up stashed coins, but not always hidden items or players** *([CONFIRMED]
  2026-09-28, user)*. A reveal that misses a hidden item or player is normal, not a failed search.
- **An empty search answers with `Your search revealed nothing.`**; a reveal surfaces the
  `You notice … here.` survey.
- **Paradigm: a search's `You notice … here.` reply is one unbroken line, however long; the room
  display's own floor list is broken at word boundaries by the game, but not after every row**
  *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, report `paradigm-20261009-164508`, its Wire section; Realm: Paradigm, Stock
  not recorded)*.
  - **The display.** A vault's floor list of 341 stacks (989 items) filled 86 rows of an 80-column
    screen, and came in 69 pieces each ended by a carriage return. No row is longer than 79 characters
    and every row ends between words. A row of fewer than 79 characters ends with the line break. A row that fills
    all 79 is followed by a space and no line break, and the terminal's own right margin wraps it: 10 of
    the 69 pieces ran to 153–312 characters, two to four rows each (one of 236 is rows of 79, 79 and 76
    joined by single spaces).
  - **The reply.** `sea` in the same room answered with 111–120 stacks in about 2,100–2,300 characters
    and no line break at all; the terminal wraps it at its right margin, mid-word.
  - A Paradigm room has no item cap (*Items, inventory & equipment → Room item capacity: drop
    refusal*), so nothing bounds either one's length.
- **The reply lists the hidden stacks the search found, not the whole floor** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09,
  report `paradigm-20261009-164508`, Paradigm; the mechanism [OBSERVED] 2026-10-10 from the Stock DLL and
  [CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10 by the user for Paradigm, both in *Items, inventory & equipment → Hiding items in
  a room (stashing)*; Realm: both)*. The vault's replies held 111–120 stacks where its display held 341.
  A room whose display showed
  `34 rope and grapple`, `10 pulsating heart`, `scorpion tail` and 28 other stacks answered `sea` with
  `You notice 2 wooden skiff, 2 rope and grapple, scorpion tail, pulsating heart, 10 black diamond here.`:
  two stacks the display didn't show, and three it did, under smaller counts. Searches sent one after
  another gave `8`, `9` or `10 black diamond`, and one left `pulsating heart` out.
  - The hidden copies are in addition to the visible ones: 34 visible + 2 hidden rope and grapple is 36
    in the room. (This was an open question here on 2026-10-09; settled 2026-10-10.)
- (Targeted `sea <dir>` hidden-exit reveals are a separate path — see *Hidden exits — `sea <dir>` reveal
  wording*.)
- **Client use:**
  - `LineExtractor` joins the rows the terminal's margin wrapped into one line, so every line reader is
    handed the whole reply at once, and a display's 79-column rows together with the row after them.
    `CasterMessageMatcher.LiteralRunsOccurInOrder` keeps the message templates' regexes off a line they
    can't match (report `paradigm-20261009-164508`: the client stood still for seconds on each reply).
  - What the client does with a reply's counts is in *Items, inventory & equipment → Hiding items in a
    room (stashing)*.
  - Auto-search holds the `sea` past the fight and fires it **once** the room clears, then keeps the
    walker held briefly so the revealed `You notice … here.` survey lands and the get engines collect it
    **before** the loop sets up sneaking and steps on. One search per room; empty rooms (no fight)
    search on entry as before.
  - **The post-search hold is released *reactively*:** the walker is let go the instant
    `Your search revealed nothing.` arrives rather than sitting out the whole settle window — so a room
    with nothing hidden costs only the command→reply round-trip, not a fixed per-room wait. The settle
    window survives only as a short fallback for the case where the reveal *does* surface loot (the
    `You notice …` survey), which the get engines then need a beat to collect.
  - **The room a walk / loop / auto-lair STARTS from is searched too** (report paradigm-20260909-055045):
    auto-search normally arms on room *entry*, but the room you're standing in when movement begins was
    entered earlier — before auto-search was armed, or at login — so it never got that entry search.
    Movement start arms + searches it before the walker steps out, deduped against the last room actually
    searched so a loop's later legs (each starting from a room already searched on arrival) don't
    re-search.
  - The Stock spill sweep's own `sea` at a trail stop waits for the room to be clear of hostiles
    (`DeathRecoveryManager.TrySearchStop`), and is reported to auto-search
    (`AutoSearchManager.NoteSearchedByOther`) so the movement-start search doesn't repeat it.

### Toll exits
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **Toll exits gate on total wealth, not a specific coin.** A room exit tagged `(Toll: N)` in the map
  data requires the crosser to carry a **wealth value of `N × 100`** (copper farthings — the same
  consolidated `Wealth:` figure), held **on them** (carried coin, not banked).
- **The refusal line reads `You do not have enough to cover the toll of N gold crowns.`** — but "N gold
  crowns" is just how the message phrases the copper-value bar (`N` gold = `N × 100` copper), NOT a
  demand for that coin specifically: any mix of denominations totalling `N × 100` copper-value passes.
  So affordability is `TotalCopperValue >= TollGold * 100`.
- **The check is per-crosser.** Every party member needs their own `N × 100` on hand, and a member who
  can't cover it is refused at the gate and left behind while the rest pass.
- **Stock: the toll is taken before the room's entry rule and the monsters' parting attack, and paying it ends a sneak** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_move_user` @0x417e0e–0x417e76; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The payer sees `You just paid`, the coins handed over, then ` in toll charges.`, and the move goes on (which coins a charge takes, and how the list reads, is in *Money, banks & shops → How a charge takes coins, and when the purse is re-bucketed*). Paying clears that move's "sneak held" flag (@0x417e38), so a sneaking mover goes through every toll exit on the lost-sneak path. Each follower pays on its own follow move (*Party → Following the leader: follow / drag movement*).
- **Client use:**
  - `MovementFilter.IsTollGateBlocked` judges a toll on the purse the last full inventory read recorded, and a purse nobody has read refuses no toll. Two events put that record in doubt, and while it is in doubt no toll or fare is taken, until the next full read (`MovementFilter.NotePurseRead`):
    - **a death** (`MovementFilter.NoteDeath`), because the coin carried goes with the pile (*Death & corpse recovery → Coins in the deathpile*), unless the death was in an arena room (*Death & corpse recovery → Death threshold & consequences*). At 3.157.10 a death left the inventory record untouched, and a walk started from the graveyard went through the first toll on its way on the coin carried before the death (report `paradigm-20261010-145529`, Paradigm; the `i` read after that death showed `Wealth: 0 copper farthings`). From 3.159.21 the record is marked stale at a death and read again at the graveyard; a stale record reads as "purse unknown", which is why the gate is told of the death itself.
    - **a refusal the client took the purse to cover** (`MovementRefusalDetector.PaidCrossingRefused` → `MovementFilter.NoteCrossingRefused`). The client then sends one `i` (`OwedPurseRead`).
  - **A refusal closes the exit refused, whatever the record and the data said of it** (`MovementFilter.NoteCrossingRefused`, the exit taken from `RoomTracker.ExitInFlight`). The price the line named is the exit's price from then on, and the exit is open whenever the purse on record covers it, coin picked up since included, once the record can be believed: at once when the record already said the purse was short, and otherwise from the first full inventory read after the refusal (`MovementFilter.IsRefusedCrossing`). A line in a coin other than gold crowns names no price the client can value: that exit opens again at a full read once the trip it was refused on is over. The refused exits are dropped with the character's profile and with the game-data set.
    - Known gap: with two typed moves queued when the refusal comes, the exit refused can't be told, so no exit is recorded and only the doubt about the purse applies.
  - Neither engine sends a refused toll step again, and both hold their re-plan for the `i` the refusal asked for, for no longer than `OwedPurseRead.AnswerBound` (3 s, the `rm` ask's bound), so that it is made on the purse as read and not with every toll closed. `AutoWalkManager.TryReplanOrFail` then re-plans round the toll or to a failure. `LoopRunner.RerouteFromCurrentRoom` re-expands the loop, and `LoopRunner.UnpaidRefusalFor` takes the way round where one exists between those two waypoints and stops the loop where none does.
  - A walk or loop with no way but a toll or fare the crosser's own purse doesn't cover fails naming the exit, its price and the purse it was judged on (`PaidCrossingDescriber`, `MovementFilter.DescribePurseFor`), on the terminal as well as in the Navigation window. A sole-crossing sailing is not sailed, and a loop is refused for a fare, only for the crosser's own purse (`MovementFilter.IsOwnPurseShort`). A toll a party can't all get through closes the same way and is named with who can't pay: *Gating a party's route through toll and level exits*.
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-10-10):
  - A refusal is the game's word: "the toll shouldnt have been used in the first place, if we think we had the money to cross the toll but then are refused, resolve the purse discrepancy then on the users next walk queue, it shouldnt try to use it."
  - A loop whose circuit crosses a toll or fare the purse can't pay, with no way round, is not started, and one refused mid-lap stops.
  - With Auto-All off a refusal sends no `i`: "auto-all off means the user is in full control anyway, thats their problem." The read stays owed and goes out when the switch is back on.

### Gating a party's route through toll and level exits
*Status: CONFIRMED (the level half as first recorded; the toll half is the user's ruling of 2026-10-10) · Realm: both*

- **A leader routing the party must confirm every member can cross before taking a toll / level
  route**, because a toll is per-crosser (*Toll exits*; each follower runs the exit for itself on its own follow move, *Party → Following the leader: follow / drag movement*).
- **Toll — Client policy** (user, 2026-10-10: "for toll's specfiically, either all party members can make it, or we go around if possible, if not possible abandon the walk. we read all of their purses when we think we're going through it to verify, so if they dont respond, assume they cant, and if we can pay for it, for them, give them the money they need and continue through it"):
  - **Every follower's purse is asked with `@wealth` before the leader's engine steps through a toll exit** (each member's client replies with their wealth, the same round-trip shape as `@health` / `@level`). A member who gives no usable answer inside the probe's window (4 s) counts as unable to pay.
  - **All can cover the toll** (`wealth >= TollGold * 100`): the party goes through.
  - **Someone is short or silent, funding is on, and the leader can spare it**: the leader hands each of them what they lack (a silent member the whole toll) with `give {amount} {currency} to {someone}` (*Items, inventory & equipment → Giving items and coins to another player (`give`, `share`)*), waits for the game's confirmation of each hand-over, then goes through.
  - **Otherwise the toll is not taken**: the route goes round it where a way round exists, and where none does the walk is abandoned, the terminal naming the toll, who is short or silent and by how much. A loop decides the same at its toll leg and stops with that reason when it has no way round.
  - **Funding is a setting, off until ticked** (user, 2026-10-10: "if the party leader has extra there should be a setting in settings -> cash + items tab, to "fund party members tolls/rides if short" which uses the party leaders cash from hand or bank if its making a bank trip"; default: "default off"). `CashSettings.FundPartyTolls`, the character's Cash section. Off, no coin is handed over, and a short or silent member closes the crossing for the trip; the closing line names the setting.
  - **What the leader keeps** (user, 2026-10-10: "yes first protect the leaders crossing requirement, if their keep on hand is less than that, protect the crossing amount, if their keep on hand is more than that, protect the keep on hand amount"): the larger of (what the leader needs to cross itself: its own toll or fare here, its own tolls and fares on the rest of the route as planned, and `MovementFilter.ReservedCopper`) and the Cash tab's keep-on-hand amount. Only coin above that funds members. Without the rest of the route, a leader with 12 gold at the first of two 5 gold tolls handed a member 5, paid 5, and stood at the second with 2. (An earlier note, 2026-10-10, had keep on hand not held back; superseded the same day by this ruling.)
  - **Overpay when exact change can't be made** (user, 2026-10-10: "if it doesnt make the leader unable to cross, yes"): exact change is preferred; otherwise the smallest amount above the shortfall the coins carried make, and only while the leader still holds what it keeps. **No other ceiling** (user, 2026-10-10, asked whether a whole runic for a gap of three gold is wanted or should be capped: "yes no cap is fine"). `PartyTollGate.OverpayCeiling` is the one place it is decided. (An earlier note had exact change only, `OverpayAllowedCopper` = 0, with the question open; superseded 2026-10-10.)
  - **Rides are tolls for this** (user, 2026-10-10: "there are only 2 tolls in the entire game, the gate leaving silvermere to the east and the boat ride"; the setting is named "tolls/rides"): an NPC's paid transport (*Greet teleports — an NPC transports a player who asks*) and a sailing (*Boat travel — the sea captain's `secure passage to <place>`*) are asked about, funded and closed exactly as a toll exit is. Both charge whoever types the keyword with a `price` directive, which is judged on total copper like a toll on both realms (*Money, banks & shops → How a charge takes coins, and when the purse is re-bucketed*), so a hand-over before the keyword serves the same way. (An earlier note kept fares on the poorest purse just read, a member nobody had read not counted, and a sole-crossing sailing sailed with its warning on a follower's purse; superseded 2026-10-10. A sailing gated on level alone still sails with its warning.)
    - The two imported sets hold more toll exits than those two (57 exits with a `(Toll: N)` hint in v1.11p and 58 in Paradigm 1.9.1, two of them `(Toll: 0)` in each, counted 2026-10-10): the Silvermere gate `1/1381`↔`1/1382` and Rhudaur's bank door `2/2528`→`2/2568` at 5 gold, map 17's Crimson / Grand Hallway / Golden / Ebony passages at 5,000 and 10,000 gold, and on Paradigm `14/1791`→`14/1792` at 80,000 gold. The check is data-driven and treats them all alike.
    - Not covered: the Quicksylver Carriage Service's `buy passage to <town>` (rooms `15/845`–`15/847`, TBInfo 2923 / 2937 / 2938, `price` 4,000 to 10,000 copper then a `random` table of landings, both sets). The client builds no route edge for it, so no walk takes it.
  - **Every lap** (user, 2026-10-10: "neither get looped. but if needed the member will need to be covered every loop"): a member short again at a later crossing is paid for again; nobody is paid twice for one crossing.
  - **By hand** (user, 2026-10-10: "no"): a toll or ride the user steps through themselves is not checked.
  - **Bank** (the same ruling: "from hand or bank if its making a bank trip"): a bank stop a trip is already making also draws what the members are short of the trip's tolls and fares; no bank trip is made for it. The path-item purchase detour's withdrawal draws it too, and a stash room set as the bank in Settings counts as a bank for it (user, 2026-10-10, asked both: "yes").
  - (An earlier form of this topic had any member who can't cover the toll, or doesn't reply, make the party avoid that toll room for the passing; its Client use note had an unread follower gate the toll, while the code skipped an unread follower. Both superseded 2026-10-10.)
- **Level:** use the member level already **stored in game data** (each player's recorded level); only
  when it's suspected stale, **re-poll in the room with `@level`**. A member outside the exit's
  `(Level: MIN to MAX)` window means the party routes around that exit.
  - Every client answers `@level` — formats vary by client, parsed leniently (the parser also tolerates
    the `{ }` wrap another MudPlay client adds to its reply).
  - **Until a member answers, their `who` title's level band is used with the LOW end as the
    conservative floor** (they could be as low as the band's minimum, so a `MinLevel` gate clears only
    if even that floor clears it).
  - An exact reading counts as **fresh only for the current local day** — a member could have levelled
    since.
- **Client use:**
  - Toll half: `PartyTollGate`, with `PartyWealthProbe` / `PartyWealthTracker` for the purses.
    - **When it asks.** `MovementFilter.WarmForRoute` fires `PartyWealthTracker.Probe` when a walk or a loop leg is planned over a route that crosses a paid exit, at most once in 30 s. At the toll step itself (`AutoWalkManager.TurnedAsideAtToll`, `LoopRunner.TurnedAsideAtToll` → `PartyTollGate.BeforeTollStep`) an answer or a silence no older than 30 s is used as it stands (`PartyWealthTracker.FreshPurse`); anything older, or anything from before the last toll the party was let through, is asked for again there (`PartyWealthTracker.Verify`), and the step is held under the `PartyToll` movement gate until the round is over. The readings are voided at the moment a toll step is let go (`PartyTollGate.NoteTollTaken` → `PartyWealthTracker.ExpireReadings`), not on the room change: the engines send the next step from inside the arrival, and a toll right behind a toll was otherwise judged on purses read before the first was paid. Never asked from a route search: BFS looks at toll edges the party will not walk. Only a message shaped like an answer is read as a purse (`PartyWealthProbe.TryParseWealthReply`: our own `(= N copper)` / `no coins on hand`, or another client's `{Wealth: …}`); a telepath that mentions coins is not.
    - **What it decides** (`PartyTollGate.Judge`). With funding off (`PartyTollGate.FundingOn`, `CashSettings.FundPartyTolls`) a short or silent member closes the crossing, and the summary names the setting. With it on, what the leader can spare is the purse on record less what it keeps (`PartyTollGate.Kept`): the larger of (the leader's own toll or fare, its own tolls and fares on the rest of the route, and `MovementFilter.ReservedCopper`, a train trip's fees) and keep on hand (`KeepOnHandCopper`, the deposit floor's own conversion). The rest of the route is summed by the engine at the step and handed to the check (`AutoWalkManager.OwnChargesPastTheStepDue`, the path's own steps past the one due, a sailing included; `LoopRunner.OwnChargesOnTheRestOfTheLap`, to the end of the lap), so a toll on a branch the route doesn't take is not counted. `PartyTollGate.Closes` is asked by route searches, which have no path: a step closed only for what is kept back for later crossings marks the short members unable at that crossing ("isn't paid for here: <amount> is kept for your own tolls and fares further on this route"), as a failed hand-over does, so the planner doesn't send the walk straight back. Both settings are values handed to the check on the UI thread when the profile loads, is saved or closes (`AppServices`, `RefreshPartyTollSettings`), because `Closes` runs on a route search's thread and the profile's settings dictionary isn't safe to read there. **Exact change, else the least above it** (`PartyTollGate.CountOut`): coins are counted out largest first, which finds exact change whenever the coins make it because each coin is a whole number of the one below; when they don't, the hand-over is the smallest amount above the shortfall the coins make, and only when it fits inside the spare. Several short members are planned in every order (`PartyTollGate.PlanHandOvers`) and the order that hands over least is kept. When no plan fits, those members can't be covered ("the coins carried don't make <amount> without going past what you can spare"). The limit on an overpay is `PartyTollGate.OverpayCeiling`, which is the spare and nothing less. The decision line and a terminal notice (`[Party toll: …]`, `PartyTollGate.Notice`) give each hand-over and, in coins, how much over the shortfall it is ("1 runic to <member> to cover 3 gold: 99 platinum 97 gold over"). (Before 2026-10-10 the spare ignored keep on hand and `OverpayAllowedCopper` = 0 allowed exact change only, the message being "can't make <amount> from the coins carried", because `CurrencyHoldings.PlanCover`'s rounding up by one coin, which train funding uses, would hand over a platinum piece or a runic for a gap of a few gold. With overpay ruled in, that is now what happens when such a coin is all the leader carries and it can be spared.)
    - **Rides** (2026-10-10). `PartyTollGate.BeforeTollStep` takes a toll exit or an exit with `RoomExit.FareCopper` (an NPC's ask-transport); `PartyTollGate.BeforeSailing` takes the `secure passage` verb at its dock (`AutoWalkManager.TurnedAsideAtToll` for both, `LoopRunner.TurnedAsideAtToll` for exits; a loop sails nothing). A sailing is keyed as a fare into its port, which is how `MovementFilter.DescribeBoatBlock` asks `PartyTollGate.Closes` about it. `MovementFilter.IsFareGateBlocked` and `DescribeBoatBlock` judge a fare on the leader's own purse and on that closure, no longer on `PartyWealthTracker.MinWealth`; a sailing the party is closed to is not set out for (`AutoWalkManager.WalkToImmediate`), and the walk with no other way names it with "the party can't all pay". What a member was handed for a fare stops standing for what they hold when the leader arrives in the room the fare leads to, since a sailing is no exit (`PartyTollGate.NoteRoomChanged`).
    - **A trip's bank stop** (2026-10-10). The one bank trip that prices a walk's tolls is the train trip's funding errand (`TrainFundingRouter`, a leader's own Train Now or armed run with the party in tow). At a bank leg it has the purses read (`PartyTollGate.AfterReadingPurses`, one `@wealth` round, bounded by `TrainFundingRouter.PartyPurseWindow`, 6 s), then adds to its `with` what the members are short of the trip's tolls and fares from that bank on (`PartyTollGate.FundingNeededFor`, `TrainFundingRouter.PartyTollTopUp`), less what the purse will already hold beyond the errand's own bill, and never past the balance, since a `with` for more than the balance draws nothing (*Money, banks & shops → Bank commands: balance / withdraw / deposit*). The errand's own bill is unchanged (keep on hand restored, fee and tolls on top), so the leader leaves the bank with at least what it keeps plus what the members lack. What the members lack never starts a bank trip: it is not part of the bill that decides one.
      - **The path-item purchase detour** (`PathItemShopRouter`, bank then shop). At its bank stop, when the rest of the walk (bank to shop to destination, `AppServices.PathItemTripTolls`) crosses a toll or fare, the purses are read and the `with` for the item is raised by what the leader keeps for those crossings (`PartyTollGate.KeptFor`) plus what the members are short (`AppServices.PathItemPartyTollTopUp`). The item takes everything carried and drawn for it, so without the leader's own share the members' share would be the first thing the leader kept. Capped by the deposit this session has seen at that bank (`AppServices.KnownDepositAt`); with none known, nothing is added. Cash that covers the item makes no bank stop, whatever the members lack.
      - **A stash room set as the bank** (`CashSettings.BankRoomKey` naming a marked stash room). The train errand's stop there searches, reads the pile, and takes a chosen copper value of it (`CashManager.CollectSurveyed`), so it takes the members' shortfall with its own after reading their purses (`TrainFundingRouter.TakeWithThePartysShare`), out of what the search showed. Any other stash room gives up the errand's own shortfall only. The path-item detour has no stash stop: with a stash room set as the bank it sends `with` there, which a stash room doesn't answer, and it adds nothing (no balance is known for it).
      - Not built: the party train trip (`PartyTrainCoordinator`), which prices no tolls.
      - (An earlier note, 2026-10-10, had the path-item detour and stash stops not built; superseded the same day by the user's "yes" to both.)
    - **The hand-over.** One `give` per denomination (`CoinGiveCommand`), confirmed by `InventoryManager.CoinsGivenAway` (the giver's coin line in either wording, with the count the game printed, which on Stock is what the recipient kept). A refusal the line names the member in (`InventoryManager.GiveRefused`), a count below what was sent, or no line inside `PartyTollGate.GiveConfirmWindow` (4 s) makes that member unable to be paid for at that toll. A line that comes after the window, for up to `PartyTollGate.LateConfirmationWindow` (2 min), is still credited to the member's reading and to what they were paid at that toll, and a silent member is taken to hold what they were paid there until a toll is crossed, so nobody is handed the same toll twice for a slow line. A coin noun whose first word is none of the four metals is valued as the fifth coin. A late line is credited only when it is worth what one of the gives sent and not yet answered was worth, so coin handed over by hand or by another feature is not taken for the toll's. `Why would you want to give to that?` (`InventoryManager.CoinGiveMisaimed`; *Items, inventory & equipment → Giving items and coins to another player (`give`, `share`)*), the answer to a coin give at a hidden member, fails the hand-over in hand when there is only one; with several out it is noted, and when the window passes with one member alone unconfirmed that member is recorded as "could not be given coin" with that line as the reason. With more than one unconfirmed nobody is said to be hidden: one of them may only be slow, so each is recorded as having given no answer. `You do not have that much <metal>!` (`InventoryManager.CoinGiveLackedCoins`) fails the one in hand the same way. A sneaking member is funded like any other. **Who is left out of the count**: only a member the client knows is not with the leader (`PartyComebackManager.KnownLeftBehind`: being fetched or queued, dropped by the game's own line, left by a train trip, left at a loop's gate, waiting for Auto-Lair's pass); the decision line names them. A member merely not listed in the room is counted, and a hand-over to them that gets no line makes them unable: they may be hidden, or have come in after the room was drawn, and the ruling is everyone or nobody. What a member was paid at a toll stops standing for what they hold when the tracker confirms the room beyond that toll (`PartyTollGate.NoteRoomChanged`), not when the step is let go: a step that bounces is retried without a second hand-over.
    - **Known, and left as they are** (2026-10-10): a crossing closed for what is kept back for later ones stays closed for the trip even when a later re-plan no longer crosses them; a loop keeps back the rest of the lap, not the laps after; an overpay has no ceiling but what the leader keeps, by ruling, so a leader carrying only runics hands one over for a gap of a few gold (an earlier note here had exact change only closing a toll to a leader rich in large coins, with `OverpayAllowedCopper` the knob; and one had the leader's own later tolls not kept back; both superseded 2026-10-10); a member paid for at one toll keeps the coin if the route then turns away from a dearer toll further on; a closure made because a hand-over went unanswered stands until the trip ends even when its line then arrives late; and a pickup that passes through an idle `MovementController` drops the trip's closures, so the toll is asked about again on the way back. What was confirmed is added to the member's reading (`PartyWealthTracker.NoteGiven`), so `MemberGateJudge` (through `PartyWealthTracker.LastReading`) judges a later drop at the toll on what they now hold.
    - **The exit closed to the party.** `MovementFilter.IsTollGateBlocked` asks `PartyTollGate.Closes`; the engine at the toll plans again (`AutoWalkManager.ReplanInPlace`, `LoopRunner.StartInternal` as a recovery), and a plan with no other way fails through `PaidCrossingDescriber.DescribeUnpaid` with "the party can't all pay" and `PartyTollGate.DescribeClosed`. A follower nobody has asked closes nothing: the ask is made at the toll. **A closure is kept for the trip** (`PartyTollGate.JudgeForTrip`), past the 30 s the answers are good for, until `MovementController` goes idle (`NoteTripEnded`), the followers are no longer the ones it was made for, the short members' own fresh answers and what the leader can now spare cover what was lacking, or a fresh judgement lets the party through. **The turn is made as soon as the answers show it**: `PartyWealthTracker.RoundSettled` → `AutoWalkManager.ReplanIfATollAheadIsClosed` / `LoopRunner.ReplanIfATollAheadIsClosed` plan again at once between steps, and when the step in flight has landed otherwise. A walk with no route for want of a toll or fare leaves `AutoWalkManager.LastUnpaidFailure`, which `SellDetourManager.GoToShop` reads so that the shop is passed over that time and not written off.
    - **A member the toll still turned away** is `PartyComebackManager`'s (*Party → A follower who can't move is left behind*, the leader-side policy). A toll the party was let through voids every reading, so the purses are asked again before the toll is tried again after a pickup; a member handed coin at that toll whom the leader has since gone back for from it (`PartyComebackManager.WentBackFor`) and who is short again is not paid for twice, and the route goes round or the walk ends. One who got through and is short on a later lap is paid for again.
    - With the master switch off nothing is asked, given or held. No `PlayerRemoteControls` flag is involved on the leader's side; a follower's client answers `@wealth` under its own remote-command permissions (`RemoteCommandCatalog`: `PlayerRemoteControls.QueryInventory`), and one that doesn't answer is a silent member.
    - `PartyWealthTracker.MinWealth` (through `MovementFilter.PartyWealthProvider`) is now only how the route warm-ups know a party is led, and the bug report's "poorest known purse" line. (An earlier note had `MovementFilter.CannotAfford` with it remain the fare and boat-fare rule; superseded 2026-10-10, and `CannotAfford` is gone.)
  - Level half is implemented: `MovementFilter.IsExitBlocked` + `PartyLevelProbe` /
    `PartyLevelTracker`. **Always-on** — routing a following party around a gate it can't clear is never
    wanted OFF (the alternative strands a member), so there's no opt-in toggle; the only gate is "am I
    leading a party".
  - An exact level reading comes from an `@level` reply and is stamped with the time it was learned
    (`PlayerObservation.LevelAt`); `PartyLevelTracker.WarmStaleLevels` re-fires `@level` for any unknown
    member, or one whose reading isn't from today, when a walk's planned route actually crosses a level
    gate.
  - That freshness poll is route-scoped and debounced the same way the `@wealth` toll poll is: fired from
    `MovementFilter.WarmForRoute` only when the levels-permitted shortest route genuinely uses a level
    gate. The ordinary keep-warm refresh is the once-a-day party probe (see
    *Party → Party intel probe: `@level` / `@version` on partying*), not a roster-change poll.

### Room-level entry blocks — an early-engine mechanism with no MDB representation
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-14 (user + other devs + data check) · Realm: Stock (Paradigm differs)*

- **Rare — the first room of this kind encountered, and probably a leftover of early MajorMUD engine
  design.** Do not expect the pattern to be common; treat it as a known one-off until another turns up.
- **The block is a property of the room being ENTERED, not of any exit.** `1/2150` ("Newhaven, Arena")
  carries an engine-side level range of **1 to 3**. The engine does not test it while traversing an
  exit — it tests when you attempt to **enter the room**, so every way in is blocked by the same rule.
- **Neither the room's range nor the block appears anywhere in the MDB.** This is not an exporter
  dropping a field: the MDB has **no field for a room-level gate at all**. The mechanism predates the
  table format.
- **Do not confuse it with an ordinary exit-level gate**, which is a real and fully-supported MDB
  feature. Both exist in the same room on stock `1.11p`:

  | from `1/2146` | destination | in the MDB |
  |---|---|---|
  | `W` | `1/2190` Newhaven, Healer | `(Level: 1 to 3)` — a genuine **exit** gate |
  | `D` | `1/2150` Newhaven, Arena | nothing — the **room** block, unrepresentable |

  The two produce a similar player-facing effect and are unrelated in origin.
- **`1/2150` has three inbound exits on stock** — `1/2146 D`, `1/2152 S` (Dungeon, Entrance) and
  `1/2155 U` (internal to the Arena) — and the room block applies to all of them, which is why no single
  exit modifier could express it.
- **Paradigm's dats edited this exit** so the gate does surface there as an exit modifier
  (`D -> 1/2150 (Level: 0 to 5)`, a different window from stock's room range).
- **There is no room/exit overlay tier** — overlays cover Items and Monsters only — so this cannot be
  corrected with a per-tier game-data override.
- **General lesson: absence of a gate in the data is not proof the game has no gate.** Treat a refusal
  on an exit the graph believes is open as possible evidence of a room-level block.
- **The engine's room-entry rule, and its lines** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_user_allowed_in_room` @0x4172ff, `_move_user` @0x418fb6; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. `_user_allowed_in_room` prints its own reason and `_move_user` then adds `You are not permitted in that room!`, so each of these refusals is two lines:
  - an `Arena` room (room type 2) and a level above the room's maximum (`+0x464`): `You have progressed too far for this room.` Only the upper bound is tested there;
  - a `Protected` room (room flag 1), outside tournament mode: in auto-combat `You may not enter that room while in combat.`; in a retaliation period `You may not enter that room during a retaliation time-period.` (@0x4174b5);
  - a `Colliseum` room (type 5) entered from a room that isn't one, while the arena switch (`0x4790e8`) is on (arenas in normal mode): with HP below half of max `You are not healthy enough to enter that room.` (@0x417525), or the retaliation line (@0x41755a).
  - The rule runs after the exit's own gate and before the monsters' parting attack (the order of checks in *Refused ("bonked") moves*). The room types and flags are named in *Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*.
- **Client use:**
  - `RoomGraphManager.ApplyStockArenaEntryBlock` stamps `MinLevel 1 / MaxLevel 3` on the stock
    `1/2146 D → 1/2150` exit at graph-build (Stock only; skipped if the exit already carries a gate), so
    the router, route picker and room tooltip read it like the west exit.
  - `MovementFilter.IsLevelGateBlocked` short-circuits on `if (!exit.HasLevelGate) return false;`, so any
    inbound left ungated — the `1/2152 S` inbound is still ungated in the graph — lets an over-level
    character be routed into the Arena and refused by the server. The refusal is handled (it reads as a
    failed move, not a stall), but nothing stops the router re-planning the same way through an ungated
    inbound.

### Guardian-monster doors opened by `ask`
*Status: CONFIRMED (game data v1.11p map 9, MMUD Explorer cross-check)*

- **A placed "guardian" monster whose greet dialogue raises a door on its own room is opened by
  `ask <monster-noun> <topic>` — the spoken password lifts the gate.** Some pick/bash-proof `Door` exits
  aren't operated by a room verb or a remote lever at all; the barrier is a stationed monster who lifts
  it when the player asks the right keyword.
- **Confirmed case: the grove shadow guard.** Room `9/1423` carries `Lair='(Max 2): 503,[…]'` placing
  shadow guard **#503** (`GreetTXT 1433`), and the door `9/1423 W → 9/1425` (Morukai's chamber) has an
  impassable stat requirement so it can't be picked or bashed.
  - The greet decodes as: block `1433` lists topics `morukai / orfeo / passage / phoenix / prophecy`,
    each pointing at `1435` (empty, `LinkTo 1436`); block `1436` is
    `checkability 133 4 : remoteaction 1423 66 0 3 : message 1841`.
  - So asking any of those five keywords fires `remoteaction 1423 … 3` — **direction index 3 = W** —
    operating this room's own west exit.
- **The spoken command is `ask <noun> <topic>` where `<noun>` is the last word of the monster's name**
  ("shadow guard" → `guard`), e.g. `ask guard morukai`.
- **The five topics are alternatives** that all open the same door — the walker sends only one.
- **The open is quest-gated and the gate is untrackable by the client.** `checkability 133 4` gates the
