## Party

How MajorMUD parties form, move, lose and regain members, and how party clients (MudPlay and MegaMUD) signal each other: `par` output, follow/drag movement, drop / death / training effects, ailment and pause signalling, and the telepath probes and requests members exchange.

### Party size bounds
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **A party holds at least 2 and at most 6 members.** Party size: minimum 2, maximum 6.
- **On Stock the maximum comes from the member list: each player holds five member slots, so a party is six at most** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_add_to_group` @0x41e0cc–0x41e0ed, `_cmd_invite` @0x4568dc–0x456965; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. A pending invite takes a slot just as a member who joined does. `_add_to_group` adds nothing and prints nothing when the list is full, and `_cmd_invite` prints the inviter's `You have invited %s to follow you.` whether or not a slot was found. So an invite into a full list reads as sent to the inviter, the invitee is told nothing, and the invitee's `join` is answered `You must be invited first!`.

### Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`) · Realm: Stock*

- **`invite <name>` runs these checks in order** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_invite` @0x456420, party branch @0x456763; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  1. no name: `Syntax: INVITE {user name}` (@0x45644e);
  2. any `invite <x>` clears the inviter's sneaking and hidden flags (@0x456474–0x45647c), before the target is looked up;
  3. nothing of that name in the room: `You don't see %s here!`, with the word as typed (@0x4567be);
  4. the target isn't a player: `Syntax: INVITE {user name}` (@0x4567ee);
  5. yourself: `Why would you invite yourself?` (@0x45696d);
  6. the target is hidden and the inviter lacks the see-hidden status bit (`0x6f5 & 0x20`, as in *Movement & navigation → Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals*): `You don't see %s here!` (@0x45682f–0x456853);
  7. `_is_user_forgotten(target, inviter)` is true: `You cannot invite %s.` (@0x456876–0x456892; the forget list is in *Talk & chat channels → `forget`*);
  8. otherwise the inviter's rank becomes front (@0x4568ac). A target newly added to the list sees `%s has invited you to follow %s.` (the inviter's name, then `him` or `her`) and a prompt, and the inviter sees `You have invited %s to follow you.` Inviting someone already on the list prints only the inviter's line.
- **`join <name>` is `follow <name>`** (`_cmd_join` @0x4542ff calls `_cmd_follow`; same source). `join <number>` is another command, a broadcast channel (*Talk & chat channels → Channel broadcast (`'`, `-`, `br`) and `join`*), and `join gang <name>` is the gang form.
- **`follow <name>` / `join <name>`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_follow` @0x453f38; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - any use clears the resting and meditating flags (@0x453f54–0x453f5d);
  - bare `follow` while following: `You are no longer following %s.` (@0x453f71–0x453f8b); bare `follow` otherwise: `Syntax: FOLLOW {user/monster}`;
  - the target isn't in the room: `You don't see that anywhere!`; a monster: `Following a monster - Not implemented yet.`; some other kind of thing: `Why would you want to follow that?`; yourself: `Why would you follow yourself?`;
  - not on that player's list: `You must be invited first!` (@0x45413a);
  - success: the follower sees `You are now following %s` (no full stop), and the leader `%s started to follow you.` and a prompt (@0x4540a8–0x45410b). `_add_to_group(leader, follower, 1)` then copies the leader and every other listed member into each member's list (@0x41e0f9–0x41e15c).
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` Before the invite check, `follow <player>` clears the typist's own member list of everyone but the target (@0x454064–0x45408b), and it doesn't test whether the typist already follows or leads. Does a leader who types `follow <name>` or `join <name>` and is refused (`You must be invited first!`) lose their own party on Stock? Nothing that puts the list back was found; not seen in a capture.
- **`leave`** (@0x453e37–0x453e51; same source): a follower stops following and sees `You are no longer following %s.` For a player who follows nobody, a leader included, the command goes to the broadcast-channel branch (`You just left group %d.`) or isn't handled (@0x453e5e–0x453f2f). The leader's command is `disband party`.
  - **How many words `leave` takes** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_leave` @0x453cd9–0x453d0c; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*: with more than two words `_cmd_leave` does nothing; `leave gang` is the gang command (`You have left %s.`, or `You are the leader - you may not leave your gang. Use DISBAND GANG`, or `You are not currently in a gang.`); `leave` alone, and `leave` with any one other word (`leave party`), take the party branch above.
  - **On Paradigm `leave party` leaves the party** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user screenshot)*: the follower sees `You are no longer following <leader>.` and the leader `<name> is no longer following you.` (*A follower who can't move is left behind*).
  - **The spellings the game takes are `le`, `lea`, `leav` and `leave`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`: `_parse_command` run in an emulator returns command 56 for each of the four, and entry 56 of the `_handle_commands` jump table @0x4137a6 is @0x413dc1, the call to `_cmd_leave`; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*; the list is in *Wire, prompt & command output → Command words and abbreviations*. (Was `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`: "does `lea` or `leav` leave the party?"; settled 2026-10-10 from the DLL.) `ComebackRequester` reads the same four typed by the user as leaving, on both realms.
- **`disband party`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_disband` @0x458835–0x458871; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. With the word `party` exactly, it calls `_stop_following(you, -1)`: each follower sees `You are no longer following %s.`, and `_cmd_disband` prints nothing to the one who typed it. Any other argument: `Syntax: DISBAND {Party/Gang}`. The command doesn't test for being a leader.
- **`uninvite <name>`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_uninvite` party branch @0x456de4; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The name is looked up in the room and then among all players (`_find_any_action_target` @0x456e58). Not a player: `Syntax: UNINVITE {user name}`; yourself: `Why would you uninvite yourself?` Otherwise `_stop_following(you, target)` runs (a target following you sees `You are no longer following %s.`), the target leaves your list, your rank goes to 0 if the list is now empty, and you see `%s has been removed from your followers.` That line prints even when the target was never on your list.
- **`_stop_following` prints one line only, `You are no longer following %s.`, and only to the follower** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_stop_following` @0x41de75, `_remove_from_group` @0x41dd96; Realm: Stock)*.
  - Called for one follower it drops that one. Called with −1 it drops everyone following the player (@0x41dee9–0x41df68), each getting the line and a prompt, and then `_remove_from_group` clears the player's own list and rank and takes the player off every in-game player's list; a member left with an empty list gets rank 0.
  - Each follower it drops is put through `_remove_from_group` as well (@0x41dea7, @0x41df1a), so a follower dropped this way is off every member list, where one whose follow move was merely refused stays on them (*A follower who can't move is left behind*).
  - **Neither `<name> is no longer following you.` nor `Your party has been disbanded.` is a Stock line**: neither string is in `wccmmud.dll`, `wccmmpls.dll` or the Stock message table. Both are on record from Paradigm captures (*A follower who can't move is left behind*; *Wire, prompt & command output → Realm exit / logoff sequence*). The leader-side party lines found in the Stock DLL are `%s started to follow you.` and `%s has been removed from your followers.`

### Co-location and the `Also here:` line
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 (user; report `stock-20260828-124347` + scrollback); restated for the leader's `par` CONFIRMED 2026-10-09 (user) · Realm: both (the user spoke generally both times; the one open case is tagged inline)*

- **Party members are always co-located: a party is a single room.** If a name shows as an active (non-invited) `par` row, they are in your room, full stop. So the correct "is this member reachable?" gate is *party membership* (`par`), **not** the room's `Also here:` line. *(2026-08-28, user)*
- **A member the leader's `par` lists as following is in the leader's room** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "another member in our party, that is actively in our par, has to be in our room")*. A follower is always with the leader; one who isn't has been dropped from the party.
  - "Actively" is a full row. An `[Invited]` row is on the list and not following (*`par` output block*), so it says nothing about the room, and a member the reply leaves out is not in the party at all.
  - Nothing on record contradicts it on either realm. On Stock the engine prints a full row from the follow fields alone, with no room test (*`par` output block*), and a follow move it refuses ends the follow in the same tick (*A follower who can't move is left behind*), so the two agree. The one open case is Paradigm's dropped (0 HP) member, whom `par` is believed to keep listing though only a `drag` moves them (*Dropped ally rescue*, `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` there).
- **A party member may be missing from `Also here:` for two reasons, and neither means they left the room.** *(2026-08-28, user — report `stock-20260828-124347` + scrollback)*
  1. **The leader you're FOLLOWING is never listed in `Also here:`.** The game prints `You are following <leader>.` as a separate status line instead, and `Also here:` shows only the *other* occupants. The reverse also holds: when **you** lead, your followers **do** appear in your `Also here:` (you follow no one).
  2. **A member who is HIDING is removed from `Also here:`** (see *Movement & navigation → Hiding — sneak vs hide, the hide state machine, and search reveals*). They're still in the room and in `par`.

**Client use:**
- `PartyPathItemGate.OnGateCrossed` / `OnPartyListRead`: after the leader crosses an item gate with a member credited from a remembered hand-over, one `par` (`PartyPoller.RequestPar`) is asked, and a member its reply no longer lists as following loses the credit (*Movement & navigation → Protective-item gates — exit-gated vs room-spell-gated*).

### `par` output block
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **`par` output must never be read as a room name.** The party-list command replies with a fixed block whose **first line is `You are following <leader>.`** (the follower's follow status), then `The following people are in your travel party:`, then one indented roster row per member (`<name>  (<class>)  [K/M: N%] [H: N%]  - Frontrank/Backrank`).
- **The block routinely lands just before a dragged room, in room-title colour.** A follower's party tracking polls `par` constantly, so this block often lands in the room-display buffer just before a dragged room. `You are following <leader>.` renders in the **same bright cyan** the room title uses, so the colour-anchored room-name detector will grab it unless the `par` lines and the drag line are treated as block boundaries.
- **`par` lists live membership only** (see *Dropped ally rescue* and *Member death shows as an invited slot in `par`* for what a dropped or dead member looks like).
- **Stock: how the engine builds the block** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_party` @0x43b569; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - **The row format** is `  %-30.30s %-12.12s` (the name as `First Last`, the class as `(%s)`), then ` [%c:%3.3s%%]` or nine spaces, then ` [H:%3.3s%%]%c%c%s`.
    - The bracket's letter is `K` for a class whose record holds 5 at `+0x40`, else `M` (@0x43b829–0x43b83e).
    - Both percentages are whole-number divisions, `cur*100/max`; mana reads 0 when max mana is 0 (@0x43b752–0x43b792). When the bracket is left out is in *`par` row: secondary-resource bracket*.
    - The first letter after the HP bracket is `P` when the member's field `+0xbe` is non-zero, else a space (@0x43b8ab–0x43b8ba). The field wasn't identified in the DLL; that `P` means poisoned is the rule in *Party ailment signaling and cross-client sync (MegaMUD parity)*.
    - The second letter is `R` when the member is resting, else `M` when meditating, else a space (@0x43b889–0x43b8a7).
    - The rank is ` - Frontrank` (rank 1), ` - Backrank` (rank 2) or ` - Midrank` (anything else).
  - **`[Invited]` means "on my list, but not following our leader".** The row is `  %-30.30s %-12.12s [Invited]` (@0x43b6e1). A listed member gets a full row only when they follow the player you follow, follow you, or are the one you follow (@0x43b63a–0x43b680). A listed member who follows nobody, or someone else, prints as `[Invited]`, whether they were only invited or joined and stopped following.
  - **A full row is decided by the follow fields; `_display_party` reads no room field.** A listed member who is following prints the same row, with live HP and mana, wherever they stand.
  - **Your own row is printed last, every time**, also after `You are not in a party at the present time.`: the no-rows branch (@0x43b905–0x43b933) falls through to the self row (@0x43b93a), and it resets your rank to 0.
  - **Members who have left the game are taken off your list while `par` prints** (@0x43b8eb).
  - **`par` takes no argument and doesn't end a rest**: its dispatcher case tests only the word count (@0x4145ab–0x4145bd), where the rank commands beside it clear the resting and meditating flags (*Party ranks*).
- **Client use:**
  - `RoomDisplayParser.PartyChatterBoundaryPattern` treats the `par` lines and the drag line as block boundaries. The room the follower lands in is displayed immediately after ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --`, so that drag line is the natural boundary.
  - `PartyManager.ParRow` reads the optional `P` flag and the `R` / `M` state letter between the HP bracket and the rank.
  - `PartyManager.OnPartyDissolved` resets the `par` block reader on `You are not in a party at the present time.`, so the self row printed after it isn't taken for a member.
  - **An `[Invited]` row makes this client the leader only when it follows nobody** (**Client policy**, 2026-10-10). The block's opening `You are following <leader>.` is read (`KnownPatterns.PartyParFollowing`) and outranks what the client believes; with it, or while the client believes it follows someone, an `[Invited]` row marks that member as not following and changes nothing about who leads. The leader's own row as `[Invited]` raises `PartyManager.LeaderListedAsInvited` (*A follower who can't move is left behind*). Before, any `[Invited]` row set `PartyState.SelfIsLeader`, which let go of `PartyFollowerMovementGate`'s hold on the follower's own walk, loop or Auto-Lair and of the leader `PartyRejoinCoordinator` remembers: another member's `[Invited]` slot did it while the client still followed.

### `par` row: secondary-resource bracket
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **A `par` row omits its secondary-resource bracket entirely when that resource is exactly 0 points.** The bracket is mana `[M:N%]` for casters, kai `[K:N%]` for Mystics / monks, and the rule holds for mana and kai alike.
- **It's a 0-*points* rule, not a 0-*percent* one.** A caster with a few points left still prints `[M: 0%]` (bracket present).
- **The row keeps its `[H:N%]` bracket**, so a drained member is a member row missing its secondary field, not a dropped member.
- **On Stock the bracket is left out whenever the computed percentage is 0, not only at 0 points** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_display_party` @0x43b7ff, nine spaces printed in its place @0x43b853; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The percentage is the whole-number `cur*100/max`, so a caster with 2 of 250 mana prints no bracket, and that code never prints a bracket reading 0%. The 0-points rule in this topic, with `[M: 0%]` still printed at a few points, is Paradigm's only *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-09, user: "the 0 point print is paradigm only, on stock it disappears like you found")*. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`; settled 2026-10-09.)
- **Client use:**
  - A bracket-less row must still parse (or reconciliation drops the member).
  - An absent bracket on a known-caster row (`BaselineMp > 0`) means 0, not "unchanged."

### Party ranks
*Status: [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`) · Realm: Stock*

- **A rank change prints one line to the mover and one to the rest of the group** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_change_user_rank` @0x41e169; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - front: `You have moved to the front ranks of your group.` / `%s just moved to the front rank in your group.`
  - back: `You have moved to the back ranks of your group.` / `%s just moved to the back rank in your group.`
  - middle: `You have moved to the middle ranks of your group.` / `%s just moved to the middle of your group.`
- **Refusals** *(same source)*:
  - alone: `You are not in a party at the present time.`, the line `par` prints for a player with no party;
  - a player who follows nobody (the leader) can't go to the back or the middle: `You may not enter the backrank of your own party.` (@0x41e308), `You may not leave your current rank in your own party.` (@0x41e4af);
  - `You are the only one in the front rank.  You may not leave.` (two spaces after the first full stop);
  - `There would not be enough people left in the frontrank if you did that.`, when the others in front are fewer than those in back (@0x41e354–0x41e367);
  - `You are the only one in the back rank.  You may not leave.`
- **Inviting anyone puts the inviter in the front rank** (`_cmd_invite` @0x4568ac; *Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`*).
- **The three rank commands end a rest**: each clears the resting and meditating flags before it runs (@0x4144ea, @0x414524, @0x41455e). Which words the dispatcher binds to them wasn't read.
- What a rank does in a fight is in *Combat → Monster target selection — who it swings at once fighting*; how `par` prints it is in *`par` output block*.

**Client use:**
- `PartyManager.OnMemberRankChanged` reads the other-member line (`KnownPatterns.PartyMemberRankChanged`: front, middle or back) and updates that member's rank without waiting for the next `par`.

### Following the leader: follow / drag movement
*Status: CONFIRMED (live follower capture, Darkwood Forest)*

- **A party follower is dragged one room per leader step, announced by ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --`.** Movement is leader-driven: when the party leader walks, the game moves every follower one room the same way and prints this line immediately *before* the follower's new room display. The follower sends no bytes and issues no movement command of its own (`PartyFollowerMovementGate` holds its engines), so this line (`-- Following your Party leader <dir> --`) is the **only** signal that a dragged follower moved.
- **The direction is the long-form word the game prints** (`north`, `northeast`, `up`, …). Verified from a live follower capture walking Darkwood Forest (northeast / east / southeast / southwest / south drags).
- **Hidden/foliage exits drag the follower with no direction.** Some Darkwood Forest exits are text-only: the leader prints `<leader> shoves aside the foliage, and disappears among the trees.` and the follower is pulled through with `You push through the dense foliage, and walk onto a small path.` — **no** ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --` line and **no** cardinal direction. The follower's room changes but there is nothing to feed `NoteFollowMove`, so the tracker sees the new room as a mismatch and must recover via replay/candidate resolution rather than a predicted step.
- **Stock: a follower is moved by its own move, of kind "following the party leader"** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_fast_update_character` @0x422b6b, `_move_user` @0x417692; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The engine calls `_move_user(follower, dir, 3)` from two places:
  - right after the leader's own move succeeds, for every follower whose user number is below the leader's, through the direction the leader took (@0x4230c5–0x423108);
  - otherwise on the follower's own fast update (@0x422bc8–0x422bdb): `_direction_player_travelling(leader, follower)` (@0x41d9ee) looks the follower's room up in the leader's 20-entry trail (the arrays `track` reads: *Movement & navigation → Tracking (`track`)*) and returns the exit toward the room the leader went to next, passing over a `Remote Action` exit (@0x41da9e). The follower's HP must be above 0 and the leader in the game.
  - **So every follower moves in the same fast tick as the leader**: those with a lower user number at once, the others when their own fast update comes round later in the same pass. The leader's move is itself made on the tick, not when the command is typed (*Movement & navigation → Per-hop movement speed*).
  - Each follower runs the exit for itself: its gates, its toll, its pre- and post-spells and its refusals (*A follower who can't move is left behind*; *Movement & navigation → Toll exits*).
- **Stock: `set follow` decides whether a follower sees the room** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_set` @0x459070–0x4590dc and @0x45a21a–0x45a2b8, `_move_user` @0x4190a8–0x4190d1; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. In the generic move path a follower is sent ` -- Following your Party leader %s --`, then one room display (`_display_room_desc` @0x41954e, or @0x4195f8 after a sneak roll of their own that held), then a prompt (@0x41970f–0x419723).
  - `set follow` toggles a per-player flag (`+0x700` bit 0); `set follow blind` sets it and `set follow normal` clears it; any other word answers `Valid follow options: BLIND, NORMAL`. Setting it prints `You will only see the fact that you have moved when following.`, clearing it `You will see your normal room descriptions when following.` `pro` shows it as its `Follow Mode:        Blind|Normal` row (`_display_profile` @0x43afa1; the whole sheet is in *Wire, prompt & command output → Character settings — `set` and the `pro` sheet*). A new character starts Normal (`_create_player` @0x416633).
  - **In Blind mode a follow move prints the follow line and no room display**: both display calls are skipped for move kind 3 with the flag set (@0x419528–0x419535, @0x4195d2–0x4195df).
  - **The follow line and the Blind test are in the generic path only.** The exit types that carry their own move code print no follow line there and display the room whatever the mode: an `Item` exit when the item is carried (move @0x417c6d, display @0x417cba), an `Action` exit (type 5; display @0x4180ad), a `Text` exit with a pass message (display @0x4183fd; the foliage case in this topic), a `Trap` (display @0x4186ab) and a `Spell Trap` (display @0x418884). On those a follower's only sign of the move is the room display.
  - **A sneaking follower keeps sneaking**: for a follow move with the sneak flag set, `_move_user` prints `Sneaking...` to the follower and makes the usual sneak roll (@0x417742–0x41776e, roll @0x417947).
  - **A follower can't drag**: on a follow move, a follower who is dragging someone sees `You may not drag someone while in a party!` and the drag is dropped (@0x41776f–0x4177ac).
- **Client policy: a party follower never flees** *(user, 2026-10-10: "a party follower should not flee while in a party, ever.")*. A run of its own walks a follower out of the party (*A follower who can't move is left behind*, the own-move bullet), so no flee of any kind starts while the client is in a party and not its leader: the low-HP and low-mana runs, hit and run, a failed backstab's run, the PvP flee by rooms or to a Flee room, and the run from a `Flee` monster (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Neutral monsters and kill-on-sight*).
  - In the low-HP run's place the follower telepaths the party's healer through `@heal` when that is wired (`PartyRestSync.RequestHeal`); in the others' place nothing is sent. A hit-and-run character stands and fights. A PvP *Flee then hang up* hangs up at once, as when there is nowhere to run.
  - **The wimpy jump is not a flee** *(user, 2026-10-10, asked whether a follower's `sys goto <wimpy location>` in place of a hang-up counts as fleeing: "this is allowed, like a hangup.")*. A follower whose health rule would hang up, and whose Health tab has *Sys goto wimpy instead of hanging* set, still makes the jump (`HealthManager.ExecuteEscape`, unchanged), as it would still hang up.
  - (Before 2026-10-10 a follower with no party heal to ask for ran, and so did a follower's hit and run, failed backstab and PvP flee.)
  - **Client use:** `HealthManager.TryFlee` refuses the start of every run (`_isPartyFollower`), `HealthManager.CommitFleeReaction` holds a follower's low HP or mana, and `PvpResponder.StartFlee` refuses both PvP flees.
- **Client use:**
  - The client keys on the follow line to stay located; without it the tracker keeps its old anchor, reads every new room as a mismatch and falls to Lost within a few rooms.
  - The follow line is handled via `FollowMoveObserver` → `RoomTracker.NoteFollowMove`. `NoteFollowMove` wraps `RoomTracker.NoteMoveSent`'s prediction core but flags the move as a follow-drag, so its near-instant arrival isn't taken for a passive re-look.
  - `FollowModeTracker` reads the `set follow` mode off the `pro` sheet's `Follow Mode:` row and the command's two replies. When it is Blind the client logs a warning and says so once in the terminal, since a follow move then prints no room for `RoomTracker` to confirm against. The mode is in the bug report. The client never sets the mode and never sends `pro` to learn it (user, 2026-10-09: few players know the setting; keep it passive).

### A follower who can't move is left behind
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-26 (user; report `paradigm-20260926-195517`) for Paradigm (wire text observed there); the Stock engine's side is [OBSERVED] 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 (Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`) in the bullets marked Stock · Realm: differs*

- **The realms differ on a follower an exit turns away** (a toll, a door, an item, a class, race, level or alignment gate, a room permission). The detail and the sources are in the bullets of this topic; this is the short form.
  - **Stock** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`: `_move_user` @0x417692, `_fast_update_character` @0x423108–0x423114 and @0x422be7, `_display_party` @0x43b63a–0x43b686)*: the follower **stops following but stays on the leader's member list**. The leader's `par` shows them as `[Invited]`. The leader is printed nothing. `<name> is no longer following you.` and `Your party has been disbanded.` do not exist in the Stock DLLs or the Stock message file.
  - **Paradigm** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user; the bullet "An exit that turns followers away drops each of them the same way" in this topic)*: the follower is dropped from the party, has no row in the leader's `par`, and has to be invited again. The leader sees `<name> is no longer following you.` for each, and `Your party has been disbanded.` when every follower was dropped.
  - **Three things on the Stock side are settled from the DLL's code** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-11, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`, the sites re-read that day; Realm: Stock)*. They have still not been seen in a capture of a live board.
    1. **A Stock leader's `par` prints the refused follower's row as `[Invited]`.** The follower stays on the leader's list; for a viewer who follows nobody, a listed member whose own follow field is 0xffff reaches the branch that prints `  %-30.30s %-12.12s [Invited]` (`_display_party` @0x43b63a–0x43b686).
