**Client use:**
- **Stock, a follower dropped at a gate:** nothing prints for the leader, so the leader's client learns of it only from a `par` reply, where the member reads `[Invited]`. The row stays on the roster, flagged invited (`PartyManager.AddOrTouchMember`); `ReconcileMissingFromPar` takes off only a member the reply leaves out. An invited row is not asked or counted for a gate item, and the hand-over remembered for it is forgotten by the `par` asked after a gate crossing (`PartyPathItemGate.OnPartyListRead`; the rule is in *Movement & navigation → Protective-item gates — exit-gated vs room-spell-gated*). No `MemberLeftBehind` is raised, so `PartyComebackManager` doesn't go back for the member until their `@comeback` asks.
- **Stock: a member still on the leader's list is brought back with a `join`, not an invite** (**Client policy**, 2026-10-11). It rests on the facts settled from the DLL's code in the first bullet of this topic (the `[Invited]` row in play, and a `join` that works with no fresh invite; `[OBSERVED]` 2026-10-11, not seen in a live capture). Every part of it still falls back to the invite flow, which is what Paradigm keeps unchanged (`OnStock` false on `PartyManager`, `PartyComebackManager`, `ComebackRequester`).
  - **What the client goes by.** The game tells a Stock leader nothing, so "still on our list" is the member's row on the roster (`PartyComebackManager.StillOnOurList`): a row is taken off only by a line that says so or by a `par` that leaves the member out. A member the game did take off the list with no line to the leader (held, stunned or too heavy when the leader moved) keeps a row until the next `par`, which is one reason the fallback is needed whatever a capture shows. On the follower's side "still listed" is: no `You are no longer following …` has come (the party state still names the leader, or `PartyManager.ListedWithLeader` does).
  - **An invite to a member already on the list prints them nothing** (*Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`*, check 8 of `invite`), which is why the old flow waited out its window on Stock.
  - **Leader, end of a pickup** (`PartyComebackManager.ReInviteAndAwait` → `AskBack`): with a row for the member it telepaths `@join` and sends no `invite`. If no `<name> started to follow you.` comes within 5 s (`JoinFirstWait`) it sends the `invite` after all; for a member who had a `@wait` out when they asked it invites at once. `@join` needs *Request invite* granted to the leader on the member's side; ungranted, that client answers the Failure message and the fallback invite goes out.
    - **The invite always goes out while the pickup still waits** (`InviteDelayWithin`): with *If leading, wait only* positive and under twice `JoinFirstWait` the join gets half of that wait; at 0 the invite is sent together with the `@join`. (A first form gave the join 5 s whatever the wait was, so a wait under 5 s timed the pickup out with no invite sent; corrected 2026-10-11.)
    - **The `@join` obeys Settings → Party *Send @join nags to invited members*** (`PartyComebackManager.SendJoinToInvited`, **Client policy**, 2026-10-11): with it off no `@join` is sent at a pickup or on Auto-Lair's pass, and the invite goes out at once as on Paradigm.
  - **Leader, Auto-Lair's on-sight promise** (`OnEntitiesObserved`): the same `AskBack`, where before a row on the roster made it pass the member over, so on Stock the promise was never kept. Its fallback invite is sent only while the member is still in the room view and Auto-Lair is still running (`OnJoinFallbackTick`); otherwise it is dropped, with the on-sight cooldown, and the pass that next finds them asks again.
  - **Leader, a full party** (`BeginRecovery`): the asking member's own row isn't counted against the six. Before, a party of six answered its own left-behind member `my party is full` and sent `@forget`.
  - **Leader, a loop's invite wait** (`AutoPartyManager.ExpireInviteWaits`): no `uninvite` for a member who followed us and now reads `[Invited]` (`PartyManager.IsLeftBehindOnOurList`); the `uninvite` would take them off the list, and a `join` of theirs would then need an invite. The nag stops and they aren't auto-invited again for the uninvite-suppression time. Such a row keeps one of the list's slots (*Party size bounds*) until the member joins again, leaves the game, or is uninvited by hand.
  - **Follower** (`ComebackRequester.TryJoin`): it sends `join <leader>` itself when the leader it asked answers `found you …` or is seen in the room (`NotePlayerInRoom`), needing no grant on either side. One join goes out whether it is this one or the one the leader's `@join` asks for (`PartyEssentialHandlers.JoinSent`, `JoinAlreadySent`). On `You must be invited first!` (`KnownPatterns.PartyMustBeInvited`) within 3 s of a join the client sent it stops joining for that split, drops `ListedWithLeader` (`PartyManager.NoteNotListedWith`) and waits for the invite, taken as before (*`@comeback` (follower → leader)*, **The invite that ends the pickup is taken**).
  - **Follower, a follow given up** (`PartyManager.NoteFollowGivenUp`): the roster goes solo as before and the leader is kept as `ListedWithLeader`. A `par` read while it is set records its rows without applying them, so the old party's `[Invited]` rows don't make the client a leader; a reply that no longer lists the leader, and every line that says where the client stands (a follow, `You are no longer following …`, `You are not in a party at the present time.`, an invite or follower of its own, the leader leaving the game, its own drop or dropped link), clears it. The bug report's Party section shows it, and tags a leader's roster row `listed, not following`.
- Path C runs only for a drop within 5 s of a move of ours (`RoomTracker.LastMoveSentAt`, `PartyComebackManager.OwnMoveWindow`); a follower who stops following at any other time left by themselves and isn't gone back for (report `paradigm-20261007-183903`).
- On the follower's side `ComebackRequester` sends `@comeback` when `You are no longer following <leader>.` follows one of the three refusals a follower gets on a follow move it can't make: `You can't seem to move anywhere!` and `You are too stunned to move anywhere!` (`KnownPatterns.MovementFailedStuck`; the stunned line added 2026-10-09) and the too-heavy line (`KnownPatterns.MovementFailedHeavy`). The `hide` refusals that open with the same words (`… to move anywhere to hide!`) are not read as one. Since 2026-10-10 it also asks for the follow moves that end without that line; every trigger, and what is never one, is in *`@comeback` (follower → leader)*.
- `PartyManager.LeaderListedAsInvited` is raised when our own `par` lists the leader we believed we followed as `[Invited]`, before the row is applied (`ComebackRequester.NoteLeaderListedAsInvited`).
- One step that leaves several followers behind prints the leader's line for each. `PartyComebackManager.OnMemberLeftBehind` goes back for the first and queues the rest (`QueueRecovery`); each is fetched in turn, with the room its own `@comeback` named when one came, and the stopped walk, loop or Auto-Lair is put back after the last. Before 2026-10-10 the second was answered `comeback already in progress` and never gone back for. A follower outside any party of ours after the disband is still honoured: `PartyManager.OnLeftBehind` stamps each into the *If leading, accept @comeback for* window, and the disband doesn't clear it.
- `PartyManager.OnLeftBehind` → `MemberLeftBehind` → `PartyComebackManager` path C: backtrack, re-invite, then `PartyAilmentTracker.NoteInferredHold` (Held chip + `@wait` pause over the full "If leading, wait only" window) and a `@waiting` telepath the follower answers with `@ok` once nothing holds it (`PartyEssentialHandlers.OnWaiting`).
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-09-26): gated on *Re-invite lost party members*; only a running walk / loop / Auto-Lair goes back.
- **Client policy** (user, 2026-09-26): a member left behind within 5 s of their own `@ok` (`PartyEssentialHandlers.OkedWithin`) gets the full wait window after rejoining, and their `@ok` is ignored for it (`NotePause(ignoreOk)`). No `@waiting` is sent in that case.
- **Client policy** (2026-10-08): a member dropped behind a move the engines didn't make is left to the player, whatever engine is up behind it (`RoomTracker.LastMoveWasManual`). That is a move typed by hand, and equally one sent by a macro, a trigger or a relayed `@do`: each reaches the game the same way and pauses the engines as a typed move does, so a recovery started for it was a walk born paused that set off on Resume, 100 s after the member had been fetched by hand (report `paradigm-20260929-221642`). A member an engine's own step leaves behind is gone back for even when a pause lands with it.
- **Client policy** (2026-10-08): `<name> started to follow you.` for the member being recovered ends the recovery at any stage, not only once the leader has reached them and re-invited (`PartyComebackManager.OnMemberFollowConfirmed`); the walk back is stopped and the interrupted walk, loop or Auto-Lair is put back (reports `paradigm-20261007-134824`, `paradigm-20260929-221642`).

### Losing the leader disbands the party
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **Losing the leader disbands the whole party, whether the leader disconnects or dies.** There is no grace-window auto-invite for a lost leader. On the leader's own death, the party is gone by the time they respawn in the graveyard.
- **The followers stay where they were** *([OBSERVED] report `paradigm-20260923-092317`, Paradigm)*: a leader whose link dropped re-entered the realm 26 s later in the room it had dropped in, and both followers were still on that room's `Also here:` line.
- **Stock: leaving the game runs `_stop_following(user, -1)`** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cleanup_when_user_leaves` @0x420e1d; callers `_ljngame_lofrou` @0x408d59 (logoff), `_ljngame_huprou` @0x4091ac (hang-up), `_ljngame_sttrou` @0x407073, `_fast_update_character` @0x4231a3 (the end of the exit wait), `_check_kill_user` @0x419b34 (death), `_commit_suicide` @0x46e9b5 and again @0x46eed1; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. Each follower of a departing leader sees `You are no longer following %s.` and a prompt, and is off every member list. A departing follower is taken off every list and the leader is printed nothing. What the call does and leaves is in *A follower who can't move is left behind*, the `_stop_following(x, -1)` bullet.

**Client use:**
- `PartyReformCoordinator` snapshots the followers at the drop and, on the first room display back in the game, has `PartyManager.BeginLeaderReconnectReform` and `AutoPartyManager.NoteLeaderReconnectReform` hold movement and re-invite each follower once seen in the room.
- A loop that was running restarts on the first prompt after the reconnect. That prompt comes with the room display the reform fires on and is read before the display's lines, and a loop started bare sent its first step before the reform's hold went up, leaving the followers behind (report `paradigm-20260923-092317`). With a reform still waiting for its room display, `LoopRunner` starts the loop behind `MovementCoordinator.ReconnectReformGate` and drops that gate once the reform has seen the room, when the reform's own holds are up. The held loop is an ordinary paused run: Stop stops it, and a member's `@comeback` interrupts it. **Client policy:** if no room is displayed within 5 s the gate is dropped anyway.

### Dropping (0 HP) or instant death removes you from the party
*Status: CONFIRMED; suicide / instant-death detail CONFIRMED 2026-08-25 (user)*

- **Dropping (hitting 0 HP) doesn't just immobilize you. It removes you from the party game-side.** After a miracle-save death the `par` check reads `You are not in a party at the present time.` even though the client still believed it was partied and following the leader. *([CONFIRMED])*
- **A dropped character still tracks the leader's room only because the leader `drag`s them.** Following is an artifact of the drag, not live party membership. *([CONFIRMED])*
- **`suicide` / instant death also removes you, with no drop stage.** *([CONFIRMED 2026-08-25, user])* A `suicide` (or any instant death that costs a life) skips the mortally-wounded / 0-HP drop entirely. It goes straight to `After a LONG thought, you take your own life.` → `You now have N lives remaining.` → respawn.
  - Party removal still happens: a **follower** sees `You are no longer following <leader>.` and is out of the party, and a **leader**'s party **disbands**.
  - There's no `<name> drops to the ground!` line, since the character never passed through the mortally-wounded state.
- **Stock: the removal is made in `_check_kill_user`, for a drop and a death alike** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_check_kill_user` @0x419a33, call @0x419a58–0x419a93; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. As soon as the checked player's HP is 0 or below it calls `_stop_following(user, -1)`, ahead of the death-threshold test (@0x419ad9–0x419af3):
  - everyone following that player is dropped, each seeing `You are no longer following %s.` and a prompt (@0x41df05–0x41df4c). This is the leader-drops case;
  - then `_remove_from_group(user)` (@0x41df63) clears the player's own member list and rank and takes the player off the member list of every player in the game (@0x41de2a–0x41de6d); a member left with an empty list gets rank 0;
  - the dropped player's own follow field isn't cleared there. It is cleared on their next fast update (@0x422ba3 → @0x422bfd) or at the leader's next move (@0x4230f1 → @0x42311f);
  - these three functions print nothing to the dropped player, or to the leader of a dropped follower. `_check_kill_user` has 27 call sites, which weren't read, so a caller may print more (the `suicide` case in this topic has the follower seeing `You are no longer following <leader>.`).

### Dropped ally rescue
*Status: mixed (per-bullet tags below; bullets without a tag are Unrated)*

- **The drop line is seen party-side and by the dropped character** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user; same wording on Stock)*. When a character drops, everyone in the room (the party included) sees `<name> drops to the ground!`. The dropped character sees it with their **own** name (observed: `Raijin drops to the ground!`). That line is the party-side signal that a member has gone down.
- **The drag prints to the dragged character on every move** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-28, user; same wording on Stock)*. Once someone starts it, the drag prints `<leader> is dragging you around.` to the dragged character on each of the dragger's moves (observed: `MudPlay is dragging you around.`).
- **Drag is manual, never automatic.** **Any player** can `drag <name>` a dropped character *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*; in a party it's normally the leader who does it after seeing the drop line. Nothing drags them on its own. Dragging only relocates the still-mortally-wounded body. It does **not** revive them or restore party membership.
- **A dropped ally is revived with `aid` and/or a heal.** A dropped ally sits at 0 HP or below and can't act for themselves. They must be brought back by **`aid <name>`** and/or a **heal** that lifts their HP above 0. So a party leader watching `<member> drops to the ground!` should **aid and heal that member** (drag is a separate, optional relocation choice, not the rescue).
  - `aid` alone doesn't lift them at once, on either realm: it stops the bleeding and they climb 1 HP per 30 s until positive (see *Health, resting & recovery → 0 HP — dropped / bleeding out*). Until then they still can't act, answer an `@health` or accept an invite. A heal gets them up sooner.
- **A dropped ally leaves `par` — immediately on Stock** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-26, user)*. On **Stock** a dropped member is removed from the party at once and no longer appears in the `par` roster (`par` lists live membership only). On **Paradigm** `par` is believed to keep showing them with a negative HP% *([NEEDS CONFIRMATION])*; they can't be moved except by `drag`, and what happens to their party standing once dragged and moved on Paradigm isn't known. Their vitals therefore stop refreshing from `par`, so tracking a dropped, then partially-recovered ally's HP needs an out-of-band poll.
- **An `@health` telepath polls a member's vitals.** *([CONFIRMED])* Sending an ally a telepath `@health` makes their client's @health responder reply with their current HP / MA. This is an out-of-band way to read a member's health when `par` won't show it (e.g. after they've dropped off the roster).
- **A name-targeted heal still lands on a dropped ally who's been aided.** *([CONFIRMED])* Even though an aided-but-still-dropped ally isn't in `par` anymore, a heal cast **at them by name** still reaches them. A party healer can keep topping them up until they fully recover / rejoin.
- **Recovering to positive HP does NOT auto-rejoin the party. A re-invite is required.** *([CONFIRMED])* The drop removed the character from the party game-side, so bringing them back above 0 HP (via `aid` + heal) restores their ability to act but **not** their membership.
  - The **party leader must `invite <name>` again** to pull them back into the group. Until then, the recovered character is solo even though they're standing right there.
  - This holds both ways. When the **local** character recovers from a self-drop, the client must NOT resurrect the wiped roster; it waits for a real follow / `par` signal (which only arrives after the leader's re-invite). When a **leader** revives a dropped member, the rescue sequence is `aid` + heal **then** `invite <name>`.
- **Which commands a dropped character can still send is in *Health, resting & recovery → 0 HP — dropped / bleeding out***: on Stock the engine keeps a fixed allowed list with the telepath on it, and refuses `bg`, `par` and the directed say `>` among others. A dropped member's telepath (an `@health` reply) is refused on Paradigm and gets out on Stock (same topic; user 2026-10-09).
- **Stock: the `drag` command's checks and lines, in order** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_cmd_drag` @0x455fa4; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*:
  - bare `drag` while dragging: `You are no longer dragging %s.`;
  - the target isn't a player: `Syntax: DRAG {user name} [{direction}]`; yourself: `Why would you want to drag yourself around?`; someone is already dragging them: `%s is already being dragged.`; the target is hidden from you: `Syntax: DRAG {user name} {direction} ` (with a trailing space);
  - the target's HP is above 0: the dragger sees `%s is too healthy to be dragged.`, the target `%s tried to drag you from the room.`, and the room `%s attempted to drag %s out of the room.`;
  - in a `Colliseum` room with the arena switch on (*Monsters, lairs & spawns → Monster roaming and following*): `You may not drag from the colliseum`;
  - `drag <name>`: `You are now dragging %s.`; `drag <name> <dir>` queues the move at once, or prints `There are no exits upwards!` / `There are no exits downwards!` / `There are no exits to the %s!`;
  - any `drag` clears the dragger's resting and meditating, sneaking and hidden flags (@0x455fc2, @0x4560bc).
- **Stock: what each dragged move prints** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_move_user` @0x41951b, @0x419563–0x4195ca; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*. The dragger sees `You are dragging %s.` ahead of their own room display. The dragged player sees `%s is dragging you around.`, then their own room display and a prompt, whatever their `set follow` mode (*Following the leader: follow / drag movement*). The room's leave and arrival lines carry ` (Dragging %s)` after the direction (@0x41790c).
  - A dragged player over 100% encumbrance sees `You are too heavy to be dragged!` and the drag ends, while the dragger still moves (@0x417880–0x4178d8).
  - A dragged player whose HP has risen above 0 is let go; that branch prints no line (@0x4178da–0x417903).
  - A follower can't drag: see *Following the leader: follow / drag movement*.
- **Client use:**
  - Client reaction: treat a member's drop as a **wait condition** and pause farming / movement to stay with them. Aid them, keep **healing them by name** despite their absence from `par`, and wait out the climb to positive HP. Then check their HP via an `@health` telepath until they recover, and (if leading) **re-invite** them once they're up.
  - **Client policy (user, 2026-09-27):** the hold is timed off the climb, not a fixed timeout. A `@health` reply at negative HP gives the exact time (`(1 − hp)·30 s`); with no reply, the realm's death floor gives the longest it can take (`|floor|·30 s`).
  - Implemented in `AllyDroppedHandler`. It:
    - asserts `MovementCoordinator.AllyDownGate`
    - sends `aid <name>` and one `@health`
    - restarts the stand-up clock when our aid lands (the death-floor worst case unless a reply timed it)
    - exposes the aided ally to `CastingDirector`'s downed-ally heal category
    - polls `@health` from the expected stand-up time on
    - re-invites, when leading, on the first positive `@health`
    - releases once they reach the party-heal bar, rejoin, leave or die — or 60 s past the expected stand-up with no sign of them, or 120 s after standing without reaching the bar
  - Its own recent-leader memory recognises a dropped leader that a leader-disconnect already wiped from the roster.

### Member death shows as an invited slot in `par`
*Status: CONFIRMED*

- **A dead non-leader member leaves the active party but shows in the leader's `par` as an invited (pending) slot.** That slot is **indistinguishable from a genuine pending invite**.
- **A member death is recognized from the room line `<Name> has died.`, not from `par`.** The line is emitted where they're killed. The leader keys roster cleanup off that named member by **uninviting** them; there's no automatic removal.
- **On Stock the engine takes a member at 0 HP or below off every player's member list** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-09, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll` `_check_kill_user` @0x419a93 → `_stop_following(user, -1)` → `_remove_from_group` @0x41de2a–0x41de6d; Realm: Stock, Paradigm not recorded)*, for a drop and a death alike (*Dropping (0 HP) or instant death removes you from the party*). An `[Invited]` row is printed only for a player still on the viewer's list (*`par` output block*), so by that code a dead member leaves no row in the leader's `par` unless something puts them back on the list; nothing that does was found, and no Stock capture shows it either way. The invited slot in this topic is taken as Paradigm's only *(user 2026-10-09: "yes i think so")*. (Was `[CONFLICT — ask the user]`.)
- **Client use:**
  - Never infer a death by diffing `par` alone. A died-and-now-invited name looks identical to a recruit we're still waiting on; only the death line disambiguates.
  - `KnownPatterns.PartyMemberDied` reads both room lines, `<Name> has died.` and the Stock DLL's `<Name> is dead.` (*Death & corpse recovery → Death lines & the miracle-save*; the second added 2026-10-09). A monster's own death sentence that ends the same way (`The roc hatchling lets out a squeal, and is dead.`) isn't read as a name. `PartyDeathRosterCleanup` uninvites only a name that then shows `[Invited]`, so on Stock, where the dead member leaves no row, nothing is sent; the member's buff timers are cleared on either line.

### Training drops you from the party
*Status: CONFIRMED (report `stock-20260801-002423`)*

- **Training (`train` / `train stats`) is a realm excursion. It briefly drops you out of and back into the realm**, emitting `<Name> just left the Realm.` then `<Name> just entered the Realm.` to everyone in the room.
- **The party effect depends on who trained.**
  - A **follower's** train drops only that follower. This is the same as a disconnect: they are removed server-side and need a fresh leader invite to rejoin. They do **not** auto-rejoin on return.
  - The **leader's** train disbands the whole party (see *Losing the leader disbands the party*). The leader sees `You are not in a party at the present time.` on return.
- **Self perspective (the character doing the training): entering the train-stats screen breaks up OUR OWN party server-side.** Our client must reset its own `PartyState` on train-stats entry to match:
  - a **leader** clears its whole roster (party disbanded)
  - a **follower** clears the "following `<leader>`" state (no longer following)
- **Client use:**
  - Route `<Name> just left the Realm.` through the same member-drop correlation as a disconnect. A trained follower is then stamped into the reconnect grace window and auto-re-invited on their `just entered the Realm.`. Members who train at staggered times each get re-invited as they individually re-enter within the window.
  - Skipping the `PartyState` reset leaves a stale "following" state that makes the client **reject the leader's fresh re-invite**. Both the `@join` handler and the invite auto-accept no-op on "already following `<leader>`", so the follower never rejoins (report `stock-20260801-002423`).
- **Client policy: a party train trip is not asked back from** *(user, 2026-10-10: "train trips should be excluded but if this happens because a gated trainer was picked that someone cant enter, the leader should realize that and pick them up when the training is done")*.
  - **On the leader nothing stops the trip.** While a trip runs (`PartyTrainCoordinator.TripRunning`, and likewise the leader's own train or spell-shop run with the party in tow, `TrainerWalkManager.OwnRunActive`) neither the game's `<name> is no longer following you.` nor a member's `@comeback` starts a pickup or stops the trip's walk (`PartyComebackManager.OnMemberLeftBehind`, `OnComeback`). Each member the trip leaves is kept with the room they were left in: the room the leader's step left when the game said so, replaced by the room their own request names. A `@comeback` during the trip is answered once, `{I can't yet, I'm on a train trip. I'll come for you when the training is done}` (`PartyComebackManager.TrainTripReply`, only when `Settings.Talk.WarnOnInvalidRemoteCommand` lets denials be said), and kept.
  - **When a trip ends by itself the leader fetches everyone it left, in turn**, whether it finished or failed on its own, however long ago they dropped, on whatever client they are (`PartyTrainTripRoll.Close` → `PartyComebackManager.TrainTripEnded`; a run of the leader's own ends through `TrainerWalkManager.OwnRunOver`): the ordinary pickup, from the room kept for each, after the loop or walk the trip paused has been put back, and with none to put back as well. A member following again by then isn't fetched. Everyone who set out and isn't following at the end is named in the log and their `@comeback` is taken as a party member's from then (`PartyManager.ExpectComebackFrom`): being a member when the trip began is what authorises it, not the *If leading, accept @comeback for* time.
    - **The return distance doesn't bound that fetch.** *Return distance* is for a request out of the blue; a member the leader's own trip walked away from is fetched from however far, and a search with no room goes down the whole of the leader's trail (`BeginRecovery`, `tripFetch`). An ordinary `@comeback` is bound by it as before.
    - **A room the leader guessed is checked on arrival.** The room kept from the game's drop line is the one the leader's step had just left. If the member isn't seen there (the same `Also here:` test a backtrack makes), nobody is invited into the empty room and the engine isn't held for the follow wait: the leader answers `{didn't find you where the trip left you - @comeback with your room and I'll come}` and their request is fetched as the trip's own. A request that names another room while the leader is on the way turns the walk there; a room the member named is not checked.
    - **Who the game never reported.** A Stock leader isn't told of a follower it drops (**Where the game tells a leader nothing (Stock)**), so the trip can end with them still on its list. The roll knows who set out: for the *If leading, accept @comeback for* time after the trip a request from any of them is the trip's fetch, with no engine to go back to and from beyond the return distance (`PartyComebackManager.TakeAwaitedAfterTrip`).
    - **With the master switch off at the end of the trip** the list is kept and fetched when the switch is back on, by the rule a `@comeback` kept for the switch is replayed by: only within the *If leading, accept @comeback for* time of the trip's end (`PartyComebackManager.SettleAfterMasterSwitch`).
  - **A trip the player took over fetches nobody** *(the standing policy of 2026-10-08 for a pickup the player took over, applied to the trip)*. A second Stop, a run started over the held trip ("No" to *Resume it first?*), Reset States, or the trip's walk stopped under it (`PartyTrainCoordinator.EndTrip`, `OnWalkEvent`; for the leader's own run `TrainerWalkManager.Cancel` and its stopped walk) end the trip without a fetch: who was left, and where, is logged, named once in a terminal notice (`[Train trip ended early - left behind: … Not going back for them on its own]`), and stays authorised, so a `@comeback` they send is a member's and is answered by whatever the leader is doing then.
  - **The member's side.** The leader's `PartyTrainTripRoll` telepaths `@ptrain trip on` to every member that speaks `@ptrain` when a trip sets out and `@ptrain trip off` when it ends (`PartyTrainCoordinator.ReceiveTrip`). The member takes "off" from that leader even after an exit has turned it out of the party (`RemoteCommandManager.PartyTrainEligibility`). A member left behind while a trip is on holds its `@comeback` and sends it when told the trip is over (*`@comeback` (follower → leader)*, held back). An "on" with no "off" lapses after 15 minutes, and the held request goes out then; the leader's own fetch at the end of the trip doesn't depend on it.
  - **Where the game tells a leader nothing (Stock)**, the leader learns of a member the trip left only from that member's `@comeback`, during the trip or after it. A member on a client that sends none is not known to be missing until a `par` shows it, and is not fetched: there is no room to go to.
  - A member with a train order still walks to the trainer's room by itself (`PartyTrainCoordinator.ReceiveTrain`).

### The level-11 train is a class-gated quest
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-23 (user); how it works CONFIRMED 2026-09-26 (user)*

- **The 10→11 train is a quest, not a normal trainer visit.** It needs a **key from the mummy NPC** on the
  **third level** of the crypt below the **Silvermere graveyard**. The key opens a hall whose exits are each
  **class-gated**; the trainers that perform the 10→11 train — the **(class) spirits** — wait at the end,
  at the bottom of the crypt.
- **So only same-class characters can make the trip together**; a mixed party splits at the hall. That is
  why the step is only easily auto-trainable running solo.
- **Training stats after the 10→11 train, in the spirit's room, teleports you out** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-30, user; report `paradigm-20260930-085259`) · both realms*.
  - **No message marks the move.** In the capture, `train` → `Welcome to level 11!`, then `train stats` and SAVE on the creation screen. The next thing on the wire was the room display of Graveyard, Tomb Entrance 1/834, where the train had been in Large Tomb 1/2300.
  - **Every class lands in the same room, Graveyard, Tomb Entrance 1/834** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-30, user)*. Each class has its own 10→11 trainer room with its class spirit in it, and all of them send you to 1/834.
  - **Stock does the same** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-09-30, user)*.
- **Client use:**
  - Party auto-train stops members at level 10 by default (Auto-Trainer → *Leave the level 11 train to a solo trip*).
  - The teleport lands while the train-stats screen's send hold is still up: the new room's `Also here:` comes before the `Obvious exits:` line that lifts it. Combat's attack there is held and re-decided when the hold lifts (`CombatManager.OnWireReleased`, report `paradigm-20260930-085259`). Room tracking re-localises off the room display.

### Targeted casts on a hiding member
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-28 (user + screenshot)*

- **The only time a targeted cast on a party member misses is when that member is HIDING.** The server answers **`You do not see <name> here!`** (and the member isn't in `Also here:`).
- **Client use:**
  - Don't pre-gate single-target party casts on `Also here:`; that wrongly skips the followed leader and any hidden member. Attempt the cast based on party membership.
  - If `You do not see <name> here!` comes back, back that member off until you **move** or they **reappear in `Also here:`** (they unhid). Don't re-fire the cast, and repeat the failure, every round.

### Resting observed in the party
*Status: mixed (rest line CONFIRMED; rest-to-use-the-wait is **Client policy**, user directive 2026-07-11)*

- **A party member sitting down to rest is announced to everyone else in the room as `<name> stops to rest.`** *([CONFIRMED])* `<name>` is the given name. The actor's own view uses a different verb form (`You stop to rest.`), so the third-person line never matches the resting player's own row.
- **The meditate-observation line is not yet confirmed.** Do not guess it.
- **Rest-to-use-the-wait.** *(**Client policy**, user directive, 2026-07-11)*
  - When the party **leader** is `@wait`-held and **not poisoned**, the leader rests (or meditates) to use the forced downtime, until the wait clears.
  - A **follower** that sees the leader rest/meditate rests/meditates too, **unless the follower is poisoned** (poison ticks break rest and waste the downtime).
  - Poison blocks resting altogether — see *Health, resting & recovery → Poison prevents resting* (CONFIRMED 2026-08-17), which supersedes this 2026-07-11 note's claim that only these two downtime-rest paths gate on poison.
- **Client use:**
  - The `<name> stops to rest.` line flips `PartyMember.Resting` the instant it's seen, ahead of the 5-second `par` poll, so a follower can mirror the leader's rest immediately.

### Party ailment signaling and cross-client sync (MegaMUD parity)
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-12 (user)*

This covers how a client learns which ailments afflict itself and its party members, and how it warns the party. It is modelled to interoperate with MegaMUD, so MudPlay and MegaMUD clients can party together and each engine reacts identically.

- **Self (most reliable): a client knows its OWN ailments from the apply and wear-off spell messages.** This is authoritative for self; the statline carries no ailment flag.
- **Poison is NOT announced.** In a party it is read from each member's **`P` flag on the `par` party screen**; solo, from the poison apply message.
  - A member's poison chip is set when `P` is present in the par row and cleared when it drops.
  - `par` carries no other ailment letter.
- **Blind / Diseased / Confused / Held are announced verbosely on SAY as a bare token**: `@blind`, `@diseased`, `@confused`, `@held`.
  - **Wire form:** the sender types the token `.`-prefixed (`.@blind`, `.@held`, …; the leading `.` sends it on say), and observers see the bare token (`@blind`). The same holds for `@panic` (sent as `.@panic`).
  - There is **no `on`/`off` argument**; MegaMUD sends the bare token on apply only.
  - An observer sets the named member's chip on the bare token.
  - Confusion has no realm cure, so its announce only lights the chip. It is kept because ignore-confusion behavior applies to party members too.
  - *Historical:* MudPlay formerly sent a paired `.@X on` / `.@X off` toggle (it lacked wear-off detection at the time). MegaMUD uses bare tokens; the clear comes from the signals below.
  - **Client policy (user, 2026-10-14, report `paradigm-20261014-214037`): MudPlay says the token again when it follows a leader while still afflicted.** The user, left behind while knocked down and then fetched: "it should tell the leader/room hey i'm held, not just wait for it to wear off". A held follower drops out of the party when the leader moves (*A follower who can't move is left behind*), so the apply-time say reached a party it is no longer in. On `You are now following <leader>.` with an ailment still on, the bare token goes out again under the same gates as at apply, with one `@wait` carrying the first held reason's note. Every hold in the data carries HoldPerson (74), which Freedom (81) ends (*Spells, buffs & conditions → Ailment identification — which spells cause disease / poison / blind / hold*; *Spells, buffs & conditions → Cure-spell identification — which spells REMOVE each ailment*), so a member with a cure-holds spell can free us.
- **No say signal is sent on wear-off.** A member's chip clears on **whichever of these is observed first**:
  - a **witnessed cure** on that member (our cast, or one seen cast on them in the room)
  - the **spell's duration timing out**
  - the **par `P` flag dropping** (poison)
  - a **`@status`** reply of "no ailments"
- **The only clear signal the afflicted member emits is `@ok`**, a telepath to the leader to release the wait.
- **Ailment duration is deterministic.** When a monster's ailment spell *lands* (a "resist" means it never landed, so there's no chip at all), the duration is a specific number the spell record computes from **that monster's cast level**.
  - The same spell on different monsters differs only because their cast levels differ.
  - So an observer that witnessed the apply computes the exact duration (`Dur` rounds × spell-round seconds, at the caster's cast level) and auto-clears the chip when it elapses, with no fudge beyond clock jitter.
- **Client use:**
  - MudPlay reads its own ailments with `ConditionTracker`, matched against the Messages table.
  - `PartyManager.FollowingLeader` → `AilmentSyncEngine.NoteFollowingLeader` says the tokens again and re-asks the `@wait` (`PartyRestSync.RequestWait`, `resend`) on following a leader while afflicted; logged under `Ailment`, and the bug report's Party section shows the last one (report `paradigm-20261014-214037`). A receiving MudPlay leader lights the chip and pauses (`PartyAilmentTracker`; another member only once its roster has us back, since a member off its roster is ignored), and `CastingDirector.PickPartyCure` casts the configured cure-holds spell on a member whose Held chip is lit.
  - `PartyAilmentTracker.WitnessApplies` lights a member's chip from the ailment record's witness line and arms its duration. A line that names only the victim (`{target} is knocked flat!`) counts, since an on-hit effect names nobody else. `AppServices.ResolveAilmentDurationSeconds` takes the length from the monster the line names when one of that name in the room carries the spell, otherwise the longest among in-room monsters that carry it; an on-hit effect runs the spell's base `Dur` (*Combat → Monster on-hit procs (`AttHitSpell-N`) are physical attacks, not casts*). With nothing resolved the chip keeps a 180 s cap.
  - A chip clears on a witnessed cure only when the game data lists that spell as curing the ailment (`CureSpellIndex`), whatever sits in the cure slots (**Client policy**, user 2026-10-03). `merciful grace` (#804) is Heal + CurePoison + DispellMagic(BlindUser) in both sets, so it clears poison and blind chips and never a held one. *[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]: a player reports it cures the ultangir's knockdown (#318) on Paradigm; the 1.9.1 data shows nothing on it that removes a hold.*

### `@wait` / `@ok` party pause
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-12 (user); pause-flag detail CONFIRMED*

- **An afflicted follower telepaths `@wait` to the leader and `@ok` when it clears (follower → leader, TELEPATH).**
  - A follower afflicted by poison / blind / confused / diseased / **held** telepaths **`@wait`** to the leader, unless that ailment's `Ignore<X>` is set.
  - It telepaths **`@ok`** when its last non-ignored ailment clears.
- **MegaMUD's `@wait` names its reason in parentheses after the token**, e.g. `@wait (HP's too low)`. The receiver acts on the token alone; the note is for the person reading it.
  - Wording seen from a MegaMUD client *([OBSERVED] a contributor's capture of a MegaMUD follower telepathing a MudPlay leader, 2026-09-11; no report on file)*: `(HP's too low)`, `(blinded)`, `(confused)`, `(waiting on message condition)`.
  - `(can't move)` for a hold *([OBSERVED] report cited in Chapter 13 → A follower who can't move is left behind)*.
  - **MegaMUD sends `(waiting on message condition)` for a poison wait and for a disease wait** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-02, user)*. The user believes MegaMUD also uses it for other conditions that have no wording of their own; which ones is not recorded.
  - **MegaMUD sends nothing for a mana wait** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-02, user)*.
- **A follower's `@ok` goes out only when its last wait reason clears.** A reason that never clears suppresses every later `@ok`, and the leader then stays paused until its own wait timer expires, each time.
- **`@wait` / `@ok` is a leader-directed pause flag, not a momentary signal.** The leader stays paused until **either** the same member telepaths `@ok`, **or** the leader's own wait timer expires.
  - The timer is the "If leading, wait only (s)" cap (`PartySettings.IfLeadingWaitTotalSec`).
  - On expiry the leader gives up and resumes, so a dropped / AFK member can't strand the party forever.
- **The leader-side "ignore @wait when leading" opt-out drops inbound `@wait` before it ever pauses.**
- **`@waiting` (leader → follower, TELEPATH) is MudPlay's nudge that the leader is holding for an `@ok`.** It is sent after re-collecting a follower who was left behind (see *A follower who can't move is left behind*). *(**Client policy**, user, 2026-09-26.)*
- **Held follows the same `@wait` / `@ok` flow and cannot be suppressed.** A held member can't move, so the party waits for them. Held has no `Ignore` gate, so it is never suppressible.
  - **Both signals pause the leader.** A held member telepaths `@wait`/`@ok` *in addition to* announcing its `.@held` on say: the say lights the member's chip, and the `@wait` pauses the leader. The inbound `@held` say also routes through the same pause (`PartyEssentialHandlers.NotePause`), and that member's `@ok` on cure releases it.
- **All of this is party-only.** Solo (no party / no leader / you ARE the leader), nothing is telepathed. Self recognition and clearing run entirely off the apply/wear-off spell messages.
- **Client use:**
  - **Every `@wait` MudPlay sends names its reason** (**Client policy**, user 2026-10-02): MegaMUD's wording where MegaMUD has one, MudPlay's own where it doesn't. `PartyRestSync.RequestWait` sends:
    - MegaMUD's: `HpNote` `(HP's too low)`, `BlindNote`, `ConfusedNote`, `HeldNote` `(can't move)`, and `ConditionNote` `(waiting on message condition)` for a poison or a disease wait;
    - MudPlay's own: `ManaNote` `(mana's too low)` (MegaMUD sends nothing for a mana wait) and `TooHeavyNote` `(too heavy to move)` (`TooHeavyWaitSignal`).
    - `HealthManager.PartyWaitNote` picks the pool for a Health wait from its gates, HP first when both are short. A test fails if a wait reason is added without a note.
  - Only the wait that starts the hold telepaths, so the note is the first reason's; a second reason is held without a new `@wait` (Health and TooHeavy re-send, with their own note).
  - `PartyRestSync.HeldReasons` is the set an `@ok` waits on. A release that leaves others held is logged with what still holds (`Party` category), and the bug report's Party section lists it. Nothing auto-releases a long-held reason: a timeout would send the leader on while the follower still can't move (**Client policy**).
  - **Client policy — nothing is signalled with the master switch off** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: "no holds should be sent, if the master switch is off". With `AutoModeController.KillSwitchEngaged`, `PartyRestSync` telepaths no `@wait`, `@ok` or `@heal`, `AilmentSyncEngine` announces no ailment, and `MovementCoordinator` parks every hold but the user's pause (`ParkHoldsForMasterSwitch`). A `@wait` already sent is released as the switch goes off (`PartyRestSync.ReleaseForMasterSwitch`, one `@ok`: a release is not a hold, and a leader whose wait limit is 0 would otherwise stand for good). When the switch comes back on the parked holds are asserted before movement is released, and a reason still held is asked once with its own note (`PartyRestSync.ResyncAfterMasterSwitch`; the health engine re-asks for itself).
  - **Client policy — inbound signals are remote commands** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: "no remote command except @auto-all on or off should work, if the master switch is off". An inbound `@waiting` or `@comeback` is dropped at `RemoteCommandManager` with no reply while the switch is off. An inbound `@wait` or `@ok` is not acted on either (no reply, and the `PartyWaitGate` it would raise is parked), but who is waiting is still recorded, so that at switch-on the leader holds for a follower who asked and not for one who has since said `@ok`; the wait limit counts from switch-on (`PartyWaitMovementGate`).

### `@panic` leader warning
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-09-12 (user)*

- **`@panic` is a party-wipe warning (leader → party, SAY).** A party **leader** whose HP crosses its **"hang if below"** floor says the bare token **`@panic`** (sent as `.@panic`). It then hangs up (or `break` + `sys goto <wimpy>` if opted in).
- **Two checkboxes gate it:** **"use @panic while leading"** (send) and **"ignore @panics"** (receive).
- **A member not ignoring `@panic` reacts the same way**, hanging up or doing break + sys-goto-wimpy, per its own settings.
- **Client policy** *(user, 2026-10-09)*: with the master switch off (`AutoModeController.KillSwitchEngaged`) a received `@panic` is answered only when `GeneralSettings.AllowHangupInAllOffMode` is set (`HealthManager.RespondToReceivedPanic`): "if that option isnt on, and all auto's are off, none of our auto systems should respond". The leader's own `.@panic` goes out with its low-HP hang-up, so it follows that hang-up's switches.

### `@comeback` (follower → leader)
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-31 (user; report `stock-20260731-082602`); when a follower sends it CONFIRMED 2026-10-10 (user) · Realm: both (a client rule; the game lines it reads are tagged inline)*

- **`@comeback` is a follower→leader telepath.** The follower asks the leader to come back and re-grab/re-invite it.
- **It is messaging only.** It must **never** drive a walk on the follower's own client.
- **A follower sends it whenever it is left behind, with three exceptions** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user)*:
  - "in all situations where a party member gets left behind, and it wasn't because they died or we removed them from party... the party member should be sending a @comeback signal, which is what tells the party leader it needs to come back for them." Asked about an exit that requires an item: "yes"; about moving while they got held: "yes".
  - "as a party member, getting left behind should trigger a @comeback unless we specifically were uninvited from the party or a teleport spell removed us and we're waiting for the rejoin effort or we voluntarily leave the party either by using the command or a manual move".
  - It is also sent after a disconnect and reconnect, when the follower doesn't see the leader in the room or the leader left before re-inviting (2026-07-31, user).
  - (An earlier note said a follower sends it in exactly two left-behind cases, the reconnect and a movement-preventing affliction the leader didn't wait out; superseded 2026-10-10.)
- **The wire form is `@comeback <map>/<room>`, or a bare `@comeback`** (**Client policy**). The room is named only when the follower's own position is confirmed; a bare one has the leader backtrack the way it came. The leader's client answers by telepath, in braces: `{coming to your location for pickup}`, `{backtracking up to N room(s) to find you}`, `{comeback already in progress}`, and when it isn't coming `{I can't I'm idle}` (no walk, loop or Auto-Lair running), `{my party is full - can't take you back}`, `{can't find a path to you - you're on your own}`, `{you're N rooms off (limit M) - can't come, forget me}`, `{tried reaching you Nx and couldn't - forget me}` or `{no path history to backtrack - going idle}` (`PartyComebackManager.BeginRecovery`). Three answers say "later", not "no": `{I can't yet, I'm on a train trip. I'll come for you when the training is done}`, `{I can't yet, an exit on my way turned you away. I'll invite you when my next pass finds you}` (Auto-Lair) and `{didn't find you where the trip left you - @comeback with your room and I'll come}`. A leader that set out and gave up says `{path failed - resuming}`, `{can't reach <map>/<room> - resuming}` or `{follow timed out - resuming anyway}`.
  - **These are sent whatever `Settings.Talk.WarnOnInvalidRemoteCommand` says, with three exceptions** (**Client policy**; *[CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user*): the follower's client reads them (`ComebackRequester.OnTelepathIn`). The exceptions follow the setting and are said only when denials are: a loop's refusal (`PartyComebackManager.LoopGateRefusal`) and the two `{I can't yet, …}` answers, the train trip's (`TrainTripReply`) and Auto-Lair's (`LairGateReply`). Asked whether the loop's refusal should always be sent because the follower's client reads it: "no, it should match whether the refusals are verbose or silent".
  - **Replies are plain ASCII** (`WireText.Ascii`, applied where a reply is sent). (Until 2026-10-10 these answers carried a long dash where the hyphen now is: `{path failed — resuming}`. `ComebackRequester` matches the words either side of it, so a client on either version reads the other's.)
- **How a follower's client can tell it was left behind.** The game says so outright in some cases only (*A follower who can't move is left behind*), so the client reads four signs:
  1. **`You are no longer following <leader>.` behind a follow move that couldn't be made.**
     - *Stock* `[OBSERVED]`: the held, stunned and too-heavy refusals print it (`_move_user` @0x4176d1–0x417843), and so does a hold or stun from the monsters' parting attack, with no refusal line before it (@0x418fe2–0x419003).
     - *Paradigm* `[OBSERVED]`: a knocked-down follower gets it with no refusal line the client knows (report `paradigm-20260922-085609`), which is why a hold in force when the line lands counts too. The leader's side of a too-heavy follower is report `paradigm-20260926-195517`; what that follower was printed isn't on record.
  2. **An exit's refusal with no move of the follower's own in flight.** A follower sends no moves, so the line answers the follow move the game made for it.
     - *Stock* `[OBSERVED]`: this is the whole of it. The follow ends with no further line for a shut door, a missing item or key, a toll, a level, class, race or alignment gate, a room that isn't permitted, or no exit (`_fast_update_character` @0x4230fb–0x42311d).
     - *Paradigm* `[CONFIRMED]` 2026-10-10 (the screens in *A follower who can't move is left behind*): the follow line, the exit's refusal, then `You are no longer following <leader>.` So there the refusal comes under sign 1, and by its shape: the follow line with no arrival behind it, whatever the refusal says. (Asked earlier the same day the user had said "i dont remember if it says they stopped following you or not but i think it does"; the screenshot settled it.)
     - **A shut door is not such an exit** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user: "a shut door no one can go through")*: it stops the leader as it stops the followers, so nobody is left behind at one. The client still reads a door's refusal that no move of its own drew as a refused follow move, since the line prints only when the game tried one.
  3. **The leader seen leaving with no follow move behind it**: `<leader> just left to the <dir>.` and no ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --` or new room.
     - *Stock* `[OBSERVED]`: the leader's departure is told to the room before any follower is moved, and a follow move that goes through a generic exit always prints the follow line (`_move_user` @0x4192b1–0x4193d4, @0x4190a8–0x4190d1; the capture in *A follower who can't move is left behind*).
     - *Paradigm* `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]`: does a follower who goes along see `<leader> just left to the <dir>.` and then ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --` in the same burst, as on Stock? The follower's screen of 2026-10-10 (*A follower who can't move is left behind*) has another member's `just left to the east.` and then the follow line; the leader's own departure line isn't in it. Since Paradigm prints the follow line even for a move it then refuses, this sign adds little there: sign 1 carries it.
  4. **The follower's own `par` listing the leader as `[Invited]`.** Read on both realms: the client has no realm test here.
     - *Stock* `[OBSERVED]` (`_display_party`; *A follower who can't move is left behind*); not seen in a capture.
     - *Paradigm*: not a sign there. A follower an exit turns away is out of the party with no `[Invited]` row left behind (*A follower who can't move is left behind*, the screens of 2026-10-10), and the `You are no longer following <leader>.` line has already said so.
- **The same line with none of that before it is not a left-behind.** `You are no longer following <leader>.` is also what an uninvite, a `disband party`, the follower's own `leave` or bare `follow`, the leader's drop, death, teleport or leaving the game print (*Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`*; *Dropping (0 HP) or instant death removes you from the party*; *Movement & navigation → CMD-driven room teleports split the party*). On Stock the engine has no other line for any of them, so a follower can't tell which of those it was.
  - **On Stock a follower can tell an exit's refusal from an uninvite** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-10, Stock 1.11p `wccmmud.dll`; the two paths in *A follower who can't move is left behind* and *Party commands: `invite`, `join` / `follow`, `leave`, `uninvite`, `disband party`*)*: the refusal prints the exit's own line and no `You are no longer following …`, and leaves the follower on the lists (`[Invited]` in `par`); the uninvite prints `You are no longer following …` with no refusal and takes the follower off them (`You are not in a party at the present time.`). *Paradigm*: both end on the same `You are no longer following …`, and the exit's case is told by what comes before it: the follow line with no arrival (*A follower who can't move is left behind*).
  - **The bare line sends nothing** *([CONFIRMED] 2026-10-10, user, of a follower's own `leave party` and of the leader's `uninvite`: "that case should not send a comeback … in this case they should not send an @comeback")*. On Paradigm the two are one line with nothing before it, and a follow that failed is the follow line, no arrival and then the line (*A follower who can't move is left behind*). So a leader taken away by a teleport with no regroup coming, which also prints only the bare line, is not asked back.
- **Client policy** (2026-10-10, from the user's rule): `ComebackRequester` sends one `@comeback` per incident.
  - **Windows.** A refusal or the leader's departure counts toward the `no longer following` line for 3 s. Signs 2 and 3 wait 2 s before they are acted on, so a follow line or the `no longer following` line that names the cause arrives first; in that time a new confirmed room, or the map no longer being sure of the room, means the follower is not standing where the leader left it. A refusal is the answer to a move of the follower's own for as long as that move is unanswered (`RoomTracker.OwnMoveInFlight`: a leader's drag waiting for its room is not one), and to a typed command that isn't talk for 2 s. `The door is closed in that direction!` is never a refused move (*Movement & navigation → `look <dir>` — peeking an adjacent room*).
  - **A failed follow is read by its shape** (2026-10-10, from the user's ruling): ` -- Following your Party leader <dir> --`, then at least one line from the game that is no arrival, then `You are no longer following <leader>.` within 3 s of the follow line. Whatever the line between says, it is taken for the exit's refusal. A refusal the client does know, a hold in force, and the held / stunned / too-heavy lines send on the `no longer following` line as before.
    - **What counts as the arrival:** the room confirmed (`RoomTracker.MoveConfirmed`) or a new room, a room's `Obvious exits:` line, and the lines a room that shows nothing is entered with (`KnownPatterns.RoomPitchBlack`, `RoomVeryDark`, `You are blind.`, and `You are blind!`, the one line a room too bright to see in is shown as; *Movement & navigation → Dark rooms — no name, no exits, traversal inferred from no bonk*). A refused move shows no room.
    - **Nothing at all between the two lines is not a failed follow**: that is a follow in `set follow blind` (no room is shown for it, *Following the leader: follow / drag movement*) with an uninvite, a disband or a teleport soon after it.
    - **The map's drag is taken back.** `FollowMoveObserver` books a drag on the follow line, and a refusal the detector doesn't know leaves it booked; the shape's verdict un-counts it (`RoomTracker.NoteFollowDragRefused`), so the request names the room the follower stands in.
    - **Known gap:** with more than 3 s between the follow line and the `no longer following` line (lag) and a refusal in wording the client doesn't know, the shape isn't seen and nothing is sent.
    - **Known gap, the other way:** a follow that shows no room at all (`set follow blind`), then any line that isn't chat (a monster or player walking in), then an uninvite within 3 s of the follow line has the shape of a failed follow, and a `@comeback` is sent for it (review probe, 2026-10-10). The onset of blindness in that window is read as an arrival, since `You are blind!` is also the too-bright room's line.
  - **A verdict with no refusal the client knows behind it waits 2 s for the prompt.** The follow line or `<leader> just left to the <dir>.` and then `You are no longer following <leader>.` is also what a follower dropped by the monsters' parting attack may see, and the prompt that carries its HP comes after the line.
  - **The invite that ends the pickup is taken** (2026-10-10; the user: a follower an exit stopped "has to be reinvited"). The leader we asked back is a leader whose `<name> has invited you to follow …` is followed whatever that player's *Join party if invited* box says (`ComebackRequester.IsLeaderWeAsked` → `AutoPartyManager.ForceAcceptFrom`), until we follow again, they decline, or 10 minutes pass. It rests on the request having been sent: with *Auto-request @comeback when left behind* off the invite is taken only where *Join party if invited* is ticked for that leader, and with the master switch off no invite is taken at all.
  - **Withheld for good, and logged with the reason:**
    - an uninvite or disband, which is the bare line (no failed follow move before it);
    - a teleport split: the bare line behind the leader's departure through an exit that casts on the walk (`RoomExit.CastsOnWalk`; *Movement & navigation → Cast-on-walk exits and random teleports*). And the leader's own teleport: when the leader relayed the keyword of a teleport out of the follower's room with `@party` in the last 15 s (`PartyEssentialHandlers.PartyDirectiveRelayed`), a verdict with no refusal the client knows behind it (the follow-line shape, or the leader's departure alone) is that teleport, and the bare line's log names it. No other relayed command, and no relay from another member, bears on it, and a relay never outweighs a refusal the client knows;
    - a voluntary leave: `leave` in any spelling the game takes (`le` … `leave`, alone or with one more word that isn't `gang`) or a bare `follow` (`fo` … `follow`) typed in the last 5 s (forgotten once the follower follows again), or a manual move in the last 5 s that the game didn't refuse (`RoomTracker.ManualMoveObserved`: a keystroke, a macro, a relayed command). `follow <name>` and `join <name>` join someone and are not a leave;
    - a death or drop: the follower's own (`RoomTracker.PlayerDeathObserved`, `PlayerState.IsMortallyWounded`), or the leader's `is dead` / `has died` / `drops to the ground!` line in the last 10 s;
    - not following anyone (solo or leading), and the setting off.
  - **Held back, and sent when it clears:** the master switch off, the board's menu, a held send gate, and the leader's party train trip (*Training drops you from the party*). The request goes out once the client can send, while the follower still isn't following and within the Party tab's *If leading, accept @comeback for* time of the incident (`ComebackRequester.RetryWindow`); a train trip doesn't count against that time while it runs.
  - **One per incident.** After a request is sent or withheld nothing more is sent until the follower is following again (`You are now following <leader>` or a follow line). The leader's answer is logged and kept for the bug report; a decline is not asked again. A fresh `You are no longer following …` always opens a new incident.
  - **A follower whose leader refuses, or never comes, stops counting itself a follower** *(user, 2026-10-10, asked what a Stock follower should do when its leader declines or never returns: "option A", which was to drop the follower state as soon as the leader refuses or the "accept @comeback for" time runs out)*. Stock ends a follow at an exit without a line to the follower (sign 2), so nothing else would end it there, and the client would hold its own movement for a leader who isn't coming.
    - **What ends it:** a refusal from the leader that was asked (`{I can't I'm idle}`, the loop's `{I can't, my loop goes through an exit you can't pass}`, party full, no path, too far, `forget me`, `going idle`); no word and no pickup within the Party tab's *If leading, accept @comeback for* time of the request; a request that could not be sent for that long; and the leader having set out and given up (`{path failed - resuming}`, `{can't reach … - resuming}`, `{follow timed out - resuming anyway}`).
    - **What doesn't:** `{I can't yet, …}` (a train trip that comes when the training is done, Auto-Lair's next pass) and any answer that says the leader is coming. After one of those the leader is waited on for 15 minutes, the bound a train trip nobody called off is given (`ComebackRequester.PromisedWait`), and then the follow is given up as above. Which answers those are is the leader's own list (`PartyComebackManager.SaysComingOrLater`: `coming to your location for pickup`, `backtracking up to`, `comeback already in progress`, `I can't yet`, `didn't find you`, `found you`, `got you`).
    - **Any other braced telepath from the leader changes nothing** (**Client policy**, 2026-10-10): the reply to another command, or a leader's generic `{command invalid or not allowed}`, is not an answer to the request, and the wait already running stands. (Earlier any braced telepath that was no decline stretched the wait to 15 minutes, so a leader's denial held the follower for longer than no answer would have.)
    - **What giving up does:** the party state is cleared as the game's own `You are no longer following <leader>.` clears it (`ComebackRequester.FollowGivenUp` → `PartyManager.NoteFollowGivenUp`), which lets go of the follower's movement hold (`PartyFollowerMovementGate`) and puts the flee and hang-up rules back to a solo character's. Logged at Info with the reason, and shown on the bug report's last-incident line. If the leader does come and invites, the usual invite rules apply: after a refusal that is *Join party if invited*; after a lapse or a give-up the invite is still one this client asked for (**The invite that ends the pickup is taken**). On Stock the leader is kept as `PartyManager.ListedWithLeader` and the client joins by itself when that leader turns up (*A follower who can't move is left behind*, the Client use bullet "Stock: a member still on the leader's list is brought back with a `join`, not an invite").
    - **Paradigm is untouched:** the game's own line has ended the follow before the request goes out, so there is nothing left to give up.
    - A `par` typed afterwards on Stock still lists the leader as `[Invited]`, and with no follow of our own that row reads as an invite of ours (*`par` output block*, the `[Invited]` row bullet).
  - **A dropped link is the reconnect's incident.** `ComebackRequester.NoteDisconnected` stands the watch down until the follower follows again, so the one request for that split is `PartyRejoinCoordinator`'s, inside its own window.
  - **Order with `@wait`.** A held or too-heavy follower's `@wait (reason)` goes out on the refusal line and the `@comeback` on the `no longer following` line behind it (the Stock capture in *A follower who can't move is left behind*).
- **Client use:**
  - The client's `ComebackRequester` is correctly telepath-only.
  - A follower must not auto-navigate itself back to a stale self-selected walk-to target.
  - What happens to movement after a death is in *Death & corpse recovery → Death wipes all effects*.
  - `ComebackRequester.OnNoLongerFollowing` (sign 1), `OnExitRefused` (sign 2, `KnownPatterns.DirectionFailed`), `OnDeparture` (sign 3, `KnownPatterns.RoomEntryDeparture`) and `NoteLeaderListedAsInvited` (sign 4, from `PartyManager.LeaderListedAsInvited`); `ExclusionFor` holds the withheld cases and `CannotSendNow` the held-back ones. Gate: `OtherSettings.AutoRequestComebackWhenLeftBehind` and the master switch.
  - Leader side: `PartyComebackManager` fetches members left behind together one after the other (`QueueRecovery`; the gated-followers capture in *A follower who can't move is left behind*), and a re-invited member who never follows is waited on for 90 s when *If leading, wait only* is 0 (no limit).
  - **Client policy, leader side: what each engine does about a member an exit turned away** (all four the user's, 2026-10-10). The exits meant are the ones that admit only some (`RoomExit.AdmitsOnlySome`: an item or ticket, a toll or fare, a level, class, race or alignment window; a door is not one), crossed by an engine's own step: not by hand, not by the pickup walk itself (`PartyComebackManager.OnRoomChanged`).
    - **A loop doesn't go back; a walk-to does** *("if the leader is looping through a gate the party member cannot pass, the party leader should not accept a comback for them, it should reject them. but on a walk to, it absolutely should comeback for them.")*.
    - **A walk-to goes back once** *(asked what a walk-to should do when the same member is turned away again after the pickup, with the choices of ending the walk with a notice, carrying on without them, or going back every time: "option A")*. The leader goes back and re-invites; if the walk is under way again and the same member is turned away at the same exit (the same room and exit), the walk ends there, with one terminal notice naming the member and the exit and a log line, and no second pickup is started (`PartyComebackManager.EndWalkAt`). Their `@comeback` after that gets the answer the leader's state calls for (`{I can't I'm idle}` once the walk has ended). Another gated exit further on gets its own one pickup. An errand's walk (a bank or sell trip) counts as a walk-to. Where the game tells the leader nothing of the drop (Stock), the member's second request for that exit is what ends the walk.
    - **Auto-Lair doesn't break off** *("auto-lair will just pick them up again on its next pass in the room when they walk to them again, this situation is 99.99% unlikely as where gates are set, people don't loop through them.")*. No pickup walk is started. Auto-Lair carries on, and when it next reads a room that has the member in it, it sends `invite <name>` (once a minute at most per member; `PartyComebackManager.OnEntitiesObserved`). Their `@comeback` meanwhile gets one answer, `{I can't yet, an exit on my way turned you away. I'll invite you when my next pass finds you}` (`PartyComebackManager.LairGateReply`), only when denials are said. Auto-Lair stopped for good ends the promise. A member Auto-Lair leaves for another reason (held, too heavy) is gone back for as before.
    - **For a loop, only an exit of its own circuit, crossed by a step of the loop.** The exits are read off the running loop (`LoopRunner.CircuitExits`). A gate on the walk to the circuit's first room, on a train trip's walk, or crossed by hand with the loop paused is not the loop's: the loop won't leave the member there again, and they are gone back for.
    - **Only when the exit is what turned this member away** (the ruling's "a gate the party member cannot pass"). A member who has a wait or a hold out with the leader (`@wait`, `@held`) was stopped by that (`MemberSignalledHold`), and so was one whose `@ok` came in the 5 s before they were left: on its face an `@ok` is a release, but they said they were free and then didn't move, which is the premature-`@ok` rule (*A follower who can't move is left behind*). A member the exit is known to admit was stopped by something else (`MemberCanPass`, from `MemberGateJudge`): a level inside the window (the `@level` probe), the class and race the exit asks for (their `who` line), a purse that covers the toll or fare (their last `@wealth` answer), every item it asks for remembered in their hands (`PartyHandOverMemory.CopiesRememberedFor`). Both are gone back for, by a loop and by Auto-Lair. One condition known to be missing settles it the other way. **Where the leader can't tell** (a level never probed, an item nobody counted, an alignment window), **the gated step counts as the cause**. The wait is read in the same handler that then lets it go (`PartyComebackManager.OnMemberLeftBehind` → `ReleaseMemberWait`), so the reading doesn't depend on which listener of the game's line runs first.
    - **What the game does beats what the leader holds of the member.** A member the leader went back for from an exit, and who is dropped at that same exit again by a later step, is gated there whatever the judge says (a stale level, a purse the toll itself emptied, a condition the map doesn't carry): a loop refuses them from then on, however long after, Auto-Lair leaves them to its next pass, and a walk-to ends as above (`PartyComebackManager.JudgeGateDrop`). It is forgotten when the loop is stopped for good or fails (so a loop the user starts again judges afresh), when Auto-Lair stops for good, when the walk is over, and when a `par` lists the member as following after a later engine step through that exit. A member who signals a hold each time is still gone back for each time.
    - **How the leader learns of the drop.** Where the game says so (`<name> is no longer following you.`, Paradigm), the judgement is made on that line, for the step it came behind, and stands. Where the game tells a leader nothing (Stock), the request is judged: one naming a room against the engine's latest gated step out of that room, one naming no room against its latest gated step anywhere, and only when that step came after the member was last known to follow (their join, or a `par` that listed them) (`PartyComebackManager.GateVerdictForRequest`).
    - A loop's refusal is `{I can't, my loop goes through an exit you can't pass}` (`PartyComebackManager.LoopGateRefusal`), said only when `Settings.Talk.WarnOnInvalidRemoteCommand` lets denials be said, and the loop carries on. The follower's client logs it as a decline, asks no more, and gives the follow up (**A follower whose leader refuses, or never comes, stops counting itself a follower**).
    - An idle leader still answers `{I can't I'm idle}`.
    - **A train trip** is the other case where nobody is gone back for at once: *Training drops you from the party*.
    - `@forget` from a member who is waiting their turn, kept for the end of a trip or awaited after one, noted at a loop's gate, or to be invited on sight takes them off each (`PartyComebackManager.OnForget`).
    - The pickup ends with `invite <name>` from the leader (`PartyComebackManager.ReInviteAndAwait`) and, on the member's side, the join described under **The invite that ends the pickup is taken**. On Paradigm the invite is always sent. On Stock a member still on the leader's list is told to `@join` first and invited only if that doesn't bring them back (*A follower who can't move is left behind*, the Client use bullet "Stock: a member still on the leader's list is brought back with a `join`, not an invite"; an earlier form of this bullet said the invite was always sent, superseded 2026-10-11).
  - `PartyRejoinCoordinator` sends the reconnect `@comeback`, once, inside the Party tab's *If leading, accept @comeback for* window.
  - The bug report's Party section has the last incident (`ComebackRequester.LastIncidentSummary`).

### `@join` while already following
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-07-10 (capture)*

- **A follower client that receives `@join` while it is already following someone denies it.** It answers the telepath with **`I'm following someone; denied.`**, so `@join` is not idempotent against an existing follow.
- **This shows up downstream when a reform re-invite was lost.** The leader's `@join` nag then telepaths a member who never dropped their follow state, and the join is refused.
- **Client use:**
  - Landing the re-invite at the right time (post-arrival) avoids the nag path entirely.

### Party intel probe: `@level` / `@version` on partying
*Status: CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 (user design)*

- **When we start partying with a player, the client telepaths them intel probes.** This is `PartyProbeManager`. It works whether or not we lead, and is gated by Settings → Party "probe stats on partying" (default on).
- **`@health` fires on every join.** This is `PartyPoller`, for the live party-window HP/MA vitals (unchanged).
- **`@level` + `@version` fire only the first time we party with that player on a given local day.**
  - Gated by `PlayerObservation.LastPartiedUtc`, the same once-per-calendar-day way `GreetManager` rate-limits auto-greets.
  - The `@level` reply is recorded by `PartyLevelProbe` (the sole `@level` recorder).
  - The `@version` reply is recorded onto the player record (`PlayerObservation.Version` / `VersionAt`).
- **`@version` reply shape: the answering client returns its name + version, brace-wrapped**, e.g. `{MudPlay 2.37.0}` or `{MegaMud 1.03u}`. It is recorded verbatim.
  - The reply is correlated to the member we just probed within a short window.
  - It must be a brace-wrapped, letter-led payload carrying a digit. This rejects denial / chat lines and the `@level`/`@health` replies that share the window.
- **`@health` reply shape: `{HP=cur/max,MA=cur/max}`, with a MegaMUD member's status text after the numbers** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-15, report `paradigm-20261015-085123`)*: e.g. `{HP=878/878,MA=132/132, Losing HPs}` and `{HP=…,MA=…, Resting, Cant move}`. The text can run to several words.
  - **Client use:** `PartyPoller` and `AllyDroppedHandler` take anything up to the closing brace after the numbers. Taking one word only, they never read that member's reply, and the Party window showed no mana for them.
- **`@have <item>` reply shape differs by client** *([OBSERVED] 2026-10-15/16, reports `paradigm-20261015-095304`, `paradigm-20261016-031735`)*:
  - MudPlay: `{yes - 1x 'rope and grapple'}` or `{no - nothing matching 'rope and grapple'}`, brace-wrapped like every remote-command reply.
  - MegaMUD: `{yes: 1}`, a bare count with no item named.
  - `[NEEDS CONFIRMATION]` MegaMUD's reply when the member holds none hasn't been captured. A member who doesn't answer counts as holding none anyway (*Movement & navigation → Protective-item gates — exit-gated vs room-spell-gated*, Client policy 2026-10-09).
  - **Client use:** `PartyInventoryProbe` takes the braces off before matching (it matched only the unwrapped form, so every member's copy went uncounted), and credits a MegaMUD count to the oldest query still waiting on that member.
- **A recorded exact level supersedes the title-derived band, UNLESS the band's floor has risen above the exact reading** (`TitleRange.Min > exact`). This is exact-vs-title-band reconciliation (`PartyLevelEstimate`).
  - A floor above the exact reading means the player has clearly trained since we last asked: their `who` title moved up to a band starting above our recorded level.
  - In that case the **title band wins** until we re-learn an exact level at or above the band's floor.
  - A lower or overlapping band never overrides a valid exact; only a band whose floor has passed it does.
  - Example: recorded level 9, title band now 10-14 → the band wins, so the member reads 10-14, not a stale 9, until a fresh `@level` lands ≥ 10.
